240 | Electrical | Conduits, cable trays, wires, distribution boards, outlets and switches and luminaires, Revit's Electrical panel on the same run and the same fixtures. A conduit (eletroduto) and a wire are round, a cable
tray (eletrocalha) a width by a depth, each at a height over its level at each end (a riser stands upright), in a named `system` (a circuit: Circuito 3) that IFC carries as an `IfcSystem`. The project starts with PVC and
steel conduits, perforated trays in three sizes and copper wires, and a distribution board (12, 24 and 36 circuits), a ceiling and a recessed luminaire, an outlet and a switch, each at the mounting height its type says
(an outlet's 300, 1100 or 2100 mm to its centre; a luminaire hung from the slab), original drawings in the project's language, the luminaires, outlets and switches carrying connectors (voltage, poles, a load for each
type, per phase on a three-phase outlet; `inspect` warns of a device without one), written as `IfcCableCarrierSegment` (`CONDUITSEGMENT`, `CABLETRAYSEGMENT`; a `CABLELADDERSEGMENT` from another tool is read as a tray),
`IfcCableSegment`, `IfcElectricDistributionBoard`, `IfcOutlet`, `IfcSwitchingDevice` and `IfcLightFixture`, and read back. The project also keeps Revit's Electrical Settings: voltages (each with the band a device may
read within), distribution systems (phases, wires and the voltages each supplies) and wire types (material, insulation, temperature and an ampacity for each section, always in mm²), through `voltage`,
`distribution_system` and `wire_type`; it starts with 230/400 V, 127/220 V, 220/380 V and 277/480 V, and copper wires of the NBR 5410 tables (PVC 70 °C, XLPE or EPR 90 °C) and of the NEC (THHN, THW; AWG sizes kept in
mm²), whose ampacities are the contributor's and unchecked. Manage > Electrical Settings edits all three in one dialog, applied as one undo step. |
-----
243 | Reinforcement | `rebar` makes reinforcing bars: a round bar of a diameter (3 to 100 mm) and a steel grade (CA-50 unless told) bent along points in mm, in the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces, which it goes
with; `closed` makes a hoop, and `count` with `step` a layer of bars or hoops along a beam. A schedule of rebar lists grade, diameter, length, count and weight (steel at 7850 kg/m³) and, grouped, is a bar schedule. IFC
writes and reads each as an `IfcReinforcingBar`, aggregated to its host. The 3D view draws them as tubes (inside their host, so hide it to see them), a section draws the bars it cuts as dots over the poché, and a plan
draws each bar of its level as a thin line (solid under the cut plane, dashed over it and under the view range's top, a bar that stands as a dot, bars lying on one another drawn once), hidden with the category.
`reinforce` arms a beam, a column, a footing or a floor (round columns and footings, and sloped floors, too) by rules: the engineer gives the cover (or the host's `Cobrimento` parameter) and how many bars, how thick and
how far apart (a beam's bars below and above, stirrups with closer ends and hooks, skin bars and anchors; a column's bars on each face, stirrups and ties; a footing's two layers of mesh with their ends turned up; a
floor's meshes below and above, stopping short of its outline and openings), and it lays them out inside the cover, checks they fit with room between them and says what to change; a beam's bars and a column's end in
hooks if told, some of a beam's bottom bars bend up at each end to the top at an angle (`bent`) and a column's bars step in toward its axis near the top (`jog`); each bar is on a layer, and reinforcing again replaces
what it made and leaves bars drawn by hand. `hosts` arms a list alike, all or none (up to 1000 hosts and 20000 bars), and `reinforcement_preset` keeps a named set of the parameters for a kind of host in the project,
which `reinforce` takes with `preset` and lets what is given replace. The numbers are the engineer's; `check` "NBR 6118" (with the aggressiveness class and `fck`) adds notes, never a refusal, where the bars made fall
short of its usual limits (cover, bar sizes and spacings, stirrups, least and most steel, skin bars), typed from public handbooks and not from the standard's text, so check one against a copy before relying on it. On the
desktop, the Structure tab's Reinforce (RF) opens a dialog for the elements selected (any number, of one kind), with the fields of their kind, saying a refusal inside itself, keeping what was typed for the next of its
kind, saving the fields as a preset to choose for another and deleting one, and with Remove Bars for the bars it made. Not yet: bends other than a hook, a bent-up bar and a column's jog, round beams, bars beyond a
section's cut seen through the concrete. |
-----
249 | Views | A floor plan per level with Revit's view range: cut at its cut plane (1200 mm up by default), what lies below seen from it down to the bottom, faint beyond it down to the view depth, and roofs overhead up to
the top: wall poché with clean joins at any angle, compound walls' layers, hatched with their materials' cut patterns where they're wide enough (else lighter where they aren't structure), door swings, window glass, room
tags, grid bubbles, dimensions, door and window tags; PNG and SVG, which letter the view's name at the plan's bottom left (the window letters it too, over the canvas and on the screen only, which File > Settings can
hide; a viewport on a sheet has its own title). Sections and elevations along any line: the cut in poché (a roof's along its slope, a compound wall's, floor's, roof's or ceiling's with its layers), what lies beyond in
hidden line, levels named with their heights, grids; the four building elevations in one go; their marks on every plan; PNG. Crop regions on plans and sections: the view shows only what's inside, grids stopping at its
edge with their bubbles. A reflected ceiling plan per level: its walls cut at 2300 mm (over the doors, through the windows), looking up at the ceilings, their tiles and the shafts through them, and at the beams and
columns over the cut up to the ceilings, in projection (one over a ceiling is hidden by it). A 3D view, from any angle: walls with their doors and windows cut out, slabs and ceilings with their shafts cut out, columns,
stairs and roofs, door leaves and glass, shaded (each layer in its material's colour), with an edge wherever faces meet, but none between the facets of a curve (a curved wall's, a round form's, an imported mesh's where
its triangles turn less than 20°), which shades smoothly across them; PNG. A plan or a section always has a scale, 1 : n (1 : 100, or 1/8" = 1'-0" in feet and inches, until set): it stands for paper at that scale, and
its annotation (lettering, grid bubbles, marks, dimension ticks) and its line weights are that paper's, so on screen a line is as thick as it would print at the zoom (at least a pixel; Thin Lines draws all of them one).
A line weight is a pen, 1 to 16, or 0, a hairline, the thinnest line the screen, a PNG or a printer draws, at any scale and zoom; what pens 1 to 16 draw is the project's Line Weights (Manage > Line Weights, as Revit's):
the model's pens at each of a list of scales, a view taking the nearest scale's, and the annotation's (dimensions, tags, text, grids, levels, marks) at any scale, edited by scale, added and deleted, applied as one undo
step and saved with the project. Which pen each model category draws its own lines in, cut and seen, is the project's Object Styles (Manage > Object Styles, as Revit's), in every plan and section, a view's
Visibility/Graphics over them. Detail lines draw in one view (a plan, a section, an elevation or a sheet) in a line style: a pen, a colour and a line pattern, its freely ordered gaps, straight strokes, dots, centered
parallel offsets, waves, zigzags and text in mm on paper so it reads the same at any scale; the Line Pattern Creator previews straight or curved paths and letters text with bundled IBM Plex Sans, while geometry and
dimensions keep the centerline (Manage > Line Styles, styles and patterns made, changed, renamed and deleted as one undo step; a project starts with Thin, Medium and Wide Lines, a Hairline, Hidden, Centre and Overhead
Lines). A cut wall's outline is inked over its poché, and not across where walls join. A plan or a section has a detail level too: coarse (what it cuts in one poché, an opening as its gap and jambs), medium (a compound
element's layers and an opening's leaf, swing and glass) or fine, as it has always drawn (the layers' patterns too); the 3D view has a visual style: shaded, hidden line (paper-white faces with their edges, what a face
hides staying hidden) or wireframe (every edge, seen through the faces). A viewport takes its view's scale; a sheet keeps annotation at paper size. A view fitted into an image (a PNG, Zoom to Fit) leaves as much room
round it as its annotation takes at its scale, which grows with the scale, so 1 : 500 doesn't cut its grid bubbles or level names off. A level can have more plans than its own, as Revit's Duplicate View makes them
(`duplicate_view`, DP): each a plan view with its own view range, crop and graphics and its own dimensions, tags, notes and spot elevations over the same model; with detailing it starts with its source's annotation; a
dependent view follows its parent's view range and graphics (scale and detail too), has a crop of its own, and shows its parent's annotation as well as its own. They go on sheets, take view templates and have ceiling
plans as levels do. Sections, elevations, schedules, sheets and the 3D view aren't duplicated yet. The 3D view is parallel (axonometric) or in perspective, as through a camera: picked from Projection in its Properties
(or `perspective`), seen through a lens of a focal length typed there, from an eye raised or lowered to a height typed there, and orbited, panned, zoomed, picked and edited as ever, on the processor or the graphics card.
The Camera tool (`camera`) makes a view of its own, as Revit's does: an eye and a target are clicked in a plan (each at a height over it, typed in the Options Bar), and a named 3D view in perspective opens looking from
the eye at the target; it is listed under 3D Views in the Project Browser, opens from its own camera, and its name, eye, target and lens are read and changed in Properties, whether it is open or its mark on the plan is
picked (`camera` reads or changes one too, by name or id; a view with no camera shows the azimuth and elevation it is framed by on a sheet instead). The camera shows on its level's plan as a mark at its eye with a line
to what it looks at: it is picked there and opened by its right-click menu (or a double click), and its eye and target follow the mouse as the view is orbited, panned or zoomed, so leaving the view and coming back stands
it where it was left. The 3D view has a section box, as Revit's: six planes square to the axes that keep what lies between them, the model's surfaces and its point clouds alike, turned on and off with BX or its
Properties, each face dragged by its grip in the view or typed in Properties, its extents kept while it's off; the levels it doesn't reach are left out. A plan can follow it (Section Box in the plan's Properties): it
then shows what the box keeps, cut at the box's top, seen down to its bottom and cropped to its sides, and snaps to a scan where the box's top cuts it |
-----
252 | Visibility and graphics | What each view hides, and how it draws the rest, as Revit's Visibility/Graphics does, for each plan, section, elevation and 3D view: whole categories left out (walls, doors, rooms, grids,
dimensions, levels in a section…), or single elements; lines and fills overridden by category, by element and by view filter: a colour, weight and dash for what the view cuts and for what it sees (a plan's below its cut
plane, the annotation; in 3D, and in a section beyond its line, the edges' colour), the cut's poché colour or a 3D view's surface colour (a weight is a pen, 0 a hairline at any scale), halftone (halfway to the paper)
and, in 3D, transparency, where what lies behind shows through and a click still picks the element (halftone and transparency only add: a filter or an element can't take its category's away). A hidden door or window
leaves its opening in the wall, and snaps, Tag All, Select All and a view's framing take what it shows. View filters pick elements out by rules, a schedule filter's (a field of the category, how to compare it, a value,
project parameters among the fields), on the categories chosen; a view applies them in order, the first prevailing where they disagree, and one that hides hides whatever the others say; an element's own override beats
the filters', and those beat the category's. View templates keep a view's categories, filters, phase, design options, scale, detail level, visual style and, for a plan, view range under a name, for other views to follow:
what a template controls isn't the view's to change, and changed, every view following it follows. A project's filters and templates are saved with it; sheets print each view as its graphics say |
-----
253 | Phasing and design options | Phases in order, as Revit's Phasing has them (a project starts with Existing and New Construction): each element is made in one (its `Phase Created`, the first unless it says) and may be
taken down in a later one (`Phase Demolished`), so in a view's phase it is new, existing, demolished (taken down in it) or temporary (made and taken down in it), and what is made after the phase, or taken down before it,
isn't there. A view has a phase (the project's last unless it says) and a phase filter, which shows each status as its category does, as the project's overrides for that status say (existing in halftone and demolished
dashed red to begin with, both yours to change) or not at all; a project starts with Show All, Show Complete, Show New, Show Previous + Demolished and Show Previous + New. A door or window with no phase of its own
follows its wall. Phases are added, inserted, renamed and combined, and what was made, taken down or shown in one goes along; phase filters are made and changed. Design options are sets of options, as Revit's Design
Options: an element in an option of a set (`Design Option`, `set: option`) shows only in a view that shows that option, the set's primary unless the view chooses, and one in none shows everywhere. Options are added,
renamed, made the primary and taken out (one with elements in it stays until they are moved); accepting the primary keeps its elements and takes the others' and the set away, and deleting a set takes its elements too.
What a session makes is made in the phase of the view it is drawn in, when that view has a phase or a phase filter of its own, and in the active design option; a copy is made in them too, and isn't taken down with the
element it was copied from, while what is made with a phase or an option given keeps it. Schedules and view filters read the phase and the option as fields (a schedule sorts and groups the phases in the project's order,
Existing before New Construction, whatever their names; a rule that names a phase, an option or a set follows it when it is renamed or combined); the desktop's Demolish tool (DW) takes an element down in the phase of the
view it is clicked in, and a second click takes it back; templates can control a view's phase and its options; sheets print each view in its phase; a project's phases, filters, overrides and sets are saved with it. A
project saved before phases that holds a project parameter named `Phase Created`, `Phase Demolished` or `Design Option` opens with it renamed (`Phase Created Parameter`), its values with it |
-----
256 | Project parameters | Values of your own that each element of their categories holds (text, numbers, lengths, yes or no, unset a no), as Revit's project parameters are: set in Properties or with `modify`, shown,
filtered and sorted in schedules and read by their formulas, and written to IFC in a `Project Parameters` property set and read back from it; renamed, schedules follow; taken off a category, its elements and schedules
lose them |
-----
263 | Files | `.bimcraft` projects (JSON, file format 12: every save is 12, so an earlier build refuses even a plain project saved by this one, saying it is from a newer BIMCraft); IFC4 export with storeys, walls swept up
from their plan outline (mitred where they join, an arc in short chords) or, attached to a roof, as closed shells, walls, floors, roofs and ceilings with their material layer sets (each material with its colour), slabs
(sloped ones as closed shells), ceilings as coverings, spaces and columns, walls, slabs, doors and windows with their `Qto_*BaseQuantities` (a wall's side area and volume gross and less its openings, a slab's area and
volume less its openings), beams (`IfcBeam`), footings (`IfcFooting`), pipes (`IfcPipeSegment`), conduits, cable trays and wires (`IfcCableCarrierSegment`, `IfcCableSegment`) and structural columns and floors, each along
its own axis and, if structural, with `LoadBearing` in its `Pset_*Common`, the runs of a system assigned to an `IfcSystem` of its name, stairs and ramps as their flights, landings and railings (each railing with its
rail's top line as its axis), roofs as closed shells of flat faces (hip, gable, shed or flat), openings that cut the walls and hold the doors and windows, an opening for each slab, ceiling and roof a shaft passes
through, masses as building element proxies of object type `Mass` (a lofted one as a closed face set), and components as furniture, sanitary or waste terminals, pipe fittings, valves, distribution boards, outlets,
switching devices, communications appliances, light fixtures or proxies, named `Family:Type` as Revit names them, each form a closed face set in its material's colour, each element's values of the project parameters in a
`Project Parameters` property set (dimensions, tags, notes and spot elevations belong to views, and stay out of it), and each element's phase and design option in a `BIMCraft_Phasing` property set: its `Phase Created` is
always named in it, the first phase too (said to be implied, for another tool to read; a door or window says only what it holds, as one with no phase follows its wall), `Phase Demolished` and `Design Option` where it
holds them, and the project's phases in order, with the phase filters, overrides and option sets it changed, in one on the project, and, as IFC says it, its `Status` in its `Pset_*Common` (`EXISTING`, `DEMOLISH`, `NEW`
or `TEMPORARY`, for another tool to filter the work by); a project that uses none of it writes none |
-----

A type change updates every region using it; the palette's Type Selector controls the instance's type. Non-masking fills keep cut foreground patterns and projected model lines visible; masking fills cover the model.
Sketches snap to visible model edges, detail lines, existing region boundaries and their own geometry, with the configured snaps and angle guides. |

491 | `reinforcement_preset` | | `name?`, `kind?` (beam, column, footing, floor), `params?` (what `reinforce` takes, but the host), `rename?`, `delete?`: a named set of parameters, kept in the project; no `name` lists them |

`existing`, `demolished` or `temporary`: an override, null takes it away}): the project's phases in order, and how a phase filter draws a status it says overridden. An element is made in a phase by its `Phase Created`

535 | `phase_filter` | | `name`, `new?`, `existing?`, `demolished?`, `temporary?` (`by-category`, `overridden` or `not-displayed`), `delete?`: how a view shows each status of what is in its phase; a view applies one with

536 | `option` | | `set?`, `options?` ([names]), `primary?`, `option?`, `rename?`, `delete?`, `accept?`, `now?` (`set: option`, or null: the option this session makes elements in): sets of design options; an element is in
one by its `Design Option` parameter, and a view chooses which to show with `graphics {options}` |

takes the nearest scale's), the annotation's at any; pen 0 is always a hairline; without any, what they are |

540 | `object_styles` | | `categories?` ({category: {`projection?`, `cut?`}: pens 0 to 16}), `reset?`: the project's Object Styles, the pen each model category draws its own lines in, seen and cut, in every plan and section,
under a view's Visibility/Graphics; without either, each category's |
-----
541 | `line_pattern` | | `name?`, `segments?` (1–32 freely ordered Gap/`space`, Straight/`dash`, `dot_length`, `offset`, `wave`, `zigzag`, `text` segments; lengths in paper mm), `rename?`, `delete?`: create/edit a graphic
line pattern. Offset has `length`, `count` (2–9), `distance`; waves/zigzags have `length`, `frequency` (cycles per segment), `amplitude`; text has `length`, `size`, `text`, in bundled IBM Plex Sans, flowing along curves.
Geometry and dimensions retain the centerline. Without a name, lists every pattern |
-----
542 | `line_style` | | `name?`, `pen?` (0 to 16), `color?`, `pattern?` (a line pattern's name, or `Solid`), `rename?`, `delete?`: a line style of the project's, what detail lines draw in; without `name`, every one |

# Phases and design options

Moved from the root `CLAUDE.md`, word for word: the root keeps the rules and the map, and this file is read when the area is touched.

Phases (`Model::phases`, in order) and design options (`Model::option_sets`, `phasing.rs`) are values an element holds among its
`params`, under names no project parameter or family parameter may take (`phasing::CREATED`, `DEMOLISHED`, `OPTION`; `Phase Created` is the first
phase when it has no value, `Design Option` is `set: option`; `open` renames an older file's project parameter of such a name), so `modify`, copies, schedules (`From::Param` in `schedule::OWN`)
and view filters reach them as any other. `phasing::status` says what an element is at a phase's place in the order (new,
existing, demolished, temporary, or not there); a door or window with none of its own follows its wall (`phasing::value`), and
annotation, which holds no params, belongs to a view. A view's `Graphics` hold `phase` (the project's last unless it says),
`phase_filter` (every status by category unless it says; `Model::phase_filters` show each status by category, overridden or
not at all, and `Model::phase_overrides` draw the overridden ones, never hidden or see-through) and `options` (`{set: option}`,
a set's primary unless it says); `Look::of` hides what a phase, a filter or an option leaves out and paints what a filter
overrides, below the view's own overrides. `Session::phase` and `Session::option` are what commands make (`Session::stamp`
gives each new element its `Phase Created` (none for the first phase, but a door or window is named, or it would follow its
wall) and its `Design Option` where it holds none; a copy takes the session's and loses its `Phase Demolished`; `split`, undo,
redo and the commands that replace the project stamp nothing); a refused command leaves them as they were; they
belong to the session, not the model, and the desktop sets them before each command (`BimApp::made_in`): the phase of the view
on screen when it has a phase or a phase filter of its own, and the active design option (`activate`, which shows it in the
view too). What was made in the first phase holds no value, so a phase put in before the first, or the first deleted, names it first
(`phasing::pin_first`; a door or window follows its wall, which is named). Deleting or combining a phase moves what was in it to
`into` (`phasing::move_phase`), and renaming a phase, an option or a set takes the elements, the views and the rules of filters
and schedules along; accepting a set keeps the primary's elements and deletes the rest.
IFC carries them in property sets named `ifc::PHASING`, `BIMCraft_Phasing`. An element that holds a phase or an option gets one:
`Phase Created` (always: the first phase is named too, with `ifc::IMPLIED` as its description where the element holds none, but a
door or window holds only what it says, or one with no phase would stop following its wall), `Phase Demolished` and `Design
Option`, as text. The project gets one when an element holds a phase or an option, or it changed its phases, filters or overrides,
or has an option set: `Phases`, a list of the names in order, and, where it changed them, `Phase Filters`, `Phase Overrides` and
`Design Option Sets` as the JSON a project file holds them in; a project that uses none of it writes none, and the file is as it
was. A phased project also says, for any tool that reads IFC's own words, what the work does to each element: `Status`
(`ifc::ifc_status`) in its `Pset_*Common` (`ifc::common_pset`, the one set that holds `LoadBearing` too), `DEMOLISH` where it is
taken down, `TEMPORARY` where that is in the phase it was made in, `EXISTING` where it was made in the first phase and `NEW`
else; a door or window with no phase says its wall's. It is written, not read: the import still takes phases from `BIMCraft_Phasing`. `import.rs` reads them beside the project parameters: what the project can't have (a phase or an option it hasn't, a
demolition before the creation, a list or a JSON that breaks `phasing::check_project`) is left out and listed, and the element
stays (it is the property, not the element, that breaks the rule); an implied `Phase Created` is no value; no other set is read, so
one another tool writes for phases, `Phasing` say, changes nothing.
A schedule sorts and groups `Phase Created` and `Phase Demolished` by the phase's place in `Model::phases`, not by its name, no
`Phase Demolished` coming after every phase (`schedule::sorts_as`); its filters still compare the names. The desktop's Demolish
tool (DW, `BimApp::demolish`, in the Modify tab's Phasing panel) runs `modify {params: {Phase Demolished}}` on the element clicked in a
plan, a section or the 3D view: the phase of the view on screen (the project's last unless it has one), or null when the element
already comes down in it, one undo step a click. A door or window that only follows its wall gets a note instead, and an element that
holds no `params` (annotation, levels, grids, shafts) says so and changes nothing.
The view control bar's Renovation menu (`BimApp::renovation_menu`, `phasing.rs` in the desktop, the same in both profiles) says in plain
words which phase of the work a plan, a section or the 3D view shows: All (no phase and no phase filter of its own, the view as it
starts), Existing (the project's first phase, every status by its category), Demolition (the last phase through a filter that hides
what is new, draws what stood before by its category and what comes down overridden) and New (the last through one that draws what
stood before overridden and hides what comes down). A pick is one `graphics {phase, phase_filter}`, one undo step. The words map onto
filters by what they do, never by their names, which a project renames or has in its own language (`RENOVATION`, `renovation`,
`filter_for`): the project's `Show Previous + Demolished` and `Show Previous + New` to start with. A choice the project has no
filter for is greyed out and says so, a view whose phase and filter match none of them shows Custom, the menu is greyed out where
a view template sets the phase, and the Sketch scale leaves it out with the rest of phasing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run each argument as its own `run --cmd ...` session on the original (or mine with -m), print outputs.
usage: t.py [-m] [-s] [-p prefix_cmd]... cmd...
  -s : also save x.bimcraft and print given sections (-k key)
  -p : a command to run before each test cmd (repeatable)
  -c : compare with mine
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a82ef70e7d948a64e/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
pre = []
keys = []
cmp = False
cut = 600
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-c': cmp = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-p': pre.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-k': keys.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w': cut = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
def run1(exe, cmd):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='t')
    args = [exe, 'run']
    for p in pre: args += ['--cmd', p]
    args += ['--cmd', cmd]
    if keys: args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    out = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip().split('\n')
    out = out[len(pre):] if p.returncode == 0 or len(out) > len(pre) else out
    res = '\n'.join(l[:cut] for l in out if l)
    err = p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()
    s = res + (('\nERR: ' + err[:cut]) if err else '')
    if keys and os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')):
        doc = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
        for k in keys:
            s += '\n  [%s] %s' % (k, json.dumps(doc.get(k, '<absent>'), ensure_ascii=False)[:cut])
        s += '\n  top: ' + ','.join(doc.keys())
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return s
for cmd in a:
    o = run1(exe, cmd)
    print('>>', cmd)
    print(o)
    if cmp:
        m = run1(MINE, cmd)
        if m != o:
            print('!! MINE DIFFERS:')
            print(m)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""q.py 'cmd1' 'cmd2' ... : run each as a separate `run --cmd` against the original; print reply/error.
Options: -s (prepend each with a script of several commands separated by ';;'), -m (use mine too)."""
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/cloud-agent')
from orig import run
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2ffdd25819f1e2dc/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
args = sys.argv[1:]
both = False
if args and args[0] == '-m':
    both = True; args = args[1:]
for c in args:
    parts = c.split(';;')
    a = ['run']
    for p in parts:
        a += ['--cmd', p.strip()]
    out, _ = run(a, cwd=os.getcwd())
    s = (out[1] + out[2]).strip().replace('/workspace/assets/test_cloud_formats/', '@/')
    if both:
        o2, _ = run(a, cwd=os.getcwd(), exe=MINE)
        s2 = (o2[1] + o2[2]).strip().replace('/workspace/assets/test_cloud_formats/', '@/')
        mark = 'SAME' if (s2 == s and o2[0] == out[0]) else 'DIFF'
        print('[%s] %s\n   O(%d): %s' % (mark, c, out[0], s))
        if mark == 'DIFF':
            print('   M(%d): %s' % (o2[0], s2))
    else:
        print('%s\n   (%d) %s' % (c, out[0], s))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the original (or mine with -m) with a list of commands in a temp dir.
usage: o.py [-m] [-k] [-s] [-e K=V] cmd1 cmd2 ...   (each 'id {json}')
 -s: save project and print selected sections; -k keep dir
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, tempfile, json, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a950f58ddd6484974/target/release/bimcraft-cli')

def run(cmds, exe=ORIG, save=False, env=None, cwd=None, extra=None):
    d = cwd or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='o')
    args = [exe, 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    if save:
        args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    if extra:
        args += extra
    e = dict(os.environ)
    if env:
        e.update(env)
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=300)
    proj = None
    if save and os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')):
        proj = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
    if not cwd:
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), proj

if __name__ == '__main__':
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    exe = ORIG; save = False; secs = []
    while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
        if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-s': save = True; secs = a[1].split(',') if len(a) > 1 else []; a = a[2:]
        else: break
    code, out, err, proj = run(a, exe, save)
    sys.stdout.write(out)
    sys.stdout.write(err)
    print('code', code)
    if proj:
        for s in secs:
            print(s, json.dumps(proj.get(s), ensure_ascii=False)[:3000])

"""Feed picture bytes to the original (or mine) and get the reply/error and decoded pixels."""
import os, sys, json, base64, tempfile, subprocess, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/media-agent')
from o import run, ORIG, MINE
import pnglib

def feed(data, exe=ORIG, name='p.png', save=True):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='pic')
    path = os.path.join(d, name)
    open(path, 'wb').write(data)
    c = 'material ' + json.dumps({"name": "G", "texture": {"kind": "image", "path": path}})
    code, out, err, proj = run([c], exe, save=save, cwd=d)
    res = {'code': code, 'out': out.replace(d, '<D>'), 'err': err.replace(d, '<D>')}
    if proj and 'images' in proj:
        imgs = proj['images']
        k = list(imgs)[0]
        png = base64.b64decode(imgs[k]['png'])
        res['id'] = k
        res['png'] = png
        res['name'] = imgs[k]['name']
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return res

def pixels(res):
    return pnglib.decode_stored(res['png'])

insert : {path, ids?: [id, …]} elements of another project (.bimcraft or .ifc) brought into this one: those `ids` names (their ids there), else all of them, and what they point at that this project hasn't (a level they stand on is this project's of the same name, where it has one). Each keeps its id unless this project has that id, and its GUID unless this project has that GUID: then it's a copy, with a GUID of its own (the same file inserted into itself is copied whole). What they point at among themselves follows them. A name or a number taken here gets ` 2`, ` 3`…; types, families, materials and parameters this project hasn't come by name, and so do the line styles (with their line patterns), fill patterns, filled region types and detail groups a detail line, a filled region or a group uses. Returns `ids` {there: here}, `copies`, `library`, `left_out`

link : {path, name?, at?: [x, y], angle?: degrees} another project (.bimcraft or .ifc) shown in this one as a reference that can't be edited, as Revit's Link Revit: its walls, floors, roofs, columns, stairs and the rest of what it builds are drawn in the plans, sections and 3D views, halftone, and snapped to; nothing of it is selected, scheduled, checked or exported. It stands with its origin at `at` (default [0, 0]) turned `angle` about it; its levels stand at their own elevations, on this project's levels at the same height. `path` is read now and again by `reload`, and kept as given: a relative one is relative to this project's file. `name` defaults to the file's. Returns `id`, `name`, `elements`

import_cad : {path | cad, name?, level?, view?, at?: [x, y], position?, units?, scale?, angle?, layers?, colors?, link?} brings in a DXF drawing (`path`: an ASCII DXF of any version, or a DWG, which the desktop and the command line read as DXF) or places one the project holds again (`cad`, its name), as an element in every plan of `level`, or with `view` (a plan) in that view only. `units` of the drawing: auto (the default: what its file says, else mm), mm, cm, m, in or ft; or `scale`, mm to each of its units. `position`: center (the default: the middle of the drawing on `at`, the origin unless given) or origin (its origin on `at`); `angle` turns it about `at`, degrees. `layers`: visible (the default: those its file has on and thawed), all, or a list of those to show. `colors`: preserve (the default), invert or black. `link: true` remembers the file, so `reload_cad` and opening the project read it again. Returns its id, the drawing's name, its unit, entities and layers, its extents in the model, how many entities lie far from the rest (they're left out of its extents) and what was left out, with `notes` on what a DWG's read left out

material : {name, color?: "#rrggbb" | [r, g, b], transparency?: 0-100, cut?, surface?, texture?: {kind?, size?: [w, h], angle?, offset?: [x, y], path?, image?} | null, rename?, delete?: true} a material of the project's library, created or changed: its colour in shaded 3D views, its `transparency` there (percent of what lies behind it that shows through, 0 opaque; the starter Glass has 70), the pattern its cut shows in plans and sections (where a layer is wide enough to hold it), and the one its surfaces show at its size in the building (a floor's top in plan, a ceiling's underside in its ceiling plan). Patterns: none, solid, diagonal, crosshatch, horizontal, vertical, grid, brick, concrete, insulation, or the name of one of the project's fill patterns (see `fill_pattern`), kept while the material shows it and renamed with it. Its `texture` is what its surfaces look like in the 3D view, over its colour, a tile of it `size` mm across and up, turned `angle` degrees and moved `offset` mm: a pattern drawn in code, `kind` brick, block, boards, concrete, plaster, tile, roof, fabric, metal or insulation (at its natural size unless `size` says); or `image`, a picture: the PNG or JPEG file at `path`, taken into the project (up to 1024 px a side, 24 pictures), or one the project holds (`image`, its id from `inspect`); null takes the texture away. `rename` renames it, the layers using it following; `delete` takes it away, while no layer uses it. `inspect` lists the library and the pictures

modify : {id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it

move : {ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy], end?: start|end} moves elements in plan; walls joined to a moved wall stretch to stay joined, and doors and windows slide along their walls. With `end`, only that end of one wall moves

copy : {ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy]} copies elements, with the doors and windows of copied walls; returns the copies' ids

rotate : {ids: [id,…], about: [x, y], angle, copy?} turns elements about a point by `angle` degrees, counter-clockwise; walls joined to them stay joined, and doors and windows turn with their walls

mirror : {ids: [id,…], axis: [[x, y], [x, y]], copy?} mirrors elements across the line through two points; mirrored doors and windows face the other way

delete : {ids: [id,…]} deleting a wall deletes its doors and windows, deleting those their tags; a view takes its notes and spot elevations, and what a spot elevation reads takes it; dimensions lose what's deleted

purge : {kinds?: [type|family|material|picture|filter|template, …], dry_run?} takes out what nothing uses, again for what that leaves unused: types and families unless `kinds` says; a category keeps a type and a family a type; with `dry_run` it lists what would go and changes nothing

inspect : {} levels, element counts, types, warnings and undo history

render : {family?, type?, mode?: 3d|plan|elevation, wall_thickness?, view?: a level's, section's or elevation's name or id, a sheet's number, or {3D}, ceiling?, width?, height?, path?, azimuth?, elevation?, eye_elevation?} a family on its own with `family` — its `type` (the first by default) standing in a model of its own, in a wall `wall_thickness` mm thick (200) if it's a door's or a window's, nothing of this project's touched or left behind: `3d` (as seen from the south-east), `plan` (what its symbols draw) or `elevation` (front-on, as seen from the north), a PNG as `pngBase64` or at `path`. Without it: a level's floor plan (with `ceiling`, its reflected ceiling plan, looking up from 2300 mm), a section, an elevation, a sheet (at 5 px a paper mm), or the 3D view seen from `azimuth` degrees round from east (counter-clockwise) and `elevation` degrees up (by default from the south-east, 30° up), fitted; in perspective (see `perspective`) through its lens, and with `eye_elevation` from an eye that high (mm) looking at the same point, as a PNG (pngBase64), or written to a path: .png, .svg for a plan, .pdf for a sheet. A plan, section, elevation or sheet that could not draw something as asked (a fill pattern too dense for the view, more ink behind a region than is kept above it) says so in the reply's `notes`

section_box : {view?: a 3D view's name or id ({3D} unless given), on?: true | false (true unless given), min?: [x, y, z], max?: [x, y, z]} the box a 3D view is cut to, as Revit's Section Box: six planes square to the axes, keeping what lies between `min` and `max` (mm; each at least 10 mm past the other on every axis), the model's surfaces and its point clouds alike, so a scan's floors and ceilings can be cut away to show its walls. What it cuts away isn't drawn or picked. A corner not given stays where it was; turned on with none, it's fitted round the model, 300 mm clear of it. `on: false` turns it off and keeps its extents for when it's turned on again

library : {kind?, name?} the project's library with its ids and GUIDs, as elements have them: each type (`kind` `type:wall`, `type:door`, `type:beam`…), material, picture, family, parameter, view filter and template (`view-filter`, `view-template`), phase, phase filter, design option set and design option (`option-set`, `design-option`, named `set: option`), family type and family parameter (`family-type`, `family-parameter`, named `family: name`); and `parts`, what entries hold that has its own id and GUID: each type's layers and each family's forms and symbols (`kind` `layer`, `form`, `symbol`; `name` the type's or the family's). Wherever a command takes an entry by name, its GUID does too

elements : {category?, level?, limit?, offset?} elements with their `id` (six digits, what commands take) and `guid` (made once, never changed), fields and derived values (length, height, area_m2…); what an element points at (its level, host, view…) it holds by GUID. Wherever a command takes an element, its id or its GUID will do

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive `mcp --connect` against the fake window.

usage: bridge.py [-m] [-a 'extra args'] [-j bridge_json_override] [-w seconds_between_lines] ACTIONS_JSON line...
  ACTIONS_JSON: see fakewin.py ('-' for the default: hello ok then echo)
  Lines are MCP messages; '@init' expands to initialize.
  Prints CLI stdout/stderr/exit and the window log.
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, json, tempfile, time, shlex
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'
TOKEN = 'f00dfeedcafe0123456789abcdef0001'

a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
extra = []
bj = None
wait = 0.0
trunc = 1000
connect = ['--connect']
while a and a[0].startswith('-') and len(a[0]) == 2:
    if a[0] == '-m':
        exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-a':
        extra = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-c':
        connect = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-j':
        bj = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w':
        wait = float(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-t':
        trunc = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else:
        break
actions = a[0]
if actions == '-':
    actions = json.dumps(['{"ok":true}\n', {"default": {"echo": True}}])
lines = [INIT if x == '@init' else x for x in a[1:]]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='br')
xdg = os.path.join(d, 'xdg')
os.makedirs(os.path.join(xdg, 'bimcraft'))
portfile = os.path.join(d, 'port')
logfile = os.path.join(d, 'log')
open(logfile, 'w').close()
srv = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '/tmp/mcp-agent/fakewin.py', portfile, logfile, actions])
for _ in range(100):
    if os.path.exists(portfile) and open(portfile).read():
        break
    time.sleep(0.05)
port = int(open(portfile).read())
if bj is None:
    bjs = json.dumps({"port": port, "token": TOKEN})
else:
    bjs = bj.replace('PORT', str(port))
open(os.path.join(xdg, 'bimcraft', 'bridge.json'), 'w').write(bjs)
env = dict(os.environ)
env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = xdg
env['HOME'] = d
connect = [x.replace('PORT', str(port)) for x in connect]
work = os.path.join(d, 'work')
os.makedirs(work)
t0 = time.time()
p = subprocess.Popen([exe, 'mcp'] + extra + connect, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, cwd=work, env=env)
if wait:
    for l in lines:
        p.stdin.write((l + '\n').encode())
        p.stdin.flush()
        time.sleep(wait)
    p.stdin.close()
    out = p.stdout.read(); err = p.stderr.read(); p.wait()
else:
    out, err = p.communicate(('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode() if lines else b'', timeout=120)
el = time.time() - t0
time.sleep(0.2)
srv.kill()
for l in out.decode('utf-8', 'replace').splitlines():
    print('OUT:', l[:trunc] + ('...(%d)' % len(l) if len(l) > trunc else ''))
if err:
    print('ERR:', err.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), end='')
print('EXIT:', p.returncode, ' (%.1fs)' % el)
print('--- window log')
for l in open(logfile):
    print('  ' + l.rstrip('\n')[:trunc])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run ONE session: each arg is a --cmd (in order); print each reply line; optional save + section dump.
usage: s.py [-m] [-k key]... [-f file] [-o openfile] cmd...
  -k key : save x.bimcraft at the end and print that top-level key (repeatable); '-k top' prints key order
  -f file: copy file into the temp dir
  -o path: open this project first (positional arg to run)
  -e     : print elements
  -l kind: print library entries of that kind
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
keys = []
files = []
opn = None
els = False
libk = []
while a and a[0].startswith('-') and len(a[0]) == 2:
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-k': keys.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-o': opn = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-e': els = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-l': libk.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='s')
for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
args = [exe, 'run']
if opn: args.append(opn)
for c in a: args += ['--cmd', c]
save = bool(keys or els or libk)
if save: args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
print(p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').rstrip())
err = p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()
if err: print('ERR:', err)
if save and os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')):
    doc = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
    for k in keys:
        if k == 'top': print('  top:', ','.join(doc.keys()))
        else: print('  [%s] %s' % (k, json.dumps(doc.get(k, '<absent>'), ensure_ascii=False)))
    if els:
        for k, v in doc['elements'].items():
            print('  el', k, json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False))
    for kind in libk:
        for k, v in doc['library'].items():
            if v['kind'] == kind: print('  lib', k, v)
shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One session: run each arg as a --cmd in order (orig, or mine with -m); print each reply line.
  -k key : save the project and print this top-level key (repeatable); -K prints all top keys
  -w N   : cut lines at N chars
  -f file: copy file into the temp dir first; -o path: open this project first (positional)
  -c     : compare with mine (prints MINE DIFFERS on any difference)
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
keys = []
cut = 1000
files = []
opn = []
cmp = False
top = False
while a and a[0].startswith('-') and a[0] != '--':
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-c': cmp = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-K': top = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-k': keys.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w': cut = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-o': opn.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
def run(exe):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='s')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    args = [exe, 'run'] + opn
    for c in a: args += ['--cmd', c]
    if keys or top: args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    out = []
    for l in p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').split('\n'):
        if l: out.append(l[:cut])
    err = p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()
    if err: out.append('ERR: ' + err[:cut])
    out.append('exit %d' % p.returncode)
    fp = os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')
    if (keys or top) and os.path.exists(fp):
        doc = json.load(open(fp))
        for k in keys:
            out.append('[%s] %s' % (k, json.dumps(doc.get(k, '<absent>'), ensure_ascii=False)[:cut]))
        out.append('top: ' + ','.join(doc.keys()))
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out
o = run(exe)
print('\n'.join(o))
if cmp:
    m = run(MINE)
    if m != o:
        print('!! MINE DIFFERS:')
        import difflib
        for l in difflib.unified_diff(o, m, 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=0):
            print(l[:cut])
    else:
        print('== same')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Many independent sessions: each arg is one test command, run after the -p prefix commands.
Prints the test command's reply (or error). -c compares with mine. -k key: save & print key.
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
pre = []
keys = []
cut = 500
cmp = False
exe = ORIG
hist = False
files = []
opn = []
while a and a[0].startswith('-') and a[0] != '--':
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-c': cmp = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-H': hist = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-p': pre.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-k': keys.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w': cut = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-o': opn.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
def run1(exe, cmd):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='m')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    args = [exe, 'run'] + opn
    for p in pre: args += ['--cmd', p]
    args += ['--cmd', cmd]
    if hist: args += ['--cmd', 'inspect']
    if keys: args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    lines = [l for l in p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').split('\n') if l]
    npre = len(pre) + len(opn)
    res = lines[npre:]
    h = None
    if hist and p.returncode == 0:
        try:
            h = json.loads(res[1])['history']
        except Exception:
            h = '?'
        res = res[:1] + res[2:]
    s = '\n'.join(l[:cut] for l in res)
    err = p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()
    if err: s += '\nERR: ' + err[:cut]
    if hist: s += '\n  history: %s' % h
    fp = os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')
    if keys and os.path.exists(fp):
        doc = json.load(open(fp))
        for k in keys:
            s += '\n  [%s] %s' % (k, json.dumps(doc.get(k, '<absent>'), ensure_ascii=False)[:cut])
        s += '\n  top: ' + ','.join(doc.keys())
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return s
nd = 0
for cmd in a:
    o = run1(exe, cmd)
    if cmp:
        m = run1(MINE, cmd)
        if m != o:
            nd += 1
            print('>>', cmd)
            print(o)
            print('!! MINE:')
            print(m)
    else:
        print('>>', cmd)
        print(o)
if cmp:
    print('%d of %d differ' % (nd, len(a)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, struct
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    b = open(f, 'rb').read()
    print('==', f, len(b), 'bytes')
    print(' sig', b[:4], 'src', struct.unpack('<H', b[4:6]), 'enc', struct.unpack('<H', b[6:8]))
    vmaj, vmin = b[24], b[25]
    print(' version %d.%d' % (vmaj, vmin), 'sysid', b[26:58].rstrip(b'\0'), 'sw', b[58:90].rstrip(b'\0'))
    hs, off, nvlr = struct.unpack('<HIL', b[94:104])
    fmt, reclen, npts = struct.unpack('<BHI', b[104:111])
    print(' header_size', hs, 'offset_to_points', off, 'nvlr', nvlr, 'format', fmt, 'reclen', reclen, 'legacy_count', npts)
    print(' by_return', struct.unpack('<5I', b[111:131]))
    sc = struct.unpack('<3d', b[131:155]); of = struct.unpack('<3d', b[155:179])
    print(' scale', sc, 'offset', of)
    mm = struct.unpack('<6d', b[179:227])
    print(' maxx minx maxy miny maxz minz', mm)
    if hs > 227:
        print(' extra header', b[227:hs].hex())
        if vmin >= 4 and hs >= 375:
            wf, evlr, nevlr, n64 = struct.unpack('<QQIQ', b[227:255])
            print(' 1.4: waveform', wf, 'evlr', evlr, 'nevlr', nevlr, 'count64', n64)
    print(' after header..offset', b[hs:off].hex())
    print(' points', b[off:].hex())

results.content:
modify : {id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it

copy : {ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy]} copies elements, with the doors and windows of copied walls; returns the copies' ids

delete : {ids: [id,…]} deleting a wall deletes its doors and windows, deleting those their tags; a view takes its notes and spot elevations, and what a spot elevation reads takes it; dimensions lose what's deleted

inspect : {} levels, element counts, types, warnings and undo history

schedule : {name?, category?, categories?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?, path?} a schedule view, as Revit's View > Schedules makes one, and its table: columns, rows, the `elements` each row lists, and totals (and a .csv file with a path, or an .xlsx workbook for a path ending .xlsx). A new one needs `name` and `category`: rooms, doors, windows, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, columns, structural columns, footings, beams, strip footings, components, stairs, ramps, railings or levels, or `multicategory`, as Revit's Multi-Category Schedule: a row for each element of `categories` (["walls", "doors"…]; none, every built one but rooms, levels and masses), with the fields they share (Category, Family, Type, Level, Count, Width, Height, Length, Thickness, Area: a wall's length by its height, a door's width by its height; Material: its type's structure layer's, a run's type's, a family's), each empty where its category has none; `category` alone reads its own (Room Schedule, Door Schedule, Window Schedule, Wall Schedule, Floor Schedule, Level Schedule, each the project's once changed). `fields`: its columns, in order, each a field's name (`available` lists them: its category's own, Count, project parameters, a component's family's parameters) or {name, formula?, kind?: number|length|area|yesno, heading?, total?}; with a formula, a calculated field worked out from the row's other fields as a family's formulas are (lengths in mm, areas in m²; `Area * 120`); `total` sums it in a totals row. `filters`: [{field, op: equals|not-equals|greater|greater-or-equal|less|less-or-equal|contains|not-contains|begins-with|not-begins-with|ends-with|not-ends-with|has-value|has-no-value, value}, …], the elements all of them keep (text in any case, numbers as the schedule shows them, an unset yes or no as no). `sort`: [field or {field, descending?}, …], in turn (its first column unless it says; Phase Created and Phase Demolished in the project's order of phases, a phase never demolished after the last); `grouped`, a row for each set of the sort fields' values: Count and totals summed, and a field whose values differ left empty. Each one given replaces the last; `fields: []` goes back to its category's

graphics : {view?: a level's, section's or elevation's name or id, or {3D} (the lowest level's plan unless given), hide?: [category, …], show?: […], hide_elements?: [id, …], show_elements?: […], categories?: {category: override | null, …}, elements?: {id: override | null, …}, filters?: [{filter, hidden?, projection?, cut?, halftone?, transparency?}, …], phase?: name | null, phase_filter?: name | null, options?: {set: option | null, …}, layers?: {drawing: [layer, …] | null, …}, template?: name | null, background_grid?: {visible?, main?: {enabled?, color?: [r,g,b], pen?: 0..16}, sub?: {enabled?, color?, pen?}, spacing?: [X,Y] (mm), divisions?: [X,Y] (1..1000), rotation?: degrees (-360..360)} | null, reset?: true} what a view hides and how it draws the rest, as Revit's Visibility/Graphics does; with none of those, the view's settings as they are. A category hidden (walls, floors, rooms, grids, dimensions, levels…, in any case, singular or plural) leaves all its elements out of that view, and `hide_elements` the elements given. In a 3D view rooms are hidden unless shown (`show: [rooms]`), every new 3D view so; shown, each is a see-through solid. Subcategories are hidden and shown as categories are, and go with their category: under rooms, `roomreference` (the cross at each room's point, hidden unless shown, as Revit's Rooms > Reference) and `roomseparator` (room separation lines). An override is {hidden?, projection?: style, cut?: style, halftone?, transparency?}, a style {color?, weight? (a pen, 0 to 16: 0 a hairline, the thinnest line the screen or printer draws at any scale; 1 to 16 widths on paper from 0.10 to 4 mm, 4 being 0.18 mm and 10 0.35 mm, a cut wall's outline), dash? (solid, dashed, dotted), fill?, foreground?, background?}, a colour [r, g, b] or "#rrggbb". Foreground and background override independent pattern layers: {pattern: a fill pattern's name | null, color?: [r,g,b]}; a null pattern hides that layer; a null foreground or background restores inheritance. They draw in plans, ceiling plans, section cuts and filled regions, using drafting patterns at paper scale and model patterns at model size. Projection is what a plan sees below its cut plane, a section beyond its line and the annotation; cut is what the view cuts; `fill` is the cut's poché, or a 3D view's surface; in a 3D view, and in what a section sees beyond its line, a projection's `color` is the colour of the edges (weight and dash draw lines, and those are vectors). Halftone draws it halfway to the paper; transparency (percent) sees through it in a 3D view. Halftone and transparency only add: a filter or an element can lighten what its category doesn't, not take its category's away. Overrides merge into the last (null takes a field or the override away); an element's own beats the filters applied (the first prevailing), which beat the category's. `filters` replaces the list applied; `template` follows a view template; `reset` takes away all of the view's own settings. `phase` is the phase the view shows (the project's last unless it says) and `phase_filter` how it shows each status of what's in it (see `phase`); `options` chooses the design option it shows of a set (the set's primary unless it says; see `option`); `layers` the layers of each CAD drawing it hides, by the drawing's name (null shows them all again)

filter : {name, categories?: [category, …], rules?: [{field, op, value}, …], delete?: true} a view filter, as Revit's parameter filters are: the elements of its categories (any a schedule can be of: walls, doors, rooms, components…) that hold every rule, a schedule filter's (`field` of the category, `op`: equals, not-equals, greater, greater-or-equal, less, less-or-equal, contains, not-contains, begins-with, not-begins-with, ends-with, not-ends-with, has-value, has-no-value; `value`), and every element of them without rules. A view applies it with `graphics {filters}`, hiding what it picks out or drawing it another way. Gone, views stop applying it. Replies with the filter and the ids it picks out; `name` alone reads one

template : {name, from?: a level's, section's, elevation's or 3D view's name or id, like?: another template's name, kind?: plan | section | 3d | null, rename?, controls?: [categories, filters, range, phase, options, scale, detail, style, background_grid], view_range?: {top?, cut?, bottom?, depth?}, phase?, phase_filter?, options?, scale?: 1 | … | 100000, detail?: coarse | medium | fine, visual_style?: shaded | hidden_line | wireframe, background_grid?: grid settings as in graphics, hide?, show?, categories?, filters?, reset?, delete?: true} a view template, as Revit's: settings under a name for views to follow with `graphics {template}`. `kind` is the views it is for (plans, elevations and sections, or 3D views; null, any), which `from` sets; `like` makes a new one a copy of another (Duplicate); `rename` names it anew, and its views follow it under that name. `from` takes a view's categories (hidden and overridden), filters and, a plan's, view range, its phase and phase filter, its design options, its scale, detail level and visual style; `controls` is what views following it get from it (all nine unless it says) and cannot change for themselves: its categories, its filters, a plan's view range, its phase with its phase filter, its design options, its scale (`scale` command), its detail level (`detail`), its visual style (`visual_style`). `hide`, `show`, `categories`, `filters`, `phase`, `phase_filter`, `options`, `scale`, `detail`, `visual_style`, `background_grid` and `reset` change it as they change a view; `view_range` merges into its range. Changed, every view following it follows. Gone, they keep their own settings. `name` alone reads one

elements : {category?, level?, limit?, offset?} elements with their `id` (six digits, what commands take) and `guid` (made once, never changed), fields and derived values (length, height, area_m2…); what an element points at (its level, host, view…) it holds by GUID. Wherever a command takes an element, its id or its GUID will do

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For every catalog command: execute with {} (and with a bogus param set) in normal and --read-only mode."""
import subprocess, json, sys, tempfile, os
cat = json.load(open('/tmp/mcp-agent/catalog.json'))
ids = [c['id'] for c in cat]
paramsets = [{}, {"id": 999999}, {"path": "nonexistent_dir/x.bimcraft"}]
if len(sys.argv) > 1:
    paramsets = [json.loads(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]]


def run(args, lines):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='ro')
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'mcp'] + args, input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=600)
    out = []
    for l in p.stdout.decode().splitlines():
        v = json.loads(l)
        if 'error' in v:
            out.append('RPCERR ' + v['error']['message'])
        else:
            r = v['result']
            t = r['content'][0].get('text', '<%s>' % r['content'][0].get('type'))
            out.append(('ERR ' if r.get('isError') else 'OK ') + t[:150].replace('\n', ' '))
    return out


for ps in paramsets:
    lines = []
    for i, c in enumerate(ids):
        lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "execute", "arguments": {"command": c, "params": ps}}}))
    # each command in a fresh process would be best, but a session per command is costly; use one fresh process per command
    for i, c in enumerate(ids):
        n = run([], [lines[i]])
        r = run(['--read-only'], [lines[i]])
        n = n[0] if n else 'NONE'
        r = r[0] if r else 'NONE'
        tag = 'SAME' if n == r else 'DIFF'
        print('%s %s %s\n    N: %s\n    R: %s' % (tag, json.dumps(ps), c, n, r))
        sys.stdout.flush()

import sys, zlib, struct, random
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/media-agent')
from pic import feed, pixels
import pnglib as P
random.seed(3)
def show(name, data, expect=None):
    r = feed(data)
    if r['code'] != 0:
        print(name, 'ERR', r['err'].strip()); return None
    W,H,rows = pixels(r)
    flat = [p for row in rows for p in row]
    if expect is not None:
        bad = [(i, e, g) for i,(e,g) in enumerate(zip(expect, flat)) if tuple(e) != tuple(g)]
        print(name, W, H, 'mismatches', len(bad), bad[:8])
    else:
        print(name, W, H, flat[:16])
    return flat
# 16-bit gray: all 65536 values in a 256x256 image
vals = list(range(65536))
px = [[vals[y*256+x] for x in range(256)] for y in range(256)]
d = P.make_png(256,256,px,depth=16,ctype=0)
flat = show('gray16', d)
hi = [(v>>8) for v in vals]
rnd = [ (v*255+32767)//65535 for v in vals]
r2 = [ (v+128)//257 for v in vals]
got = [p[0] for p in flat]
print(' hibyte', sum(a==b for a,b in zip(hi,got)), ' round', sum(a==b for a,b in zip(rnd,got)), ' (v+128)/257', sum(a==b for a,b in zip(r2,got)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy a TTF, replacing its name table with one naming a new family.
usage: mkfont.py src.ttf dst.ttf "Family" [subfamily] [--typo "TypoFamily"] [--nomac] [--nowin] [--lang 0x409]
"""
import struct, sys

def build_name(records):
    # records: list of (platform, encoding, language, nameid, bytes)
    records = sorted(records, key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3]))
    count = len(records)
    string_offset = 6 + 12 * count
    out = struct.pack('>HHH', 0, count, string_offset)
    data = b''
    for (pl, enc, lang, nid, b) in records:
        out += struct.pack('>HHHHHH', pl, enc, lang, nid, len(b), len(data))
        data += b
    return out + data

def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    src, dst, fam = a[0], a[1], a[2]
    sub = 'Regular'
    typo = None
    mac = True
    win = True
    lang = 0x409
    rest = a[3:]
    i = 0
    while i < len(rest):
        if rest[i] == '--typo': typo = rest[i+1]; i += 2
        elif rest[i] == '--nomac': mac = False; i += 1
        elif rest[i] == '--nowin': win = False; i += 1
        elif rest[i] == '--lang': lang = int(rest[i+1], 0); i += 2
        else: sub = rest[i]; i += 1
    raw = open(src, 'rb').read()
    sfnt, num = struct.unpack('>IH', raw[:6])
    tables = []
    for t in range(num):
        tag, cs, off, ln = struct.unpack('>4sIII', raw[12 + 16*t: 28 + 16*t])
        tables.append([tag, cs, off, ln])
    full = fam + ('' if sub == 'Regular' else ' ' + sub)
    ps = (fam + '-' + sub).replace(' ', '')
    recs = []
    names = {1: fam, 2: sub, 4: full, 6: ps}
    if typo:
        names[16] = typo
        names[17] = sub
    for nid, s in names.items():
        if win:
            recs.append((3, 1, lang, nid, s.encode('utf-16-be')))
        if mac:
            recs.append((1, 0, 0, nid, s.encode('mac_roman')))
    newname = build_name(recs)
    body = bytearray(raw)
    while len(body) % 4: body += b'\0'
    off = len(body)
    body += newname
    for t in tables:
        if t[0] == b'name':
            t[2] = off; t[3] = len(newname)
    for idx, t in enumerate(tables):
        struct.pack_into('>4sIII', body, 12 + 16*idx, t[0], t[1], t[2], t[3])
    open(dst, 'wb').write(bytes(body))

main()

import sys, zlib, struct
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/media-agent')
from pic import feed
import pnglib as P
SIG = P.SIG
raw = b'\x00' + bytes([10,20,30,40,50,60]) + b'\x00' + bytes([70,80,90,100,110,120])
def mk(*chunks):
    return SIG + b''.join(chunks)
IH = P.ihdr(2,2,8,2)
IE = P.chunk('IEND', b'')
def ID(d, crc=None): return P.chunk('IDAT', d, crc)
z = zlib.compress(raw)
def stored(data, final=1):
    n = len(data)
    return bytes([final, n & 255, n >> 8, (~n)&255, ((~n)>>8)&255]) + data
zs_nofinal = b'\x78\x01' + stored(raw, 0)
cases = {
 'wrong adler': mk(IH, ID(z[:-4] + b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'), IE),
 'no adler': mk(IH, ID(z[:-4]), IE),
 'half adler': mk(IH, ID(z[:-2]), IE),
 'garbage after stream': mk(IH, ID(z + b'garbage'), IE),
 'nonfinal stored then nothing': mk(IH, ID(zs_nofinal), IE),
 'nonfinal stored then bad block': mk(IH, ID(zs_nofinal + b'\xff\xff'), IE),
 'bad zlib header': mk(IH, ID(b'\x78\x00' + z[2:]), IE),
 'zlib cm 9': mk(IH, ID(b'\x79\x9c' + z[2:]), IE),
 'zlib fdict': mk(IH, ID(b'\x78\xbb' + z[2:]), IE),
 'zlib window 15+': mk(IH, ID(b'\x88\x98' + z[2:]), IE),
 'corrupt zlib + bad crc': mk(IH, ID(b'\x78\x9c\xff\xff\xff', crc=1), IE),
 'short + bad crc': mk(IH, ID(zlib.compress(raw[:5]), crc=1), IE),
 'split idat': mk(IH, ID(z[:3]), ID(z[3:10]), ID(z[10:]), IE),
 'split idat with text between': mk(IH, ID(z[:3]), P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00b'), ID(z[3:]), IE),
 'idat after complete then text then idat': mk(IH, ID(z), P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00b'), ID(z), IE),
 'zero idat then data': mk(IH, ID(b''), ID(z), IE),
 'zero idat after': mk(IH, ID(z), ID(b''), IE),
 'bad crc chunk after idat': mk(IH, ID(z), P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00b', crc=3), IE),
 'bad crc critical after idat': mk(IH, ID(z), P.chunk('ABCD', b'a\x00b', crc=3), IE),
 'bad crc PLTE before idat': mk(IH, P.chunk('PLTE', bytes(6), crc=3), ID(z), IE),
 'truncated after idat (in next len)': mk(IH, ID(z))+b'\x00\x00',
 'garbage after idat': mk(IH, ID(z)) + b'garbagegarbagegarbage',
 'ihdr bad depth + bad crc': mk(P.chunk('IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB',2,2,3,2,0,0,0), crc=1), ID(z), IE),
 'ihdr length 12': mk(P.chunk('IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBB',2,2,8,2,0,0)), ID(z), IE),
 'ihdr length 14': mk(P.chunk('IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBBB',2,2,8,2,0,0,0,0)), ID(z), IE),
 'first chunk not ihdr': mk(P.chunk('tEXt', b'a\x00bcdefghijk'), IH, ID(z), IE),
 'iend before idat': mk(IH, IE, ID(z)),
 'stored partial + eof in idat sequence': mk(IH, ID(b'\x78\x01' + stored(raw)[:10]), IE),
}
names = sys.argv[1:] or list(cases)
for n in names:
    r = feed(cases[n])
    print('%-40s' % n, r['code'], (r['out'].strip().split('\n')[0])[60:130] if r['code']==0 else '', r['err'].strip().replace('line 1 (material): material: <D>/p.png: ',''))

import math
