results.content:
reinforce | {host | hosts: [id, …], preset?, cover?, grade?, grade_stirrup?, clearance?, …} bars by rules for a beam, a column, a footing or a floor: the engineer says how many, how thick and how far apart (no standard's number sets them) and it lays them inside the cover and checks that they fit, saying what to change. All: `cover` (mm: one number, or {top, bottom, sides}, top and bottom the faces of a beam, a footing or a floor and the ends of a column; else the host's Cobrimento or ConcreteCover parameter), `grade` (CA-50), `grade_stirrup` (the stirrups' and ties'), `clearance` (least mm between bars; their thickness, at least 20, unless told). A spacing is the most between bars: they are spread evenly, so the last is where the first is from the other end. Beam: `bottom` and `top` {count, diameter, hook?} (`hook`, the straight leg in mm turned up from the bottom bars and down from the top ones at both ends, or {start, end}); `bottom.bent` {count, angle?, top?} bends `count` of the inner bottom bars up at each end (layer `bent`): they run `top` mm along the top face from each end (a fifth of the length unless told), slope down `angle` degrees (15 to 75, 45 unless told) and run along the bottom, and have no hook; `stirrup` {diameter, spacing, ends?: {length, spacing}, hook?} (`ends` closer in the first and last `length` mm; `hook` a tail in mm at the ends); `skin` {diameter, spacing} up each side between the rows; `anchor` {start?, end?} mm the bars run past the ends (0 flush, none a cover short). Column: `bars` {diameter, x?, y?, hook?, jog?} (`hook`, a leg turned into the section at the foot and the top, or {below, above}; `jog` {by, from_top, slope?} steps the bars in `by` mm toward the axis, starting `from_top` mm below the top and running `slope` mm up for each mm across (6 unless told), to leave room for the column above; bars along each face across its width and across its depth, corners counted, 2 each; a round column takes `count` instead of x and y, evenly round its circle, with hoops of 24 sides), `stirrup`, `ties` {diameter, hook?} across a rectangular section between bars that are not at a corner (`hook`, a tail in mm at each end), `anchor` {below?, above?}. Footing: `mesh` {x?, y?: {diameter, spacing}, hook?} (hook turns the ends up; a round footing's bars stop at its circle). Floor: `bottom` and `top` {x?, y?: {diameter, spacing}, hook?} (bars along east and north; `hook`, a leg turned up from a bottom mesh and down from a top one), stopping a cover short of its outline and its openings; a sloped floor's bars follow its top, the cover square to it. The bars are `rebar` elements of the host, each on a `layer`; reinforcing again replaces the ones it made and leaves any drawn by hand. `check` "NBR 6118" (with `aggressiveness` 1 to 4 for the cover, and `fck` in MPa) adds `notes` to the reply where the bars made fall short of that standard's usual limits (cover, bar sizes and spacings, stirrups, least and most steel, skin bars): they are notes, ne

tag | {ids?: [id,…], label?, level?, category?, offset?: [dx, dy], leader?} tags elements with a field of theirs: a door's or window's mark, a room's name, else the type, or `label`, any field its category's schedule has (`Height`, `Area`, a project parameter); doors, windows, walls, columns, components, floors, ceilings, roofs, rooms, runs and stairs. `offset` mm from the point it names (beside the wall for a door or window, else up and right); without ids, every door and window on the level not tagged yet, or of `category`

family | {name?, category?: furniture|casework|plumbing|lighting|generic|door|window, parameters?: [{name, kind?: length|number|angle|yesno|material, instance?, value?, formula?}], types?: {type: {parameter: value}}, forms?: [{plane?: xy|xz|yz, profile?: [[a, b], …], circle?: {centre: [a, b], radius}, axis?: [[a, b], [a, b]], from?, to, material?, visible?, void?}], symbols?: [{line?: [[x, y], …] | arc?: {centre: [x, y], radius, from?, to} | text?: {at: [x, y], height, value, align?: left|center|right} | dot?: {centre: [x, y], radius}, visible?}], form?: {id | guid, …a form's fields}, symbol?: {id | guid, …a symbol's fields}, delete_form?: [id | guid, …], delete_symbol?: [id | guid, …], operation?: swing|double-swing|sliding|double-sliding|folding|fixed (a door's or window's, for IFC and schedules), kind?: which fixture or fitting it is, for IFC's predefined type (plumbing: wc|lav|sink|laundry|shower|bath|bidet|urinal; drain: floor_drain|floor_waste|roof_drain; pipefitting: bend|tee|cross|transition|coupling; "" clears it), connectors?: [{kind: power|switch, system: power-balanced|power-unbalanced|switch, poles?: 1-3, voltage?, load_va?, power_factor?, classification?}], rename?, delete?: true, dry_run?, path?, save?} a family of the project's, BIMCraft's own parametric component: created, changed, read, or loaded from the .json file at `path` (a family as `inspect` shows it, with its `name`). Without `name` it lists the project's families, each its category and how many types, forms and symbols it has; with only a `name` it reads one — its definition, each of its types' parameter values worked out, and `warnings` — and changes nothing: no undo step, no file. `dry_run` reads a change the same way and replies what it would do (`changes`: the parameters and types added, taken away and changed, the forms and symbols replaced, patched and deleted by id, the `rename`) instead of doing it; a change that's refused comes back as an error, as it would without it. `form` merges its fields over the one form of that `id` or `guid` (a `null` takes a field away; its place, its id and its GUID stay), `delete_form` takes those forms away; `symbol` and `delete_symbol` do the same for symbols — where `forms` and `symbols` still replace whole lists. Every reply carries `warnings`: what's worth knowing and doesn't stop the change (a void cutting no solid, a form outside the opening or thicker than its wall, a door's or window's plan with no symbols). Its forms are profiles drawn in its own axes (x along a component's angle, y to its left, z up from its base) and swept: `xy` up from `from` to `to`, `xz` along y, `yz` along x. With an `axis`, a line in that plane, the profile is turned about it instead, `from` to `to` degrees (up to 360, right-handed from the axis' first point toward its second; it can't cross the axis): a pipe, a bowl, a lamp shade. A `void` is no solid: it cuts the solid forms listed before it that it passes through, a hole, a notch, a sink's bowl, and is ne

schedule | {name?, category?, categories?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?, path?} a schedule view, as Revit's View > Schedules makes one, and its table: columns, rows, the `elements` each row lists, and totals (and a .csv file with a path, or an .xlsx workbook for a path ending .xlsx). A new one needs `name` and `category`: rooms, doors, windows, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, columns, structural columns, footings, beams, strip footings, components, stairs, ramps, railings or levels, or `multicategory`, as Revit's Multi-Category Schedule: a row for each element of `categories` (["walls", "doors"…]; none, every built one but rooms, levels and masses), with the fields they share (Category, Family, Type, Level, Count, Width, Height, Length, Thickness, Area: a wall's length by its height, a door's width by its height; Material: its type's structure layer's, a run's type's, a family's), each empty where its category has none; `category` alone reads its own (Room Schedule, Door Schedule, Window Schedule, Wall Schedule, Floor Schedule, Level Schedule, each the project's once changed). `fields`: its columns, in order, each a field's name (`available` lists them: its category's own, Count, project parameters, a component's family's parameters) or {name, formula?, kind?: number|length|area|yesno, heading?, total?}; with a formula, a calculated field worked out from the row's other fields as a family's formulas are (lengths in mm, areas in m²; `Area * 120`); `total` sums it in a totals row. `filters`: [{field, op: equals|not-equals|greater|greater-or-equal|less|less-or-equal|contains|not-contains|begins-with|not-begins-with|ends-with|not-ends-with|has-value|has-no-value, value}, …], the elements all of them keep (text in any case, numbers as the schedule shows them, an unset yes or no as no). `sort`: [field or {field, descending?}, …], in turn (its first column unless it says; Phase Created and Phase Demolished in the project's order of phases, a phase never demolished after the last); `grouped`, a row for each set of the sort fields' values: Count and totals summed, and a field whose values differ left empty. Each one given replaces the last; `fields: []` goes back to its category's

filter | {name, categories?: [category, …], rules?: [{field, op, value}, …], delete?: true} a view filter, as Revit's parameter filters are: the elements of its categories (any a schedule can be of: walls, doors, rooms, components…) that hold every rule, a schedule filter's (`field` of the category, `op`: equals, not-equals, greater, greater-or-equal, less, less-or-equal, contains, not-contains, begins-with, not-begins-with, ends-with, not-ends-with, has-value, has-no-value; `value`), and every element of them without rules. A view applies it with `graphics {filters}`, hiding what it picks out or drawing it another way. Gone, views stop applying it. Replies with the filter and the ids it picks out; `name` alone reads one

circuit | {load, apparent?, demand?, power_factor?, phases?: FN|FF|3F|3FN, system?: 127/220|220/380|230/400, use?: lighting|power, length?, method?, insulation?: pvc|epr, conductor?: flexible|rigid, ambient?, grouped?, bundle?, spacing?, soil?, section?, breaker?, drop_limit?, reduced_neutral?} one electrical circuit sized as NBR 5410:2004 asks, for copper: `load` in W (or VA with `apparent`), `demand` (0 to 1, 1) and `power_factor` (over 0 to 1, 1; a first value, not a claim about the load), `phases` (FN one phase and neutral, the default; FF; 3F; 3FN balanced), the voltage `system` (127/220), `use` (power: 2.5 mm² at least; lighting 1.5), `length` to the farthest load (mm; none: no drop is checked), the installation `method` of Tabela 33 (7: a conduit in masonry; also 1 to 8, 11, 11A, 61, 61A), `insulation` (pvc 70 °C, or epr 90 °C), `conductor` (flexible, the larger resistance; or rigid), `ambient` °C (30 in air, 20 in soil), `grouped` circuits in the conduit (this one included), `bundle` (method 11 cables bundled), `spacing` between buried conduits (mm) and `soil` resistivity (K·m/W), and a `section` (mm²) and `breaker` (A) already chosen, which are never made smaller. Replies with the design current, the section and breaker that give I_B ≤ I_n ≤ I_Z (which gives I_2 = 1.45 I_n ≤ 1.45 I_Z for the breakers of NBR NM 60898) with the drop within `drop_limit` (4 %), the current the section carries, the drop, the conductors (phases, neutral, protective), the factors, and what the chosen section and breaker give. It changes nothing; aluminium, trays, several layers, short circuit and harmonics are not checked. It has no shortcut: Revit has no tool for it

library | {kind?, name?} the project's library with its ids and GUIDs, as elements have them: each type (`kind` `type:wall`, `type:door`, `type:beam`…), material, picture, family, parameter, view filter and template (`view-filter`, `view-template`), phase, phase filter, design option set and design option (`option-set`, `design-option`, named `set: option`), family type and family parameter (`family-type`, `family-parameter`, named `family: name`); and `parts`, what entries hold that has its own id and GUID: each type's layers and each family's forms and symbols (`kind` `layer`, `form`, `symbol`; `name` the type's or the family's). Wherever a command takes an entry by name, its GUID does too

filter_selection | {ids: [id or GUID, …], by?, keep?: [value, …]} Revit's Filter on a selection: `groups` [{value, count, ids}, …], the values `by` takes among the elements (by default `Category`, whose values are categories' keys: wall, door, detail_line…; else a parameter as `fields` lists them, values as schedules show them, `""` for none), and `fields`, the parameters every one of them has, to filter by. With `keep`, `ids`: those holding one of its values, the selection to keep; it selects nothing itself, a front end does

results.content:
rebar | {points: [[x,y,z],…], diameter, host?, grade?, layer?, closed?, count?, step?, level?} a reinforcing bar bent along `points` (mm; z over the level), `diameter` mm thick (3 to 100), of steel `grade` (CA-50 unless told). `host` is the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces (the level is then its level) and it goes with; `closed` joins the last point to the first, a hoop. With `count` bars (up to 1000), each is `step` [dx,dy,dz] from the last: a layer of bars, or hoops along a beam. Returns their ids. Its schedule lists Grade, Diameter, Length and Weight (kg, of steel at 7850 kg/m³), and a grouped one is a bar schedule

wire | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a wire (condutor) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` its outside diameter; `system` names its circuit

cabling | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} structured cabling (cabeamento estruturado, NBR 14565) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` the cable's outside diameter; `system` names the link or the network it belongs to

type | {category: wall|floor|ceiling|door|window|column|structuralcolumn|footing|roof|railing|beam|stripfooting|pipe|duct|conduit|cabletray|wire|downconductor|groundconductor|cable, name, thickness? | width?, height?, sill?, operation? | width?, depth?, round?, material? | height?, spacing?} creates the type, or changes it everywhere it's used. A column's, a structural column's or a footing's type is a `width` by `depth`, or `round` (`width` across); a run's (a beam's, a pipe's, a cable tray's…) too, made of a `material` of the library. A wall type may have `layers` [{function?: structure|substrate|thermal|membrane|finish, material?, thickness}, …] from its exterior side in: it's as thick as they are, its core from its first structure layer to its last, and a new `thickness` goes to its structure. A ceiling type may have `grid`: its square tiles' width, mm, which reflected ceiling plans draw (0, none); a railing type, `height` (its rail over what it runs along) and `spacing` (its balusters' centres, 0 for none). Floor, roof and ceiling types may have `layers` too, from the top down; a layer's `material` is one of the library's (see `material`)

component | {family, type?, at: [x,y], level?, angle?, offset?, mirrored?, params?: {parameter: value}} a family's type placed, its first by default: at a point on a level, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise, `offset` mm up from the level, and with `mirrored` flipped across its own x axis; `params` sets its instance parameters (`modify` merges into them, a null taking one back to the family's)

modify | {id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it

delete_type | {category?: wall|floor|door|window|column|roof|ceiling|railing|…, family?, type?} deletes a type of a category (`category` and `type`), a family (`family`) or one of a family's types (`family` and `type`), as Revit's Delete on one in the Project Browser does; refused while an element uses it (it says how many), and for the last type of a category or of a family

rename_type | {category?: wall|floor|door|window|column|roof|ceiling|railing|…, family?, type, name} renames a type of a category (`category` and `type`) or one of a family's types (`family` and `type`) to `name`, as Rename in Type Properties does: the elements of it, and what else names it, follow, and it keeps its GUID; refused for a name another type of it has. Text types and filled region types rename with `rename` on `text_type` and `filled_region_type`

purge | {kinds?: [type|family|material|picture|filter|template, …], dry_run?} takes out what nothing uses, again for what that leaves unused: types and families unless `kinds` says; a category keeps a type and a family a type; with `dry_run` it lists what would go and changes nothing

library | {kind?, name?} the project's library with its ids and GUIDs, as elements have them: each type (`kind` `type:wall`, `type:door`, `type:beam`…), material, picture, family, parameter, view filter and template (`view-filter`, `view-template`), phase, phase filter, design option set and design option (`option-set`, `design-option`, named `set: option`), family type and family parameter (`family-type`, `family-parameter`, named `family: name`); and `parts`, what entries hold that has its own id and GUID: each type's layers and each family's forms and symbols (`kind` `layer`, `form`, `symbol`; `name` the type's or the family's). Wherever a command takes an entry by name, its GUID does too

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Make a project with the original from commands, then patch it with a python expression.
usage: mk.py out.bimcraft 'patch-python (doc is the JSON; lib(kind,name) gives a guid)' cmd...
"""
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, json, os, shutil
out = sys.argv[1]
patch = sys.argv[2]
cmds = sys.argv[3:]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
if p.returncode != 0:
    print(p.stdout.decode(), p.stderr.decode()); sys.exit(1)
doc = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
def lib(kind, name):
    for k, v in doc['library'].items():
        if v['kind'] == kind and v['name'] == name: return v['guid']
    raise KeyError((kind, name))
def libid(kind, name):
    for k, v in doc['library'].items():
        if v['kind'] == kind and v['name'] == name: return k
    raise KeyError((kind, name))
els = doc['elements']
exec(patch)
json.dump(doc, open(out, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Make patched projects and open each in the original (and mine with -c), printing results."""
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, json, os, shutil
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
cmp = '-c' in sys.argv
base_cmds = ['wall {"points":[[0,0],[5000,0]]}', 'option {"set":"Kitchen","options":["A","B"]}']
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
for c in base_cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
base = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
shutil.rmtree(d)
patches = [l for l in open(sys.argv[1]).read().split('\n') if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
for patch in patches:
    doc = json.loads(json.dumps(base))
    def lib(kind, name):
        for k, v in doc['library'].items():
            if v['kind'] == kind and v['name'] == name: return v['guid']
        raise KeyError((kind, name))
    def libid(kind, name):
        for k, v in doc['library'].items():
            if v['kind'] == kind and v['name'] == name: return k
        raise KeyError((kind, name))
    els = doc['elements']
    exec(patch)
    res = []
    for exe in (['/workspace/executable'] + ([MINE] if cmp else [])):
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        json.dump(doc, open(os.path.join(d, 'p.bimcraft'), 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', 'p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'phase', '--cmd', 'option {"set":"Kitchen"}', '--cmd', 'level {"elevation":9000}'], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
        res.append((p.stdout.decode()[:400] + ' ERR: ' + p.stderr.decode()[:400]).replace('\n', ' | '))
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    print('##', patch)
    print('  ', res[0])
    if cmp and res[1] != res[0]:
        print('!! MINE:', res[1])

"""Run the original (or mine with -m) with env overrides: envrun.py [-m] VAR=val ... -- args..."""
import os, subprocess, sys, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/text/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
env = dict(os.environ)
both = False
while a and a[0] != '--':
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE
    elif a[0] == '-b': both = True
    elif a[0].startswith('-u'):
        env.pop(a[0][2:], None)
    else:
        k, v = a[0].split('=', 1)
        env[k] = v
    a = a[1:]
a = a[1:]
exes = [ORIG, MINE] if both else [exe]
outs = []
for e in exes:
    p = subprocess.run([e] + a, capture_output=True, env=env, cwd='/tmp/styles-agent/text')
    o = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace') + p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    outs.append(o)
    print(o.rstrip())
if both:
    print('SAME' if outs[0] == outs[1] else 'DIFF')

import sys, zlib, struct, random
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/media-agent')
from pic import feed, pixels
import pnglib as P
random.seed(11)
def box(src, w, h):
    nw, nh = max(1, w//2), max(1, h//2)
    out = []
    for y in range(nh):
        row = []
        for x in range(nw):
            q = [src[min(2*y+dy, h-1)][min(2*x+dx, w-1)] for dy in (0,1) for dx in (0,1)]
            row.append(tuple((sum(p[c] for p in q)+2)//4 for c in range(3)) + (255,))
        out.append(row)
    return out, nw, nh
for (w,h) in [(1,2000),(3,2000),(2050,5),(4100,3)]:
    px = [[(random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256)) for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)]
    r = feed(P.make_png(w,h,px))
    W,H,rows = pixels(r)
    # model: iterative halving
    cur, cw, ch = [[p+(255,) for p in row] for row in px], w, h
    while cw > 1024 or ch > 1024:
        cur, cw, ch = box(cur, cw, ch)
    ok = (cw,ch)==(W,H) and all(tuple(cur[y][x])==tuple(rows[y][x]) for y in range(H) for x in range(W))
    # model 2: one-step box of 2^k
    print((w,h), '->', (W,H), 'iterative model', ok)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For each element of cats.bimcraft, run modify with an unknown field to read its struct's field order."""
import subprocess, json, tempfile, os, shutil
doc = json.load(open('/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/cats.bimcraft'))
seen = set()
for k, v in doc['elements'].items():
    c = v['category']
    if c in seen: continue
    seen.add(c)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    shutil.copy('/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/cats.bimcraft', os.path.join(d, 'p.bimcraft'))
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', 'p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'modify {"id":%s,"zzz":1}' % k], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    e = p.stderr.decode().strip()
    i = e.find('expected one of')
    print(c, ':', e[i + 16:] if i >= 0 else e)
    shutil.rmtree(d)

from pic import feed, pixels
g = open('/workspace/assets/test_library/gray.jpg','rb').read()
m = open('/workspace/assets/test_library/mono.jpg','rb').read()
cases = {
 'ffd8 only': b'\xff\xd8',
 'ffd8ff': b'\xff\xd8\xff',
 'ffd8 x': b'\xff\xd8\x00\x00',
 'ffd9': b'\xff\xd9',
 'gray trunc 10': g[:10],
 'gray trunc 50': g[:50],
 'gray trunc 100': g[:100],
 'gray trunc 150': g[:150],
 'gray no eoi': g[:-2],
 'gray': g,
 'mono': m,
 'ffd8ffd9': b'\xff\xd8\xff\xd9',
 'garbage after soi': b'\xff\xd8' + b'garbage' * 5,
 'sof2 marker': g.replace(b'\xff\xc0', b'\xff\xc2'),
 'sof3 lossless': g.replace(b'\xff\xc0', b'\xff\xc3'),
 'sof1': g.replace(b'\xff\xc0', b'\xff\xc1'),
 'sof9 arith': g.replace(b'\xff\xc0', b'\xff\xc9'),
 'sof5': g.replace(b'\xff\xc0', b'\xff\xc5'),
}
for n, d in cases.items():
    r = feed(d, name='p.jpg')
    s = ''
    if r['code'] == 0:
        W,H,rows = pixels(r)
        s = str((W,H,rows[0][:3]))
    print('%-20s' % n, r['code'], s[:100], r['out'][60:140].strip() if r['code']==0 else '', r['err'].strip().replace('line 1 (material): material: <D>/p.jpg: ',''))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For each font name, try text_type {name: T, font: f} and report accepted/normalized/drawn_with."""
import os, subprocess, sys, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/text/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
args = sys.argv[1:]
env = dict(os.environ)
exe = ORIG
cmd = 'text_type'
while args and (('=' in args[0] and not args[0].startswith('{')) or args[0] in ('-m', '-d')):
    if args[0] == '-m': exe = MINE
    elif args[0] == '-d': cmd = 'dimension_type'
    else:
        k, v = args[0].split('=', 1); env[k] = v
    args = args[1:]
names = args
if len(names) == 1 and names[0].startswith('@'):
    names = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(names[0][1:]) if l.strip()]
for f in names:
    c = json.dumps({'name': 'T', 'font': f}, ensure_ascii=False)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', '--cmd', cmd + ' ' + c, '--cmd', cmd], capture_output=True, env=env, cwd='/tmp')
    out = p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print(repr(f), 'REFUSED', p.stderr.decode().strip()[:300])
        continue
    r = json.loads(out[0])
    l = json.loads(out[1])
    font = r['type']['font']
    dw = l.get('drawn_with', {}).get('T')
    print(repr(f), '->', repr(font), 'drawn_with', repr(dw))

import subprocess, sys, tempfile, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
def ok(ll, ln):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'voltage {"name":"N","nominal":%r}' % ln, '--cmd', 'voltage {"name":"L","nominal":%r}' % ll,
            '--cmd', 'distribution_system {"name":"X","phases":3,"wires":4,"l_l":"L","l_n":"N"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    return p.returncode == 0, p.stderr.decode().strip()
mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == 'scan':
    ln = float(sys.argv[2])
    for ll in [float(x) for x in sys.argv[3:]]:
        print(ll, ll / ln, ok(ll, ln))
elif mode == 'bisect':
    ln = float(sys.argv[2]); lo = float(sys.argv[3]); hi = float(sys.argv[4])
    # lo is ok, hi not ok (or vice versa)
    a = ok(lo, ln)[0]; b = ok(hi, ln)[0]
    assert a != b, (a, b)
    for i in range(40):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if ok(mid, ln)[0] == a: lo = mid
        else: hi = mid
    print('boundary between', lo, hi, 'ratio', lo / ln, hi / ln)

import math, subprocess, tempfile, sys
s = math.sqrt(3)
F = {
    'i': lambda ll, ln: abs((ll / ln) / s - 1) <= 0.03,
    'ii': lambda ll, ln: abs(ll - s * ln) / (s * ln) <= 0.03,
    'iii': lambda ll, ln: 0.97 < ll / (ln * s) < 1.03,
    'iv': lambda ll, ln: abs(ll / ln - s) <= 0.03 * s,
    'v': lambda ll, ln: abs(ll - s * ln) <= 0.03 * s * ln,
    'vi': lambda ll, ln: abs(ll / (s * ln) - 1) <= 0.03,
    'vii': lambda ll, ln: abs(ll / ln / s - 1.0) < 0.03,
}
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
def ok(ll, ln):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    args = [ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'voltage {"name":"N","nominal":%r}' % ln, '--cmd', 'voltage {"name":"L","nominal":%r}' % ll,
            '--cmd', 'distribution_system {"name":"X","phases":3,"wires":4,"l_l":"L","l_n":"N"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    return p.returncode == 0
found = 0
for ln in [127.0, 7.3, 230.0, 1.1, 333.3, 50.0, 12.7]:
    for edge in [1.03, 0.97]:
        base = edge * s * ln
        v = base
        for k in range(-6, 7):
            x = base
            step = k
            while step > 0:
                x = math.nextafter(x, 1e9); step -= 1
            while step < 0:
                x = math.nextafter(x, 0); step += 1
            res = {n: f(x, ln) for n, f in F.items()}
            if len(set(res.values())) > 1:
                o = ok(x, ln)
                good = [n for n, r in res.items() if r == o]
                print(ln, repr(x), 'orig', o, 'consistent:', good)
                found += 1
print('found', found)

arguments.content:
import subprocess, tempfile, json, shutil, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
cands = sys.argv[1:]
for c in cands:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    p = subprocess.run([ORIG, 'run', '--cmd', 'standard ' + json.dumps({"set": c}, ensure_ascii=False)], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    if p.returncode == 0:
        r = json.loads(p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')[0])
        print(repr(c), '->', r.get('standard'))
    else:
        print(repr(c), 'ERR', p.stderr.decode().strip()[-80:])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Import PAT texts (one session each) on the original (and mine with -c), print the import reply and
the resulting non-default fill patterns (listing).
usage: pi.py [-c] [-r] [-x extra_cmd] file_with_cases
  cases file: cases separated by a line '====', each case's text is the PAT text
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, json
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/fills/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
cmp = False
replace = False
extra = []
quiet = False
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0] == '-c': cmp = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-r': replace = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-x': extra.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
src = open(a[0], encoding='utf-8').read()
cases = src.split('\n====\n')
DEFAULT = set(['Brick 225 x 75', 'Crosshatch', 'Diagonal Crosshatch', 'Diagonal Down', 'Diagonal Up', 'Horizontal', 'Sand', 'Solid fill', 'Tile 300', 'Vertical'])
def run(exe, text):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='pi')
    p = {'text': text}
    if replace: p['replace'] = True
    args = [exe, 'run']
    for e in extra: args += ['--cmd', e]
    args += ['--cmd', 'import_fill_patterns ' + json.dumps(p), '--cmd', 'fill_pattern']
    r = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    out = r.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip().split('\n')
    out = out[len(extra):]
    s = ''
    if out and out[0]:
        s += out[0] + '\n'
    if len(out) > 1:
        pats = json.loads(out[1])['patterns']
        for k, v in pats.items():
            if k not in DEFAULT or replace:
                s += '   %s: %s\n' % (k, json.dumps(v))
    if r.stderr:
        s += 'ERR: ' + r.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip() + '\n'
    return s
nd = 0
for i, c in enumerate(cases):
    o = run(ORIG, c)
    if cmp:
        m = run(MINE, c)
        if m != o:
            nd += 1
            print('### case %d DIFFERS: %r' % (i, c[:300]))
            print(' orig:', o)
            print(' mine:', m)
        elif not quiet:
            print('### case %d same' % i)
    else:
        print('### case %d: %r' % (i, c[:300]))
        print(o)
if cmp:
    print('%d/%d differ' % (nd, len(cases)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Try phase names through the command; print reply/err."""
import subprocess, json, tempfile, os, shutil, sys
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
cmp = '-c' in sys.argv
tmpl = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] != '-c' else 'phase {"name":%s}'
names = ["A\tB", "A\n", "\tA", "-A", "(A)", "A.", "Ä", "😀", "A😀", "😀A", "A ", " A", "A​", "​A", "A\u0007", "_A", "A_", "#", "a" * 256, "a" * 257, " " + "a" * 256, "A:B", "A/B", "'A'", '"A"', "　A", "A　", " A", "Á", "́A", "Ⅻ", "١", "A ", "!", "...", "*A*", "A*", "[A]", "{A}", "<A>", "A>", "%"]
for n in names:
    res = []
    for exe in ['/workspace/executable'] + ([MINE] if cmp else []):
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', '--cmd', tmpl % json.dumps(n)], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
        out = p.stdout.decode().strip()
        out = out[-150:]
        res.append(out + ' ERR: ' + p.stderr.decode().strip()[:300])
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    print(repr(n)[:40], '=>', res[0])
    if cmp and res[0] != res[1]:
        print('   !! MINE:', res[1])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random sweep of the compressor against the original (colour and point streams)."""
import sys, random, subprocess
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
modes = ['rand', 'small', 'text', 'const', 'runs', 'mix']
rnd = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0)
count = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100
maxn = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 200000
jobs = []
for i in range(count):
    m = rnd.choice(modes)
    n = int(rnd.choice([rnd.uniform(1, 100), rnd.uniform(1, 5000), rnd.uniform(1, maxn)]))
    jobs.append((m, max(1, n), rnd.randrange(1 << 30)))
def go(j):
    m, n, s = j
    r = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/cloud-agent/zcmp.py', m, str(n), str(s), '1'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return j, r.stdout
bad = 0
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    for j, out in ex.map(go, jobs):
        if 'bad 0 of 1' not in out:
            bad += 1
            print(j, out)
print('sweep done, bad', bad, 'of', len(jobs))

import subprocess, tempfile, json, shutil, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
exe = ORIG
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args and args[0] == '-m':
    exe = MINE; args = args[1:]
units = args[0]
scales = [float(x) if '.' in x or 'e' in x else int(x) for x in args[1:]]
W = [0.1, 0.13, 0.15, 0.18, 0.2, 0.22, 0.25, 0.28, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.4, 2]
# 32 max per call
out = []
for i in range(0, len(scales), 32):
    chunk = scales[i:i + 32]
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    cmd = 'line_weights ' + json.dumps({"model": [{"scale": s, "widths": W} for s in chunk]})
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', '--cmd', 'units {"length":"%s"}' % units, '--cmd', cmd], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print('ERR', p.stderr.decode()[:300]); continue
    r = json.loads(p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')[-1])
    for m in r['model']:
        out.append((m['scale'], m['name']))
for s, n in out:
    print(s, '|', n)

import subprocess, tempfile, json, shutil, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
exe = ORIG
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args and args[0] == '-m':
    exe = MINE; args = args[1:]
units = args[0]
scales = [float(x) if '.' in x or 'e' in x else int(x) for x in args[1:]]
W = [0.1, 0.13, 0.15, 0.18, 0.2, 0.22, 0.25, 0.28, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.4, 2]
# 32 max per call
out = []
for i in range(0, len(scales), 32):
    chunk = scales[i:i + 32]
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    cmd = 'line_weights ' + json.dumps({"model": [{"scale": s, "widths": W} for s in chunk]})
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', '--cmd', 'units {"length":"%s"}' % units, '--cmd', cmd], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print('ERR', p.stderr.decode()[:300]); continue
    r = json.loads(p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')[-1])
    for m in r['model']:
        out.append((m['scale'], m['name']))
for s, n in out:
    print(s, '|', n)

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure how long the CLI waits for the window. usage: timing.py MODE [max_secs]
MODE: hello  -> window never answers hello
      req    -> window answers hello, never answers the request
      partial-> window sends a partial line and never finishes
"""
import socket, subprocess, sys, time, os, tempfile, json, threading
mode = sys.argv[1]
maxs = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
exe = os.environ.get('EXE', '/workspace/executable')
s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); s.listen(4)
port = s.getsockname()[1]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(d + '/bimcraft')
open(d + '/bimcraft/bridge.json', 'w').write(json.dumps({"port": port, "token": "tok"}))
env = dict(os.environ); env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = d
t0 = time.time()
lines = ['{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"inspect_model"}}']
p = subprocess.Popen([exe, 'mcp', '--connect'], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, cwd=d)
conns = []


def srv():
    c, _ = s.accept()
    conns.append(c)
    f = c.makefile('rb')
    l = f.readline()
    print('%.2f got hello %r' % (time.time() - t0, l)); sys.stdout.flush()
    if mode == 'hello':
        return
    if mode == 'partial':
        c.sendall(b'{"ok":')
        return
    c.sendall(b'{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}\n')
    l = f.readline()
    print('%.2f got req %r' % (time.time() - t0, l)); sys.stdout.flush()


threading.Thread(target=srv, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(0.3)
p.stdin.write(('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode()); p.stdin.flush()
while time.time() - t0 < maxs:
    if p.poll() is not None:
        break
    time.sleep(0.1)
el = time.time() - t0
if p.poll() is None:
    print('still running after %.1fs' % el)
    p.kill()
out, err = p.communicate()
print('exit', p.returncode, 'after %.2fs' % el)
print('OUT', out.decode()[:500])
print('ERR', err.decode()[:500])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy a TTF, replacing its name table with one naming a new family.
usage: mkfont.py src.ttf dst.ttf "Family" [subfamily] [--typo "TypoFamily"] [--nomac] [--nowin] [--lang 0x409]
       [--rec pl,enc,lang,nid,text]... [--only-recs] [--noname]
"""
import struct, sys

def build_name(records):
    records = sorted(records, key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3]))
    count = len(records)
    string_offset = 6 + 12 * count
    out = struct.pack('>HHH', 0, count, string_offset)
    data = b''
    for (pl, enc, lang, nid, b) in records:
        out += struct.pack('>HHHHHH', pl, enc, lang, nid, len(b), len(data))
        data += b
    return out + data

def enc(pl, e, s):
    if pl == 3 or pl == 0:
        return s.encode('utf-16-be')
    return s.encode('mac_roman')

def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    src, dst, fam = a[0], a[1], a[2]
    sub = 'Regular'
    typo = None
    mac = True
    win = True
    lang = 0x409
    extra = []
    only = False
    noname = False
    rest = a[3:]
    i = 0
    while i < len(rest):
        if rest[i] == '--typo': typo = rest[i+1]; i += 2
        elif rest[i] == '--nomac': mac = False; i += 1
        elif rest[i] == '--nowin': win = False; i += 1
        elif rest[i] == '--lang': lang = int(rest[i+1], 0); i += 2
        elif rest[i] == '--rec':
            pl, e, lg, nid, text = rest[i+1].split(',', 4)
            extra.append((int(pl, 0), int(e, 0), int(lg, 0), int(nid, 0), text)); i += 2
        elif rest[i] == '--only-recs': only = True; i += 1
        elif rest[i] == '--noname': noname = True; i += 1
        else: sub = rest[i]; i += 1
    raw = open(src, 'rb').read()
    sfnt, num = struct.unpack('>IH', raw[:6])
    tables = []
    for t in range(num):
        tag, cs, off, ln = struct.unpack('>4sIII', raw[12 + 16*t: 28 + 16*t])
        tables.append([tag, cs, off, ln])
    full = fam + ('' if sub == 'Regular' else ' ' + sub)
    ps = (fam + '-' + sub).replace(' ', '')
    recs = []
    names = {1: fam, 2: sub, 4: full, 6: ps}
    if typo:
        names[16] = typo
        names[17] = sub
    if not only:
        for nid, s in names.items():
            if win:
                recs.append((3, 1, lang, nid, s.encode('utf-16-be')))
            if mac:
                recs.append((1, 0, 0, nid, s.encode('mac_roman')))
    for (pl, e, lg, nid, text) in extra:
        recs.append((pl, e, lg, nid, enc(pl, e, text)))
    newname = build_name(recs)
    body = bytearray(raw)
    while len(body) % 4: body += b'\0'
    off = len(body)
    body += newname
    for t in tables:
        if t[0] == b'name':
            if noname:
                t[0] = b'nam_'
            t[2] = off; t[3] = len(newname)
    for idx, t in enumerate(tables):
        struct.pack_into('>4sIII', body, 12 + 16*idx, t[0], t[1], t[2], t[3])
    open(dst, 'wb').write(bytes(body))

main()

import subprocess, json, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
def run(cmds):
    args = [ORIG, 'run']
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, cwd='/tmp')
    return p.stdout.decode().strip(), p.stderr.decode().strip()
sched = {}
cats = ['wall', 'floor', 'ceiling', 'roof', 'door', 'window', 'room', 'column', 'component', 'stair', 'ramp', 'railing', 'mass',
        'structuralcolumn', 'footing', 'beam', 'stripfooting', 'pipe', 'duct', 'conduit', 'cabletray', 'wire', 'downconductor',
        'groundconductor', 'cable']
for c in cats:
    o, e = run(['schedule ' + json.dumps({"name": "S", "category": c})])
    sched[c] = json.loads(o)['available']
allnames = sorted(set(n for v in sched.values() for n in v))
for c in cats:
    refused = []
    accepted = []
    msgs = set()
    for n in allnames:
        o, e = run(['parameter ' + json.dumps({"name": n, "categories": [c]})])
        if e:
            refused.append(n)
            m = e[e.find('`' + n + '`: ') + len(n) + 4:]
            msgs.add(m.replace(n, '<N>'))
        else:
            accepted.append(n)
    inlist = [n for n in refused if n in sched[c]]
    notinlist = [n for n in refused if n not in sched[c]]
    acc_in = [n for n in accepted if n in sched[c]]
    print(c, '| refused in avail:', inlist, '| refused not in avail:', notinlist, '| accepted though in avail:', acc_in)
    print('   msgs:', msgs)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stand-in experiments: for each scenario (families to install in a fresh HOME/.fonts), make text types
for the probe fonts and print drawn_with for each.
usage: standin.py "Fam A|Fam B" "Fam C" ...   (each arg is one scenario; families separated by |)
  -f "Arial,Times New Roman"   probe fonts (comma separated)
  -m                           run mine too, compare
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, json, shutil, tempfile
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/text/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
SRC = '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf'
a = sys.argv[1:]
probes = ['Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Times New Roman', 'Courier New', 'Calibri', 'Cambria']
both = False
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0] == '-f': probes = a[1].split(','); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-m': both = True; a = a[1:]
    else: break
def run(exe, home):
    env = dict(os.environ); env['HOME'] = home; env.pop('XDG_DATA_HOME', None)
    args = [exe, 'run']
    for i, f in enumerate(probes):
        args += ['--cmd', 'text_type ' + json.dumps({'name': 'P%02d' % i, 'font': f})]
    args += ['--cmd', 'text_type']
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, env=env, cwd='/tmp')
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return 'ERR ' + p.stderr.decode().strip()
    d = json.loads(p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')[-1])
    return ', '.join('%s->%s' % (f, d['drawn_with']['P%02d' % i]) for i, f in enumerate(probes)) + ' | fonts=' + ','.join(d['fonts'])
for sc in a:
    home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='home', dir='/tmp/styles-agent/text')
    os.makedirs(home + '/.fonts')
    fams = [x for x in sc.split('|') if x]
    for i, f in enumerate(fams):
        subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/styles-agent/text/mkfont.py', SRC, '%s/.fonts/f%02d.ttf' % (home, i), f], check=True)
    o = run(ORIG, home)
    print('[%s]' % sc, o)
    if both:
        m = run(MINE, home)
        if m != o:
            print('   MINE:', m)
    shutil.rmtree(home)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ply.py 'header lines (\\n-separated, without end_header)' 'body' [extra]
body: for binary, a python expression producing bytes (struct.pack...); for ascii, text with \\n escapes.
Writes t.ply and runs the original (and mine with -m)."""
import sys, os, struct, subprocess
args = sys.argv[1:]
flag = []
if args and args[0] == '-m':
    flag = ['-m']; args = args[1:]
hdr, body = args[0], args[1]
extra = args[2] if len(args) > 2 else ''
h = hdr.encode().decode('unicode_escape')
if 'ascii' in h.split('\n')[1] if len(h.split('\n')) > 1 else False:
    b = body.encode().decode('unicode_escape').encode('latin1')
else:
    b = eval(body, {'struct': struct, 'P': struct.pack})
data = (h + '\nend_header\n').encode('latin1') + b
open('/tmp/cloud-agent/t_ply.bin', 'wb').write(data)
# reuse tf.py by passing the raw content through a file
subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/cloud-agent/tfile.py'] + flag + ['/tmp/cloud-agent/t_ply.bin', 'ply', extra])

from o import run, ORIG, MINE
import pnglib
exe = MINE if '-m' in sys.argv else ORIG
G = '/workspace/assets/test_library/grass.png'
T = '/tmp/media-agent/t/tall.png'
TI = 'img-5836c312f1e85605'
GI = 'img-9266612a07a4f48d'
def tex(n, d): return 'material ' + json.dumps({"name": n, "texture": d})
os.makedirs('/tmp/media-agent/t/many', exist_ok=True)
paths = []
for i in range(26):
    p = '/tmp/media-agent/t/many/p%02d.png' % i
    open(p, 'wb').write(pnglib.make_png(1, 1, [[(i, 0, 0)]]))
    paths.append(p)
seqs = [
 [tex("A", {"kind":"image","path":G}), tex("B", {"kind":"image","path":T}), tex("A", {"kind":"image","image":TI})],
 [tex("A", {"kind":"image","path":G, "size": [10,10]}), tex("B", {"kind":"image","path":T}), tex("A", {"kind":"image","image":TI})],
 [tex("A", {"kind":"image","path":G, "size": [10,10]}), tex("A", {"kind":"image","image":GI})],
 [tex("M%d" % i, {"kind":"image","path":paths[i]}) for i in range(25)],
 [tex("M%d" % i, {"kind":"image","path":paths[i]}) for i in range(24)] + [tex("M0", {"kind":"image","path":paths[25]})],
 [tex("M%d" % i, {"kind":"image","path":paths[i]}) for i in range(24)] + [tex("M24", {"kind":"image","path":paths[0]})],
]
for s in seqs:
    code, out, err, proj = run(s, exe, save=True)
    print(' | '.join(x[9:120] for x in s)[:600], '=>', code)

        print('  ', l[:400])
    print('  ', err.strip()[:600])

"""Make a project file from the default one with edits to a section.
usage: craft.py out.bimcraft section 'json-of-entries-to-merge' [--replace]
"""
import json, subprocess, sys, os, tempfile
out, section, entries = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], json.loads(sys.argv[3])
replace = '--replace' in sys.argv
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--save', os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')], capture_output=True, check=True)
doc = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
if replace:
    doc[section] = entries
else:
    sec = doc.get(section, {})
    sec.update(entries)
    doc[section] = sec
open(out, 'w').write(json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))

import os, subprocess, json
def run(*cmds):
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd='/tmp', capture_output=True)
    return p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
for n in [150, 160, 170, 180, 200, 300]:
    t = ''.join('*P%03d\n0,0,0,0,1\n' % i for i in range(n))
    o, e = run('import_fill_patterns ' + json.dumps({'text': t}), 'fill_pattern {"name":"Nope"}')
    e = e.rstrip('\n')
    msg = e.split(': ', 1)[1] if ': ' in e else e
    full = 'fill_pattern: there\'s no fill pattern `Nope`; make one with `lines` (there are: ' + ', '.join(sorted(['Brick 225 x 75', 'Crosshatch', 'Diagonal Crosshatch', 'Diagonal Down', 'Diagonal Up', 'Horizontal', 'Sand', 'Solid fill', 'Tile 300', 'Vertical'] + ['P%03d' % i for i in range(n)])) + ')'
    print(n, len(e), len(msg), len(full), repr(e[-60:]))
    if '…' in msg:
        k = msg.index('…')
        print('   kept chars:', k, 'kept bytes', len(msg[:k].encode()), 'full chars', len(full), 'more', len(full) - k)

def run(*cmds):

    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]

"""Run commands (original, or mine with -m), save, print library entries that differ from the default
project (by id), plus given sections. usage: lib.py [-m] [-k section]... cmd...
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, json, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/text/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
keys = []
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-k': keys.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run([exe, 'run', '--save', d + '/base.bimcraft'], capture_output=True, check=True)
args = [exe, 'run']
for c in a: args += ['--cmd', c]
args += ['--save', d + '/x.bimcraft']

    for k in keys:
        print('[%s]' % k, json.dumps(x.get(k), ensure_ascii=False))
    print('top:', ','.join(x.keys()))
shutil.rmtree(d)

import subprocess, json, sys, tempfile, shutil, os
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
def run(cmds, f='pv.bimcraft', save=True):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    shutil.copy('/tmp/styles-agent/elec/' + f, d)
    args = [ORIG, 'run', f]
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    if save: args += ['--save', 'out.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    o, e = p.stdout.decode().strip(), p.stderr.decode().strip()
    els = None
    if os.path.exists(d + '/out.bimcraft'):
        doc = json.load(open(d + '/out.bimcraft'))
        els = {k: v.get('params') for k, v in doc['elements'].items() if 'params' in v or k in ('100002', '100003')}
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return o, e, els

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Binary search the PLY header length limit: the position of end_header the reader still finds."""
import sys, os, tempfile, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/cloud-agent')
from orig import run
def make(pos):
    # 'end_header' starts at byte `pos`
    head = 'ply\nformat ascii 1.0\nelement vertex 1\nproperty float x\nproperty float y\nproperty float z\n'
    pad = pos - len(head)
    # comment lines to fill
    s = head
    while pad > 0:
        n = min(pad, 1000)
        if n < 9:
            s = s[:-1] + ' ' * n + '\n'; pad -= n; continue
        line = 'comment ' + 'x' * (n - 9) + '\n'
        s += line; pad -= len(line)
    assert len(s) == pos, (len(s), pos)
    return s + 'end_header\n0 0 0\n'
def ok(pos):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    open(d + '/t.ply', 'w').write(make(pos))
    out, _ = run(['run', '--cmd', 'point_cloud {"path": "t.ply"}'], cwd=d)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out[0] == 0, out[2].strip()
lo, hi = 70000, 1780000
print(ok(lo), ok(hi))
while hi - lo > 1:
    m = (lo + hi) // 2
    if ok(m)[0]: lo = m
    else: hi = m
print('last ok pos', lo, ok(lo), 'first bad', hi, ok(hi))

import subprocess, json, sys, tempfile, shutil, os
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
def run(cmds, f='pv.bimcraft', save=True):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    shutil.copy('/tmp/styles-agent/elec/' + f, d)
    args = [ORIG, 'run', f]
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    if save: args += ['--save', 'out.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    o, e = p.stdout.decode().strip(), p.stderr.decode().strip()
    els = None
    if os.path.exists(d + '/out.bimcraft'):
        doc = json.load(open(d + '/out.bimcraft'))
        els = {k: v.get('params') for k, v in doc['elements'].items() if 'params' in v or k in ('100002', '100003')}
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return o, e, els
vals = {'Len': [-5, 0, 1500.5, 1e12, "1500", True, None, [1]], 'N': [-5, 1e300, 2.5, "x", False], 'Ok': [False, True, 0, "yes"],
        'Fire Rating': ["", "  ", "a" * 300, 5, None]}
for k, vs in vals.items():
    for v in vs:
        c = 'modify ' + json.dumps({"id": 100002, "params": {k: v}})
        o, e, els = run([c])
        print(c[:100], '=>', (o.split('\n')[-2] if not e else e)[:200])
        if not e: print('     ', els.get('100002'))

import subprocess, json, tempfile, os, shutil, sys
mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'delete'
cmds = [
 'option {"set":"K","options":["A","B"]}',
 'wall {"points":[[0,0],[6000,0],[6000,5000],[0,5000]],"closed":true}',   # 100002-100005
 'door {"wall":100003,"offset":1000}',  # 100006
 'window {"wall":100002,"offset":3000}',  # 100007

 'stair {"start":[8000,0],"end":[8000,5000]}',  # 100011
 'railing {"host":100011}',  # 100012...
 'spot {"at":[3000,2500]}',
 'beam {"points":[[0,2000],[3000,2000]]}',
 'room {"point":[3000,2500]}',
 'dimension {"refs":[{"wall":100002,"face":"centre"},{"wall":100004,"face":"centre"}],"at":[7000,2500]}',
]
mods = [
 'modify {"ids":[100002,100003],"params":{"Design Option":"K: B"}}',
 'modify {"id":100008,"params":{"Design Option":"K: B"}}',
 'modify {"id":100011,"params":{"Design Option":"K: B"}}',
]
tail = sys.argv[2:]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
for c in cmds + mods + tail: args += ['--cmd', c]
args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
for c, o in zip(cmds + mods + tail, p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')):
    print(c[:70], '=>', o[:200])
print('ERR', p.stderr.decode())
if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')):
    doc = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft')))
    json.dump(doc, open('/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/cascade.bimcraft', 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    for k, v in doc['elements'].items():
        print(k, v['category'], json.dumps({kk: vv for kk, vv in v.items() if kk in ('host', 'params', 'refs', 'view', 'hosts')})[:200])
shutil.rmtree(d)

import subprocess, json, sys
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
def run(cmds):
    args = [ORIG, 'run']
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run each line of a file as its own session (orig; with -c also mine, printing differences).
usage: batch.py [-c] [-p pre]... [-w width] file
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/text/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
cmp = False
pre = []
w = 400
files = []
quiet = False
while a:
    if a[0] == '-c': cmp = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-p': pre.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w': w = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
lines = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(a[0]) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
def run(exe, cmd):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    args = [exe, 'run']
    for f in files:
        if f.endswith('.bimcraft'): args.append(os.path.basename(f))
    for p in pre: args += ['--cmd', p]
    args += ['--cmd', cmd]
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    out = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip().split('\n')
    last = out[-1] if out else ''
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return 'ERR ' + p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()
    return last
nd = 0
for l in lines:
    o = run(ORIG, l)
    if cmp:
        m = run(MINE, l)
        if m != o:
            nd += 1
            print('>>', l)
            print('   ORIG:', o[:w])
            print('   MINE:', m[:w])
        elif not quiet:
            print('ok', l[:150])
    else:
        print('>>', l)
        print('  ', o[:w])
if cmp:
    print('DIFFS:', nd, 'of', len(lines))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run commands (execute) in a fresh normal session, then print the undo history from inspect.
usage: hist.py 'cmd {json}' ...
"""
import subprocess, json, sys, os, tempfile
lines = []
for i, c in enumerate(sys.argv[1:]):
    cmd, _, rest = c.partition(' ')
    params = json.loads(rest) if rest.strip() else {}
    lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "execute", "arguments": {"command": cmd, "params": params}}}))
lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "insp", "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "inspect_model"}}))
args = os.environ.get('ARGS', '').split()
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'mcp'] + args, input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=os.environ.get('CWD') or tempfile.mkdtemp())
for l in p.stdout.decode().splitlines():
    v = json.loads(l)
    if v['id'] == 'insp':
        d = json.loads(v['result']['content'][0]['text'])
        print('HISTORY', d.get('history'))
    else:
        r = v.get('result') or v.get('error')
        t = r['content'][0]['text'] if 'content' in r else r
        print(v['id'], 'ERR' if r.get('isError') else 'OK', str(t)[:200].replace('\n', ' '))

"""Run cmp.py on sequences of commands (each line of the file is one sequence, commands split by ' ;; ')."""
import os, subprocess, sys
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
fn = sys.argv[1]
extra = sys.argv[2:]
n = 0
bad = 0
for line in open(fn, encoding='utf-8'):
    line = line.rstrip('\n')
    if not line.strip() or line.startswith('#'):
        continue
    cmds = [c.strip() for c in line.split(' ;; ') if c.strip()]
    args = ['python3', '/tmp/tools/cmp.py'] + extra + ['--', 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    args += ['--cmd', 'inspect', '--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, env=dict(os.environ, MINE=MINE))
    n += 1
    out = p.stdout.decode()
    if 'SAME' not in out.split('\n')[-2:]:
        bad += 1
        print('### ', line[:300])
        print(out[:3000])
print('%d of %d sequences differ' % (bad, n))

arguments.content: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Run a sequence of tool calls given as TOOL:ARGSJSON, print results and final history/levels. usage: scr.py 'script:{"text":"..."}' 'execute:{"command":"undo"}' ... env ARGS, CWD, EXE """ import subprocess, json, sys, os, tempfile lines = [] for i, c in enumerate(sys.argv[1:]): tool, _, rest = c.partition(':') lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": json.loads(rest) if rest else {}}})) lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "insp", "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "inspect_model"}})) args = os.environ.get('ARGS', '').split() exe = os.environ.get('EXE', '/workspace/executable') p = subprocess.run([exe, 'mcp'] + args, input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=os.environ.get('CWD') or tempfile.mkdtemp()) for l in p.stdout.decode().splitlines(): v = json.loads(l) if v['id'] == 'insp': r = v['result'] if r.get('isError'): print('INSPECT ERR', r['content'][0]['text'][:300]) continue d = json.loads(r['content'][0]['text']) print('HISTORY', d.get('history'), 'LEVELS', [(x['name'], x['elevation']) for x in d.get('levels', [])], 'NAME', d.get('name'), 'COUNTS', d.get('counts')) else: r = v.get('result') or v.get('error') t = r['content'][0].get('text', '') if 'content' in r else r print(v['id'], 'ERR' if r.get('isError') else 'OK', str(t)[:300].replace('\n', ' ')) if p.stderr: print('STDERR', p.stderr.decode()[:500])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the section headers and packets at each points fileOffset (raw parse, no XML), plus header fields."""
import sys, struct, re
PAGE = 1024
def p2l(off): return (off // PAGE) * (PAGE - 4) + off % PAGE
for fn in sys.argv[1:]:
    b = open(fn, 'rb').read()
    L = bytearray()
    for i in range(0, len(b), PAGE): L += b[i:i + PAGE - 4]
    print('==', fn, 'file', len(b), 'logical', len(L))
    if len(b) >= 48:

        print(' header: version %d.%d physlen %d xmloff %d xmllen %d page %d' % (maj, mnr, plen, xoff, xlen, psize))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write LAS corpus cases into /tmp/cloud-agent/corpus/las_*.las"""
import struct, os
D = '/tmp/cloud-agent/corpus'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
P = struct.pack
RECLEN = {0: 20, 1: 28, 2: 26, 3: 34, 4: 57, 5: 63, 6: 30, 7: 36, 8: 38, 9: 59, 10: 67}
RGB_AT = {2: 20, 3: 28, 5: 28, 7: 30, 8: 30, 10: 30}
def header(vmin=2, fmt=2, reclen=None, count=0, scale=(0.001, 0.001, 0.001), offset=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
           hsize=None, off_points=None, vmaj=1, count64=None, nvlr=0, sig=b'LASF', bbox=(0,) * 6):
    if reclen is None: reclen = RECLEN.get(fmt & 0x3f, 26)
    if hsize is None: hsize = 227 if vmin <= 2 else (235 if vmin == 3 else 375)
    if off_points is None: off_points = hsize
    h = bytearray(sig)
    h += P('<HH', 0, 0) + bytes(16)
    h += bytes([vmaj, vmin]) + bytes(32) + bytes(32)
    h += P('<HH', 1, 2020)
    h += P('<HIIBHI', hsize, off_points, nvlr, fmt, reclen, count if count < (1 << 32) else 0)
    h += P('<5I', 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    h += P('<3d', *scale) + P('<3d', *offset) + P('<6d', *bbox)
    assert len(h) == 227
    if hsize > 227:
        ext = bytearray(hsize - 227)
        if hsize >= 235: ext[0:8] = P('<Q', 0)
        if hsize >= 375 and vmin >= 4:
            ext[8:16] = P('<Q', 0); ext[16:20] = P('<I', 0)
            ext[20:28] = P('<Q', count if count64 is None else count64)
        h += ext
    return bytes(h)
def rec(fmt, x, y, z, i=0, rgb=None, reclen=None):
    if reclen is None: reclen = RECLEN[fmt & 0x3f]
    r = bytearray(reclen)
    r[0:12] = P('<3i', x, y, z)
    r[12:14] = P('<H', i)
    if rgb is not None and (fmt & 0x3f) in RGB_AT:
        a = RGB_AT[fmt & 0x3f]
        r[a:a + 6] = P('<3H', *rgb)
    return bytes(r)
cases = {}
def las(name, hdr, recs=b'', pad=b''):
    cases[name] = hdr + pad + recs
# formats 0..10 with two points
for f in range(11):
    las('fmt%d' % f, header(vmin=4 if f >= 6 else 2, fmt=f, count=2), rec(f, 0, 0, 0, 100, (255, 0, 0)) + rec(f, 1000, 2000, 3000, 300, (0, 65535, 128)))
las('v10', header(vmin=0, fmt=1, count=2), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v13', header(vmin=3, fmt=1, count=2), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v14_legacy_only', header(vmin=4, fmt=1, count=2, count64=0), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v14_both_diff', header(vmin=4, fmt=1, count=1, count64=2), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v12_hsize_235', header(vmin=2, fmt=1, count=2, hsize=235), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v14_hsize_227', header(vmin=4, fmt=1, count=2, hsize=227), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v14_hsize_300', header(vmin=4, fmt=1, count=2, hsize=300), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('v13_hsize_227', header(vmin=3, fmt=1, count=2, hsize=227), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('reclen_longer', header(fmt=1, count=2, reclen=40), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5, reclen=40) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6, reclen=40))
las('reclen_short1', header(fmt=1, count=2, reclen=27), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5, reclen=27) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6, reclen=27))
las('zero_points', header(fmt=1, count=0))
las('neg_scale', header(fmt=1, count=2, scale=(-0.001, 0.001, 0.001)), rec(1, 0, 0, 0) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10))
las('inf_scale', header(fmt=1, count=2, scale=(float('inf'), 0.001, 0.001)), rec(1, 0, 0, 0) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10))
las('nan_scale_z', header(fmt=1, count=2, scale=(0.001, 0.001, float('nan'))), rec(1, 0, 0, 0) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10))
las('inf_offset_x', header(fmt=1, count=2, offset=(float('inf'), 0, 0)), rec(1, 0, 0, 0) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10))
las('zero_scale_and_nan', header(fmt=1, count=2, scale=(0.001, 0.0, 0.001), offset=(float('nan'), 0, 0)), rec(1, 0, 0, 0) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10))
las('laz_bit6', header(fmt=0x41, count=1), rec(1, 0, 0, 0))
las('laz_bit7_fmt11', header(fmt=0x8b, count=1), rec(1, 0, 0, 0))
las('fmt_11_v10', header(vmin=0, fmt=11, count=1, reclen=26), rec(2, 0, 0, 0))
las('fmt6_v12', header(vmin=2, fmt=6, count=1), rec(6, 0, 0, 0))
las('v_major0', header(vmaj=0, fmt=1, count=1), rec(1, 0, 0, 0))
las('v_1_255', header(vmin=255, fmt=1, count=1), rec(1, 0, 0, 0))
las('sig_lower', header(sig=b'lasf', fmt=1, count=1), rec(1, 0, 0, 0))
las('vlr_pad', header(fmt=1, count=2, off_points=227 + 60, nvlr=1), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6), pad=bytes(60))
las('off_before_header', header(fmt=1, count=2, off_points=100), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 5) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 6))
las('intensity_const', header(fmt=1, count=2), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 500) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 500))
las('intensity_range', header(fmt=1, count=4), rec(1, 0, 0, 0, 100) + rec(1, 10, 10, 10, 200) + rec(1, 20, 0, 0, 150) + rec(1, 30, 0, 0, 133))
las('rgb_8bit', header(fmt=2, count=2), rec(2, 0, 0, 0, 0, (1, 2, 3)) + rec(2, 10, 10, 10, 0, (255, 128, 0)))
las('rgb_le1', header(fmt=2, count=2), rec(2, 0, 0, 0, 0, (1, 0, 0)) + rec(2, 10, 10, 10, 0, (0, 1, 1)))
las('rgb_256', header(fmt=2, count=2), rec(2, 0, 0, 0, 0, (256, 0, 0)) + rec(2, 10, 10, 10, 0, (0, 128, 129)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write LAS corpus cases into /tmp/cloud-agent/corpus/las_*.las"""
import struct, os
D = '/tmp/cloud-agent/corpus'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
P = struct.pack
RECLEN = {0: 20, 1: 28, 2: 26, 3: 34, 4: 57, 5: 63, 6: 30, 7: 36, 8: 38, 9: 59, 10: 67}
RGB_AT = {2: 20, 3: 28, 5: 28, 7: 30, 8: 30, 10: 30}
def header(vmin=2, fmt=2, reclen=None, count=0, scale=(0.001, 0.001, 0.001), offset=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
           hsize=None, off_points=None, vmaj=1, count64=None, nvlr=0, sig=b'LASF', bbox=(0,) * 6):
    if reclen is None: reclen = RECLEN.get(fmt & 0x3f, 26)
    if hsize is None: hsize = 227 if vmin <= 2 else (235 if vmin == 3 else 375)
    if off_points is None: off_points = hsize
    h = bytearray(sig)
    h += P('<HH', 0, 0) + bytes(16)
    h += bytes([vmaj, vmin]) + bytes(32) + bytes(32)
    h += P('<HH', 1, 2020)
    h += P('<HIIBHI', hsize, off_points, nvlr, fmt, reclen, count if count < (1 << 32) else 0)
    h += P('<5I', 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    h += P('<3d', *scale) + P('<3d', *offset) + P('<6d', *bbox)
    assert len(h) == 227
    if hsize > 227:
        ext = bytearray(hsize - 227)
        if hsize >= 235: ext[0:8] = P('<Q', 0)
        if hsize >= 375 and vmin >= 4:
            ext[8:16] = P('<Q', 0); ext[16:20] = P('<I', 0)
            ext[20:28] = P('<Q', count if count64 is None else count64)
        h += ext
    return bytes(h)
def rec(fmt, x, y, z, i=0, rgb=None, reclen=None):
    if reclen is None: reclen = RECLEN[fmt & 0x3f]
    r = bytearray(reclen)
    r[0:12] = P('<3i', x, y, z)
    r[12:14] = P('<H', i)
    if rgb is not None and (fmt & 0x3f) in RGB_AT:
        a = RGB_AT[fmt & 0x3f]
        r[a:a + 6] = P('<3H', *rgb)
    return bytes(r)
cases = {}
def las(name, hdr, recs=b'', pad=b''):
    cases[name] = hdr + pad + recs

steps.message:
I've implemented `line_weights`, `object_styles`, `units`, `room_area`, `language` and `standard` in my private copy, and every comparison against the original came out identical. I touched nothing in the worktree and made no commits.

**Tests run (all identical to the original):**
- 115 single commands, comparing reply, error text, undo history and the saved sections plus top-level key order.
- 32 sequences in en, pt, es, cs, it, nl, sv and de projects and in ft-in units, compared with cmp.py (stdout, stderr, whole saved file).
- 21 sequences on three files saved by the original and then opened.
- 5,094 scale names (imperial and metric, including tolerance edges).

**Files:**
- `/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/src/styles/weights.rs`: both commands.
- `/tmp/styles-agent/settings/repo/src/styles/settings.rs`: the other four, plus `inspect_entries`.
- It also exposes `parse_language`, `parse_standard`, `standard_of`, `room_area_of` and `weights::project_units` for other code to use.

**Per command:**
- **`line_weights`:**
  - The default widths are hardcoded tables. Metric projects get scales 10–500; in/ft/ft-in projects get the architect's scales 12–384.
  - Scale names: `1 : n`, or in imperial units the architect's form (`1/8" = 1'-0"`, down to 1/64", tolerance 1e-9) or the engineer's (`1" = 10'-0"`, feet ≥ 10).
  - Setting either part stores the whole section; `reset` removes it.
  - Error texts follow serde, including keys read in sorted order and structs accepted as arrays. Check order: count, then scale range and duplicates after sorting, then model widths, then annotation widths.
  - Unknown parameters are ignored. An undo step is made only when the file changes.
- **`object_styles`:**
  - The file keeps a sorted map of category to projection and cut pens.
  - `component` covers the 18 family categories.
  - An entry that ends up equal to what the category would inherit anyway is removed.
  - `own` in the listing means the category has its own entry.
- **`units`:** the six codes, trimmed and lowercased. The error quotes the value as typed.
- **`room_area`:** only `centre` or `finish`, exact case; `centre` removes the key. A non-string, even `null`, gets an error with no "not …" part. It is the only one of these six that rejects unknown keys: the first one in sorted order.
- **`language`:**
  - It accepts all 9 codes, not just a subset as you expected, plus names (`pt-BR`, `Português`, `dutch`, `vlaams`…).
  - The error text still says "use en, pt, es or sv".
  - Only the `language` key changes.
- **`standard`:**
  - Codes have aliases (abnt/brasil/brazil, international, asme/aia/us/usa, en/europe, japan). Each adapt flag falls back to `adapt_all`, which defaults to true.
  - It replaces the line weights and merges 12 object-style entries.
  - It switches units only across the metric/imperial divide, to the standard's own units.
  - It always makes an undo step (`mark_step`). The reply is the full listing.
  - With no `standard` key, the project counts as `iso`; the pt template has `nbr`.

**Shared-file edits needed (made in my copy only):**
1. `src/project.rs` TOP_ORDER: move `"standard"` from after `"room_area"` to between `"line_weights"` and `"object_styles"`. Observed order: `…,view_templates,phases,phase_filters,phase_overrides,option_sets,line_weights,standard,object_styles,line_patterns,…`.
2. The reinforcement presets section is saved as `"reinforcement"`, not `reinforcement_presets`. It sits between `dimension_types` and `voltages`; TOP_ORDER should change.
3. `common.rs` `check_keys` walks keys in insertion order, but the original reports the first unknown key in sorted order (`{"zzz":1,"bbb":2}` gives `bbb`). This needs fixing for every command that uses it.

**What the core must provide:**
- `inspect` should merge `crate::styles::inspect_entries(s)`. I tested a three-line loop at the end of `inspect.rs` in my copy. Keys:
  - `units`: always `"mm"`.
  - `project_units`: the project's units.
  - `room_area`: `centre` or `finish`.
  - `standard`: the code.
  - `language` is already the core's.
- `inspect` shows no `line_weights` or `object_styles` keys.
- The original's `new {"language": …}` accepts the same names and trimming as `language`; the core's `new` should call `settings::parse_language`.
- Room areas, sheets and drawing pens should read these settings through the accessors above.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a bridge scenario from a JSON spec against the original (or MINE with -m), print everything.
spec: {"args": ["--read-only"], "connect": ["--connect"], "bridge": {...} (PORT replaced),
       "hello": "<reply line>", "steps": [{"call": [tool, args] | "line": "<raw mcp line>", "reply": "<line>" | null}],
       "init": true}
Output: MCP stdout lines, stderr, exit, then each line the window received (repr of bytes).
"""
import json, os, socket, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading, time
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = '/workspace/executable'
if a and a[0] == '-m':
    exe = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
    a = a[1:]
spec = json.load(open(a[0]))
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'
TOKEN = spec.get('token', 'f00dfeedcafe0123456789abcdef0001')
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
srv.listen(8)
port = srv.getsockname()[1]
replies = [spec.get('hello', '{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}')]
lines = [INIT] if spec.get('init', True) else []
for st in spec.get('steps', []):
    if 'call' in st:
        tool, args = st['call']
        lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": len(lines), "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": args}}))
    else:
        lines.append(st['line'])
    if st.get('reply') is not None:
        replies.append(st['reply'])
received = []


def serve():
    while True:
        try:
            c, _ = srv.accept()
        except Exception:
            return
        buf = b''
        while True:
            d = c.recv(65536)
            if not d:
                received.append(('EOF', buf))
                break
            buf += d
            while b'\n' in buf:
                l, buf = buf.split(b'\n', 1)
                received.append(('LINE', l))
                if replies:
                    r = replies.pop(0)
                    if r == '@close':
                        c.close()
                        received.append(('CLOSED', b''))
                        break
                    c.sendall(r.encode() + b'\n')
            else:
                continue
            if received and received[-1][0] == 'CLOSED':
                break


threading.Thread(target=serve, daemon=True).start()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate src/mcp/text.rs from the original's initialize / tools/list replies."""
import json, subprocess, sys, os, tempfile
OUT = sys.argv[1]
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05"}}'
TL = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'


def run(args):
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'mcp'] + args, input=(INIT + '\n' + TL + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=tempfile.mkdtemp())
    ls = p.stdout.decode().splitlines()
    return json.loads(ls[0]), json.loads(ls[1]), ls


i0, t0, raw = run([])
ir, tr, _ = run(['--read-only'])
base = i0['result']['instructions']
ro = ir['result']['instructions']
assert ro.startswith(base)
ro_note = ro[len(base):]
# the bridge note, from a known capture
bridge_note = " You are attached to the window the user has open: what you make is in their project, to see and to undo. new_model and open are not available; the user starts and opens projects in the window."
assert t0 == tr
tools = t0['result']['tools']
tools_json = json.dumps(tools, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), sort_keys=True)
# the raw line must be exactly the compact sorted form
assert raw[1] == json.dumps({"id": 1, "jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"tools": tools}}, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), sort_keys=True)


def rs(s):
    assert '"#' not in s
    return 'r#"' + s + '"#'


out = []
out.append('//! The texts the MCP server says: its instructions and its tools, as the original says them.')
out.append('')
out.append('/// What `initialize` gives an agent as `instructions`.')
out.append('pub const INSTRUCTIONS: &str = %s;' % rs(base))
out.append('')
out.append('/// Added to the instructions with `--connect`.')
out.append('pub const BRIDGE_NOTE: &str = %s;' % rs(bridge_note))
out.append('')
out.append('/// Added to the instructions when the project is read-only (`--read-only`, or a window that says so).')
out.append('pub const READ_ONLY_NOTE: &str = %s;' % rs(ro_note))
out.append('')
out.append('/// `tools/list`: the tools, their descriptions and input schemas (keys sorted, as they are sent).')
out.append('pub const TOOLS: &str = %s;' % rs(tools_json))
open(OUT, 'w').write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('ok', len(base), len(ro_note), len(tools_json))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run cases through cmp.py. A case file has one case per line: commands separated by ' ;; '.
A line starting with 'FILE <path>' sets a project file opened first for the following cases (FILE - for none).
Each case runs: run [file] --cmd c1 --cmd c2 ... --cmd inspect? --save x.bimcraft
usage: batch.py casefile [-v]
"""
import subprocess, sys, os
cmp = '/tmp/tools/cmp.py'
env = dict(os.environ)
env.setdefault('MINE', '/tmp/styles-agent/elec/repo/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
verbose = '-v' in sys.argv
nosave = '-n' in sys.argv
f = None
ok = bad = 0
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    line = line.rstrip('\n')
    if not line.strip() or line.startswith('#'):
        continue
    if line.startswith('FILE '):
        f = line[5:].strip()
        if f == '-': f = None
        continue
    cmds = [c.strip() for c in line.split(' ;; ')]
    args = ['python3', cmp]
    if f: args += ['-f', f]
    args += ['--', 'run']
    if f: args.append(os.path.basename(f))
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    if not nosave: args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, env=env)
    out = p.stdout.decode()
    if out.strip().endswith('SAME'):
        ok += 1
        if verbose: print('SAME', line[:150])
    else:
        bad += 1
        print('DIFF', line[:300])
        print('   ' + '\n   '.join(out.strip().split('\n')[:30]))
print('ok', ok, 'bad', bad)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A window that accepts and closes at once (optionally after a delay, optionally reading first)."""
import socket, subprocess, sys, time, os, tempfile, json, threading
mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'now'
exe = os.environ.get('EXE', '/workspace/executable')
s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); s.listen(4)
port = s.getsockname()[1]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(d + '/bimcraft')
open(d + '/bimcraft/bridge.json', 'w').write(json.dumps({"port": port, "token": "tok"}))
env = dict(os.environ); env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = d


def srv():
    while True:
        c, _ = s.accept()
        if mode == 'now':
            c.close()
        elif mode == 'rst':
            import struct
            c.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack('ii', 1, 0))
            c.close()
        elif mode == 'readclose':
            c.recv(10)
            c.close()


threading.Thread(target=srv, daemon=True).start()
p = subprocess.run([exe, 'mcp', '--connect'], input=b'{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}\n', capture_output=True, env=env, cwd=d, timeout=30)
print('exit', p.returncode)
print('OUT', p.stdout.decode()[:500])
print('ERR', p.stderr.decode()[:500])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build fixture projects with the original binary: fixtures.txt has 'name: cmd ;; cmd ;; ...' lines."""
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, os, shutil
for line in open(sys.argv[1]).read().split('\n'):
    if not line.strip() or line.startswith('#'): continue
    name, cmds = line.split(':', 1)
    cmds = [c.strip() for c in cmds.split(' ;; ')]
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    args += ['--save', 'x.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print(name, 'FAILED', p.stderr.decode())
    else:
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(d, 'x.bimcraft'), '/tmp/styles-agent/phasing/fx/%s.bimcraft' % name.strip())
        print(name, 'ok')
    shutil.rmtree(d)

W=/tmp/mcp-agent/w5
rm -rf $W; mkdir -p $W/d
cd $W
/workspace/executable run --save proj.bimcraft > /dev/null
ln proj.bimcraft hard.bimcraft
ln -s $W d/linkdir

echo "== own file deleted"
cp proj.bimcraft gone.bimcraft
( sleep 0.5; rm -f $W/gone.bimcraft ) &
python3 - <<'EOF'
import subprocess, time, json

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Probe PLY float colour mapping: one point with red = v (float), another 0; print what red becomes."""
import sys, os, json, base64, zlib, tempfile, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/cloud-agent')
from orig import run
typ = sys.argv[1]
vals = sys.argv[2:]
for v in vals:
    hdr = 'ply\nformat ascii 1.0\nelement vertex 2\nproperty float x\nproperty float y\nproperty float z\nproperty %s red\nproperty %s green\nproperty %s blue\nend_header\n' % (typ, typ, typ)
    body = '0 0 0 %s 0 0\n1 1 1 0 0 0\n' % v
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    open(d + '/t.ply', 'w').write(hdr + body)
    out, res = run(['run', '--cmd', 'point_cloud {"path": "t.ply"}', '--save', 'o.bimcraft'], cwd=d)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    if out[0] != 0:
        print(v, out[2].strip()); continue
    doc = json.loads(res['o.bimcraft'])
    c = list(doc['clouds'].values())[0]
    u = zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(c['colours']))
    print(v, '->', u[0])
