results.content:
242:| Data (lógica, dados e voz) | Data outlets, voice outlets, racks, patch panels, the cable trays of the Electrical tab and structured cabling, the vocabulary of NBR 14565. Cabling is a run like a wire, round, in a named `system` (a link, a network), a Cat6, a Cat6A or an optical cable to start from. The project starts with a data and a voice outlet (a plate with its jacks cut in), a patch panel and a floor rack in three sizes, each at the height its type says, original drawings in the project's language, written as `IfcOutlet` (`DATAOUTLET`, `TELEPHONEOUTLET`), `IfcCommunicationsAppliance` (`NETWORKAPPLIANCE`) and, for the rack, which IFC4 has no class for, an `IfcBuildingElementProxy` of object type `Rack`, and read back into a family of the same category (an `IfcOutlet` of another type is read as a power outlet) |
250:| Linked models | `link` (LK, Manage > Link Model) shows another project, a BIMCraft file or an IFC, as a reference in this one, as Revit's Link Revit does: what it builds (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, columns, beams, stairs, railings, pipes and the other runs, components, masses) is drawn halftone in plans, ceiling plans, sections and the 3D view and written into the images, sheets and PDFs, and the picks snap to it. It can't be selected or edited, and the schedules, the checks and the IFC export never see it, so an architect's model is the base to draw the electrical wiring or the plumbing over. It stands origin to origin, moved and turned as the link says (its Origin and Angle in Properties, or `move` and `rotate` on it; it is picked in the Project Browser's Linked Models group, where a right click reloads or removes it); a level of it at the height of one of the project's stands on that one, the others are named after the link. A project keeps the path (relative to its file where it can be) and reads the file again when it opens, saying which links it couldn't read; Reload All, in the right-click menu of the Project Browser's Linked Models, reads them again. A linked project's own links, views, sheets and annotation stay out. Still to come: shared coordinates, per-view visibility and overrides of a link, hosting on a linked wall, and unloading |
251:| CAD drawings | `import_cad` (Insert > Import CAD, or Link CAD) brings a DXF drawing in, as Revit's Import CAD and Link CAD do: an ASCII DXF of any version, read from the public DXF reference, or a DWG (2000 to 2018), which the desktop and the command line read as DXF through acadrust (MPL-2.0, unmodified), in a process of its own. Its unit comes from the file or is chosen; its middle or its origin goes on the project's origin; it shows the layers its file has on, or all, or those listed; its colours are kept, inverted or black. It is drawn under the model in the plans of its level (or in one plan only), with its layers' colours, line weights and linetypes, text and solid hatches, and the picks snap to its ends, middles, centres and crossings, so walls can be traced over it. It moves, turns and copies as one element; `cad_layers` hides its layers everywhere or in one view (Visibility/Graphics' Imported Categories), `cad_query` names the entity at a point, and a linked one is read again by `reload_cad` and when the project opens. The project keeps the drawing's file, so it opens without it. Still to come: DXF and DWG export, exploding an import, and images and PDFs as underlays |
253:| Phasing and design options | Phases in order, as Revit's Phasing has them (a project starts with Existing and New Construction): each element is made in one (its `Phase Created`, the first unless it says) and may be taken down in a later one (`Phase Demolished`), so in a view's phase it is new, existing, demolished (taken down in it) or temporary (made and taken down in it), and what is made after the phase, or taken down before it, isn't there. A view has a phase (the project's last unless it says) and a phase filter, which shows each status as its category does, as the project's overrides for that status say (existing in halftone and demolished dashed red to begin with, both yours to change) or not at all; a project starts with Show All, Show Complete, Show New, Show Previous + Demolished and Show Previous + New. A door or window with no phase of its own follows its wall. Phases are added, inserted, renamed and combined, and what was made, taken down or shown in one goes along; phase filters are made and changed. Design options are sets of options, as Revit's Design Options: an element in an option of a set (`Design Option`, `set: option`) shows only in a view that shows that option, the set's primary unless the view chooses, and one in none shows everywhere. Options are added, renamed, made the primary and taken out (one with elements in it stays until they are moved); accepting the primary keeps its elements and takes the others' and the set away, and deleting a set takes its elements too. What a session makes is made in the phase of the view it is drawn in, when that view has a phase or a phase filter of its own, and in the active design option; a copy is made in them too, and isn't taken down with the element it was copied from, while what is made with a phase or an option given keeps it. Schedules and view filters read the phase and the option as fields (a schedule sorts and groups the phases in the project's order, Existing before New Construction, whatever their names; a rule that names a phase, an option or a set follows it when it is renamed or combined); the desktop's Demolish tool (DW) takes an element down in the phase of the view it is clicked in, and a second click takes it back; templates can control a view's phase and its options; sheets print each view in its phase; a project's phases, filters, overrides and sets are saved with it. A project saved before phases that holds a project parameter named `Phase Created`, `Phase Demolished` or `Design Option` opens with it renamed (`Phase Created Parameter`), its values with it |
262:| Element ids | Every element, model or annotation, view, sheet or schedule, has an id, six digits from 100000 up, which commands, schedules and the desktop show and take, and a GUID, made once and never changed, as Revit's ElementId and UniqueId: what points at an element (a wall its level, a door its wall, a dimension what it measures, a viewport its view) holds its GUID, so an element that comes in from another file under a new id (Insert from File, `insert`; the same file inserted into itself is copied whole, each copy with a GUID of its own) breaks nothing. IFC writes each element's GUID as its GlobalId and reads it back as one; a file from before GUIDs opens with them, its ids moved up to six digits (1 is 100000). The library has them too: each type, material, picture, family, project parameter, view filter and template, phase, phase filter, design option set and design option has an id (counting down from 999999, so a new project's elements still start at 100000) and a GUID, kept through renames; in a file, whatever names one (a wall's type, a layer's material, a view's template, the phase an element is made in, its values of project parameters, keyed by the parameter's) holds its GUID, so renaming changes nothing in a file but the name. Commands take a library entry by its name or its GUID; `library` lists them, and Insert from File matches them by GUID, then by name. So do their parts: each type's layers and each family's forms and plan symbols hold an id and a GUID, kept while they stay where they are in their list (a type's layers given again, the Family Editor's forms moved), a copy getting its own; a family's types and parameters are library entries, so a component's type and its instance values (keyed by the parameter) are GUIDs in a file, and the materials a family's forms and parameters name too. Inside a family, its forms and types name its own parameters as its formulas do |
344:Autosave runs in the background every two minutes while the model has unsaved changes (File > Settings > Files changes
345:the interval or disables it). A saved project's recovery copy is `<project filename>.autosave.bimcraft` beside the project;
346:an untitled project's copy is under the system temporary folder's `bimcraft-autosave` directory. Opening a project with a
347:copy offers **Recover**, **Discard**, or **Postpone**. Recover opens unsaved work, Discard removes the copy, and Postpone
348:protects it for later through File > Recover Autosave. Orphaned untitled copies are offered at startup. Successful Save
349:or an explicit Don't Save removes the current recovery copy, except a postponed copy. See [autosave design](docs/autosave.md).
386:| Phasing | Manage > Phasing (PH). Project Phasing lists the phases in order: type a name and Add at End, Insert Before or Insert After the one picked, Rename it, or Combine with Previous or Next, which takes it out and gives what was made, taken down and shown in it to its neighbour. Phase Filters picks a filter (New Filter makes one) and sets how it shows each of New, Existing, Demolished and Temporary: By Category, Overridden or Not Displayed. Graphic Overrides edits how each status draws where a filter says Overridden, and Apply Overrides sends it as one command. A view's Phasing group in Properties holds its Phase Filter and its Phase (the last unless one is picked); a selected element's holds Phase Created and Phase Demolished, and its Design Option once the project has any |
393:| Edit types | Edit Type opens Type Properties, one dialog for every kind of type, as Revit's: the family and the type at the top with Duplicate and Rename, the type's parameters in a table under group bars that fold (Construction, Dimensions, Materials and Finishes, Graphics, Text…), and OK, Cancel and Apply. Change the type everywhere it's used, Duplicate it into a new one, or Rename it (what's of it follows). A wall type's layers, from the exterior in, or a floor's, roof's or ceiling's, from the top down: each one's function, material and thickness; Insert Layer, and Out and In (Up and Down) and Delete on each |
401:| Views | The Project Browser opens floor plans, ceiling plans, elevations, sections, the 3D view and schedules in tabs; View > Close Inactive closes the others. Its tabs keep it to Views, Schedules, Sheets or Families (Legends are still to come), and its search narrows it as you type, marking what matched: each word must match an entry or a group it's in (`ceiling 2`), `*` stands for any run of characters and `?` for any one. View > Duplicate View (DP) makes a plan view of the plan on screen, plain, with detailing or as a dependent; so does a right click on a plan in the Project Browser, where a plan view also has Delete, and a plan view's name, view range and crop are in Properties as a level's are. The Project Browser's Families lists each system category's types (walls, floors, doors…) and the project's component families; a right click on a type or a family has Delete, which the project refuses while something uses it. Manage > Link Model (LK) links another project, and the Project Browser lists the linked models. Manage > Purge Unused (PU) lists what nothing uses, by kind (types and families checked, as Revit's), and takes it out in one undo step. A right click in any view opens a menu of what it and the selection can do: Cancel, Edit Type, Select All Instances, Delete, Hide Element, Hide Category, Override Graphics, Zoom to Fit, Zoom In, Zoom Out, and in 3D Home View |
411:| Settings | File > Settings (Ctrl+, or the cog on the Quick Access Toolbar): the theme, language, ribbon and palettes under User Interface, with Plans' two working aids, the origin marker (a small mark at the project's 0, 0 with the directions of x and y) and the view's name in a plan's bottom left corner, both on at first and drawn on the screen only, never in a PNG, a sheet or a printout; background autosave and its interval under Files; whether to look for updates. Performance holds Draw the 3D view on the graphics card (off until you turn it on); the rest of Performance, and Graphics, show settings still to come, greyed out. They're kept in `settings.json` beside the favorites, with where the palettes are |

# Background autosave and recovery

The desktop takes a recovery snapshot every two minutes when the committed model has unsaved changes. File > Settings >
Files offers an interval of 1–120 minutes and an off switch, persisted in the user's settings. Recovery discovery still
runs when automatic saving is off. The interval is measured with a monotonic clock and does not reset on every edit:
continuous modeling must not starve autosave. There are no periodic dialogs, focus changes, or successful-save notices.

## Approach and research

- Rust's [Arc documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Arc.html) describes shared immutable ownership and
  copy-on-write. BIMCraft already uses `Arc<Model>` for undo and rollback. The UI passes a reference-counted snapshot to
  one worker; serialization and every recovery-file operation run there. There is no model mutex, UI-thread model copy,
  or wait for a writer. At most one snapshot is outstanding, so a slow disk cannot accumulate obsolete full models.
- Qt's [QSaveFile](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qsavefile.html) documents writing a temporary file and committing it to avoid
  partial documents. BIMCraft follows that pattern using Rust's
  [NamedTempFile::persist](https://docs.rs/tempfile/latest/tempfile/struct.NamedTempFile.html#method.persist): write beside
  the destination, sync the complete file, then atomically replace the old one, without a direct-write fallback.
  Unix also syncs the containing directory. Normal project Save uses the same replacement helper.
- Recovery files are independent of the saved project. Saving a snapshot leaves the project path, dirty state, selection,
  undo history, and saved project untouched. The background worker executes the ordinary `autosave {path}` command on
  its snapshot. Recovery uses `recover {path, project?}`, with the same migrations and validation as Open.

These are full snapshots, rather than a new command journal: the existing native project reader can validate and migrate
them, including after a process is killed. The worker retains a bounded amount of snapshot work, though serialization
still consumes CPU and memory in proportion to model size. This does not implement incremental persistence.

## Files and lifecycle

- A saved project `house.bimcraft` uses `house.bimcraft.autosave.bimcraft` in the same directory. No numbered history is
  accumulated. An in-progress replacement cannot truncate the previous complete recovery copy.
- Untitled work uses `<system temp>/bimcraft-autosave/untitled-<GUID>.autosave.bimcraft`. The name is unique per document.
  On first Save, its temporary snapshot is removed and subsequent snapshots go beside the saved project. The operating
  system may clear its temporary directory, so untitled recovery cannot promise survival of a reboot or system cleanup.
- A small adjacent `.lock` file holds an OS file lock for each claimed backup. Another live window's copies are skipped;
  process termination releases its locks automatically. Lock files deliberately remain to avoid unlink/relock races.
- Save, Save As, New, Open, explicit Don't Save, and normal close queue cleanup after outstanding writes, so a late writer
  cannot recreate a discarded snapshot. Merely destroying an app object does not delete snapshots. A failed Save leaves
  recovery intact. Exports leave the native project and recovery lifecycle alone.

Opening a native project checks for its adjacent recovery copy even if the original is damaged. Startup also scans for
orphaned untitled snapshots. No timestamp comparison suppresses a discovered backup: the user decides its relevance.

| Choice | Result |
|---|---|
| Recover | Validate and open the backup as unsaved work. Save targets the original project, or asks for Save As for untitled recovery. The backup remains until saved or explicitly discarded. |
| Discard | Delete only the chosen recovery snapshot, leaving the saved project and current model alone. Failed deletion keeps it available. |
| Postpone, Escape, or dismiss | Continue using the current model and preserve the copy. File > Recover Autosave reopens the choices; reopening the project offers them again. |

A postponed copy must not be overwritten by subsequent editing or Save. While it is unresolved, new autosaves use a
separate temporary snapshot. Save As also checks the destination for an existing recovery copy. Recovery of corrupt or
unsupported data reports the error and keeps both the current project and recovery choices available. Recovering over
new unsaved edits first uses the usual Save / Don't Save / Cancel prompt.

## Verification

Core tests cover snapshot consistency, unchanged original/undo state, ordered save/remove operations, bounded scheduling,
a deliberately blocked worker, corrupt data, live-window leases, and recovery after forcibly killing a subprocess.
Desktop tests cover temporary-to-adjacent saving, all three recovery choices, postponed-copy preservation through editing
and Save, corrupt backups, a damaged original, existing recovery data at a Save As destination, and untitled recovery.

A local smoke measurement with 10,000 columns (a 4.14 MB native snapshot) took about 3 microseconds to enqueue the snapshot,
33 ms for a validated model edit while the worker saved, and 55 ms to complete the snapshot. This is one generated model
on the development machine, rather than a performance guarantee for projects with complex geometry or large images.

steps.message:
You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler written in Rust; README at /workspace/README.md), as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Several agents work in parallel, each owning one area. I own the EDIT area (`src/edit/`) and delegate to you the commands `purge`, `delete_type`, `rename_type` and `match_properties`.

## Hard rules (violating any fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`.
- No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only.
- Edit ONLY `src/edit/purge.rs`, `src/edit/types.rs`, `src/edit/matchprops.rs` (you may add files `src/edit/library_*.rs` with their `pub mod` lines in `src/edit/mod.rs`, and add your commands to `always_step` there). Nothing else in the repo. Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, in `/tmp/edit-library/`. Commit only Rust.
- The sandbox refuses shell commands it can't verify (loops, heredocs, `cd` outside the worktree, `$(...)` feeding python): write Python scripts to files in /tmp and run them as `python3 /tmp/edit-library/x.py`.

## Setup
You are in a git worktree. First make sure your HEAD contains commit 89ee1af ("Editing: module skeleton"): `git log --oneline -3`; if not, `git merge --no-edit worktree-agent-a76b15059404997b3`. Build with `cargo build --release` (about 15 s).

## The codebase (read the relevant parts first)
- `src/json.rs`: `Value` (insertion-ordered `Map`, `insert_sorted`), serde_json-identical float formatting (`1000.0`), `to_compact`/`to_pretty`, `.sorted()` (replies are printed sorted by main.rs: just return the Value), `jobj!{}`.
- `src/project.rs`: `Project` = `doc` (top-level sections in file order: `types` {category: {name: def}}, `materials`, `images`, `families`, `parameters`, `view_filters`, `view_templates`, `line_styles`… ; `insert_top`, `section_mut`, `remove_top`) + `elements` (each a JSON object; a wall's `type` is its type's GUID, a component's `family`/`type` GUIDs, a view's template, a layer's material…) + `library: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (`{kind, name, guid}`: kinds `type:wall`, `material`, `picture`, `family`, `family-type`, `family-parameter`, `view-filter`, `view-template`…; `lib_find`, `lib_guid`, `lib_name`, `lib_find_guid`). Key order matters (files are compared byte for byte after normalising GUIDs): remove entries without disturbing the rest.
- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute` resolves the command, snapshots, runs, runs `crate::check::check`, rolls back on error, records an undo step labelled by the catalog label when the project changed (seen: `purge {"dry_run": true}` makes no step; `delete_type`/`rename_type` make `Delete Type`/`Rename Type` steps — check whether one that changes nothing still does; `match_properties` → `Match Properties`).
- `src/commands/params.rs` (param readers with the original's texts), `src/edit/common.rs` (`ids_param` — `ids`, else `id`, with the original's errors —, `resolve`), `src/styles/` (done by another agent: line styles/patterns, fill patterns, region types, text and dimension types, parameters, phasing — reuse e.g. `styles::common` helpers and see how they rename/delete their own library entries), `src/media/` (materials, pictures: done).
- Other areas are being written in parallel and are empty stubs now: ARCH, STRUCTURE (`type`, `family`, `component` commands), VIEWS, READERS. Don't implement their commands; your commands must work on project files made by the ORIGINAL.

## How to test
Build input projects with the original: `/workspace/executable run --script s.txt --save in.bimcraft` (walls of several types, doors, windows, components of several families, `type {...}` to make types, `family {...}`, `material {...}` with pictures (`material {"name": "M", "texture": {"path": "x.png"}}`), `filter {...}`, `template {...}`, `graphics {"template": …}`; `/workspace/executable commands` lists every command and its parameters). A fixture with one element of most categories is `/tmp/edit-agent/fx/all.bimcraft` (`python3 /tmp/edit-agent/dump.py file [ids|categories]` dumps elements). `/tmp/edit-agent/lib.py` has `run(cmds, src=file, files=[...], exe=...)` → (code, replies, stderr, project dict) and `/tmp/edit-agent/probe.py in.bimcraft 'purge {}'` prints the reply and the diff (elements, top-level sections, library); use them, don't edit files under /tmp/edit-agent. To compare with yours: `MINE=<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py -f in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd 'purge {}' --save out.bimcraft` prints SAME or the diff. The hidden tests do this kind of comparison on many inputs: replies, error texts, saved files and undo labels must match exactly.

## Your commands (specs from `/workspace/executable commands`)
- `purge` (PU, Purge Unused): "{kinds?: [type|family|material|picture|filter|template, …], dry_run?} takes out what nothing uses, again for what that leaves unused: types and families unless `kinds` says; a category keeps a type and a family a type; with `dry_run` it lists what would go and changes nothing". Seen on a new project: `{"count": 63, "dry_run": false, "removed": [{"kind": "beam type", "name": "Beam 150 x 400"}, …, {"kind": "family", "name": "Air Terminal"}, …]}`. Work out what counts as a use for each kind (elements, other types' layers, families' forms and parameters, materials' textures → pictures, views' graphics → filters, views → templates, paint, schedules, favorites?…), the cascade ("again for what that leaves unused"), the order of `removed`, what goes from the library and the sections (and empty sections), errors for bad `kinds`.
- `delete_type`: "{category?: wall|floor|door|window|column|roof|ceiling|railing|…, family?, type?} deletes a type of a category (`category` and `type`), a family (`family`) or one of a family's types (`family` and `type`), as Revit's Delete on one in the Project Browser does; refused while an element uses it (it says how many), and for the last type of a category or of a family". Seen: `{}` → `delete_type: give `category` and `type`, or `family`, or `family` and `type``; ok → `{"deleted": {"kind": "wall type", "name": "Exterior - 300mm"}}`.
- `rename_type`: "{category?, family?, type, name} renames a type of a category (`category` and `type`) or one of a family's types (`family` and `type`) to `name`, as Rename in Type Properties does: the elements of it, and what else names it, follow, and it keeps its GUID; refused for a name another type of it has. Text types and filled region types rename with `rename` on `text_type` and `filled_region_type`". Seen: `{}` → `rename_type: `name` is required: the type's new name`; `{"ids": []}` → `rename_type: `ids` isn't one of its parameters: category, family, type, name`; ok → `{"renamed": {"from": "Exterior - 300mm", "kind": "wall type", "to": "X"}}`.
- `match_properties` (MA): "{from: id, ids: [id,…]} gives the elements in `ids` the type of `from` (and, for components, its family), as Revit's Match Properties does; only elements of `from`'s category take it, the rest come back in `skipped`. Returns {modified, skipped}". Seen: `{}` → `match_properties: `from` (an element id or GUID) is required`.
For each: every error and the order of checks (category names as typed: plural, case, `structural column`…; unknown type names and the lists they give), what changes in sections, library and elements, undo steps.

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch (message ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Final message: your branch name and commit; per command what matches (tested with cmp.py) and what doesn't; what other areas must provide.

"""Probing helpers: run the original (or mine) on scripts, read the project after."""
import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, os

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a76b15059404997b3/target/release/bimcraft-cli'


def run(cmds, src=None, exe=ORIG, files=(), save=True, extra=None):
    """cmds: list of 'id {json}' strings. Returns (code, replies, stderr, project dict or None)."""
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='lib')
    try:
        args = [exe, 'run']
        if src:
            shutil.copy(src, os.path.join(d, 'in.bimcraft'))
            args.append('in.bimcraft')
        for f in files:
            shutil.copy(f, d)
        open(os.path.join(d, 's.txt'), 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
        args += ['--script', 's.txt']
        if save:
            args += ['--save', 'out.bimcraft']
        if extra:
            args += extra
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        lines = [l for l in p.stdout.splitlines() if not l.startswith('{"format":"bimcraft"')]
        if src and lines:
            lines = lines[1:]
        replies = []
        for l in lines:
            try:
                replies.append(json.loads(l))
            except Exception:
                replies.append(l)
        proj = None
        if save and os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'out.bimcraft')):
            proj = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'out.bimcraft')))
        return p.returncode, replies, p.stderr.strip(), proj
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(d)


def els(proj, cat=None):
    out = {}
    for k, v in proj['elements'].items():
        if cat and v.get('category') not in (cat if isinstance(cat, (list, tuple)) else [cat]):
            continue
        out[int(k)] = v
    return out


def short(v):
    v = dict(v)
    v.pop('guid', None)
    for f in ('level', 'top_level', 'type', 'host', 'view', 'style'):
        if f in v and isinstance(v[f], str) and len(v[f]) == 36:
            v[f] = '<g>'
    return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)


def show(proj, cat=None, keys=None):
    for k, v in els(proj, cat).items():
        if keys:
            print(k, {kk: v.get(kk) for kk in keys})
        else:
            print(k, short(v))
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the original and my build with the same args in fresh dirs; diff normalized outputs.
usage: cmp.py [-q] [-f file_to_copy]... -- args...
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, difflib
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
GUID = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r'"uid": \d+', '"uid": <UID>', s)
    m = {}
    def rep(mo):
        g = mo.group(0)
        if g not in m: m[g] = 'GUID-%d' % (len(m)+1)
        return m[g]
    s = GUID.sub(rep, s)
    s = re.sub(r"\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]{6}", ".tmpXXXXXX", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    # IFC GlobalIds
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm)+1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    return s
def run(exe, args, files, stdin):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cmp')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    before = set(os.listdir(d))
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, input=stdin, timeout=120)
    out = {'stdout': p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'stderr': p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'code': p.returncode}
    fl = {}
    for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, d)
            if rel in before: 
                pass
            try: fl[rel] = open(full,'rb').read()
            except Exception as e: fl[rel] = b'<unreadable>'
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out, fl
def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    quiet = False; files = []; stdin = None
    while a and a[0] != '--':
        if a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-i': stdin = open(a[1],'rb').read(); a = a[2:]
        else: break
    if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
    o, of = run(ORIG, a, files, stdin)
    m, mf = run(MINE, a, files, stdin)
    ok = True
    for k in ('code', 'stdout', 'stderr'):
        x = norm(str(o[k])); y = norm(str(m[k]))
        if x != y:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- {k} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x.splitlines(), y.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:40]:
                print(l[:300])
    for f in sorted(set(of) | set(mf)):
        if f not in of: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in mine'); continue
        if f not in mf: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in orig'); continue
        x, y = of[f], mf[f]
        try:
            xs = norm(x.decode('utf-8')); ys = norm(y.decode('utf-8'))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            if x != y: ok = False; print(f'--- binary file {f} differs ({len(x)} vs {len(y)} bytes)')
            continue
        if xs != ys:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- file {f} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(xs.splitlines(), ys.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:60]:
                print(l[:300])
    print('SAME' if ok else 'DIFF')
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
main()

380:| Filled regions | Annotate > Filled Region (FR) and Masking Region start a boundary sketch. Edit Type opens Type Properties for a selected region or the current sketch: duplicate and rename types; choose foreground and background patterns and colors separately; set masking; check the combined preview. A pattern's … button opens the patterns, to create and edit them. Apply/OK save the draft as one undo step; Cancel drops unapplied work. A type change updates every region using it; the palette's Type Selector controls the instance's type. Non-masking fills keep cut foreground patterns and projected model lines visible; masking fills cover the model. Sketches snap to visible model edges, detail lines, existing region boundaries and their own geometry, with the configured snaps and angle guides. |
401:| Views | The Project Browser opens floor plans, ceiling plans, elevations, sections, the 3D view and schedules in tabs; View > Close Inactive closes the others. Its tabs keep it to Views, Schedules, Sheets or Families (Legends are still to come), and its search narrows it as you type, marking what matched: each word must match an entry or a group it's in (`ceiling 2`), `*` stands for any run of characters and `?` for any one. View > Duplicate View (DP) makes a plan view of the plan on screen, plain, with detailing or as a dependent; so does a right click on a plan in the Project Browser, where a plan view also has Delete, and a plan view's name, view range and crop are in Properties as a level's are. The Project Browser's Families lists each system category's types (walls, floors, doors…) and the project's component families; a right click on a type or a family has Delete, which the project refuses while something uses it. Manage > Link Model (LK) links another project, and the Project Browser lists the linked models. Manage > Purge Unused (PU) lists what nothing uses, by kind (types and families checked, as Revit's), and takes it out in one undo step. A right click in any view opens a menu of what it and the selection can do: Cancel, Edit Type, Select All Instances, Delete, Hide Element, Hide Category, Override Graphics, Zoom to Fit, Zoom In, Zoom Out, and in 3D Home View |

Sloped: its top rises `slope` degrees (negative, falls) along the slope arrow, from its tail, where it's at the offset, toward its head. Its top's model pattern starts at `pattern_origin` and turns by `pattern_angle` (see modify). An outline, and each opening, is simple: no edge across another or along it, none ending part way along one, no spike or keyhole slit (`ceiling`, `roof` and `shaft` too, and `modify`, `move` and `edit_boundary` of any of them: they are refused, saying which edges); a file that has one still opens, and works until a command changes its outline

Its outline's and openings' corners stay at 0 unless a point is there; a line's end that is no point and no corner becomes a point at the height the top has there. Sent back with its `id`, a point or a line keeps it. A shaped floor has no slope arrow, a shaped roof no `slope`. Without `points` or `lines`, gives the shape: its points and lines with their ids, its corners at their heights, how many planes (`faces`) and its top's lowest and highest (`top`, mm above zero)

With `top`, an outline of as many points as the footprint (twin for twin, running the same way round), it is lofted straight from the footprint to it; `lean` makes one by moving the footprint sideways by [dx, dy] for its top, a sloped mass. Drawn dashed in plans and sections (the outline at the height they cut it, between the two when lofted), a see-through solid in 3D; its own category, `mass`, which views may hide. Its areas and volumes, per level too, are those of the cross sections between its outlines, exactly. Make floors from it with `mass_floors`, walls, a floor and a roof from its faces with `wall_by_face`, `floor_by_face` and `roof_by_face`
mass_floors | {mass?, type?, prune?} a floor of the footprint at each level the mass crosses, from the one at its base up to, not including, the one at its top; every mass when no `mass`. wall_by_face | {mass, faces?: [edge, …], type?, location?} a wall on each edge of the mass's footprint (numbered from its first point), or the `faces` given, as tall as the mass; its exterior finish on the edge, facing out (`location` changes that line). Ordinary walls from then on
floor_by_face | {mass, type?} a floor on the mass's top face: its top at the mass's top level, or `height` over its base. An ordinary floor from then on
roof_by_face | {mass, type?, slope?, overhang?} a roof on the mass's top face, flat unless it has a `slope` (degrees), over the mass's top level or `height` over its base. An ordinary roof from then on

The ones of `mass`, or the `ids` given, or every one in the project; what was done to them since (their type, a roof's slope) stays. A face that is gone (a footprint with fewer corners) refuses the lot and says which; a deleted mass's are ordinary elements. Revit has no default shortcut for it: UF is BIMCraft's. The reply has `updated` and `unchanged`
show_mass | {view?, show?} hides the masses in a view if it shows them, shows them if it hides them (or as `show`, a yes or no, says): the `mass` category of `graphics {hide|show}`, in one step. Placed where nothing encloses it, or in a space another room has (two rooms can't share one; the first keeps it), it is placed unbounded, a 1000 mm square, and the reply has a `warning`. Its height is Revit's: from `base_offset` mm over its level (0) up to `limit_offset` mm over its upper limit `top_level` (null: Not Bounded, over its own level). Unless given, 300 mm under the level above (`top_level` that level, `limit_offset` -300), or with none above, not bounded and 2500 mm tall. `elements` gives its `unbounded_height` and `volume_m3`, its area times that height. `frozen` (a yes or no; also `modify {id, frozen}`) keeps the boundary the room has now: it keeps its size whatever the walls do, and the walls are never searched for it again, which saves time in a project of many rooms. ce across its width and across its depth, corners counted, 2 each; a round column takes `count` instead of x and y, evenly round its circle, with hoops of 24 sides), `stirrup`, `ties` {diameter, hook?} across a rectangular section between bars that are not at a corner (`hook`, a tail in mm at each end), `anchor` {below?, above?}. Footing: `mesh` {x?, y?: {diameter, spacing}, hook?} (hook turns the ends up; a round footing's bars stop at its circle). Floor: `bottom` and `top` {x?, y?: {diameter, spacing}, hook?} (bars along east and north; `hook`, a leg turned up from a bottom mesh and down from a top one), stopping a cover short of its outline and its openings; a sloped floor's bars follow its top, the cover square to it. The bars are `rebar` elements of the host, each on a `layer`; reinforcing again replaces the ones it made and leaves any drawn by hand. `check` "NBR 6118" (with `aggressiveness` 1 to 4 for the cover, and `fck` in MPa) adds `notes` to the reply where the bars made fall short of that standard's usual limits (cover, bar sizes and spacings, stirrups, least and most steel, skin bars): they are notes, never a refusal, the numbers typed from handbooks and not the standard's text, so check one against a copy before relying on it. `preset` names a `reinforcement_preset` of the host's kind, whose parameters stand for the ones not given here. `hosts` arms each of a list alike (up to 1000, and 20000 bars in all); if one refuses, none is armed, and the refusal names it. Returns ids, count, hosts, removed, weight_kg and notes
reinforcement_preset | {name?, kind?: beam|column|footing|floor, params?, rename?, delete?: true} a named set of the parameters `reinforce` takes for one kind of host (`params`: its `cover`, `grade`, `grade_stirrup`, `clearance` and what its kind takes, and not `host`), kept in the project; `reinforce` with `preset` takes it and lets what is given with it replace its own. Without `name`, lists them. It is not checked against any host until it arms one
voltage | {name?, nominal?, min?, max?, rename?, delete?: true} a voltage of the project's electrical settings, in volts: `nominal`, and the band a device may read within, `min` to `max` (10 per cent either way unless given). Without `name`, lists them. A voltage a distribution system names cannot be deleted; renamed, the systems follow
distribution_system | {name?, phases?: 1|2|3, wires?, l_l?, l_n?, l_g?, ground?, rename?, delete?: true} a distribution system of the project's electrical settings. `wires` counts the line conductors and the neutral, not the protective one (3 phases: 3 or 4). `l_l`, `l_n` and `l_g` name the voltages between two lines, a line and the neutral, and a line and earth (at least one; `l_l` from 2 phases; with 3 phases `l_l` is about 1.73 times `l_n`), each a `voltage` of the project; "" takes one away. `ground` is the earthing: TN-S, TN-C, TN-C-S, TT or IT. A voltage the project lacks is refused, and the refusal lists the ones it has. Without `name`, lists them
wire_type | {name?, material?: copper|aluminium, temperature?, insulation?, note?, sizes?: [{section, ampacity, label?}], rename?, delete?: true} a wire type of the project's electrical settings: a conductor's `material`, working `temperature` (°C) and `insulation`, and its table, `sizes`: the `section` of each row in mm² (smallest first, never less than the row before) and the `ampacity` it carries in amperes, with a `label` for how its standard names it (12 AWG). Giving `sizes` replaces the table. `note` says where the ampacities come from. Without `name`, lists them
column | {at: [x,y], type?, angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?} a column, its width along `angle` degrees; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall, or up to `top_level`
structural_column | {at: [x,y], type?, angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?} a column of the structure, as `column` makes one but in its own category with its own types (`type` with category structural column): up to the next level, or `height` mm tall, or up to `top_level`. CL is `column`'s too; on the desktop's Structure tab it is this one
footing | {at: [x,y], type?, thickness?, offset?, angle?, level?} an isolated (pad) footing, its plan the type's (category footing), `thickness` mm thick (400) with its top `offset` mm over the level (0: at it), so it hangs below
beam | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a beam for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category beam: `width` across, `depth` deep, or round), its `justify` line (top by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level, so it hangs below) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a single segment; `system` names the system it belongs to. It slopes up to 75°
strip_footing | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, system?} a continuous footing under a wall for each segment of the points, its section the type's (category stripfooting), its top `offset` mm over the level (0: at it)
pipe | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a pipe for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category pipe: round, `width` the outside diameter), its `justify` line (centre by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a single segment, so a drain falls and a riser rises; the same point twice and two heights make one stand upright. `system` names the system it belongs to ("Água fria", "Esgoto")
duct | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a duct for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category duct: `width` across by `depth` deep, or round, `width` the diameter), its `justify` line (centre by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a single segment; the same point twice and two heights make one stand upright. `system` names the system it belongs to ("Supply air", "Exhaust")
conduit | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a conduit (eletroduto) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` its outside diameter; `system` names its circuit
cable_tray | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a cable tray (eletrocalha) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: its section the type's `width` across by `depth` deep
wire | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a wire (condutor) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` its outside diameter; `system` names its circuit
down_conductor | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a down conductor (condutor de descida, NBR 5419) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, or a flat strip; the same point twice and two heights make one stand upright down a wall; `system` names the protection system it belongs to
ground_conductor | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} an earthing conductor (condutor de aterramento, the ring or mesh of NBR 5419) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them, usually under the level (a negative `offset`)
cabling | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} structured cabling (cabeamento estruturado, NBR 14565) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` the cable's outside diameter; `system` names the link or the network it belongs to
stair | {start: [x,y], end?: [x,y] | angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, width?, riser?, tread?, landings?: [{at, turn?}, …], railings?} a stair from the middle of its first riser at `start`, climbing toward `end` (or `angle` degrees) up to the next level: as many risers as keep each at most `riser` mm (180), treads `tread` deep (280), `width` wide (1000). One straight run, as long as that makes it; or with landings (each as deep as the stair is wide) after `at` risers, the next run going on as `turn` says: 0 straight on, 90 or -90 turned left or right, 180 or -180 back beside it, to its left or right. With `railings`, a railing down each side too

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""mk.py out.bimcraft 'cmd {json}' ... : build a project with the original from commands (or a file of them)."""
import sys, subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil
out = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1])
cmds = []
for x in sys.argv[2:]:
    if '{' in x:
        cmds.append(x)
    else:
        cmds += [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(x) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='mk')
open(os.path.join(d, 's.txt'), 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', 's.txt', '--save', out], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(p.stdout.strip())
if p.returncode:
    print('ERR', p.stderr.strip())
shutil.rmtree(d)

  texts of their own: always probe.

  and `dimension` take `level`), `find` by id/GUID, `normalize_guid`, `level_of_view`.

  files as they are): `/workspace/executable run --cmd 'wall {"points":[[0,0],[10000,0],[10000,6000],[0,6000]],"closed":true}' --cmd 'door {"wall":100002,"offset":2000}' --save /tmp/views-x/in.bimcraft`,
  then `cmp.py -f /tmp/views-x/in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd '…' --save out.bimcraft`.
- `/tmp/views-tools/p.py [-m] [-f in.bimcraft] -- run …` runs one program (`-m`: ours, with MINE set)
  and prints its output and the elements (and changed top-level sections) of each .bimcraft it saved.
- `/tmp/views-tools/each.py [-b] [-f in.bimcraft] [-s 'setup cmd']… cmds.txt` runs each line of
  cmds.txt (a command, or several joined by ` ;; `) in a fresh run of the original (`-b`: of both,
  marking SAME/DIFF; `-m`: ours). Set `SCRATCH=/tmp/views-<yourpart>` for its temp dirs. The harness
  refuses shell loops and `cd … &&` chains: write command files and run the tools on them.
- `/workspace/executable commands` prints every command's spec (`params`); read yours, and
  `/workspace/docs/areas/views-and-graphics.md` (and the README's command table) for what they mean.
- Probe widely: normal cases, every optional parameter, edge cases, every error and the ORDER of the
  checks (which error wins when two things are wrong), what the model check refuses after the command
  ("text 100013: view3d 100008 isn't a plan, a section, an elevation or a sheet": category, id, text,
  no command prefix), names in every project language (`new {"language":"pt"}`…: en pt es sv cs fr nl
  de it), the saved JSON of every element and section you make, `elements {"category":…}` output for
  your categories, `undo`/`redo` after your commands (labels), and that a refused command changes
  nothing. Numbers the original works out are usually rounded to the micron (3 decimals).

# 1. autosave vs save bytes

show(r, 200)
a = r['files'].get('a.bimcraft'); b = r['files'].get('b.bimcraft')
print('same bytes', a == b, len(a or b''), len(b or b''))
r = run(['autosave {"path": "a.bimcraft"}', 'save {"path": "b.bimcraft"}'], args_before=['all.bimcraft'], files=[FX], exe=exe)
show(r, 200)
a = r['files'].get('a.bimcraft'); b = r['files'].get('b.bimcraft')
print('same bytes', a == b, len(a or b''), len(b or b''), 'same as input', a == open(FX, 'rb').read())
for p in ['""', '"."', '"/"', '"nodir/x.bimcraft"', '"s.txt/x"']:
    r = run(['save {"path": %s}' % p], exe=exe)
    print('save', p[:40], r['code'], r['out'][:2], r['err'][:300], sorted(r['files'].keys()))
# 4. history
r = run(['wall {"points": [[0,0], [5000,0]]}', 'autosave {"path": "a.bimcraft"}', 'undo', 'redo', 'autosave {"path": "a.bimcraft"}', 'undo', 'redo', 'inspect'], exe=exe)
for l in r['out']:
    d = j(l)
    if isinstance(d, dict) and 'history' in d:
        print('history', d['history'], 'path', d.get('path'))
    else:
        print(l[:200])
print(r['err'])
# opened project: autosave keeps path
r = run(['autosave {"path": "a.bimcraft"}', 'inspect', 'save {}'], args_before=['all.bimcraft'], files=[FX], exe=exe)
for l in r['out']:
    d = j(l)
    if isinstance(d, dict) and 'history' in d:
        print('history', d['history'], 'path', d.get('path'))
    else:
        print(l[:200])
print(r['err'])
# autosave over an existing file / a dir
r = run(['autosave {"path": "s.txt"}'], exe=exe)
print(r['code'], r['out'], r['err'], len(r['files']['s.txt']))
r = run(['autosave {"path": "sub"}'], exe=exe, dirs=['sub'])
print(r['code'], r['out'], r['err'])

"""Walk a struct's fields in serde's sequence form, finding each field's type and a valid value.
usage: seqwalk.py TEMPLATE PREFIX_JSON [extra valid candidates json...]
TEMPLATE is a JSON text with @ where the array goes (e.g. '@' for the root, or
'{"elements":{"100000":@}, ...}')."""
import sys, json, re
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/loader-agent')
from lib import *

tpl = sys.argv[1]
prefix = json.loads(sys.argv[2])
extra = [json.loads(x) for x in sys.argv[3:]]
probes = [True, "zz", 5, -5, 1.5, [], {}, None] + extra
STRIP = re.compile(r'^open: x\.bimcraft is not a BIMCraft project: (element \d+: )?')


def attempt(arr):
    text = tpl.replace('@', json.dumps(arr))
    code, msg, saved = open_file(text, save=False)
    return code, STRIP.sub('', msg)


i = len(prefix)
while True:
    results = []
    valid = None
    for pr in probes:
        code, msg = attempt(prefix + [pr])
        m = re.match(r'invalid length (\d+), expected', msg)
        ok = code == 0 or (m and int(m.group(1)) > i) or ('invalid length' not in msg and False)
        results.append((pr, msg))
        if ok and valid is None:
            valid = pr
    # also: does the seq end here? (field has default?)
    code, msg = attempt(prefix)
    print(f'[{i}] without it: {msg}')
    for pr, msg in results:
        print(f'    {json.dumps(pr)} -> {msg}')
    if valid is None:
        print('no valid probe; stopping. prefix =', json.dumps(prefix))
        break
    prefix.append(valid)
    i += 1
    if i > 60:
        break

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/w2'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f, k=1.0):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0 * k)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, origin, xdir, foot, h, axis=None, name='W', zbase=0.0, typ=None, usage=None):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (origin[0], origin[1], zbase), (0, 0, 1), (xdir[0], xdir[1], 0))
    reps = [f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb(foot), h)])]
    if axis:
        reps.append(f.shape([f.poly2(axis, close=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis'))
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(*reps), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    if typ:
        f.rel_type(typ, [w])
    if usage:
        f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (w,), usage)
    return w


def a(f):  # axis along the body's bottom face, no layer set
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (5000, 0), (5000, 300), (0, 300)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (5000, 0)])


def b(f):  # axis shorter than body
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000, axis=[(1000, 0), (4000, 0)])


def c(f):  # body centered, no axis, trapezoid (mitred ends)
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(-100, -100), (5100, -100), (4900, 100), (100, 100)], 3000)


def d(f):  # body only, BIMCraft-style 6-point mitre
    s1, s2 = base(f)

arguments.prompt:
Read /tmp/views-tools/BRIEF.md first and follow it (hard rules, base commit, how to test, how to finish).

YOUR PART (VIEWS-A): the commands `section`, `elevation`, `sheet`, `place`, `crop`, `duplicate_view`, in your files `src/views/sections.rs` (section, elevation), `src/views/sheets.rs` (sheet, place) and `src/views/plans.rs` (crop, duplicate_view). Implement each file's `run`, `check` (the model rules for sections, elevations, sheets, viewports, plan views and crops, e.g. "section 100003: another view is already named `S`") and `element_view` (what `elements` shows of sections, elevations, sheets, viewports, plan views beyond their saved fields). Other sub-agents do, in parallel: graphics/scale/detail/visual_style/filter/template; the 3D view commands, dimension_3d and spots; dimensions; text/tag/linework; detail lines; regions and groups. Don't do theirs.

Observed so far (verify; there's much more to find):
- `section {"start":[0,0],"end":[5000,0]}` → `{"id":100002,"name":"Section 1"}`; saved `{"guid","category":"section","name":"Section 1","start":[0.0,0.0],"end":[5000.0,0.0],"depth":null}`; `elements` adds `length` and `looking` ([0.0,1.0] for one drawn west to east). Names by project language: Section, Corte (pt), Sección (es), Sektion (sv), Řez (cs), Coupe (fr), Doorsnede (nl), Schnitt (de), Sezione (it). A name a level has: "a view is named `Level 1`, as a level is; name it otherwise" (no command prefix). Two views of one name: "section 100003: another view is already named `S`" (model check). A section may be named `{3D}`.
- `elevation {}` around a closed 10000 x 6000 box of Generic - 200mm walls (faces -100..10100 by -100..6100) makes four: North start [11100,9100] end [-1100,9100], South [-1100,-3100]→[11100,-3100], East [13100,-1100]→[13100,7100], West [-3100,7100]→[-3100,-1100] (3 m out, 1 m past the sides), each saved `{"guid","category":"elevation","name":"North","start","end","depth":null}`, reply `{"ids":[…]}`. With no walls or floors: "elevation: there are no walls or floors to look at; draw some, or give `start` and `end`". Probe `facing`, `at`, `start`/`end`, `depth`, `name`, "the four not there yet", languages, floors only, curved walls, other elements.
- `sheet {}` → `{"id":…,"number":"A101"}`, saved `{"guid","category":"sheet","number":"A101","name":"Unnamed","size":"A3"}`; `elements` adds `"paper":[420.0,297.0]` and `"viewports":[ids]`.
- `place {"sheet":"A101","view":"Level 1"}` (box of walls) → `{"at":[215.0,168.5],"id":…}`, saved viewport `{"guid","category":"viewport","sheet":<sheet guid>,"view":<view guid>,"at":[215.0,168.5],"scale":100.0}`; then a 10 m section → at [324.6,249.0]; on an A1 sheet `{3D}` → [425.5,317.0], then `Room Schedule` → [551.8,317.0]. Placing `{3D}` makes `{"guid","category":"view3d","name":"{3D}","azimuth":-45.0,"elevation":30.0}` (`common::ensure_default_3d`; `azimuth`/`elevation` params) and a schedule name makes `{"guid","category":"schedule","name":"Room Schedule","of":"room"}` (the `schedule` command is READERS' area; make the element as the original does when placed). `elements` shows a viewport's `size` ([160.8,66.0] for that 10 m section at 1:100) and `title`. The sizes and default places come from what each view shows (its extents on paper, its title?): find out how, for plans, sections, elevations, schedules (rows and columns) and the 3D view; and `scale`, the view's own scale (graphics.scale, set by the `scale` command another sub-agent writes: just read `graphics.scale` of the view), "a view goes on one sheet", errors ("place: no sheet numbered `A101`", …).
- `crop {"view":"Level 1"}` on that box (with the four elevations? check) → `{"crop":[[-2100.0,-1100.0],[12100.0,10100.0]],"view":100000}`; on a section → `{"crop":[-600.0,3600.0],"view":…}` (find out what that is); "crop: {3D} isn't a plan, a section or an elevation; only those crop", "crop: sheet A101 isn't a plan, a section or an elevation; only those crop"; `region`, `null` (uncrop), notes staying put.
- `duplicate_view {"view":"Level 1","name":"X"}` → `{"annotations":0,"id":…,"level":100000,"name":"X"}`; "duplicate_view: S1 isn't a plan: plans are duplicated, sections, elevations, schedules, sheets and the 3D view not yet"; "planview 100002: a level is already named `Level 2`; a plan view of it needs another name"; default names `<view> Copy 1`, `<view> Dependent 1` (languages?). `detailing` copies the plan's dimensions, tags, notes and spot elevations as its own (other sub-agents make those elements; build inputs with the original and copy their JSON with the view references changed, exactly as the original saves the copies); `dependent` follows its parent (`parent`).
- Views are found by `common::find_view` (check it against the original for your commands: names, ids, GUIDs, `{3D}`, sheets by number).

Also write in plans.rs `pub fn dependents(pr: &Project, gone: &std::collections::BTreeSet<u64>) -> Vec<u64>`: what else goes when these elements are deleted, as the original's `delete` takes it (the annotation in a deleted view: notes, detail lines, dimensions, tags, spots, regions, groups; a deleted plan's dependent plan views; viewports of a deleted view or sheet; a level's plan views; …). Probe `delete {"ids":[…]}` on the original to learn it (its reply lists what it deleted). Our `delete` is EDIT's and will call this.

YOUR PART (GRAPHICS): the commands `graphics`, `scale`, `detail`, `visual_style` (in `src/views/graphics.rs`), `filter` (in `src/views/filters.rs`, with `inspect_entries` for the project's view filters) and `template` (in `src/views/templates.rs`, with `inspect_entries` for the view templates). Implement each file's `run` and `check` (the model rules for a view's graphics: categories, overrides, filters applied, phases, options, layers, background grids, templates followed and what they control; the view filters and the view templates). Other sub-agents do, in parallel: section/elevation/sheet/place/crop/duplicate_view; section_box/perspective/graphic_display_options/camera/work_plane/dimension_3d/spots; dimensions; text/tag/linework; detail lines; regions and groups. Don't do theirs.

Observed so far (verify; there's much more to find):
- `graphics {}` (reads; the lowest level's plan) → `{"background_grid":{"divisions":[5,5],"main":{"color":[230,230,230],"enabled":false,"pen":0},"rotation":0.0,"spacing":[1000.0,1000.0],"sub":{"color":[245,245,245],"enabled":false,"pen":0},"visible":true},"categories":{},"controlled":[],"detail":"fine","elements":{},"filters":[],"hidden":[],"hidden_elements":[],"layers":{},"name":"Level 1","options":{},"phase":null,"phase_filter":null,"scale":null,"template":null,"view":100000,"visual_style":"shaded"}`. On `{3D}` before it exists, the same with `"name":"{3D}","view":null` (reading makes nothing); a change makes it (`common::ensure_default_3d`). Sections and elevations take graphics too.
- After `graphics {"hide":["walls"],"categories":{"doors":{"halftone":true}}}`, `filter {"name":"F1","categories":["walls"]}` (→ `{"categories":["wall"],"matches":[100002,100003,100004,100005],"name":"F1","rules":[]}`), `graphics {"filters":[{"filter":"F1","halftone":true}]}`, `scale {"view":"Level 1","scale":50}` (→ `{"name":"Level 1","scale":50.0,"view":100000}`) and `detail {"view":"Level 1","detail":"coarse"}` (→ `{"detail":"coarse","name":"Level 1","view":100000}`), the level is saved with `"graphics":{"categories":{"door":{"halftone":true},"wall":{"hidden":true}},"filters":[{"filter":<view-filter guid>,"halftone":true}],"scale":50.0,"detail":"coarse"}` after its `view_range`, and the project with `"view_filters":{"F1":{"categories":["wall"]}}` and a library entry `{"kind":"view-filter","name":"F1","guid"}`. `scale {}` reads `{"name":"Level 1","scale":100.0,"view":100000}`. The 3D view's style is saved `"graphics":{"style":"wireframe"}`.
- `template {"name":"T1","from":"Level 1"}` → `{"background_grid":{…},"categories":{"door":{"halftone":true},"wall":{"hidden":true}},"controls":["categories","filters","range","phase","options","scale","detail","style","background_grid"],"detail":"fine","filters":[{"filter":"F1","halftone":true}],"hidden":["wall"],"kind":"plan","layers":{},"name":"T1","options":{},"phase":null,"phase_filter":null,"scale":null,"view_range":{"bottom":0.0,"cut":1200.0,"depth":0.0,"top":null},"views":[],"visual_style":"shaded"}`; saved in `view_templates` as `"T1":{"kind":"plan","controls":[…],"graphics":{"categories":{…},"filters":[{"filter":<guid>,"halftone":true}]},"view_range":{"top":null,"cut":1200.0,"bottom":0.0,"depth":0.0}}` with a `view-template` library entry. A new project has three (Electrical Ceiling, Electrical Lighting, Electrical Power: `{"kind":"plan","controls":["categories"],"graphics":{"categories":{…}}}`).
- Errors seen: "graphics: Room Schedule isn't a plan, a section, an elevation or a 3D view", "graphics: wall 100002 isn't a plan, a section, an elevation or a 3D view", "graphics: no view named `A101`" (sheets aren't found by number here), "graphics: `view`: 12345 is not a view", "scale: {3D} isn't a plan, a section or an elevation; only those have one", "detail: {3D} isn't …", "visual_style: Level 1 isn't a 3D view; only those have a visual style", "filter: a new filter needs `categories`, [\"walls\", \"doors\"…]", "template: there's no view template `x`; make one with `from` (a view), or `controls` (there are: Electrical Ceiling, Electrical Lighting, Electrical Power)". `graphics {"foo":1}` is NOT refused.
- `inspect` lists `view_filters` and `view_templates` with names where the file has GUIDs: implement `inspect_entries` in filters.rs and templates.rs.
- `phase`, `phase_filter`, `options` (design options) in graphics and templates are the styles agent's phases (`crate::styles::phasing`: `check_view_graphics`, names ↔ GUIDs of `phase`, `phase-filter`, `option-set`, `design-option` library entries); fill patterns of foreground/background overrides are styles' `fill_patterns`. Read `src/styles/phasing.rs` for how they're kept and checked (it already checks a view's or a template's `graphics.phase`/`phase_filter`/`options` in the model check).
- A filter's `matches` and its `rules` are a schedule filter's (the fields of the category's schedule; ops equals… has-no-value): READERS writes schedules in parallel; write the stand-in you need (fields and values for each category: probe the original's `schedule` command, e.g. `schedule {"category":"wall"}` and its `available` fields).
- A dependent plan view (a `planview` with `parent`, made by `duplicate_view {"mode":"dependent"}`) refuses graphics/scale/detail naming its parent; a view following a template refuses what the template controls; `template` with `rename`, `like`, `kind`, `controls`, `view_range`, `delete`, `reset`, and views following it (`views` in the reply; `controlled` in graphics). `visual_style` on the 3D view and camera views. Category names "in any case, singular or plural" (walls → wall), subcategories (roomreference, roomseparator), family component categories (furniture, casework, plumbing… see the docs), `layers` of CAD drawings, `background_grid`.

arguments.description: DIMS: dimensions, constraints, text, value
arguments.prompt:
Read /tmp/views-tools/BRIEF.md first and follow it (hard rules, base commit, how to test, how to finish).

YOUR PART (DIMS): the commands `dimension` (in `src/views/dims.rs`, with the `dimension` element's `element_view` and `check`) and `dimension_constraint`, `dimension_text`, `dimension_value` (in `src/views/constraints.rs`, which also has `keep(pr)`: run after every command that changes the model, before the check, already wired into `Session::execute` through `crate::views::keep`; it solves each constrained dimension and moves what it measures to, or refuses the command saying which dimension can't be kept). Other sub-agents do, in parallel: views, sheets, crops; 3D views, dimension_3d, spots; graphics, filters, templates; text/tag/linework; detail lines; regions and groups. Don't do theirs.

Observed so far (verify; there's much more to find):
- On a closed 10000 x 6000 box of Generic - 200mm walls (ids 100002 south, 100003 east, 100004 north, 100005 west), `dimension {"refs":[{"id":100005},{"id":100003}],"at":[5000,3000]}` → `{"id":100008,"values":[10000.0]}`, saved `{"guid","category":"dimension","level":<level guid>,"kind":"aligned","refs":[{"id":<wall guid>,"face":"centre"},{"id":<wall guid>,"face":"centre"}],"at":[5000.0,3000.0],"type":<dimension-type guid>}`; `elements` adds `"labels":["10000"]`, `"values":[10000.0]` and `"type":"Diagonal - 2.5mm Arial"` (by name; `elements` is READERS' and calls our `element_view`).
- Faces: an Exterior - 300mm wall (layers exterior first: finish 100, thermal 50, structure 140, finish 10) drawn west→east at y=0, with refs right, left, centre and a grid at y=1000, measures [150,150,X] (refs sorted south to north): X = 850 (location centre), 1000 (exterior-finish: the exterior face is the LEFT one), 700 (interior-finish), 780 (core-centre), 850 (exterior-core), 710 (interior-core). `centre` is the wall's centre line, not its location line. `src/views/model.rs` has these (thickness, core, centre line, faces, arc walls).
- "dimension 100002: a dimension measures between 2 to 10000 references" (model check after the command; `dimension {"refs":[],…,"foo":1}` isn't refused for `foo`). "dimension: no level or plan view named `Nope` (the levels are: Level 1, Level 2)" (`crate::model::level_param`).
- A door is saved `{"guid","category":"door","type":<guid>,"host":<wall guid>,"offset":2000.0,"sill":0.0,"mark":"1","flip_facing":false,"flip_hand":false}` (`offset` of its middle along its wall from the wall's start, its width from `types.door[<type name>].width`; windows alike); a grid `{"guid","category":"grid","name","start","end"}`; a detail line `{"guid","category":"line","view":<view guid>,"style":<guid>,"start","end"}` (or `points`+`arcs`+`closed`, `start`+`end`+`arc`, `centre`+`radius` (a circle), `centre`+`radii`+`angle`+`span`, `control`, `fit`); a round column `{"category":"column","type":…,"at",…}` of a type with `"round":true`; a curved wall has `"arc": degrees`.
- Refs (see `/workspace/executable commands` for `dimension`, and the Dimensions section of `/workspace/docs/areas/views-and-graphics.md`): wall centre/left/right/start/end, door/window centre and jambs, grids, straight detail lines and their ends, `point: start|end` (a face's end where the outline turns off it: at the mitred corner of joined walls — so you need how walls join at corners: probe), points [x, y] on those lines, `{endpoint: [x, y]}` (within 100 mm); kinds aligned, linear (`orient`), angular, radial, diameter, arc_length; `type`; `prefix`, `suffix`, `above`, `below`, `replace`, `equality` (README's table); the reply's `values`; what the model check refuses (lines not parallel, not square to a linear one's line, points all in one place, references that went away); its `labels` as the dimension type's units/rounding say (units are styles' `units` command).
- dimension_text (segment texts), dimension_constraint (`equal`, `locked` segments; keep after every command), dimension_value (moves what the segment ends at along the dimension: walls, grids, doors/windows along their wall, detail lines — write those moves yourself in your files, as the original's `move` would move them, and learn what it saves).
- Walls, doors, grids are made by other areas (ARCH, the core's `grid` works in our binary); build inputs with the original.

arguments.prompt:

arguments.description: GROUPS: regions, groups, make_fill_pattern
arguments.prompt:
Read /tmp/views-tools/BRIEF.md first and follow it (hard rules, base commit, how to test, how to finish).

YOUR PART (GROUPS): the commands `filled_region` (in `src/views/regions.rs`, with the `region` element's `check` and `element_view`), `create_group`, `detail_group`, `repeating_detail`, `ungroup`, `group_type` (in `src/views/groups.rs`, with the `detail_groups` section, the `detailgroup`/`repeatingdetail` elements' `check` and `element_view`, and `inspect_entries`) and `make_fill_pattern` (in `src/views/makepat.rs`). Other sub-agents do, in parallel: views, sheets; 3D views, spots; graphics, filters, templates; dimensions; text/tag/linework; detail lines (`detail_line` and its edits, and the curve model in `src/views/curves.rs`). Don't do theirs.

Observed so far (verify; there's much more to find):
- `filled_region {"sketch":[[[0,0],[1000,0]],[[1000,0],[1000,1000]],[[1000,1000],[0,1000]],[[0,1000],[0,0]]]}` → `{"area_m2":1.0,"id":100012}`, saved `{"guid","category":"region","view":<level guid>,"type":<filled-region-type guid, Solid Black>,"line_style":<line-style guid, Thin Lines>,"sketch":[{"id":999467,"guid":…,"start":[0.0,0.0],"end":[1000.0,0.0]},…]}` (the sketch lines are parts, their ids from `Project::alloc_lib_id`, counting down below every id the project's parts and library use). Empty sketch: "filled_region: the sketch doesn't close into loops: there are no lines: draw the outline". The sketch solver (loops, holes, islands, arcs as 3 points, the problems it reports) is the same as ARCH's `sketch` command's (`/workspace/executable commands` describes `sketch`; ARCH writes it in parallel): write the stand-in you need. `type`, `line_style` (null: invisible), views (plans, sections, elevations, sheets), `pattern_origin`/`pattern_angle`, masking.
- After two detail lines (100002 a polyline `[[0,0],[1000,0],[1000,1000]]` with `arcs` `[0,90]`, 100003 a circle centre [0,0] radius 500), `create_group {"ids":[100002,100003]}` → `{"id":100011,"name":"Group 1"}`: the lines leave the elements, `detail_groups` holds `{"Group 1":{"members":[{"id":999466,"guid":…,"element":{"category":"line","view":0,"style":<guid>,"points":[[-353.553,-250.0],[646.447,-250.0],[646.447,750.0]],"arcs":[0.0,90.0]}},{"id":999465,"guid":…,"element":{"category":"line","view":0,"style":<guid>,"centre":[-353.553,-250.0],"radius":500.0}}]}}` (members about the middle of their bounds — the arc's bulge counts — rounded to the micron), a `{"kind":"detail-group","name":"Group 1","guid"}` library entry, and the element `{"guid","category":"detailgroup","view":<level guid>,"type":<detail-group guid>,"at":[353.553,250.0]}` in their place. `detail_group {"type":"Group 1","at":[5000,5000]}` → `{"id":…}`; `repeating_detail {"type":"Group 1","start":[0,0],"end":[10000,0],"spacing":2000}` → `{"count":6,"id":…}`, saved `{"guid","category":"repeatingdetail","view":<guid>,"type":<guid>,"start":[0.0,0.0],"end":[10000.0,0.0],"spacing":2000.0}`; `group_type {}` → `{"groups":{"Group 1":{"members":2,"placed":3}}}`. Errors: "group_type: `foo` isn't one of its parameters: name, rename, delete", "create_group: `ids`: the detail lines, filled regions and text notes to group", "detail_group: there's no detail group `x` (there are: )". Text notes in groups (a note is `{"guid","category":"text","view","at","text","type","angle"}`), regions in groups, angle/mirrored, ungroup's reply `{ids}`, the 10,000 members-a-view cap and 2,000 repeats, renames and deletes, `inspect`'s `detail_groups` (if it lists them).
- Detail lines' curves (polylines with arcs, circles, ellipses with `radii`/`angle`/`span`, splines by `control` (+`knots`) or `fit` points) are being modelled in parallel by the LINES sub-agent in `src/views/curves.rs`: write what you need of them (bounds, moves, turns, mirrors of their fields; the points a curve is drawn with, for make_fill_pattern) in your own files; we'll unify later.
- make_fill_pattern: pyRevit's Make Pattern, described in the command's spec and in `/workspace/docs/areas/views-and-graphics.md` (the "custom pattern is made of lines drawn" paragraph); it writes a fill pattern as the styles agent's `fill_pattern` keeps one (`fill_patterns` section + `fill-pattern` library entry; see `src/styles/fills.rs`).

steps.message:
Read /tmp/views-tools/BRIEF.md first and follow it (hard rules, base commit, how to test, how to finish).

YOUR PART (VIEWS-A): the commands `section`, `elevation`, `sheet`, `place`, `crop`, `duplicate_view`, in your files `src/views/sections.rs` (section, elevation), `src/views/sheets.rs` (sheet, place) and `src/views/plans.rs` (crop, duplicate_view). Implement each file's `run`, `check` (the model rules for sections, elevations, sheets, viewports, plan views and crops, e.g. "section 100003: another view is already named `S`") and `element_view` (what `elements` shows of sections, elevations, sheets, viewports, plan views beyond their saved fields). Other sub-agents do, in parallel: graphics/scale/detail/visual_style/filter/template; the 3D view commands, dimension_3d and spots; dimensions; text/tag/linework; detail lines; regions and groups. Don't do theirs.

Observed so far (verify; there's much more to find):
- `section {"start":[0,0],"end":[5000,0]}` → `{"id":100002,"name":"Section 1"}`; saved `{"guid","category":"section","name":"Section 1","start":[0.0,0.0],"end":[5000.0,0.0],"depth":null}`; `elements` adds `length` and `looking` ([0.0,1.0] for one drawn west to east). Names by project language: Section, Corte (pt), Sección (es), Sektion (sv), Řez (cs), Coupe (fr), Doorsnede (nl), Schnitt (de), Sezione (it). A name a level has: "a view is named `Level 1`, as a level is; name it otherwise" (no command prefix). Two views of one name: "section 100003: another view is already named `S`" (model check). A section may be named `{3D}`.
