results.content:
## duplicate_view | Duplicate View
{view, mode?: duplicate|detailing|dependent, name?} a new plan view of a plan's level (a level's own plan, or a plan view; sections, elevations, schedules, sheets and the 3D view aren't duplicated yet): `duplicate` (the default) has the same view range, crop and graphics and no annotation of its own; `detailing` copies the dimensions, tags, notes and spot elevations in it too, as its own; `dependent` follows its parent's view range, graphics, scale and detail (change those in the parent), has a crop of its own and shows its parent's annotation as well as its own. Named `name`, else `<view> Copy 1` (`<view> Dependent 1`). Commands that take a level or a view take it by name or id, and what is drawn, dimensioned, tagged or noted there is in it
## camera | Camera
{eye?: [x, y, z], target?: [x, y, z], lens?: mm, view?: a 3D view's name or id, name?} a 3D camera as Revit's Camera tool makes one: with `eye` (where the camera stands, mm) and `target` (what it looks at, mm) it makes a new named perspective 3D view looking from `eye` at `target` through `lens` (35 mm unless given, 10 to 600), named `name` or by number ("Camera 1", "Camera 2"…). With `view` too, it gives that 3D view the camera instead (its id stays; `{3D}` may be given one): a point left out stays as that camera has it, so `lens` alone or one point alone changes just that, and a view without a camera yet needs both. With `view` and none of `eye`, `target` or `lens` it reads the camera back: `eye`, `target`, `lens` and whether the view is in perspective (null eye/target for a view with no camera yet). The eye is never on the target, so the view always has a direction to look in
## schedule | Schedule
{name?, category?, categories?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?, path?} a schedule view, as Revit's View > Schedules makes one, and its table: columns, rows, the `elements` each row lists, and totals (and a .csv file with a path, or an .xlsx workbook for a path ending .xlsx). A new one needs `name` and `category`: rooms, doors, windows, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, columns, structural columns, footings, beams, strip footings, components, stairs, ramps, railings or levels, or `multicategory`, as Revit's Multi-Category Schedule: a row for each element of `categories` (["walls", "doors"…]; none, every built one but rooms, levels and masses), with the fields they share (Category, Family, Type, Level, Count, Width, Height, Length, Thickness, Area: a wall's length by its height, a door's width by its height; Material: its type's structure layer's, a run's type's, a family's), each empty 
## filled_region | Filled Region
{sketch: [[[x,y],[x,y]],…], view?, type?, line_style?: name | null} a filled region in a view (a plan, a section, an elevation or a sheet, in its own terms; the lowest plan by default): the loops its sketch closes into (see `sketch`: any number of outlines, a loop inside one a hole, one inside that an island), filled as type `type` (Solid Black unless told) says, its boundary in line style `line_style` (Thin Lines unless told; null, unseen: a masking region's way). It draws over the model, under the annotation; edit its sketch with edit_boundary. A model pattern starts at the region's `pattern_origin` and turns by its `pattern_angle` (see modify)
## create_group | Create Group
{ids, name?} a detail group made of detail lines, filled regions and text notes of one view, as Revit's Create Group: they become type `name`'s members (Group 1, 2… unless told), and one group of it takes their place, its origin the middle of them. Place it again with detail_group; ungroup gives its members back. Returns {id, name}
## detail_group | Place Detail Group
{type, at: [x,y], angle?, mirrored?, view?} a detail group of type `type` placed in a view (the lowest plan by default): its members drawn with their origin at `at`, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise, mirrored across their x axis first when `mirrored`. Move, copy, rotate and mirror take it whole
## repeating_detail | Repeating Detail
{type, start: [x,y], end: [x,y], spacing, mirrored?, view?} detail group `type` repeated along the line from `start` to `end`, every `spacing` mm from `start` (at most 2000 of them), each turned along the line, as Revit's Repeating Detail Component: brick coursing, blocking, batt ties. A view draws up to 10000 group members in all (a repeat places each member of the type again), so a type of 100 members repeats up to 100 times. Returns {id, count}
## place | Place View
{sheet: number or id, view: a level's, section's, elevation's, schedule's or 3D view's name or id, at?: [x, y], scale?, azimuth?, elevation?} puts the view on the sheet at 1 : `scale` (by default the view's own, see `scale`, 1 : 100 when it has none of its own; a schedule keeps its size), its middle `at` mm from the paper's bottom left corner (by default right of the views there, or in the middle); a view goes on one sheet. A schedule (Room Schedule, Door Schedule…) or the 3D view ({3D}, seen from `azimuth` and `elevation` degrees) comes to be as it's first placed
## rebar | Rebar
{points: [[x,y,z],…], diameter, host?, grade?, layer?, closed?, count?, step?, level?} a reinforcing bar bent along `points` (mm; z over the level), `diameter` mm thick (3 to 100), of steel `grade` (CA-50 unless told). `host` is the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces (the level is then its level) and it goes with; `closed` joins the last point to the first, a hoop. With `count` bars (up to 1000), each is `step` [dx,dy,dz] from the last: a layer of bars, or hoops along a beam. Returns their ids. Its schedule lists Grade, Diameter, Length and Weight (kg, of steel at 7850 kg/m³), and a grouped one is a bar schedule
## reinforce | Reinforce
{host | hosts: [id, …], preset?, cover?, grade?, grade_stirrup?, clearance?, …} bars by rules for a beam, a column, a footing or a floor: the engineer says how many, how thick and how far apart (no standard's number sets them) and it lays them inside the cover and checks that they fit, saying what to change. All: `cover` (mm: one number, or {top, bottom, sides}, top and bottom the faces of a beam, a footing or a floor and the ends of a column; else the host's Cobrimento or ConcreteCover parameter), `grade` (CA-50), `grade_stirrup` (the stirrups' and ties'), `clearance` (least mm between bars; their thickness, at least 20, unless told). A spacing is the most between bars: they are spread evenly, so the last is where the first is from the other end. Beam: `bottom` and `top` {count, diameter, hook?} (`hook`, the straight leg in mm turned up from the bottom bars and down from the top ones at
## dormer | Dormer
{host, at: [x, y], width?, height?, slope?, window?, type?} a dormer on roof `host`, its front wall across the slope through `at`: walls of `type` `width` mm (1600) apart, standing on the roof and `height` mm (1200) tall at the front, under a gable roof of its own sloping `slope` degrees (30) that runs back into the host; the host open under it, and with `window` (a window type) a window in its front. Replies with its roof, walls and window
## duct | Duct
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a duct for each segment of the points: its section the type's (category duct: `width` across by `depth` deep, or round, `width` the diameter), its `justify` line (centre by default) `offset` mm over the level at its start (0: at the level) and `end_offset` at its end (the same: level), for a single segment; the same point twice and two heights make one stand upright. `system` names the system it belongs to ("Supply air", "Exhaust")
## conduit | Conduit
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a conduit (eletroduto) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` its outside diameter; `system` names its circuit
## cable_tray | Cable Tray
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a cable tray (eletrocalha) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: its section the type's `width` across by `depth` deep
## wire | Wire
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a wire (condutor) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` its outside diameter; `system` names its circuit
## down_conductor | Down Conductor
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} a down conductor (condutor de descida, NBR 5419) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, or a flat strip; the same point twice and two heights make one stand upright down a wall; `system` names the protection system it belongs to
## ground_conductor | Earthing Conductor
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} an earthing conductor (condutor de aterramento, the ring or mesh of NBR 5419) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them, usually under the level (a negative `offset`)
## cabling | Cabling
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, offset?, end_offset?, justify?: top|centre|bottom, system?} structured cabling (cabeamento estruturado, NBR 14565) for each segment of the points, as `pipe` lays them: round, `width` the cable's outside diameter; `system` names the link or the network it belongs to
## link | Link Model
{path, name?, at?: [x, y], angle?: degrees} another project (.bimcraft or .ifc) shown in this one as a reference that can't be edited, as Revit's Link Revit: its walls, floors, roofs, columns, stairs and the rest of what it builds are drawn in the plans, sections and 3D views, halftone, and snapped to; nothing of it is selected, scheduled, checked or exported. It stands with its origin at `at` (default [0, 0]) turned `angle` about it; its levels stand at their own elevations, on this project's levels at the same height. `path` is read now and again by `reload`, and kept as given: a relative one is relative to this project's file. `name` defaults to the file's. Returns `id`, `name`, `elements`
## point_cloud | Point Cloud
{path | cloud, name?, level?, at?: [x, y], offset?, angle?, units?, spacing?, origin?} brings in a laser scan (`path`: PTS, XYZ, PLY, LAS or E57 (each of its scans placed by its pose), or a list of the files of one scan's stations, brought in as one; `units` of its coordinates mm, cm, m (the default), in or ft; one point kept in each cube `spacing` mm wide) or places one the project holds again (`cloud`, its name), as an element: its middle on `at` (the origin) and its foot on the level, or with `origin: file` where its file's coordinates put it; `offset` raises its middle over the level, `angle` turns it. Returns its id, the scan's name, the points kept and read, and where its middle was in the file
## import_cad | Import CAD
{path | cad, name?, level?, view?, at?: [x, y], position?, units?, scale?, angle?, layers?, colors?, link?} brings in a DXF drawing (`path`: an ASCII DXF of any version, or a DWG, which the desktop and the command line read as DXF) or places one the project holds again (`cad`, its name), as an element in every plan of `level`, or with `view` (a plan) in that view only. `units` of the drawing: auto (the default: what its file says, else mm), mm, cm, m, in or ft; or `scale`, mm to each of its units. `position`: center (the default: the middle of the drawing on `at`, the origin unless given) or origin (its origin on `at`); `angle` turns it about `at`, degrees. `layers`: visible (the default: those its file has on and thawed), all, or a list of those to show. `colors`: preserve (the default), invert or black. `link: true` remembers the file, so `reload_cad` and opening the project read it ag

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/lv'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def st(f, name, elev, z, agg=True):
    lp = f.lp(f.bld_lp, (0, 0, z))
    s = f.add('IFCBUILDINGSTOREY', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, None, None, E('ELEMENT'), elev)
    if agg:
        f.storeys.append(s)
    s.lp = lp
    return s


def a(f):  # elevation attr vs placement
    st(f, 'A', 1000.0, 2000.0)
    st(f, 'B', None, 5000.0)
    f.close_storeys()


def b(f):  # duplicate names
    st(f, 'X', 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, 'X', 3000.0, 3000.0)
    st(f, 'X', 6000.0, 6000.0)
    f.close_storeys()


def c(f):  # same elevation
    st(f, 'B', 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, 'A', 0.0, 0.0)
    f.close_storeys()


def d(f):  # no name
    st(f, None, 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, '', 3000.0, 3000.0)
    st(f, '  ', 6000.0, 6000.0)
    f.close_storeys()


def e(f):  # storey not aggregated
    st(f, 'Agg', 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, 'Loose', 3000.0, 3000.0, agg=False)
    f.close_storeys()


def g(f):  # building placed high
    f.lines = [l for l in f.lines]
    st(f, 'L1', 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, 'L2', 3000.0, 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()


def h(f):  # elevation in metres file
    st(f, 'L1', 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, 'L2', 3.5, 3.5)
    f.close_storeys()


def i(f):  # name trimmed?
    st(f, ' Spaced ', 0.0, 0.0)
    f.close_storeys()


def j(f):  # elevation only by placement z, attr $
    st(f, 'P', None, 1234.5)
    f.close_storeys()


def k(f):  # Name 'Level 1' duplicate with suffix collision
    st(f, 'X', 0.0, 0.0)
    st(f, 'X (2)', 1000.0, 1000.0)
    st(f, 'X', 3000.0, 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()


mk('a_attr_vs_place', a)
mk('b_dupnames', b)
mk('c_sameelev', c)
mk('d_noname', d)
mk('e_loose', e)
mk('h_metres', h, units='m')
mk('i_spaced', i)
mk('j_placeonly', j)
mk('k_dupsuffix', k)
print(' '.join(out))

results.content:
## dimension_3d | Aligned Dimension in 3D
{refs: [ref, ref], at: [x, y, z], view?, type?} an aligned dimension in a 3D view (the default 3D view unless `view` names another, by name or id), kept by the view and drawn in it and on a sheet that holds it: how far apart its two references are, along a line through `at` moved square off them. A ref is {at: [x, y, z]}, a point of the model, or {at, edge: [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]]}, a point on an edge, which it measures square to (from a point, to the edge's line; between two parallel edges, how far apart they are). `type` is a dimension type, the aligned one's unless told. On the desktop, Aligned Dimension (DI) in the 3D view runs it. Returns its id and its length
## spot_slope | Spot Slope
{at: [x, y], view?, host?} a spot slope in a level's plan (the lowest by default): how steeply the top of the floor or roof at `at` (or `host`) falls there, %, an arrow pointing downhill; it follows the top. The reply gives `slope` and `toward`, the way down in plan (null on the level)

import sys

from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/w3'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f, k=1.0):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0 * k)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, origin, xdir, foot, h, axis=None, name='W', zbase=0.0, cls='IFCWALL', body=None):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (origin[0], origin[1], zbase), (0, 0, 1), (xdir[0], xdir[1], 0))
    reps = [body if body else f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb(foot), h)])]
    if axis:
        reps.append(f.shape([f.poly2(axis, close=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis'))
    w = f.add(cls, gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(*reps), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w


def rot(pts, deg, c=(0, 0)):
    a = math.radians(deg)
    ca, sa = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
    return [(c[0] + (x - c[0]) * ca - (y - c[1]) * sa, c[1] + (x - c[0]) * sa + (y - c[1]) * ca) for x, y in pts]


def a(f):  # body rotated 30deg inside an axis-aligned placement
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), rot([(0, -100), (4000, -100), (4000, 100), (0, 100)], 30), 3000)


def b(f):  # body rotated 90deg (along y) inside an x placement
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(-100, 0), (100, 0), (100, 4000), (-100, 4000)], 3000)


def c(f):  # square footprint
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (1000, 0), (1000, 1000), (0, 1000)], 3000)


def d(f):  # thicker than long (200 long x 3000 thick along x placement)
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -1500), (200, -1500), (200, 1500), (0, 1500)], 3000)


def e(f):  # placement pointing -x
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (5000, 0), (-1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000)


def g(f):  # extrusion along x (profile vertical), like some exporters
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    prof = f.rect(200, 3000, (0, 1500))
    pos = f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(prof, 5000, pos)])
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), None, None, body=body)


def h(f):  # body rotated 30deg, axis given along it
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    pts = rot([(0, -100), (4000, -100), (4000, 100), (0, 100)], 30)
    ax = rot([(0, 0), (4000, 0)], 30)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), pts, 3000, axis=ax)


def i(f):  # body rotated 45 with placement rotated -45 (net along x)
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    c, s = math.cos(math.radians(-45)), math.sin(math.radians(-45))
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (c, s), rot([(0, -100), (4000, -100), (4000, 100), (0, 100)], 45), 3000)


def j(f):  # brep box rotated 30 in plan
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    pts = rot([(0, -100), (4000, -100), (4000, 100), (0, 100)], 30)
    P = [(x, y, 0) for x, y in pts] + [(x, y, 3000) for x, y in pts]
    faces = [(0, 3, 2, 1), (4, 5, 6, 7), (0, 1, 5, 4), (1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 0, 4, 7)]
    body = f.shape([f.brep(P, faces)], 'Brep')
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), None, None, body=body)


def k(f):  # parallelogram footprint (skewed ends)
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (4000, -100), (4300, 100), (300, 100)], 3000)


mk('a_rot30_body', a)
mk('b_body_y', b)
mk('c_square', c)
mk('d_thick', d)
mk('e_negx', e)
mk('g_ext_x', g)
mk('h_rot30_axis', h)
mk('i_net_x', i)
mk('j_brep_rot', j)
mk('k_parallelogram', k)
print(' '.join(out))

{mass?, type?, prune?} a floor of the footprint at each level the mass crosses, from the one at its base up to, not including, the one at its top; every mass when no `mass`. The floors it makes hold their mass and level (`Mass Floor`), so a second run makes no second floor: it gives the ones there the mass's footprint now (and the `type` if given), and lists in `stale` those on a level the mass no longer crosses, which `prune` deletes. The reply has `ids` (every floor of the mass), `made`, `updated`, `stale` and `removed`. `schedule {category: massfloors}` lists each mass's floor area and volu
## wall_by_face | Wall by Face
{mass, faces?: [edge, …], type?, location?} a wall on each edge of the mass's footprint (numbered from its first point), or the `faces` given, as tall as the mass; its exterior finish on the edge, facing out (`location` changes that line). Ordinary walls from then on
## tag | Tag by Category
{ids?: [id,…], label?, level?, category?, offset?: [dx, dy], leader?} tags elements with a field of theirs: a door's or window's mark, a room's name, else the type, or `label`, any field its category's schedule has (`Height`, `Area`, a project parameter); doors, windows, walls, columns, components, floors, ceilings, roofs, rooms, runs and stairs. `offset` mm from the point it names (beside the wall for a door or window, else up and right); without ids, every door and window on the level not tagged yet, or of `category`
## elevation | Elevation
{facing?: north|south|east|west, at?: [x,y], start?, end?, depth?, name?} an elevation view of the building's side `facing` (North shows the north side, looking south), from 3 m out, or through `at`; with `at` alone, of the side it's on; with `start` and `end`, along that line, looking to its left; with none, the four not there yet
## section | Section
{start: [x,y], end: [x,y], depth?, name?} a section view along the line, looking to its left (drawn west to east, it looks north): it cuts the model at the line and sees `depth` mm past it, or everything
## sheet | Sheet
{number?, name?, size?: A0|A1|A2|A3|A4} a sheet of paper, landscape (A3 by default), with a title block; numbers run A101, A102…
## text | Text
{text, at: [x, y], view?, type?, angle?, leader?: [x, y], override_format?, runs?: [{from, to, bold?, italic?, underline?}, …]} a text note, its first line's top left at `at`, in a view by name or id: a level's plan (the lowest by default; `at` in plan mm), a section or an elevation (`at` along its line from its start, and up), or a sheet by number (`at` in paper mm). Lettered as its text `type` says (2.5mm unless told; `text_type` lists and makes them: its font, its size, its border), turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise; with `leader`, a line to that point. Lines break at \n. With `overr
## dimension | Aligned Dimension
{refs: [ref, …], at: [x, y], level?, kind?: aligned|linear|angular|radial|diameter|arc_length, orient?: horizontal|vertical} aligned (the default): the distances between parallel references, along a line through `at` (between points, along the first two; points and lines, square to the lines); linear: the same with its line horizontal or vertical as `orient` says, or without one as `at` lies: east or west of the points, vertical, else horizontal (its lines must run square to it); angular: the angle between two references that meet, on the side of `at`; radial: a round column's, curved wall's,

## room_separator | Room Separator
{points: [[x,y],…], level?, closed?} room separation lines along `points`, one per segment (`closed` joins the last to the first): they bound rooms as walls do, to split an open space (a living room and its corridor) into rooms, and are nothing else, with no solid, no cut and no area. Returns their ids

wall | Wall | {points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, top_level?, top_offset?, height?, base_offset?, arc?, location?, attach_top?, attach_base?, room_bounding?} one wall per segment of its location line; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall (unconnected), or up to `top_level`, `top_offset` mm above it (0; negative, below it; the top must stay above the base). `arc`: degrees each turns from its start to its end, counter-clockwise (180, a half circle bulging to its right). `location`: the line of it the points are on: centre (the default), core-centre, exterior-finish, interior-finish, exterior-core or interior-core; its exterior side is to the left of its start to its end, so walls drawn clockwise face out. `attach_top`, `attach_base`: a roof or floor its top follows from below, or its base stands on. `room_bounding`: false for a wall rooms run past (a low wall, a balustrade); true, the default, bounds them

door | Door | {at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?, flip_hand?} in the wall under `at`, or in `wall` centred `offset` mm from its start; with `family`, a door family's `type` (its first by default), which sizes the opening and draws the door

window | Window | {at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, sill?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?} like door; `sill` defaults to the type's (a family's `Sill Height`)

dimension | Aligned Dimension | {refs: [ref, …], at: [x, y], level?, kind?: aligned|linear|angular|radial|diameter|arc_length, orient?: horizontal|vertical} aligned (the default): the distances between parallel references, along a line through `at` (between points, along the first two; points and lines, square to the lines); linear: the same with its line horizontal or vertical as `orient` says, or without one as `at` lies: east or west of the points, vertical, else horizontal (its lines must run square to it); angular: the angle between two references that meet, on the side of `at`; radial: a round column's, curved wall's, circle's or arc's radius, toward `at`; diameter: the same across, through its centre; arc_length: how long a curved wall's centre line or face, or an arc, is along it (all of it, or with two point refs after it, between them), its line an arc through `at`. A ref is {id, face?}: a wall's centre (the default), left or right face (of its start-to-end direction), start or end; a door's or window's centre, or its jamb toward its wall's start or end; a grid's line; a straight detail line, or its start or end (radial: a circle or an arc of one). With `point: start|end`, {id, face?, point} is the point at that end of the line: a wall's centre line's end, a face's corner, a grid's, a detail line's (of any shape) or a jamb's end. Or a point [x, y] on one of those lines (for radial and diameter, on a round edge; for arc_length, on the arc), or {endpoint: [x, y]}, the end of one nearest it, within 1

tag | Tag by Category | {ids?: [id,…], label?, level?, category?, offset?: [dx, dy], leader?} tags elements with a field of theirs: a door's or window's mark, a room's name, else the type, or `label`, any field its category's schedule has (`Height`, `Area`, a project parameter); doors, windows, walls, columns, components, floors, ceilings, roofs, rooms, runs and stairs. `offset` mm from the point it names (beside the wall for a door or window, else up and right); without ids, every door and window on the level not tagged yet, or of `category`

flip | Flip | {ids: [wall,…]} turns walls round about their location lines, as Revit's flip arrows do: their exterior sides go to the other side, their doors and windows stay where they are

modify | Modify | {id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it

move | Move | {ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy], end?: start|end} moves elements in plan; walls joined to a moved wall stretch to stay joined, and doors and windows slide along their walls. With `end`, only that end of one wall moves

detail_line | Detail Line | {view?, style?, and a curve: `points` [[x, y], …] (with `arcs`, each segment's turn in degrees counter-clockwise, and `closed`), `start` and `end` (with `arc` degrees or a `through` point), `centre` and `radius` (a circle), `centre` and `radii` [a, b] (an ellipse, with `angle` degrees and `span` [from, to] degrees for part of one), `control` [[x, y], …] (a spline by its control points, with `knots`), or `fit` [[x, y], …] (a spline through them, with `start_tangent` and `end_tangent`)} a detail line in a view, by name or id, in the view's own terms: a level's plan (the lowest by default; plan mm), a section or an elevation (along its line from its start, and up) or a sheet by number (paper mm). It draws in line style `style` (Thin Lines unless told), only in its view, and goes with it; with `insulation`, a width in mm, it draws as batt insulation along its curve, as Revit's Insulation; with `centre_mark` true, a small cross marks the centre of its arcs, circle or ellipse; with `cloud`, an arc length in mm, it draws as a revision cloud's scallops along it (outward round a loop, a scallop ending at each corner), of `revision` (any text, a label kept with the cloud and listed by `elements`; nothing else reads it); a line is insulation or a cloud, not both. An arc, a circle or an ellipse lies within 1,000 km of the origin (an arc of 359.9999999999° is a circle of radius 5.7e14 mm, and is refused), and a polyline's arcs take no more than 8,192 points to draw within 0.25 mm: 10,000 

phase | Phasing | {name?, before?, after?, rename?, delete?, into?, now?, overrides?} the project's phases, in order, as Revit's Phasing does: a project starts with Existing and New Construction. `name` alone adds a phase at the end (or `before` or `after` another); with `rename`, renames it (its elements, views and templates follow); with `delete`, takes it out, its elements made and taken down in `into` instead (needed while anything holds it). An element is made in a phase (its `Phase Created` parameter, the first unless it says) and may be taken down in a later one (`Phase Demolished`), set with `modify {params}`; `now` (a phase, or null) is the phase what this session's commands make is made in (the first phase leaves no value). A view shows a phase and a phase filter (`graphics {phase, phase_filter}`): what's made after it isn't there, what's taken down before it neither, and the rest is new (made in it), existing, demolished (taken down in it) or temporary (both), each shown as its phase filter says (see `phase_filter`). `overrides` ({new|existing|demolished|temporary: override | null}, merged: an override as `graphics` has it, without hidden) is how a phase filter draws what it says overridden; the first two statuses start halftone and dashed red. Replies with the phases, `now` and the overrides

import sys, json, os, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-files')
from r import *

exe = MINE if os.environ.get('MINE') else ORIG
EMPTY = '/tmp/edit-files/fx/empty.bimcraft'
src = sys.argv[1]
base = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 and sys.argv[2] != '-' else EMPTY
idsets = json.loads(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else [None]
extra_files = sys.argv[4:]
for ids in idsets:
    sb = os.path.basename(src)
    if base == src:
        files = [src]
    else:
        files = [src, base]
    cmd = 'insert {"path": "%s", "ids": %s}' % (sb, json.dumps(ids)) if ids is not None else 'insert {"path": "%s"}' % sb
    r = run([cmd, 'inspect'], files=files + extra_files, args_before=[os.path.basename(base)], args_after=['--save', 'out.bimcraft'], exe=exe)
    print('=== ids', ids)
    for l in r['out'][1:-1]:
        if l.startswith('{"counts"'):
            d = json.loads(l)
            print('  > inspect history', d['history'], 'counts', d['counts'], 'warnings', d.get('warnings'))
        else:
            print('  >', l[:1500])
    if r['err']:
        print('  ERR', r['err'])
        continue
    p = proj(r, 'out.bimcraft')
    b = json.load(open(base))
    for k, v in p['elements'].items():
        if k in b['elements'] and b['elements'][k] == v:
            continue
        print('   ', k, json.dumps(v)[:500])
    print('    next_id', p['next_id'])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""defs.py fixture 'id field value' ...: set each (alone) and print whether the field is stored, and how."""
import json, sys, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, os
exe = '/workspace/executable'
src = sys.argv[1]
A = json.load(open(src))
for spec in sys.argv[2:]:
    eid, field, val = spec.split(' ', 2)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='d')
    shutil.copy(src, os.path.join(d, 'in.bimcraft'))
    cmd = 'modify {"id": %s, "%s": %s}' % (eid, field, val)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', 'in.bimcraft', '--cmd', cmd, '--save', 'out.bimcraft'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print('%-60s ERR %s' % (cmd, p.stderr.strip()[:200]))
    else:
        B = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'out.bimcraft')))
        x = A['elements'][eid]; y = B['elements'][eid]
        if field in y:
            keys = list(y.keys())
            print('%-60s STORED %s at %d of %s' % (cmd, json.dumps(y[field])[:100], keys.index(field), keys))
        else:
            print('%-60s ABSENT%s' % (cmd, '' if x == y else ' (other change: %s)' % [k for k in set(x) | set(y) if x.get(k) != y.get(k)]))
    shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""bs.py 'template with {x}' lo hi [iters] [pattern]: binary search the boundary where the original's
reply changes from accepted (lo) to refused (hi) or contains pattern."""
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, os, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
tpl, lo, hi = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3])
iters = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 50
pat = sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv) > 5 else None
def ok(x):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='b', dir='/tmp/views-lines/scratch')
    cmds = tpl.replace('{x}', repr(x)).split(' ;; ')
    args = [ORIG, 'run']
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    out = p.stdout.decode() + p.stderr.decode()
    if pat:
        return pat not in out
    return p.returncode == 0
a, b = ok(lo), ok(hi)
print('lo', lo, a, 'hi', hi, b)
if a == b:
    sys.exit('same at both ends')
for i in range(iters):
    m = (lo + hi) / 2
    if m == lo or m == hi: break
    if ok(m) == a: lo = m
    else: hi = m
print(repr(lo), repr(hi))

point_cloud : {path | cloud, name?, level?, at?: [x, y], offset?, angle?, units?, spacing?, origin?} brings in a laser scan (`path`: PTS, XYZ, PLY, LAS or E57 (each of its scans placed by its pose), or a list of the files of one scan's stations, brought in as one; `units` of its coordinates mm, cm, m (the default), in or ft; one point kept in each cube `spacing` mm wide) or places one the project holds again (`cloud`, its name), as an element: its middle on `at` (the origin) and its foot on the level, or with `origin: file` where its file's coordinates put it; `offset` raises its middle over the level, `angle` turns it. Returns its id, the scan's name, the points kept and read, and where its middle was in the file

import_cad : {path | cad, name?, level?, view?, at?: [x, y], position?, units?, scale?, angle?, layers?, colors?, link?} brings in a DXF drawing (`path`: an ASCII DXF of any version, or a DWG, which the desktop and the command line read as DXF) or places one the project holds again (`cad`, its name), as an element in every plan of `level`, or with `view` (a plan) in that view only. `units` of the drawing: auto (the default: what its file says, else mm), mm, cm, m, in or ft; or `scale`, mm to each of its units. `position`: center (the default: the middle of the drawing on `at`, the origin unless given) or origin (its origin on `at`); `angle` turns it about `at`, degrees. `layers`: visible (the default: those its file has on and thawed), all, or a list of those to show. `colors`: preserve (the default), invert or black. `link: true` remembers the file, so `reload_cad` and opening the project read it again. Returns its id, the drawing's name, its unit, entities and layers, its extents in the model, how many entities lie far from the rest (they're left out of its extents) and what was left out, with `notes` on what a DWG's read left out

graphics : {view?: a level's, section's or elevation's name or id, or {3D} (the lowest level's plan unless given), hide?: [category, …], show?: […], hide_elements?: [id, …], show_elements?: […], categories?: {category: override | null, …}, elements?: {id: override | null, …}, filters?: [{filter, hidden?, projection?, cut?, halftone?, transparency?}, …], phase?: name | null, phase_filter?: name | null, options?: {set: option | null, …}, layers?: {drawing: [layer, …] | null, …}, template?: name | null, background_grid?: {visible?, main?: {enabled?, color?: [r,g,b], pen?: 0..16}, sub?: {enabled?, color?, pen?}, spacing?: [X,Y] (mm), divisions?: [X,Y] (1..1000), rotation?: degrees (-360..360)} | null, reset?: true} what a view hides and how it draws the rest, as Revit's Visibility/Graphics does; with none of those, the view's settings as they are. A category hidden (walls, floors, rooms, grids, dimensions, levels…, in any case, singular or plural) leaves all its elements out of that view, and `hide_elements` the elements given. In a 3D view rooms are hidden unless shown (`show: [rooms]`), every new 3D view so; shown, each is a see-through solid. Subcategories are hidden and shown as categories are, and go with their category: under rooms, `roomreference` (the cross at each room's point, hidden unless shown, as Revit's Rooms > Reference) and `roomseparator` (room separation lines). An override is {hidden?, projection?: style, cut?: style, halftone?, transparency?}, a style {color?, weight? (a pen, 0 to 16: 0 a hairline, the thinnest line the screen or printer draws at any scale; 1 to 16 widths on paper from 0.10 to 4 mm, 4 being 0.18 mm and 10 0.35 mm, a cut wall's outline), dash? (solid, dashed, dotted), fill?, foreground?, background?}, a colour [r, g, b] or "#rrggbb". Foreground and background override independent pattern layers: {pattern: a fill pattern's name | null, color?: [r,g,b]}; a null pattern hides that layer; a null foreground or background restores inheritance. They draw in plans, ceiling plans, section cuts and filled regions, using drafting patterns at paper scale and model patterns at model size. Projection is what a plan sees below its cut plane, a section beyond its line and the annotation; cut is what the view cuts; `fill` is the cut's poché, or a 3D view's surface; in a 3D view, and in what a section sees beyond its line, a projection's `color` is the colour of the edges (weight and dash draw lines, and those are vectors). Halftone draws it halfway to

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Test candidate local-coordinate transforms against the original's wall axis points.
usage: xform.py case.bimcraft case.ifc"""
import json, re, sys, math

def fmt(x):
    s = '%.6f' % x
    s = s.rstrip('0')
    return s

bim = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
walls = [e for k, e in sorted(bim['elements'].items()) if e['category'] == 'wall']
ents = {}
for line in open(sys.argv[2]):
    m = re.match(r'#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', line.strip())
    if m: ents[int(m.group(1))] = (m.group(2), m.group(3))
axes = []
for i, (t, a) in sorted(ents.items()):
    if t == 'IFCWALL':
        shape = int(a.split(',')[6][1:])
        reps = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', ents[shape][1])]
        ax = reps[1]
        poly = int(re.findall(r'#(\d+)', ents[ax][1])[1])
        pts = [ents[int(x)][1].strip('()') for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', ents[poly][1])]
        axes.append(pts)

def norm_recip(dx, dy):
    l = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy); r = 1.0/l
    return dx*r, dy*r
def norm_div(dx, dy):
    l = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
    return dx/l, dy/l

def cand_sub(o, p, d):
    vx, vy = p[0]-o[0], p[1]-o[1]
    c, s = d
    return vx*c + vy*s, vx*(-s) + vy*c

def cand_affine(o, p, d):
    c, s = d
    # columns x=(c,s), y=(-s,c); glam DMat2 inverse
    det = c*c - (-s)*s
    idt = 1.0/det
    ix = (c*idt, -s*idt)      # (y_axis.y * id, -x_axis.y * id)
    iy = (-(-s)*idt, c*idt)   # (-y_axis.x * id, x_axis.x * id)
    tx = -(ix[0]*o[0] + iy[0]*o[1]); ty = -(ix[1]*o[0] + iy[1]*o[1])
    return ix[0]*p[0] + iy[0]*p[1] + tx, ix[1]*p[0] + iy[1]*p[1] + ty

def cand_affine2(o, p, d):
    # rotation transpose without det, translation applied after
    c, s = d
    tx = -(c*o[0] + s*o[1]); ty = -((-s)*o[0] + c*o[1])
    return c*p[0] + s*p[1] + tx, (-s)*p[0] + c*p[1] + ty

cands = {'sub': cand_sub, 'affine': cand_affine, 'affine2': cand_affine2}
norms = {'recip': norm_recip, 'div': norm_div}
for nn, nf in norms.items():
    for cn, cf in cands.items():
        bad = 0
        for w, ax in zip(walls, axes):
            if w.get('arc'): continue
            o = w['start']; p = w['end']
            d = nf(p[0]-o[0], p[1]-o[1])
            for q, want in zip([o, p], ax):
                x, y = cf(o, q, d)
                got = fmt(x) + ',' + fmt(y)
                if got != want: bad += 1
        print(nn, cn, 'mismatches', bad)

graphic_display_options | Graphic Display Options | {view?: a 3D view's name or id ({3D} unless given), edges?: true | false, silhouette?: px, ambient_shadows?: true | false} how a 3D view draws its edges and shadows, as Revit's Graphic Display Options: `edges`, the lines where its surfaces meet in Shaded (on unless turned off; Hidden Line always draws them); `silhouette`, an outline that many pixels wide (a whole number, 0 to 10; 0, the default, for none) round what stands in front of what is further off or of nothing; `ambient_shadows`, soft shadows where faces meet inside a corner (off unless turned on). What is left out stays as it was; with none of them it only says what the view has

phase | Phasing | {name?, before?, after?, rename?, delete?, into?, now?, overrides?} the project's phases, in order, as Revit's Phasing does: a project starts with Existing and New Construction. `name` alone adds a phase at the end (or `before` or `after` another); with `rename`, renames it (its elements, views and templates follow); with `delete`, takes it out, its elements made and taken down in `into` instead (needed while anything holds it). An element is made in a phase (its `Phase Created` parameter, the first unless it says) and may be taken down in a later one (`Phase Demolished`), set with `modify {params}`; `now` (a phase, or null) is the phase what this session's commands make is made in (the firs

phase_filter | Phase Filter | {name, new?, existing?, demolished?, temporary?, delete?} a phase filter: how a view shows each status of what's in its phase, each `by-category` (as its category and the view's overrides say), `overridden` (as the project's overrides for that status say) or `not-displayed`. A project has Show All, Show Complete, Show New, Show Previous + Demolished and Show Previous + New; any may change. A new one starts by category throughout. One in use by a view or a template can't be deleted. Replies with the filter

option | Design Options | {set?, options?, primary?, option?, rename?, delete?, accept?, now?} sets of design options, as Revit's Design Options has them: `set` with `options` ([names]; no colons) makes a set or changes its options (one with elements in it stays), `primary` is the option a view shows unless it chooses (the first by default). An element is in an option by its `Design Option` parameter, `set: option`, set with `modify {params}` (a door or window with none is in its wall's); it shows only in a view that shows that option: `graphics {options: {set: option | null}}`. `now` (`set: option`, or null) is the option what this session's commands make is made in. `rename` renames the set, or with `option`, one o

"""lens.py file: each line a detail_line param JSON; prints the length `elements` shows for each (one run)."""
import subprocess, sys, json, tempfile, shutil

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""vs.py [-m] [-f in.bimcraft] [-s scale] [-p 'setup cmd'] cmds.txt
Each line of cmds.txt: a command making a view (section/elevation...) or `@Name` naming an existing
view. All lines run in ONE session: each view made is placed on its own sheet (A3) at the scale, and
the viewport size (and at) is printed per line."""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aed8172cff8d68ba7/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG; infile = None; scale = 1; setup = []; size = 'A3'
while a:
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-f': infile = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-s': scale = float(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-p': setup.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-z': size = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    else: break
lines = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(a[0]) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='v', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
args = [exe, 'run']
if infile:
    shutil.copy(infile, d); args.append(os.path.basename(infile))
for s in setup: args += ['--cmd', s]
n = 0
for l in lines:
    n += 1
    num = 'Z%d' % n
    if l.startswith('@'):
        view = l[1:]
        args += ['--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"%s","size":"%s"}' % (num, size)]
    else:
        args += ['--cmd', l]
        args += ['--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"%s","size":"%s"}' % (num, size)]
        view = None
    args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": num, "view": view if view else "@LAST@", "scale": scale})]
# we can't know the name of the view made before running; so run step by step: first pass to get names
# simpler: run each line in its own process, cumulative is not needed
res = []
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    dd = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='v', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
    args = [exe, 'run']
    if infile:
        shutil.copy(infile, dd); args.append(os.path.basename(infile))
    for s in setup: args += ['--cmd', s]
    if l.startswith('@'):
        view = l[1:]
        cmds = []
    else:
        cmds = [l]
        view = None
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=dd, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    if view is None:
        try:
            j = json.loads(out[-1])
            view = j.get('name') or j.get('ids')
        except Exception:
            print(l, '->', out[-1:] , p.stderr.decode().strip()); shutil.rmtree(dd); continue
        if isinstance(view, list):
            view = view[0]
    args2 = args + ['--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"ZZ","size":"%s"}' % size, '--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "ZZ", "view": view, "scale": scale}), '--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args2, cwd=dd, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    try:
        j = json.loads(out[-1])
        e = j['elements'][-1]
        print('%-70s size %s at %s' % (l[:70], e['size'], e['at']))
    except Exception:
        print(l, '->', out[-1:], p.stderr.decode().strip())
    shutil.rmtree(dd)
shutil.rmtree(d)

    elif a[0] == '-z': size = a[1]; a = a[2:]

lines = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(a[0]) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='v', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
args = [exe, 'run']
if infile:
    shutil.copy(infile, d); args.append(os.path.basename(infile))
for s in setup: args += ['--cmd', s]
n = 0
for l in lines:
    n += 1
    num = 'Z%d' % n
    if l.startswith('@'):
        view = l[1:]
        args += ['--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"%s","size":"%s"}' % (num, size)]
    else:
        args += ['--cmd', l]
        args += ['--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"%s","size":"%s"}' % (num, size)]
        view = None
    args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": num, "view": view if view else "@LAST@", "scale": scale})]
# we can't know the name of the view made before running; so run step by step: first pass to get names

res = []
for i, l in enumerate(lines):

    for s in setup: args += ['--cmd', s]
    if l.startswith('@'):
        view = l[1:]
        cmds = []
    else:
        cmds = [l]
        view = None
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=dd, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    if view is None:
        try:
            j = json.loads(out[-1])
            view = j.get('name') or j.get('ids')
        except Exception:
            print(l, '->', out[-1:] , p.stderr.decode().strip()); shutil.rmtree(dd); continue
        if isinstance(view, list):
            view = view[0]
    args2 = args + ['--cmd', 'sheet {"number":"ZZ","size":"%s"}' % size, '--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "ZZ", "view": view, "scale": scale}), '--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
    p = subprocess.run(args2, cwd=dd, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
    out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
    try:
        j = json.loads(out[-1])
        e = j['elements'][-1]
        print('%-70s size %s at %s' % (l[:70], e['size'], e['at']))
    except Exception:
        print(l, '->', out[-1:], p.stderr.decode().strip())
    shutil.rmtree(dd)

ux, uy = (b[0]-a[0])/c, (b[1]-a[1])/c

    ang = math.atan2(p[1]-cy, p[0]-cx)
    cands = {}
    da = ang - a0
    cands['r*da'] = r*da
    cands['da*r'] = da*r
    cands['r*(da mod)'] = r*((da) % (2*math.pi))
    # fraction of sweep * length
    L = r*sw
    cands['da/sw*L'] = da/sw*L
    cands['(da/sw)*L'] = (da/sw)*L

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/members-agent')
from reg import case, main

RUNS = ['beam', 'strip_footing', 'pipe', 'duct', 'conduit', 'cable_tray', 'wire', 'down_conductor', 'ground_conductor', 'cabling']
COLS = ['column', 'structural_column']
BAD = [None, 'x', '', True, False, [], [1, 2], {}, {'a': 1}, -5, 0, 1e10, -1e10, 1.5, '5']
P2 = [[0, 0], [5000, 0]]
cases = []

def j(x):
    return json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False)

# ---- runs: every key with every bad value
for c in RUNS:
    cases.append(case('%s basic' % c, '%s {"points": %s}' % (c, j(P2)), 'elements {}', 'inspect {}'))
    for key in ['points', 'closed', 'type', 'level', 'offset', 'end_offset', 'justify', 'system']:
        for v in BAD:
            p = {'points': P2}
            p[key] = v
            cases.append(case('%s bad %s=%s' % (c, key, j(v)), '%s %s' % (c, j(p))))

for c in RUNS:
    cases += [
        case('%s chain' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[3000,0],[3000,4000],[0,4000]]}' % c, 'elements {}'),
        case('%s closed' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[3000,0],[3000,4000]], "closed": true}' % c, 'elements {}'),
        case('%s closed2' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[3000,0]], "closed": true}' % c),
        case('%s closed2 eo' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[3000,0]], "closed": true, "end_offset": 5}' % c),
        case('%s chain eo' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[3000,0],[3000,4000]], "end_offset": 5}' % c),
        case('%s one point' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0]]}' % c),
        case('%s repeated' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[0,0]]}' % c),
        case('%s repeated chain' % c, '%s {"points": [[0,0],[1000,0],[1000,0],[2000,0]]}' % c),
        case('%s riser' % c, '%s {"points": [[500,500],[500,500]], "offset": 0, "end_offset": 3000}' % c, 'elements {}'),
        case('%s riser down' % c, '%s {"points": [[500,500],[500,500]], "offset": 3000, "end_offset": -200, "justify": "top"}' % c, 'elements {}'),

dimension {refs: [ref, …], at: [x, y], level?, kind?: aligned|linear|angular|radial|diameter|arc_length, orient?: horizontal|vertical} aligned (the default): the distances between parallel references, along a line through `at` (between points, along the first two; points and lines, square to the lines); linear: the same with its line horizontal or vertical as `orient` says, or without one as `at` lies: east or west of the points, vertical, else horizontal (its lines must run square to it); angular: the angle between two references that meet, on the side of `at`; radial: a round column's, curved wall's, circle's or arc's radius, toward `at`; diameter: the same across, through its centre; arc_length: how long a curved wall's centre line or face, or an arc, is along it (all of it, or with two point refs after it, between them), its line an arc through `at`. A ref is {id, face?}: a wall's centre (the default), left or right face (of its start-to-end direction), start or end; a door's or window's centre, or its jamb toward its wall's start or end; a grid's line; a straight detail line, or its start or end (radial: a circle or an arc of one). With `point: start|end`, {id, face?, point} is the point at that end of the line: a wall's centre line's end, a face's corner, a grid's, a detail line's (of any shape) or a jamb's end. Or a point [x, y] on one of those lines (for radial and diameter, on a round edge; for arc_length, on the arc), or {endpoint: [x, y]}, the end of one nearest it, within 1

text {text, at: [x, y], view?, type?, angle?, leader?: [x, y], override_format?, runs?: [{from, to, bold?, italic?, underline?}, …]} a text note, its first line's top left at `at`, in a view by name or id: a level's plan (the lowest by default; `at` in plan mm), a section or an elevation (`at` along its line from its start, and up), or a sheet by number (`at` in paper mm). Lettered as its text `type` says (2.5mm unless told; `text_type` lists and makes them: its font, its size, its border), turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise; with `leader`, a line to that point. Lines break at \n. With `override_format`, each run makes characters `from` up to `to` (counted in characters, a line break one) bold, italic or underlined (true), or not (false), whatever the type says; they stay when the type changes, and `modify` with a new `text` alone keeps them on what didn't change. Font and size are the type's

spot {at: [x, y], view?, host?} a spot elevation: in a level's plan (the lowest by default), the height of the top of what stands on the level at `at` (or of `host`), following it; in a section or an elevation, of its point `at`, along and up

tag {ids?: [id,…], label?, level?, category?, offset?: [dx, dy], leader?} tags elements with a field of theirs: a door's or window's mark, a room's name, else the type, or `label`, any field its category's schedule has (`Height`, `Area`, a project parameter); doors, windows, walls, columns, components, floors, ceilings, roofs, rooms, runs and stairs. `offset` mm from the point it names (beside the wall for a door or window, else up and right); without ids, every door and window on the level not tagged yet, or of `category`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fw.py [-m] chars... : measures the schedule heading width of each char repeated N times."""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aed8172cff8d68ba7/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
N = 100
if a and a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
if a and a[0] == '-n': N = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
mode = 'heading'
if a and a[0] == '-t': mode = 'title'; a = a[1:]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='f', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
args = [exe, 'run', '--cmd', 'sheet {"size":"A0"}']
items = []
for i, ch in enumerate(a):
    if ch == 'SPACE': ch = ' '
    if ch.startswith('=') and len(ch) > 1:
        h = ch[1:]
    else:
        h = ch * N
    items.append((ch, h))
    name = 'S%d' % i
    if mode == 'heading':
        args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": name, "category": "rooms", "fields": [{"name": "Number", "heading": h}]})]
    else:
        args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": h, "category": "rooms", "fields": [{"name": "Number", "heading": "A"}]})]
        name = h
    args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "A101", "view": name, "at": [100, 100]})]
args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
if p.stderr: print(p.stderr.decode())
j = json.loads(out[-1])
for (ch, h), e in zip(items, j['elements']):
    px = round(e['size'][0] * 5)
    print('%r width %.1f mm = %d px; per char %.4f px' % (h if len(h) < 30 else ch, e['size'][0], px, (px - 24) / (len(h) if not ch.startswith('=') else 1)))
shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fw.py [-m] [-t] file : each line of the file is a heading (or with -t, a schedule title); measures
the viewport width of a one-column schedule with that heading (or title)."""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aed8172cff8d68ba7/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
mode = 'heading'
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE
    if a[0] == '-t': mode = 'title'
    a = a[1:]
items = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(a[0]) if l.strip()]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='f', dir='/tmp/views-a/scratch')
args = [exe, 'run', '--cmd', 'sheet {"size":"A0"}']
for i, h in enumerate(items):
    h = h.replace('\\s', ' ')
    name = 'S%d' % i
    if mode == 'heading':
        args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": name, "category": "rooms", "fields": [{"name": "Number", "heading": h}]})]
    else:
        args += ['--cmd', 'schedule %s' % json.dumps({"name": h, "category": "rooms", "fields": [{"name": "Number", "heading": "A"}]})]
        name = h
    args += ['--cmd', 'place %s' % json.dumps({"sheet": "A101", "view": name, "at": [100, 100]})]
args += ['--cmd', 'elements {"category":"viewport"}']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
out = [x for x in p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n') if x]
if p.stderr: print(p.stderr.decode())
j = json.loads(out[-1])
for h, e in zip(items, j['elements']):
    px = round(e['size'][0] * 5)
    print('%-40r len %3d width %.1f mm = %d px' % (h, len(h), e['size'][0], px))
shutil.rmtree(d)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/ly'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, y, t, layers, tname='WT', direction='NEGATIVE', offset=None, colors=None, on_type=False, ifc2x3=False):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, y, 0), (0, 0, 1), (1, 0, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -t / 2), (5000, -t / 2), (5000, t / 2), (0, t / 2)]), 3000)])
    ax = f.shape([f.poly2([(0, 0), (5000, 0)], close=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis')
    if ifc2x3:
        w = f.add('IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE', gid(), None, 'W', None, None, lp, f.pds(body, ax), None)
    else:
        w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, 'W', None, None, lp, f.pds(body, ax), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    ls = []
    for i, (mname, th, cat) in enumerate(layers):
        m = f.add('IFCMATERIAL', mname, None, None) if not ifc2x3 else f.add('IFCMATERIAL', mname)
        if colors and colors[i]:
            c = f.add('IFCCOLOURRGB', None, *colors[i])
            ss = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLESHADING', c, None) if not ifc2x3 else f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLESHADING', c)
            st = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLE', mname, E('BOTH'), (ss,))
            si = f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', None, (st,), None)
            sr = f.add('IFCSTYLEDREPRESENTATION', f.ctx, 'Style', 'Material', (si,))
            f.add('IFCMATERIALDEFINITIONREPRESENTATION', None, None, (sr,), m)
        if ifc2x3:
            ls.append(f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYER', m, float(th), None))
        else:
            ls.append(f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYER', m, float(th), None, None, None, cat, None))
    lset = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSET', tuple(ls), 'LS', None) if not ifc2x3 else f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSET', tuple(ls), 'LS')
    us = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSETUSAGE', lset, E('AXIS2'), E(direction), float(offset if offset is not None else t / 2), None) if not ifc2x3 else f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSETUSAGE', lset, E('AXIS2'), E(direction), float(offset if offset is not None else t / 2))
    if ifc2x3:
        typ = f.add('IFCWALLTYPE', gid(), None, tname, None, None, None, None, None, None, E('STANDARD'))
    else:
        typ = f.add('IFCWALLTYPE', gid(), None, tname, None, None, None, None, None, None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.rel_type(typ, [w])
    if on_type:
        f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (typ,), lset)
    else:
        f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (w,), us)
    return w


def a(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, 0, 400, [('M1', 50, 'Finish'), ('M2', 50, 'Insulation'), ('M3', 100, 'LoadBearing'), ('M4', 50, 'Membrane'), ('M5', 50, 'Substrate'), ('M6', 100, None)])


def b(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, 0, 400, [('M1', 50, 'finish'), ('M2', 50, 'Core'), ('M3', 100, 'Structure'), ('M4', 50, 'Thermal'), ('M5', 50, 'Air'), ('M6', 100, 'Other')])


def c(f):  # names as material names: Brick, Concrete, Insulation, Plaster, Gypsum, Membrane without categories
    s1, s2 = base(f)

import math, itertools
a=(0.0,0.0); b=(9000.0,0.0); deg=30.0
targets = {(5500,-550): 5553.156351417149, (7500,-300): 7572.380224404302, (1500,-300): 1531.2562149428609,
           (2500,-300): 2526.809998205612, (6500,-300): 6576.8264411415585, (8500,-300): 8548.34028805685}
sw = math.radians(deg); c = 9000.0; half = sw/2
r = c/2/abs(math.sin(half)); dd = c/2/math.tan(half)
cx, cy = 4500.0, dd
a0 = math.atan2(a[1]-cy, a[0]-cx)
L = r*sw
co, si = math.cos(a0), math.sin(a0)
v0x, v0y = a[0]-cx, a[1]-cy
cnt = {}
for p, t in targets.items():
    dx, dy = p[0]-cx, p[1]-cy
    cands = {}
    lx, ly = dx*co + dy*si, -dx*si + dy*co
    g = math.atan2(ly, lx)
    cands['rot'] = g/sw*L
    cands['rot_r'] = g*r
    # normalized start vector
    ux, uy = v0x/r, v0y/r
    lx2, ly2 = dx*ux + dy*uy, -dx*uy + dy*ux
    g2 = math.atan2(ly2, lx2)
    cands['rotn'] = g2/sw*L
    cands['rotn_r'] = g2*r
    # chord tangent frame
    for k, v in cands.items():
        cnt.setdefault(k, 0)
        if v == t: cnt[k] += 1
        print(p, k, repr(v), repr(t), 'MATCH' if v == t else '')
print(cnt)

results.content:
place : {sheet: number or id, view: a level's, section's, elevation's, schedule's or 3D view's name or id, at?: [x, y], scale?, azimuth?, elevation?} puts the view on the sheet at 1 : `scale` (by default the view's own, see `scale`, 1 : 100 when it has none of its own; a schedule keeps its size), its middle `at` mm from the paper's bottom left corner (by default right of the views there, or in the middle); a view goes on one sheet. A schedule (Room Schedule, Door Schedule…) or the 3D view ({3D}, seen from `azimuth` and `elevation` degrees) comes to be as it's first placed

visual_style : {view?: "{3D}" | a 3D view's name or id, style?: shaded | hidden_line | wireframe} how a 3D view draws its surfaces: shaded (lit, in their materials' colours and textures, the default); hidden_line (paper-white with their edges, what a face hides staying hidden); wireframe (every edge, seen through the faces). Without `style` it only says what the view has; the default 3D view comes to be as it is first changed

modify : {id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it

move : {ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy], end?: start|end} moves elements in plan; walls joined to a moved wall stretch to stay joined, and doors and windows slide along their walls. With `end`, only that end of one wall moves

delete : {ids: [id,…]} deleting a wall deletes its doors and windows, deleting those their tags; a view takes its notes and spot elevations, and what a spot elevation reads takes it; dimensions lose what's deleted

render : {family?, type?, mode?: 3d|plan|elevation, wall_thickness?, view?: a level's, section's or elevation's name or id, a sheet's number, or {3D}, ceiling?, width?, height?, path?, azimuth?, elevation?, eye_elevation?} a family on its own with `family` — its `type` (the first by default) standing in a model of its own, in a wall `wall_thickness` mm thick (200) if it's a door's or a window's, nothing of this project's touched or left behind: `3d` (as seen from the south-east), `plan` (what its symbols draw) or `elevation` (front-on, as seen from the north), a PNG as `pngBase64` or at `path`. Without it: a level's floor plan (with `ceiling`, its reflected ceiling plan, looking up from 2300 mm), a section, an elevation, a sheet (at 5 px a paper mm), or the 3D view seen from `azimuth` degrees round from east (counter-clockwise) and `elevation` degrees up (by default from the south-east, 30° up), fitted; in perspective (see `perspective`) through its lens, and with `eye_elevation` from an eye that high (mm) looking at the same point, as a PNG (pngBase64), or written to a path: .png, .svg for a plan, .pdf for a sheet. A plan, section, elevation or sheet that could not draw something as asked (a fill pattern too dense for the view, more ink behind a region than is kept above it) says so in the reply's `notes`

graphics : {view?: a level's, section's or elevation's name or id, or {3D} (the lowest level's plan unless given), hide?: [category, …], show?: […], hide_elements?: [id, …], show_elements?: […], categories?: {category: override | null, …}, elements?: {id: override | null, …}, filters?: [{filter, hidden?, projection?, cut?, halftone?, transparency?}, …], phase?: name | null, phase_filter?: name | null, options?: {set: option | null, …}, layers?: {drawing: [layer, …] | null, …}, template?: name | null, background_grid?: {visible?, main?: {enabled?, color?: [r,g,b], pen?: 0..16}, sub?: {enabled?, color?, pen?}, spacing?: [X,Y] (mm), divisions?: [X,Y] (1..1000), rotation?: degrees (-360..360)} | null, reset?: true} what a view hides and how it draws the rest, as Revit's Visibility/Graphics does; with none of those, the view's settings as they are. A category hidden (walls, floors, rooms, grids, dimensions, levels…, in any case, singular or plural) leaves all its elements out of that view, and `hide_elements` the elements given. In a 3D view rooms are hidden unless shown (`show: [rooms]`), every new 3D view so; shown, each is a see-through solid. Subcategories are hidden and shown as categories are, and go with their category: under rooms, `roomreference` (the cross at each room's point, hidden unless shown, as Revit's Rooms > Reference) and `roomseparator` (room separation lines). An override is {hidden?, projection?: style, cut?: style, halftone?, transparency?}, a style {color?, weight? (a pen, 0 to 16: 0 a hairline, the thinnest line the screen or printer draws at any scale; 1 to 16 widths on paper from 0.10 to 4 mm, 4 being 0.18 mm and 10 0.35 mm, a cut wall's outline), dash? (solid, dashed, dotted), fill?, foreground?, background?}, a colour [r, g, b] or "#rrggbb". Foreground and background override independent pattern layers: {pattern: a fill pattern's name | null, color?: [r,g,b]}; a null pattern hides that layer; a null foreground or background restores inheritance. They draw in plans, ceiling plans, section cuts and filled regions, using drafting patterns at paper scale and model patterns at model size. Projection is what a plan sees below its cut plane, a section beyond its line and the annotation; cut is what the view cuts; `fill` is the cut's poché, or a 3D view's surface; in a 3D view, and in what a section sees beyond its line, a projection's `color` is the colour of the edges (weight and dash draw lines, and those are vectors). Halftone draws it halfway to the paper; transparency (percent) sees through it in a 3D view. Halftone and transparency only add: a filter or an element can lighten what its category doesn't, not take its category's away. Overrides merge into the last (null takes a field or the override away); an element's own beats the filters applied (the first prevailing), which beat the category's. `filters` replaces the list applied; `template` follows a view template; `reset` takes away all of the view's own settings. `phase` is the phase the view shows (the project's last unless it says) and `phase_filter` how it shows each status of what's in it (see `phase`); `options` chooses the design option it shows of a set (the set's primary unless it says; see `option`); `layers` the layers of each CAD drawing it hides, by the drawing's name (null shows them all again)

elements : {category?, level?, limit?, offset?} elements with their `id` (six digits, what commands take) and `guid` (made once, never changed), fields and derived values (length, height, area_m2…); what an element points at (its level, host, view…) it holds by GUID. Wherever a command takes an element, its id or its GUID will do

import sys, json, os, zlib, struct
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-files')
from r import *

def png(w, h):
    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + b'\xff\x00\x00' * w for _ in range(h))
    def chunk(t, d):
        c = struct.pack('>I', len(d)) + t + d
        return c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(t + d) & 0xffffffff)
    return b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b'IEND', b'')
open('/tmp/edit-files/fx/p.png', 'wb').write(png(4, 4))

    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + b'\xff\x00\x00' * w for _ in range(h))

        return c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(t + d) & 0xffffffff)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a script with the original, export IFC, normalise and diff against an asset.
usage: ifccmp.py script.txt asset.ifc [extra cmds...]"""
import sys, os, re, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, difflib
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
script, asset = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/members-agent')
shutil.copy(script, os.path.join(d, 's.txt'))
p = subprocess.run([ORIG, 'run', '--script', 's.txt', '--save', 'Project.ifc'], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
print(p.stdout.decode()[-2000:], p.stderr.decode())
def norm(s):
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm) + 1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    return s
a = norm(open(os.path.join(d, 'Project.ifc')).read())
b = open(asset).read()
if a == b:
    print('IFC SAME')
else:
    for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(b.splitlines(), a.splitlines(), 'asset', 'orig', lineterm='', n=1))[:80]:
        print(l[:250])
shutil.rmtree(d)

An outline, and each opening, is simple: no edge across another or along it, none ending part way along one, no spike or keyhole slit (`ceiling`, `roof` and `shaft` too, and `modify`, `move` and `edit_boundary` of any of them: they are refused, saying which edges); a file that has one still opens, and works until a command changes its outline"
}

"""assets.py [-v] [filter]: compare `convert x.ifc out.bimcraft` and `run x.ifc` between the
original and mine for each asset IFC (and the extra files in /tmp/ifc-import-agent/extra)."""
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a269fc74daf28a975/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
args = sys.argv[1:]
verbose = '-v' in args
args = [a for a in args if a != '-v']
flt = args[0] if args else None
files = sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/assets/**/*.ifc', recursive=True)) + sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/extra/*.ifc'))
env = dict(os.environ, MINE=MINE)
same = 0
for f in files:
    if flt and flt not in f:
        continue
    name = os.path.basename(f)
    res = []
    for cmd in (['run', name], ['convert', name, 'out.bimcraft']):
        p = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/tools/cmp.py', '-f', f, '--'] + cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)

    if all(r[0] for r in res):
        same += 1
        print('SAME', tag)
    else:
        n = sum(r[1].count('\n') for r in res)
        print('DIFF', tag, '(%d lines)' % n)
        if verbose:
            for ok, out in res:
                if not ok:
                    print(out[:6000])
print(same, 'same')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scenarios: what the original's own commands outside this part build (types, floors) is made by
the original into in.bimcraft; the member commands then run on it with both programs."""
import sys, os, json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/members-agent')
from reg import case, main

OURS = ('column', 'structural_column', 'footing', 'beam', 'strip_footing', 'pipe', 'duct', 'conduit',
        'cable_tray', 'wire', 'down_conductor', 'ground_conductor', 'cabling', 'elements', 'undo', 'redo', 'level', 'phase')


def split(script):
    lines = [l for l in open(script).read().splitlines() if l.strip()]
    pre = [l for l in lines if l.split()[0] not in OURS]
    ours = [l for l in lines if l.split()[0] in OURS]
    return pre, ours


def build_input(pre, name):
    d = '/tmp/members-agent/inputs'
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(d, name)
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in pre:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    args += ['--save', name]
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    if p.returncode:
        raise Exception(p.stderr.decode())
    return path


cases = []
for script, name in [('scen_structure.txt', 'structure'), ('scen_mep.txt', 'mep'), ('scen_mep2.txt', 'mep2'), ('scen_export_structure.txt', 'xstructure')]:
    sp = os.path.join('/tmp/members-agent', script)
    if not os.path.exists(sp):
        continue
    pre, ours = split(sp)
    inp = build_input(pre, name + '.bimcraft')
    cases.append(case('scen ' + name, *ours, files=[inp], open=name + '.bimcraft'))
    cases.append(case('scen view ' + name, *(ours + ['elements {}']), files=[inp], open=name + '.bimcraft'))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(cases)

import sys, json, os, subprocess, shutil, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-files')
from r import *

exe = MINE if os.environ.get('MINE') else ORIG
small = '/tmp/edit-files/fx/small.bimcraft'
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='lk')
os.makedirs(d + '/sub')
os.makedirs(d + '/snap')
shutil.copy(small, d + '/sub/small.bimcraft')
def sh(args, cwd=d):
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print('$', ' '.join(args)[:200], '->', p.returncode)
    for l in p.stdout.splitlines():
        if l.startswith('{"counts"'):
            dd = json.loads(l)
            print('    inspect history', dd['history'], 'counts', dd['counts'], 'path', dd.get('path'), 'warnings', dd.get('warnings'))
        else:
            print('   ', l[:600])
    if p.stderr: print('   ERR', p.stderr.strip()[:500])
sh(['run', '--cmd', 'save {"path": "sub/p.bimcraft"}', '--cmd', 'link {"path": "small.bimcraft"}', '--cmd', 'save {}', '--cmd', 'autosave {"path": "snap/a.bimcraft"}'])
sh(['run', '--cmd', 'recover {"path": "snap/a.bimcraft"}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}'])
sh(['run', '--cmd', 'recover {"path": "snap/a.bimcraft", "project": "sub/p.bimcraft"}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}', '--cmd', 'reload {}'])
sh(['run', '--cmd', 'open {"path": "sub/p.bimcraft"}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}'])
sh(['run', '--cmd', 'open {"path": "snap/a.bimcraft"}'])
sh(['info', 'snap/a.bimcraft'])
sh(['run', 'sub/p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'inspect'])
# modify the linked file on disk then reload
sh(['run', 'sub/small.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'wall {"points": [[0,5000],[3000,5000]]}', '--cmd', 'save {}'])
sh(['run', 'sub/p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}', '--cmd', 'reload {}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}'])
# file turned bad
open(d + '/sub/small.bimcraft', 'w').write('garbage')
sh(['run', 'sub/p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}', '--cmd', 'reload {}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category": "link"}'])
shutil.rmtree(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""langs.py [-m] [-g grep] cmds.txt: runs the command file through q.py on a new project of each language
(made by the original, plus optional setup commands from -s)."""
import os, subprocess, sys, re
a = sys.argv[1:]
mine = []
grep = None
setup = []
langs = ['en', 'pt', 'es', 'sv', 'cs', 'fr', 'nl', 'de', 'it']
while a and a[0].startswith('-'):
    if a[0] == '-m': mine = ['-m']; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-b': mine = ['-b']; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-g': grep = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-s': setup.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-l': langs = a[1].split(','); a = a[2:]
    else: break
for l in langs:
    f = '/tmp/views-a/in/lang_%s.bimcraft' % l
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--cmd', 'new {"language":"%s"}' % l]
    for s in setup: args += ['--cmd', s]
    args += ['--save', f]
    subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, cwd='/tmp/views-a/in')
    p = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/views-a/q.py'] + mine + ['-f', f, a[0]], capture_output=True)
    out = p.stdout.decode()
    print('== %s' % l)
    for line in out.split('\n'):
        if grep is None or re.search(grep, line):
            print(line)

import sys

from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/w4'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f, k=1.0):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0 * k)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, origin, xdir, foot, h, axis=None, name='W', zbase=0.0):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (origin[0], origin[1], zbase), (0, 0, 1), (xdir[0], xdir[1], 0))
    reps = [f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb(foot), h)])]
    if axis:
        reps.append(f.shape([f.poly2(axis, close=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis'))
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(*reps), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w


def e(f):  # axis on bottom face, mitred inwards trapezoid
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (5000, 0), (4800, 200), (200, 200)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (5000, 0)])


def ff(f):  # axis longer than body
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000, axis=[(-1000, 0), (6000, 0)])


def g(f):  # axis reversed relative to placement
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000, axis=[(5000, 0), (0, 0)])


def h(f):  # centred trapezoid with axis
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(-100, -100), (5100, -100), (4900, 100), (100, 100)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (5000, 0)])


def i(f):  # axis outside the body entirely (offset 1000)
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000, axis=[(0, 1000), (5000, 1000)])


def j(f):  # body with a notch: centre line crosses notch
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (5000, 0), (5000, 300), (3000, 300), (3000, 100), (2000, 100), (2000, 300), (0, 300)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (5000, 0)])


def k(f):  # parallelogram with axis on centre
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (4000, -100), (4200, 100), (200, 100)], 3000, axis=[(100, 0), (4100, 0)])


def l(f):  # axis is half of a long wall
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (300, -300), (5700, -300), (6000, 0)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (3000, 0)])


mk('e_inward', e)
mk('f_axis_long', ff)
mk('g_axis_rev', g)
mk('h_trap_axis', h)
mk('i_axis_off', i)
mk('j_notch', j)
mk('k_para_axis', k)
mk('l_half_axis', l)
print(' '.join(out))

def wall(f, s, origin, xdir, foot, h, axis=None, name='W', zbase=0.0):

    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(*reps), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w

    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (5000, 0), (4800, 200), (200, 200)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (5000, 0)])

    s1, s2 = base(f)
    wall(f, s1, (0, 0), (1, 0), [(0, 0), (5000, 0), (5000, 300), (3000, 300), (3000, 100), (2000, 100), (2000, 300), (0, 300)], 3000, axis=[(0, 0), (5000, 0)])
