for a, b, t, p in data:
    n = len(p) - 1
    th = math.radians(t)
    for cname, (cen, r) in centres(a, b, t).items():
        L = r*abs(th)
        S = (L/r) * (1 if th > 0 else -1)
        for sn, SS in [('swL', S), ('th', th)]:
            for vn in ['rotvec', 'rotvec_inc', 'rotvec_deg']:
                pts = []
                v = (a[0]-cen[0], a[1]-cen[1])
                cur = v
                if vn == 'rotvec_inc':
                    d = SS/n; cd, sd = math.cos(d), math.sin(d)
                for k in range(n+1):
                    if vn == 'rotvec':
                        ang = SS*k/n
                        ca, sa = math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)
                        q = (v[0]*ca - v[1]*sa, v[0]*sa + v[1]*ca)
                    elif vn == 'rotvec_deg':
                        ang = math.radians(math.degrees(SS)*k/n)
                        ca, sa = math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)
                        q = (v[0]*ca - v[1]*sa, v[0]*sa + v[1]*ca)
                    else:

                        cur = (cur[0]*cd - cur[1]*sd, cur[0]*sd + cur[1]*cd)
                    pts.append([cen[0] + q[0], cen[1] + q[1]])

mine = os.environ['MINE']
scen = [l.strip() for l in open('/tmp/views-graphics/t/r1.txt') if l.strip()]

    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Area","op":"greater","value":%s}]}',
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Area","op":"equals","value":%s}]}',
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Perimeter","op":"equals","value":%s}]}',
    'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Volume","op":"equals","value":%s}]}',
]
same = tot = 0
for i, l in enumerate(scen):
    cmds = [c for c in l.split(' ;; ') if not c.startswith('schedule')]
    f = '/tmp/views-graphics/rooms/r%d.bimcraft' % i
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]

    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    rows = None
    for line in p.stdout.split('\n'):
        if '"rows"' in line:
            rows = json.loads(line)['rows']
    if rows is None:
        print('no rows', i, p.stderr[:200]); continue
    for r in rows:
        for q, v in zip(queries, [r[1] - 0.5, r[1], r[2], r[3]]):

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, Bash, Edit, Read, Write</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user (single message) asked me to reimplement, as part of a multi-agent clean-room rewrite of the closed Rust program `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (README `/workspace/README.md`), the **IFC export area**: the IFC4 STEP writer for every element kind (header with FILE_NAME/project name escaping/timestamp/`BIMCraft 0.10.0`, units, project/site/building/storeys, exact entity order and numbering, GlobalIds, real-number formatting, walls with joins/arcs/attached shells/layer sets/Qto/Pset_WallCommon, openings with doors/windows and family forms as IfcTriangulatedFaceSet (with CSG voids, revolves, formulas), slabs (sloped, shaped, openings, shafts), coverings, roofs (straight skeleton, gables, courtyards, extrusion roofs, dormers, joins), spaces with Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities, columns, structural elements, runs with IfcSystem, components with IFC classes, masses, stairs/ramps/railings, rebar, type objects, materials/colours, project parameters, BIMCraft_Phasing/Status), and make `save` return the original's errors for IFC paths. My area: `src/ifc/export.rs` and any `src/ifc/export_*.rs`/`src/ifc/geom*`. Testing: build projects with the original, compare both programs' `convert in.bimcraft out.ifc` with cmp.py (normalises GlobalIds by first appearance, timestamp); reconstruct projects reproducing each asset in `/workspace/assets/test_ifc_export/*.ifc`, `/workspace/assets/test_model_geometry/*.ifc`, `test_mep_runs/mep.ifc`, `test_structure_elements/structure.ifc`, `test_structure_reinforce/rebar.ifc`; keep reconstruction scripts in /tmp. Finish: commit on worktree branch; final message: branch and commit; which assets and element kinds export identically; what doesn't and why; edits outside my area.

   **Hard rules (verbatim, violating any fails the whole project):**
   - "The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`."
   - "No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only."
   - "Your code goes in the directories you own (below). Edits elsewhere: only tiny, unavoidable ones (a `pub mod` line, a hook), listed in your report."
   - "Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, e.g. `/tmp/ifc-export-agent/`. Commit only Rust. You may spawn your own sub-agents (worktrees) to parallelise inside your area; integrate and verify their work yourself."
   - Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; never bare `git stash`; no report .md files.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - STEP numbering: entities appended in write order; `real()` = `{:.6}` of `x + 0.0` (negative zero → "0.", tiny negatives "-0."), trailing zeros trimmed keeping "."; `dir()` = `{:.12}`; strings escaped per character `\X2\XXXX\X0\` / `\X4\XXXXXXXX\X0\`, `'`→`''`, `\`→`\\`; GlobalId = 22-char IFC base64 of GUID; fresh ids from splitmix seeded by project uid (normalised in tests anyway).
   - glam-style f64 math: normalize = v*(1/len); points on lines parametric start + d*t; local coords ((p-o)·d, (p-o)·perp(d)).
   - Order: elements in id order; doors/windows deferred; hosted railings deferred; then stair aggregates, shafts, openings, rebar aggregates; tail: systems, layer sets, containment (storeys by GUID; contained then space aggregate), device psets, project parameters, commons (Status values all first), types (sorted by class then name), phasing psets.
   - Storeys written by elevation; building aggregate lists them sorted by GUID.
   - Walls: TOL=1 node joins (mitre via CCW/CW neighbours' face lines, node point included; squared if mitre parameter > thickness), T-junction (t ∈ (TOL, len−TOL), |off| within faces+TOL, cut at near face), free caps from face line ends; arcs n = ceil(|sweep|/(2·acos(1−1/R))); location offsets; Qto gross/net (openings cut to height), attached walls only Length/Width.
   - Layer sets order: wall sets (by type name), covering sets+rel, slab sets with usages sorted by offset string, wall usages; usage AXIS2 (walls offset=left), AXIS3 (slabs offset=floor offset); categories finish→Finish, thermal→Insulation, structure→LoadBearing, substrate→Substrate, membrane→Membrane.
   - Rooms: arrangement of centre lines (run on/back at joins) + separators; smallest CCW face containing point; ring starts at the half-edge with min (element id, piece); net from wall outline edges; redundant/unbounded rooms → no body/quantities.
   - Roofs: weighted straight skeleton (gables speed 0, per-edge slopes scaled by tan_min/tan_i), faces [edge start, edge end, nodes…]; heights via absolute plane: `nx=-n.x*tan, ny=-n.y*tan, dd = nx*a.x + ny*a.y + (lev+base)`, `z = (dd - (nx*p.x+ny*p.y)) - lev`, base = offset − overhang·tan(slope); thickness/cos; openings split faces sequentially along opening edges (bbox overlap test); courtyards reversed CW with edge-number mapping (given index (2n−2−k)%n when reversed); extrusion roofs one piece per profile segment (SHED_ROOF 1 seg, GABLE_ROOF 2, FREEFORM more); flat roof FLAT_ROOF; predefined HIP_ROOF/GABLE_ROOF.
   - Roof type predefined: `.FLAT_ROOF.` iff all its roofs are flat, else `.NOTDEFINED.`; roof layered types associate directly to IfcMaterialLayerSet (no usage); variable layer → `IFCMATERIALLAYER($,60.,$,$,'Variable','Substrate',$)` (material $ when none).
   - Attached walls: outline reversed (CCW), Sutherland–Hodgman clip (S starts at last vertex) by each roof piece/floor ring, brep bottom reversed/top/sides; top z from host plane relative to wall placement.
   - Families: prism triangles written: cap at `to` then cap at `from` reversed interleaved, sides (bi,bj,tj),(bi,tj,ti); xz plane flips all triangles; ear clip = fan-like (prev,cur,next) at k; circles 32 segments; dedupe points in written order; mirrored components mirror y and swap tri vertices before dedupe; voids need BSP CSG (unimplemented).
   - Phasing: element BIMCraft_Phasing (Phase Created always except doors/windows; implied description), Status in common pset (DEMOLISH/TEMPORARY/EXISTING/NEW; doors/windows without phase follow wall); project pset Phases list + changed filters/overrides + option sets (primary short name).

3. Files and Code Sections (all in worktree /workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a7aa74e0622ce519f):
   - `src/ifc/export_step.rs` (new): Step writer, `real`, `dir`, `st`, `gid`, `refs`, `fresh_gid`.
   - `src/ifc/export.rs` (rewritten): module declarations via `#[path = "export_X.rs"] pub mod X;` for step, geom, walls, openings, family, roofs, rooms, stairs, components, runs, skeleton, slabs; `export(pr,path)->String`, `save(pr,path)->Result<(),String>`; `Ex` state and all core/tail writers (described above). LayerKind enum currently `{ Wall, Slab, Covering }` (line ~205); `fn layer_set` (~line 898) writes `IFCMATERIALLAYER({mat},{th},$,$,$,'{cat}',$)` and `IFCMATERIALLAYERSET((...),name,$)`.
   - `src/ifc/export_geom.rs` (new): V2/V3 with dot, cross (perp_dot), length, normalize (recip), perp, line_cross, line_cross_t, signed_area, perimeter.
   - `src/ifc/export_walls.rs` (new): Wall, wall_of, offset_points, cap, outlines, centre_end, pt, lib_name, type_data.
   - `src/ifc/export_openings.rs` (new): doors/windows incl. family bodies, `short_type`, `face_sets`.
   - `src/ifc/export_family.rs` (new): values/formulas, meshes (no CSG yet), prism (written triangles), mesh_of, ear_clip, mirror_y.
   - `src/ifc/export_components.rs` (new): class_of table, write_component, write_devices.
   - `src/ifc/export_slabs.rs` (new): floors (level/sloped), ceilings, shafts, masses (lofted with STRIPS=16), helpers (rings_of, slope_of, prism_brep, face, rings_overlap).
   - `src/ifc/export_rooms.rs` (new): rooms/spaces and separators.
   - `src/ifc/export_runs.rs` (new): columns/footings/runs/rebar/systems.
   - `src/ifc/export_skeleton.rs` (new): weighted straight skeleton `faces(rings, speeds) -> Vec<Option<Vec<Node>>>`.
   - `src/ifc/export_roofs.rs` (new): roofs, Plane, clip_ring, split_ring, less_openings, attached_breps, follow_of, roof_extent; `write_roof` currently calls `self.typed("IFCROOFTYPE", &tname, "$,$,$,$,$,$,.NOTDEFINED.", product);` at line 363.
   - `src/ifc/export_stairs.rs` (stub): write_stair, write_ramp, write_railing, write_stair_aggregates (empty).
   - `src/commands/basic.rs` (outside area, one-line hook): `crate::ifc::export::save(&s.project, &path).map_err(|e| format!("save: {}", e))?;`
   - Scratch: `/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools/case.py` (build/cmp/all/asset; env CASES, MINE), rings.py, prof.py, gid.py, sub.py, search scripts; cases in `/tmp/ifc-export-agent/cases/` including asset reconstructions a_masses, a_structure, a_mep, a_mepruns, a_struct2, a_rebar, a_slabs, a_phasing, a_furniture (transparency 40), a_roofs, a_attached, names, empty.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Sandbox refused compound bash commands with heredocs/`cd /tmp &&`; switched to Write/Edit tools and simple commands.
   - Sub-agent spawn failed twice: "Concurrent subagent limit reached... Do not retry" → doing all work myself.

"""Filter a fuzz report: drop groups where the original failed a model check and mine opened."""
import sys, re
text = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
blocks = re.split(r'\n(?====)', text)
keep = []
for b in blocks:
    lines = b.split('\n')
    if not lines[0].startswith('==='):
        continue
    body = '\n'.join(lines[1:])
    m_orig = re.search(r'orig\[(\d)\] (.*)', body)
    m_mine = re.search(r'mine\[(\d)\] (.*)', body)
    if m_orig and m_mine:
        oc, om = m_orig.group(1), m_orig.group(2)
        mc, mm = m_mine.group(1), m_mine.group(2)
        if oc == '1' and mc == '0' and 'is not a BIMCraft project' not in om:
            continue  # a model check of the original's
        if oc == '1' and mc == '1' and 'is not a BIMCraft project' not in om and 'is not a BIMCraft project' not in mm:
            continue  # both refused by a model check (perhaps another)
    keep.append(b)
print('\n'.join(keep))
print(len(keep), 'groups', file=sys.stderr)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fz3.py file n seed: corner/split/fillet on every pair of walls (and lines) of a project file."""
import sys, json, random
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-ops')
from exp import ORIG, MINE
import t as T

src = sys.argv[1]
n = int(sys.argv[2])
random.seed(int(sys.argv[3]))
d = json.load(open(src))
walls = [int(k) for k, v in d['elements'].items() if v['category'] == 'wall']
lines = [int(k) for k, v in d['elements'].items() if v['category'] == 'line']
tests = []
for _ in range(n):
    kind = random.choice(['corner', 'corner', 'fillet', 'split'])
    pool = walls if (random.random() < 0.7 or not lines) else lines
    if len(pool) < 2:
        continue
    a, b = random.sample(pool, 2)
    if kind == 'corner':
        if random.random() < 0.5:
            tests.append('corner {"ids": [%d, %d]}' % (a, b))
        else:
            k = [[random.randint(-3000, 11000), random.randint(-3000, 9000)] for _ in range(2)]
            tests.append('corner {"ids": [%d, %d], "keep": %s}' % (a, b, json.dumps(k)))
    elif kind == 'fillet':
        tests.append('fillet {"ids": [%d, %d], "radius": %s}' % (a, b, random.choice([100, 500, 1000, 2500, 123.456])))
    else:
        e = d['elements'][str(a)]
        if 'start' not in e:
            continue
        s, t = e['start'], e['end']
        u = random.uniform(0, 1)
        p = [round(s[0] + (t[0] - s[0]) * u + random.uniform(-50, 50), 3), round(s[1] + (t[1] - s[1]) * u + random.uniform(-50, 50), 3)]
        tests.append('split {"id": %d, "at": %s}' % (a, p))
total = same = 0
rules = ("doesn't fit wall", 'too short (', 'is not a usable number', 'mm long or less', ' overlap in wall')
ruled = 0
for c in tests:
    code, out, err, proj = T.run(ORIG, src, [c])
    mc, mo, me, mp = T.run(MINE, src, [c])
    ok = (code == mc and T.norm(out) == T.norm(mo) and T.norm(err) == T.norm(me) and T.norm(proj or '') == T.norm(mp or ''))
    total += 1
    if not ok and code != 0 and mc == 0 and any(r in err for r in rules):
        ruled += 1
        same += 1
        continue
    if ok:
        same += 1
        continue
    print('DIFF', c)
    print('    orig:', (out.splitlines()[1] if code == 0 else err.strip())[:300])
    print('    mine:', (mo.splitlines()[1] if mc == 0 else me.strip())[:300])
    if proj and mp:
        for l in T.diff(json.loads(proj), json.loads(mp))[:8]:
            print('      m~', l[:300])
print('%d/%d same (%d refused by other areas\' rules)' % (same, total, ruled))

259:| Families | BIMCraft's own parametric components, never Autodesk's `.rfa`: a family has parameters (lengths, numbers, angles, yes or no, materials; each type's, or each component's), types that set them, and forms, each a profile drawn in its own axes and swept across them, every size a number or a formula as Revit's are (`Width / 2`, `if(Depth > 600, 4, 2)`), each form of a material, there while a yes/no parameter or a formula says. A new project comes with ten of them (tables, chairs, beds, sofas, desks, wardrobes, base cabinets, WCs, washbasins, bathtubs), named and worded in its language; more load from .json files. A component places a family's type at a point, turned and mirrored, its instance parameters its own; plans show it from above, the parts under a higher one hidden (a table's legs under its top), and sections and elevations beyond their line, never cut, as Revit shows furniture; the 3D view shades each form in its material's colour, textured as its material is. A form may be turned about an axis in its plane (a pipe, a bowl, a shade: `axis`, and `from` and `to` in degrees, up to a full turn), and a `void` form cuts the solid forms listed before it that it passes through (a hole, a notch, a sink's bowl, a sash round its pane), exactly: a solid cut by a solid, in any shape. The Family Editor in the desktop edits a family's parameters, types, forms and symbols as text, shows it on a preview you can turn, and makes it the project's, saves it to a `.json` file, or keeps it, with the materials it's made of, in the Favorites |
272:ceilings' (with their shafts cut out) match a hand calculation, as do the roofs' of an L-shaped house with a dormer and an
365:| Roof the building | Roof, in a plan: click inside the walls, and a roof goes on the level above, over their outline and past their faces, whatever its shape, and open over a courtyard: a loop of walls standing free inside the others, with no room in it; its hips and valleys show before you click. The Options Bar sets the slope (0° for a flat roof), the overhang, and gable ends for a rectangle. Select a roof, and Modify \| Roofs has Gable Edge: click an edge of its footprint (a courtyard's too) to stand it upright, a gable end, and again to slope it. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build cases with the original and compare my export.

usage:
  case.py build NAME            # cases/NAME.txt (a script) -> cases/NAME.bimcraft, cases/NAME.ifc (original)
  case.py cmp NAME [-n LINES]   # convert cases/NAME.bimcraft with mine and the original; diff normalised
  case.py all                   # cmp every case, print SAME/DIFF per case
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys, difflib, glob, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a7aa74e0622ce519f/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
D = os.environ.get('CASES', '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/cases')

def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm)+1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    return s

def build(name):
    txt = os.path.join(D, name + '.txt')
    bim = os.path.join(D, name + '.bimcraft')
    ifc = os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')
    args = [ORIG, 'run']
    if open(txt).read().strip():
        args += ['--script', txt]
    args += ['--save', bim, '--save', ifc]
    p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        print('BUILD FAILED', name, p.stderr.strip()[:2000])
        return False
    return True

def export(exe, bim):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='ifcx')
    out = os.path.join(d, 'out.ifc')
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'convert', bim, out], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
    s = open(out, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read() if os.path.exists(out) else ''
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr, s

def cmp(name, n=40, quiet=False):
    bim = os.path.join(D, name + '.bimcraft')
    if not os.path.exists(bim):
        if not build(name): return False
    a = export(ORIG, bim)
    b = export(MINE, bim)
    x = norm(a[3]).splitlines()
    y = norm(b[3]).splitlines()
    ok = x == y and a[0] == b[0]
    if not ok and not quiet:
        if a[0] != b[0] or a[2] != b[2]:
            print('exit/stderr: orig', a[0], a[2].strip()[:300], '| mine', b[0], b[2].strip()[:300])
        for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x, y, 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:n]:
            print(l[:400])
    return ok

def asset_check(name, path, n=30):
    """Does the original's export of cases/NAME equal the asset file (normalised)?"""
    bim = os.path.join(D, name + '.bimcraft')
    if not build(name): return False
    a = export(ORIG, bim)
    x = norm(a[3]).splitlines()
    y = open(path).read().splitlines()
    if x == y:
        print(name, 'ORIG==ASSET')
        return True
    for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(y, x, 'asset', 'orig', lineterm='', n=1))[:n]:
        print(l[:400])
    print(name, 'ORIG!=ASSET')
    return False

if __name__ == '__main__':
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    if a[0] == 'asset':
        asset_check(a[1], a[2], int(a[3]) if len(a) > 3 else 30)
    elif a[0] == 'build':
        for nm in a[1:]: build(nm)
    elif a[0] == 'cmp':
        n = 40
        if '-n' in a:
            i = a.index('-n'); n = int(a[i+1]); del a[i:i+2]
        for nm in a[1:]:
            r = cmp(nm, n)
            print(nm, 'SAME' if r else 'DIFF')
    elif a[0] == 'all':

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""cmpgrid.py file.bimcraft id x0 y0 x1 y1 step [extra-json]
Runs `linework {id, at, style}` at each grid point on both programs; reports the points whose
output differs (stdout+stderr), with a summary."""
import subprocess, sys, os, json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
a = sys.argv[1:]
f, eid = a[0], int(a[1])
x0, y0, x1, y1, step = map(float, a[2:7])
extra = json.loads(a[7]) if len(a) > 7 else {}
MINE = os.environ['MINE']
pts = []
x = x0
while x <= x1 + 1e-9:
    y = y0
    while y <= y1 + 1e-9:
        pts.append((round(x, 3), round(y, 3)))
        y += step
    x += step
def run(exe, p):
    c = {"id": eid, "at": [p[0], p[1]], "style": "Wide Lines"}
    c.update(extra)
    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', f, '--cmd', 'linework ' + json.dumps(c)], capture_output=True, cwd='/tmp/views-notes')
    out = r.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')[-1]
    return (out if r.returncode == 0 else 'ERR ' + r.stderr.decode().strip())
def probe(p):
    return p, run('/workspace/executable', p), run(MINE, p)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(probe, pts))
bad = [(p, o, m) for p, o, m in res if o != m]
for p, o, m in bad[:25]:
    print(p, '\n   orig:', o[:200], '\n   mine:', m[:200])
found = sum(1 for _, o, _ in res if not o.startswith('ERR'))
print('%d points, %d with an edge, %d differ' % (len(res), found, len(bad)))

# rooms with a round column of each diameter: find the perimeter the original compares (to the mm)
for d in [100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 800, 1000, 1500]:
    f = '/tmp/views-graphics/s/circ%d.bimcraft' % d
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--cmd', 'wall {"points":[[0,0],[10000,0],[10000,6000],[0,6000]],"closed":true}',
            '--cmd', 'type {"category":"column","name":"R%d","width":%d,"round":true}' % (d, d),
            '--cmd', 'column {"at":[3000,3000],"type":"R%d"}' % d, '--cmd', 'room {"point":[8000,3000]}', '--save', f]
    subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True)
    # bisect the perimeter added
    lo, hi = 32000.0, 32000.0 + math.pi * d + 5
    def gt(v):
        c = 'filter {"name":"F","categories":["rooms"],"rules":[{"field":"Perimeter","op":"greater","value":%s}]}' % v
        o = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', f, '--cmd', c], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1]
        return '"matches":[]' not in o
    # integer search: largest integer v with value > v
    a, b = int(lo), int(hi)
    while a < b:
        mid = (a + b + 1) // 2
        if gt(mid):
            a = mid
        else:
            b = mid - 1
    added = a + 1 - 32000
    best = []
    for n in range(6, 200):
        p = 2 * n * (d / 2) * math.sin(math.pi / n)
        if abs(round(32000 + p) - (32000 + added)) < 0.5:
            best.append(n)
    print(d, 'perimeter added ~', added, 'circle', round(math.pi * d, 2), 'n candidates', best[:3], best[-3:] if best else '')

Give it a `top` outline with as many points as its footprint (twin for twin, the same way round) and it is lofted straight between the two, or a `lean` (the footprint moved sideways for its top: a sloped mass); the plan then draws the outline at the height it cuts, the section the line where it cuts the skin, 3D a closed skin of triangles, and area, perimeter and volume, per level too, come from the cross sections between the outlines, exactly. `mass_floors` makes a floor at each level it crosses, outlined as the mass is there; the floors hold their mass and level, so running it again updates them instead of doubling them (`prune` deletes the ones on levels the mass no longer crosses; without it they are listed as `stale`). `wall_by_face` (on faces that stand plumb), `floor_by_face` and `roof_by_face` (on the top outline) make a wall on each edge, and a floor and a roof on its top face, and remember their mass and face: `update_by_face` (UF) rebuilds them from the mass as it is now, as Revit's Update to Face does, and refuses the lot, naming each, when a face is gone.     base = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(src))[0]

import json, subprocess, sys, os
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
OUT = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/rvt'

for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    src = name if os.path.exists(name) else '/workspace/assets/test_revit/%s.rvt' % name

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/slabs/lv'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    s3 = f.storey('L3', 6000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2, s3


def slab(f, s, top, cls='IFCSLAB', pt='FLOOR', t=200):
    lp = f.lp(f.bld_lp)
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, 0), (5000, 0), (5000, 4000), (0, 4000)]), t, f.ax3((0, 0, top - t)))])
    args = [gid(), None, 'S', None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None]
    if pt:
        args.append(E(pt))
    el = f.add(cls, *args)
    if s is not None:
        f.contain(s, el)
    return el


def col(f, s, z0, z1):
    lp = f.lp(f.bld_lp, (1000, 1000, z0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(400, 400), z1 - z0)])
    el = f.add('IFCCOLUMN', gid(), None, 'C', None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('COLUMN'))
    f.contain(s, el)


def wall(f, s, z0, z1):
    lp = f.lp(f.bld_lp, (0, 0, z0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)]), z1 - z0)])
    el = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, 'W', None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, el)


def cases():
    def a(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, s1, 3000)

    def b(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, s1, 2900)

    def c(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, s2, 2900)

    def d(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, s2, 7000)

    def e(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, None, 3100)

    def g(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, s3, 0)

    def h(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        col(f, s1, 3000, 6000)

    def i(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        wall(f, s1, 3000, 6000)

    def j(f):
        s1, s2, s3 = base(f)
        slab(f, s1, 3000, cls='IFCCOVERING', pt='CEILING', t=20)

    return [('a_l1_top3000', a), ('b_l1_top2900', b), ('c_l2_top2900', c), ('d_l2_top7000', d), ('e_none_3100', e), ('g_l3_top0', g), ('h_col_l1_at_l2', h), ('i_wall_l1_at_l2', i), ('j_ceil_l1_3000', j)]


for n, fn in cases():
    mk(n, fn)
print(' '.join(out))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Grid tie-breaking probe: a lattice of shape points with distinct heights; print the diagonal
chosen in each lattice cell."""
import json, subprocess, sys, re
name = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'q13'
sx = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 2000
sy = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 2000
W, H = 8000, 6000
pts = []
z = -10
lattice = []
for x in range(0, W + 1, sx):
    for y in range(0, H + 1, sy):
        lattice.append((x, y))
        if (x, y) in [(0, 0), (W, 0), (W, H), (0, H)]:
            continue
        pts.append({"at": [x, y], "z": z})
        z -= 7
cmds = ['floor {"boundary": [[0,0],[%d,0],[%d,%d],[0,%d]]}' % (W, W, H, H),
        'modify ' + json.dumps({"id": 100002, "shape": {"points": pts}})]
out = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools/probe.py', name] + cmds, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
coords = {}
for m in re.finditer(r'p(\d+) #\d+ \(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', out):
    coords[int(m.group(1))] = (float(m.group(2)), float(m.group(3)))
edges = set()
for line in out.splitlines():
    if line.startswith('  F') and '|' not in line:
        ids = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'p(\d+)', line)]
        if len(ids) == 3:
            for i in range(3):
                a, b = coords[ids[i]], coords[ids[(i + 1) % 3]]
                edges.add((min(a, b), max(a, b)))
rows = []
for y in range(H - sy, -1, -sy):
    row = ''
    for x in range(0, W, sx):
        d1 = ((float(x), float(y)), (float(x + sx), float(y + sy)))  # '/'
        d2 = ((float(x), float(y + sy)), (float(x + sx), float(y)))  # '\'
        d2 = (min(d2), max(d2))
        row += '/' if d1 in edges else ('\\' if d2 in edges else '?')
    rows.append(row)
print('\n'.join(rows))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cocircular tie-breaking probe: a convex boundary on one circle, every corner given a random
height; print the triangles as lists of points."""
import json, subprocess, sys, re, random
random.seed(int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3)
name = sys.argv[1]
which = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 'all'
circle = [(5000, 0), (4000, 3000), (3000, 4000), (0, 5000), (-3000, 4000), (-4000, 3000), (-5000, 0),
          (-4000, -3000), (-3000, -4000), (0, -5000), (3000, -4000), (4000, -3000)]
if which != 'all':
    circle = [circle[int(i)] for i in which.split(',')]
off = 10000
bnd = [[x + off, y + off] for x, y in circle]
pts = [{"at": p, "z": -10 - random.randrange(0, 1000) * 0.1} for p in bnd]
cmds = ['floor ' + json.dumps({"boundary": bnd}),
        'modify ' + json.dumps({"id": 100002, "shape": {"points": pts}})]
out = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools/probe.py', name] + cmds, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
coords = {}
for m in re.finditer(r'p(\d+) #\d+ \(([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+),([-\d.]+)\)', out):
    coords[int(m.group(1))] = (int(float(m.group(2))) - off, int(float(m.group(3))) - off)
n = len(bnd)
for line in out.splitlines():
    if line.startswith('  F'):
        ids = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'p(\d+)', line)]
        if all(i < n for i in ids):
            print(' '.join('%d:%s' % (i, coords[i]) for i in ids))
if 'FAILED' in out:
    print(out)

import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, math, sys
def kept_for(cmds):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    args += ['--save', 'a.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode: print(p.stderr); return None
    A = json.load(open(d + '/a.bimcraft'))
    rid = [k for k, v in A['elements'].items() if v['category'] == 'room'][-1]
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', 'a.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'modify {"id": %s, "frozen": true}' % rid, '--save', 'b.bimcraft'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode: print(p.stderr); return None
    B = json.load(open(d + '/b.bimcraft'))
    shutil.copy(d + '/a.bimcraft', '/tmp/edit-modify/arcroom_%d.bimcraft' % len(cmds))
    return B['elements'][rid]['kept']
for arc, chord in [(90, 4000), (60, 4000), (-60, 4000), (30, 4000), (120, 4000), (45, 2000)]:
    k = kept_for(['wall {"points": [[0,0],[6000,0]]}', 'wall {"points": [[6000,0],[6000,%d]], "arc": %d}' % (chord, arc), 'wall {"points": [[6000,%d],[0,%d]]}' % (chord, chord), 'wall {"points": [[0,%d],[0,0]]}' % chord, 'room {"point": [1000, 1000]}'])
    if not k: continue
    pts = k['centre']['outer']
    narc = len(pts) - 3
    a = math.radians(abs(arc)); R = chord / (2 * math.sin(a / 2))
    pred = math.ceil(a / (2 * math.acos(1 - 1.0 / R)))
    print(arc, chord, 'segments', narc, 'pred(1mm)', pred, 'R', R)

align | {id, reference: [[x,y],[x,y]], line: [[x,y],[x,y]], lock?: true, to?: id} aligns an element's picked line with a reference in plan: turns by the smaller angle about the picked line's midpoint, then moves it onto the reference, keeping its size. mass : {boundary: [[x,y],…], level?, top_level?, height?, base_offset?, top?: [[x,y],…], lean?: [dx,dy], name?} a mass, Revit's conceptual volume: the footprint extruded from `base_offset` above the level up to the next level, or `height` mm, or up to `top_level`. With `top`, an outline of as many points as the footprint (twin for twin, running the same way round), it is lofted straight from the footprint to it; `lean` makes one by moving the footprint sideways by [dx, dy] for its top, a sloped mass. Drawn dashed in plans and sections (the outline at the height they cut it, between the two when lofted), a see-through solid in 3D; its own category, `mass`, which views may hide. Its areas and volumes, per level too, are those of the cross sections between its outlines, exactly. Make floors from it with `mass_floors`, walls, a floor and a roof from its faces with `wall_by_face`, `floor_by_face` and `roof_by_face`

stair : {start: [x,y], end?: [x,y] | angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, width?, riser?, tread?, landings?: [{at, turn?}, …], railings?} a stair from the middle of its first riser at `start`, climbing toward `end` (or `angle` degrees) up to the next level: as many risers as keep each at most `riser` mm (180), treads `tread` deep (280), `width` wide (1000). One straight run, as long as that makes it; or with landings (each as deep as the stair is wide) after `at` risers, the next run going on as `turn` says: 0 straight on, 90 or -90 turned left or right, 180 or -180 back beside it, to its left or right. With `railings`, a railing down each side too

ramp : {start: [x,y], end?: [x,y] | angle?, level?, top_level?, height?, width?, slope?, landings?: [{at, turn?}, …], railings?} a ramp from the middle of its foot at `start`, climbing toward `end` (or `angle` degrees) up to the next level, or `height` mm, `width` wide (1200), at `slope` percent (8.33, 1 in 12), as long as that makes it; with landings `at` mm up, turning as a stair's do, and with `railings`, a railing down each side. Solid down to its level

railing : {host: a stair or a ramp, side?: left|right, type?} | {path: [[x,y],…], level?, base_offset?, type?} a railing along the stair's or the ramp's sides (both, or the one going up it on `side`), 50 mm in from its edges and climbing with it, going where it goes; or along `path`, `base_offset` mm above the level. Its type sets how high its rail stands over what it runs along, and how far apart its balusters are

family : {name?, category?: furniture|casework|plumbing|lighting|generic|door|window, parameters?: [{name, kind?: length|number|angle|yesno|material, instance?, value?, formula?}], types?: {type: {parameter: value}}, forms?: [{plane?: xy|xz|yz, profile?: [[a, b], …], circle?: {centre: [a, b], radius}, axis?: [[a, b], [a, b]], from?, to, material?, visible?, void?}], symbols?: [{line?: [[x, y], …] | arc?: {centre: [x, y], radius, from?, to} | text?: {at: [x, y], height, value, align?: left|center|right} | dot?: {centre: [x, y], radius}, visible?}], form?: {id | guid, …a form's fields}, symbol?: {id | guid, …a symbol's fields}, delete_form?: [id | guid, …], delete_symbol?: [id | guid, …], operation?: swing|double-swing|sliding|double-sliding|folding|fixed (a door's or window's, for IFC and schedules), kind?: which fixture or fitting it is, for IFC's predefined type (plumbing: wc|lav|sink|laundry|shower|bath|bidet|urinal; drain: floor_drain|floor_waste|roof_drain; pipefitting: bend|tee|cross|transition|coupling; "" clears it), connectors?: [{kind: power|switch, system: power-balanced|power-unbalanced|switch, poles?: 1-3, voltage?, load_va?, power_factor?, classification?}], rename?, delete?: true, dry_run?, path?, save?} a family of the project's, BIMCraft's own parametric component: created, changed, read, or loaded from the .json file at `path` (a family as `inspect` shows it, with its `name`). Without `name` it lists the project's families, each its category and how many types, forms and symbols it has; with only a `name` it reads one — its definition, each of its types' parameter values worked out, and `warnings` — and changes nothing: no undo step, no file. `dry_run` reads a change the same way and replies what it would do (`changes`: the parameters and types added, taken away and changed, the forms and symbols replaced, patched and deleted by id, the `rename`) instead of doing it; a change that's refused comes back as an error, as it would without it. `form` merges its fields over the one form of that `id` or `guid` (a `null` takes a field away; its place, its id and its GUID stay), `delete_form` takes those forms away; `symbol` and `delete_symbol` do the same for symbols — where `forms` and `symbols` still replace whole lists. Every reply carries `warnings`: what's worth knowing and doesn't stop the change (a void cutting no solid, a form outside the opening or thicker than its wall, a door's or window's plan with no symbols). Its forms are profiles drawn in its own axes (x along a component's angle, y to its left, z up from its base) and swept: `xy` up from `from` to `to`, `xz` along y, `yz` along x. With an `axis`, a line in that plane, the profile is turned about it instead, `from` to `to` degrees (up to 360, right-handed from the axis' first point toward its second; it can't cross the axis): a pipe, a bowl, a lamp shade. A `void` is no solid: it cuts the solid forms listed before it that it passes through, a hole, a notch, a sink's bowl, and is never seen itself (forms listed after it are whole). A `door` or `window` family stands in a wall, placed with `door` or `window` and a `family`: its forms are drawn in the opening's axes (x along the wall from the middle of the opening, y across it, 0 in the middle of the wall and + toward its exterior, z up from the sill), it must have length parameters `Width` and `Height` (the opening it makes; `Sill Height` is a window's default sill), and its formulas read `Wall Thickness`, the wall's. Sizes are mm, or formulas over its parameters as Revit's are: `Width / 2`, `if(Depth > 600, 4, 2)`, with + - * / ^, < > = <= >=, if, and, or, not, min, max, abs, sqrt, round, roundup, rounddown, sin, cos, tan (degrees). A parameter is each type's, or with `instance` each component's. `types` merges into its types (a null takes one away); `parameters` and `forms` replace its own; `material` is a material's name or a material parameter's; `visible` a yes/no parameter or formula. `inspect` lists the families. A device's `connectors` say what it draws: one `power` connector at most (a second is refused), `voltage` in volts, `load_va` in VA (a number or a formula over its parameters, so each type has its load; `power-unbalanced` may take a list, one load for each pole), `power_factor` over 0 up to 1, and its `classification` (`lighting`…); a `switch` connector carries no load. A component reports them as `connectors` in `elements`; a lighting, outlet or switch family without one counts as zero load, which `inspect` warns of; `connectors` replace their own, as `parameters`, `forms` and `symbols` do. The `symbols` of a family of any category are what its plan draws besides its forms, in its own axes, turned and moved (and mirrored) with the component or opening and hidden at coarse detail: each one `line` (points), `arc` (degrees from +x counter-clockwise, up to a full turn), `text` or `dot`, one of them, with `visible` a yes/no parameter or formula. A `text` is lettered in BIMCraft's own strokes, capitals `height` mm tall, `at` the middle of the line of text vertically (`align` says whether `at` is where it starts, its middle or its end); its anchor moves with the component but its letters always read upright, left to right, never turned or mirrored; `{Parameter Name}` in its `value` is replaced by that parameter's value (a name the family lacks is refused), up to 256 characters. A `dot` is a solid disc in ink of a radius above zero. Symbols draw in the plan and ceiling plan of the component's level whatever height it has, and on no other level's. IFC leaves symbols out

component : {family, type?, at: [x,y], level?, angle?, offset?, mirrored?, params?: {parameter: value}} a family's type placed, its first by default: at a point on a level, turned `angle` degrees counter-clockwise, `offset` mm up from the level, and with `mirrored` flipped across its own x axis; `params` sets its instance parameters (`modify` merges into them, a null taking one back to the family's)

import math
t=math.radians(60.0); a=(0.0,100.0); b=(1000.0,100.0)
c=math.hypot(b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]); r=c/(2*abs(math.sin(t/2))); m=((a[0]+b[0])/2,(a[1]+b[1])/2); h=r*math.cos(t/2)
dx,dy=b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]; l=math.hypot(dx,dy); n=(-dy/l,dx/l)
cen=(m[0]+n[0]*h, m[1]+n[1]*h)
print('cen', cen, 'r', r)
a0=math.atan2(a[1]-cen[1],a[0]-cen[0])
# intersection of x=500 with circle
ix=500.0; iy=cen[1]-math.sqrt(r*r-(ix-cen[0])**2)
print('int', ix, iy)
ai=math.atan2(iy-cen[1], ix-cen[0])
print(repr(math.degrees(ai-a0)), repr((ai-a0)*180/math.pi), repr(60.0*((ai-a0)/t)))
iyr=round(iy,3)
ai2=math.atan2(iyr-cen[1], ix-cen[0])
print(repr(math.degrees(ai2-a0)))
"

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The single user message assigns me the ARCH area of a clean-room reimplementation of the closed program `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (Rust; README at /workspace/README.md; docs in /workspace/docs, esp. docs/areas/levels-walls-roofs.md, docs/areas/massing.md, docs/shape-editing.md). I own `src/arch/` and `src/geom/` in worktree `/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa380c34464cd9919` (branch `worktree-agent-aa380c34464cd9919`). Commands: `wall`, `door`, `window`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `shaft`, `roof` (boundary from walls, overhang, slopes, gables, courtyards, extrusion, openings, join), `dormer`, `room`, `room_separator`, `stair`, `ramp`, `railing`, `mass`, `mass_floors`, `wall_by_face`, `floor_by_face`, `roof_by_face`, `update_by_face`, `show_mass`, `sketch`, `edit_boundary`, `edit_shape`, `add_point`, `add_split_line`, `reset_shape`, `falls`, `flip` — matching replies, error texts (character for character), saved JSON (field order, defaults), undo labels, and model rules (my module's `check`). Build `src/geom/` as the shared 2D geometry library (polygons, planar graph of wall centre lines and separators with room enclosure, level wall outline, wall faces/offsets, sketch solving, triangulation, skeleton). Family door/window sizes from `families` section (plain values; formulas belong to STRUCTURE). Saved projects behind test IFC assets must come out identical. Finish: commit on worktree branch; final message: branch and commit; per command what matches and what doesn't; edits outside my area; what other areas must provide or call.

   Hard rules / constraints (verbatim from the user, must remain in effect):
   - "The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`."
   - "No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only."
   - "Your code goes in the directories you own (below). Edits elsewhere: only tiny, unavoidable ones (a `pub mod` line, a hook), listed in your report."
   - "Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, e.g. `/tmp/<area>-agent/`. Commit only Rust. You may spawn your own sub-agents (worktrees) to parallelise inside your area; integrate and verify their work yourself."
   - Environment: never use bare `git stash`/`git stash pop`; commit messages must end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" (NOTE: my commits so far omitted this trailer — add it to future commits).
   - Attempting to spawn a sub-agent returned "Concurrent subagent limit reached ... Do not retry." — so I do all work myself.
   - Complex bash commands (heredocs with backticks, loops with variables, `cd x && heredoc`) are refused by the worktree checker; workaround: write Python patch scripts with the Write tool to /tmp/arch-agent/patchN.py and run `python3 /tmp/arch-agent/patchN.py`; small heredocs with `python3 - <<'PYEOF'` inside the worktree dir sometimes work.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Project = JSON `Value` elements (BTreeMap id→object in original field order), library entries `{kind,name,guid}` (types `type:wall` etc., `family`, `family-type` "Family: Type"), lib ids counting down via `alloc_lib_id()` (used for sketch line parts and shape points/lines).
   - Session runs command → `crate::arch::check_edits(before, after, cid)` (my hook) → `crate::check::check` (calls `crate::arch::check`) → rollback on error.
   - Rust Display `{}` for numbers in messages; `{:.0}` for points in sketch/shape messages; serde-like error texts (`kind_name()`).
   - Planar graph face tracing (half-edges 2i/2i+1, clockwise-next rule), outer face reversal, wall centre-line joins (line intersections), per-edge offsets (mitre/step/square end), sketch problems ranking, constrained Delaunay (i128 exact predicates on 0.01 mm grid), plane merging, Voronoi-like catchments via Sutherland–Hodgman variant, weighted straight skeleton (event-driven).
   - Test tooling: `/tmp/tools/cmp.py` (needs `MINE=<worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli`), my scripts in /tmp/arch-agent: o.py, each.py (-b both, -P prefix, -i file), craft.py, craftrun.py, order.py, fl.py (env CATS, KEYS; -b), cmpb.py, jdiff.py, show.py; copies in /tmp/arch-agent/tools reading MINE from env. Build: `cargo build --release` (~10–40 s); tests `cargo test --release <name> -- --nocapture`.

3. Files and Code Sections (all in worktree):
   - src/main.rs (outside area): added `pub mod geom;` after `pub mod edit;`.
   - src/session.rs (outside area): hook
     ```rust
     let checked = crate::arch::check_edits(&before, &self.project, &cid)
         .and_then(|_| crate::check::check(&self.project));
     if let Err(e) = checked {
     ```

   - src/styles/parameters.rs (outside area): `RESERVED` now includes "Mass Face": `&["Phase Created", "Phase Demolished", "Design Option", "Paint", "Mass Floor", "Mass Face"]`.
   - src/geom/mod.rs: P2 ops (add, sub, scale, dot, cross, len, dist, lerp, unit, left, orient), `area`, `perimeter`, `ccw`, `cw` (plain reversal), `project_t`, `seg_dist`, `inside` (edge=outside), `inside_raw`, `seg_cross`, `bbox`, `start_lowest` (min y then x), `Arc{centre,radius,a0,sweep}::new(a,b,deg)` (r=c/2/|sin(h)|, d=c/2/tan(h), centre=mid+left(unit(chord))*d), `straight(deg)` (|rad|<1e-9); modules: curves, graph, sketch, skeleton, offset, tri.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fuzz.py fixture N seed: random modify patches (several fields, mixed valid/invalid values, several ids)."""
import json, sys, random, subprocess, re
src = sys.argv[1]; N = int(sys.argv[2]); random.seed(int(sys.argv[3]))
A = json.load(open(src))
els = A['elements']
ids = list(els.keys())
fields_of = {}
def fields(i):
    if i in fields_of: return fields_of[i]
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', src, '--cmd', 'modify {"id": %s, "zzz": 1}' % i], capture_output=True, text=True)
    m = re.search(r'expected one of (.*)$', p.stderr.strip()) or re.search(r'expected (.*)$', p.stderr.strip())
    fields_of[i] = re.findall(r'`([^`]+)`', m.group(1)) if m else []
    return fields_of[i]
VALS = ['"x"', '1.5', '5', '-1', 'true', 'false', 'null', '[1,2]', '[[1,2],[3,4]]', '{}', '0', '""', '[0,0]', '"Level 1"', '"Level 2"', '100000', '100001', '"Generic - 200mm"', '{"x": null}']
out = []
for _ in range(N):
    k = random.choice([1, 1, 1, 2, 3])
    sel = random.sample(ids, k)
    fs = set()
    for i in sel:
        f = fields(i)
        if f:
            fs.update(random.sample(f, min(len(f), random.choice([1, 1, 2, 3]))))
    if random.random() < 0.1:
        fs.add(random.choice(['zzz', 'category', 'name', 'level', 'type']))
    patch = ', '.join('"%s": %s' % (f, random.choice(VALS + [json.dumps(els[sel[0]].get(f))] * 3)) for f in sorted(fs, key=lambda _: random.random()))
    idpart = '"id": %s' % sel[0] if k == 1 and random.random() < 0.7 else '"ids": [%s]' % ', '.join(sel)
    out.append('%s\tmodify {%s%s}' % (src, idpart, (', ' + patch) if patch else ''))
print('\n'.join(out))

Volume Computations) room areas are measured at the walls' faces instead (`face_lines` and the separators), the floor inside them; the IFC space
takes that outline, and its `Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities` give both whichever is set: `GrossFloorArea` and `GrossPerimeter` at
the centre lines, `NetFloorArea` and `NetPerimeter` at the faces, `Height` (the room's Unbounded Height) and `GrossVolume` and `NetVolume`. Walls, slabs, doors and windows
carry theirs too (`ifc::wall_quantities`): a wall its `Length` on its axis, `Width`, `Height` and side and volume, gross and less the
doors and windows in it (each cut to its height; joins aside), or only `Length` and `Width` when attached, as its height then varies;
a level slab its `Width` (depth), `Perimeter` and area and volume less its openings, a sloped one only its `Width`; a door or window
its `Width`, `Height`, `Perimeter` and `Area`. An attached top or base follows the roof's or floor's plane
over each part of the wall (a roof's slopes each over its own part of the plan); a mirrored wall runs back the other way.
A wall's top is `Model::own_top`, and 3D, sections, plans, IFC and what a wall is attached to all read it there (`walls::heights`
takes it, or what the wall is attached to): its `top_level`'s elevation plus its `top_offset` (file format 15, Revit's Top Offset,
mm, negative below the level), or its base plus its `height` when it has no top level, which an offset does not touch.
`Model::check` refuses a wall whose top does not come out above its base, saying how tall it comes out and by how much to raise it.
The Properties palette shows Top Offset under Top Constraint for a wall that has one.
A roof by footprint is the straight skeleton of its outline and its `courtyards` (`skeleton::faces`: the outline
counter-clockwise, the courtyards clockwise, the roof to the left of every edge): each edge moves in at speed 1, a gable's at
0, and its slope rises from it, reaching the roof's base `overhang` in from its eaves; a courtyard's edges number on after
the outline's, and every ring keeps its numbers whichever way round it runs, so `gables` stay put through a mirror.
`Roof::slopes` (file format 15) gives each edge a slope of its own, in degrees, numbered as `gables` are: 0 is the roof's `slope`,
and an empty list, every edge. `Model::roof_faces` then moves an edge in at the run over the rise of its slope, scaled so the
shallowest moves at 1 (every edge at one slope still moves at exactly 1), so edges of different slopes reach the same height
together and the slopes meet along their hips; the eaves stay level, the roof's base `overhang` in from them lowered by the roof's
`slope`, whatever the edges' own. A gable stays upright whatever its slope, and a flat roof (`slope` 0) keeps its `slopes` as it keeps
its `gables`, unused. `Model::check` refuses a list of the wrong length, saying how many edges there are, and a slope outside 0
to 75°, saying which edge. A sketch line may carry a `slope` (`SketchLine::slope`; the Slope row of Properties, with one line of a
roof's sketch picked, sets it): the roof keeps it as the `slopes` of the edges along that line (`sketch::along`), never in its
`sketch`, which `sketch::check` refuses to hold one. `edit_boundary` keeps the slope of an edge that stays or that a new
line cuts in two (an edge lying along an old one), the lines' own `slope` (0 sets the roof's) winning over it, and without
`slope` on the lines it keeps what the edges had; `edit_boundary` without a sketch gives the lines with the slope their edges share.
Over the walls (`floor_outline`, which `roof_footprint` grows by the overhang), a loop of them standing free inside the outer
ones, joined to none of them and with no room in it, is a courtyard, open through the floor and the roof; one joined to them,
or with a room in it, is rooms, and both run over it.
`Model::roof_faces` are its slopes, each the loops round it in plan (a slope can close round a courtyard whose far side is a
gable) with the plane of its underside, trimmed where it `join`s another; `Model::roof_pieces` are those less their holes
and its `openings`, convex where cut. A floor's top is at its level plus `offset`,
or with a slope arrow, there at the arrow's tail and rising `slope` degrees toward its head (`Model::floor_top`); it's its
type's thickness across the slope, so plumb it's thicker. Its `openings` are holes inside it, apart, and `Model::floor_slabs`
what's left, convex where cut. A floor's `shape` (IDEAS MOD-16, [design](../shape-editing.md)) folds its top into planes:
points `z` mm above (negative, below) where the top would be without them, and split lines it folds along, each a part
with an id and a GUID (`ShapePoint`, `SplitLine`). `Model::shape_planes` triangulates its outline, openings, points and
lines (`triangulation::constrained`), lifts each corner by the point there (a corner with none stays at 0) and merges
neighbours in one plane; `Model::floor_faces` are those planes in convex pieces, or the unshaped top, and `floor_slabs`,
the 3D view, sections and the element's details take them. In IFC a shaped slab is one closed `IfcFacetedBrep`
(`Model::shape_solid`: its top's planes, the same planes under them, plumb sides round its outline and openings, each
corner written once), and a sloped or shaped slab gives `GrossVolume` and `NetVolume`, its plan through its depth plumb;

underneath too, and has no slope arrow (`Model::check`, `shape_ok`, refuses one, and points outside the outline or in an

cross). A wall attached to one follows `Model::shape_triangles`, its top over the whole outline as if its openings were

- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it ONLY by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`.

## Getting started
1. Your worktree must start from the ARCH agent's commit 6a1b9e5 (branch `worktree-agent-aa380c34464cd9919`). Run `git log --oneline -1`; if HEAD isn't 6a1b9e5 (or a descendant of it), run `git reset --hard 6a1b9e5`.
2. Build with `cargo build --release` (about 15 s); the binary is `<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli`.
3. Probe tools are in /tmp/arch-agent/tools (copy them to your own /tmp dir; each takes the env var `MINE=<your binary>`):
   - `o.py [-m] [-c cats] [-n] cmd1 cmd2 ...` runs commands as a script on a fresh project with the original (or yours with -m), prints replies and the saved elements.
   - `each.py [-b] [-P prefixcmd]... [-i file] lines...` runs each line as its own script (after the prefix commands) and prints the result of the last; `-b` runs both programs and marks SAME/DIFF.
   - `order.py [-p prefixcmd] cmd '{bad params}' '{good params}'` finds the order in which a command validates its parameters.
   - `craft.py [-b] base.bimcraft 'python on d / E' [cmd]` writes a modified copy of a project file, opens it and runs a command (the original checks the model when opening, so this shows the model's rule messages and their order).
   - `fl.py [-b] groups.txt` (env CATS, KEYS) runs groups of commands (blank-line separated) and prints chosen fields of chosen categories.
   - `MINE=<your binary> python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py -- run --cmd '...' --cmd '...' --save x.bimcraft` runs both programs in fresh dirs and diffs exit code, stdout, stderr and every file written, after normalising GUIDs. Prints SAME or the diff. The hidden tests do this kind of comparison on many inputs, so match replies, error texts, saved files and undo labels exactly.

## The codebase (read what you need; you are in a git worktree)

- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute` runs a command, then `crate::arch::check_edits(before, after, cid)` (outline simplicity of what changed) and `crate::check::check` (every module's `check(pr)`; ARCH's is `crate::arch::check`, which runs each element's rules in id order, then cross-element rules), rolls back on any error, and records an undo step labelled by the catalog label.
- `src/commands/params.rs`: parameter readers with the original's texts (`req_num`, `opt_num` "must be a number in mm", `opt_text`, `opt_bool`, `req_point`, `opt_point`, `point_of`, `id_of`; |mm| <= 1e9). `src/model.rs`: `levels`, `elev`, `level_param`/`resolve_level` (with the original's errors), `level_above`, `find`, `normalize_guid`.
- ARCH so far (`src/arch/`): `util.rs` (helpers: `d(x)` = Rust Display of f64 as the messages print numbers, `dp(p)`, `num/numd/text/flag/pt/pts/rings` accessors, `pv/ring_v/rings_v`, `cat`, `by_ref`/`ref_word`/`ref_value`, `level_of`, `elev`, `level_guid`, `level_name`, `computation_height`, `type_names`, `type_def`, `type_guid`, `type_name`, `default_type`, `type_ref`, `check_type`, `thickness`, `layers`, `opt_ref`, `m2` (area mm² → m² 2 decimals), `put`), `walls.rs` (`Wall` struct: location line, centre line, `arc()`, `length()`, `base()`, `top()`, `spans(z)`; `cmd_wall`, `make_wall`, `cmd_flip`, `check_wall`, `joined_centres`), `openings.rs` (doors/windows, marks `next_series`), `slabs.rs` (floor/ceiling/shaft commands and checks, `clean`, `de_rings`/`de_points` serde-like readers, `opt_boundary`, `check_rings`), `roofs.rs` (roof command and checks, `wall_footprint`, `round3`), `rooms.rs` (room, room_separator, `space_at` room regions at centre lines and faces), `outline.rs` (`level_outline`: a level's wall outline and courtyards), `edits.rs` (`check_edits`), `mod.rs` (dispatch + `check`).
- `src/geom/`: `mod.rs` (P2 = [f64; 2] and vector ops, `area`, `inside`, `seg_dist`, `Arc` (centre, radius, a0, sweep) and `straight`), `graph.rs` (planar graph of segments: `Graph::build`, `faces()` traced as the original does; `arc_points`), `offset.rs` (`offset_ring` per-edge offsets), `sketch.rs` (a first sketch problem engine: `Problem`, `describe`, `ring_problems`, `parse`, `solve_one`, `to_value`), `tri.rs` (empty).
- Other areas are done by other agents (don't implement them): `modify`, `move`, `copy`, `delete` etc. (EDIT), `inspect`, `elements`, `schedule` (READERS), views/graphics (VIEWS), types/families/structure (STRUCTURE), IFC. Our build does not have them yet, so test your commands through scripts that use only ARCH commands plus `level`, `grid`, `undo`, `redo`, `save`, `open`.
- New elements get their phase/option with `crate::styles::phasing::stamp_new(&s.project, s.now_phase.as_deref(), s.now_option.as_deref(), &mut e)` before insertion (see `walls::make_wall`).

## How to work
Probe the original widely: normal cases, every optional parameter, edge cases, every error and the order of checks (`order.py`), and what the saved file holds (field order, defaults omitted or written, number formatting). Write the code, then compare with `each.py -b` / `fl.py -b` / `cmp.py` until SAME. Error texts must match character for character (numbers in messages are usually Rust's `{}` Display of f64; points `[x, y]`). Keep a list of what still differs.

## Finish

sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-ops')
from exp import build, run

random.seed(25)
rows = []
for c in range(12):
    A = [round(random.uniform(-8000, 8000), random.choice([0, 3])) for _ in range(2)]
    B = [round(random.uniform(-8000, 8000), random.choice([0, 3])) for _ in range(2)]
    text = build(['detail_line {"start": %s, "end": %s}' % (json.dumps(A), json.dumps(B))])
    cmds = []
    pts = []
    for k in range(12):
        u = random.uniform(0.05, 0.95)
        dl = random.choice([0.0, random.uniform(-99, 99)])
        d = (B[0] - A[0], B[1] - A[1])
        L = (d[0] ** 2 + d[1] ** 2) ** 0.5
        n = (-d[1] / L, d[0] / L)
        p = (round(A[0] + d[0] * u + n[0] * dl, 4), round(A[1] + d[1] * u + n[1] * dl, 4))
        pts.append(p)
        cmds.append('split {"id": 100002, "at": [%r, %r]}' % p)
        cmds.append('elements {"category": "line"}')
        cmds.append('undo {}')
    ok, rep, proj = run(text, cmds)
    if not ok:
        continue
    for i, p in enumerate(pts):
        els = json.loads(rep[3 * i + 1])['elements']
        e = [x for x in els if x['id'] == 100002][0]['end']
        rows.append(A + B + list(p) + e)
open('/tmp/edit-ops/an25.txt', 'w').write('\n'.join(' '.join(repr(float(x)) for x in r) for r in rows) + '\n')
print(len(rows))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/params/p1'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, y=0.0, name='W'):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, y, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)]), 3000)])
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w


def beam(f, s, name='B1', ot='Beam 200 x 500'):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, 3000, 2750))
    pos = f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(200, 500), 5000, pos)])
    b = f.add('IFCBEAM', gid(), None, name, None, ot, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('BEAM'))
    f.contain(s, b)
    return b


def a(f):  # Project Parameters of every kind
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {
        'Fire Rating': "IFCLABEL('60 min')",
        'Note': "IFCTEXT('a note')",
        'Cost': 'IFCREAL(12.5)',
        'Count': 'IFCINTEGER(3)',
        'Finish': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(250.)',
        'Thick': 'IFCPOSITIVELENGTHMEASURE(20.)',
        'Ok': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)',
        'Maybe': 'IFCLOGICAL(.U.)',
        'Area': 'IFCAREAMEASURE(2.5)',
        'Id': "IFCIDENTIFIER('X-1')",
    })


def b(f):  # other programs' sets
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'MyCompany_Data', {'Code': "IFCLABEL('A1')", 'Weight': 'IFCREAL(3.5)'})
    f.pset([w], 'Pset_WallCommon', {'IsExternal': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)', 'FireRating': "IFCLABEL('REI 60')", 'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.F.)'})


def c(f):  # eberick on a beam
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    bm = beam(f, s1)
    f.pset([bm], 'AltoQi_Eberick_Viga', {'Fck (MPa)': 'IFCREAL(25.)', 'Seção': "IFCLABEL('20x50')", 'Cobrimento': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(30.)'})
    f.pset([bm], 'Pset_BeamCommon', {'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)', 'Span': 'IFCPOSITIVELENGTHMEASURE(5000.)', 'Reference': "IFCIDENTIFIER('V1')"})
    f.pset([bm], 'Pset_ConcreteElementGeneral', {'ConcreteCover': 'IFCPOSITIVELENGTHMEASURE(25.)', 'StrengthClass': "IFCLABEL('C25')"})


def d(f):  # names with odd characters
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {
        'A/B': "IFCLABEL('x')",
        'c (d)': "IFCLABEL('y')",
        'e-f': "IFCLABEL('z')",
        'g.h': "IFCLABEL('w')",
        '2nd': "IFCLABEL('v')",
        'k_l m': "IFCLABEL('u')",
        'ção': "IFCLABEL('t')",
        '  pad  ': "IFCLABEL('s')",
        'x*y+z': "IFCLABEL('r')",
    })


def e(f):  # same parameter on two kinds; different value kinds
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    w2 = wall(f, s1, 2000, 'W2')
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'P': "IFCLABEL('x')", 'Q': 'IFCREAL(1.5)'})
    f.pset([w2], 'Project Parameters', {'P': 'IFCREAL(2.)', 'Q': 'IFCREAL(2.5)'})
    bm = beam(f, s1)
    f.pset([bm], 'Project Parameters', {'P': "IFCLABEL('b')"})


def g(f):  # metres file
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, 'W', None, None, f.lp(s1.lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -0.1), (5, -0.1), (5, 0.1), (0, 0.1)]), 3)])), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s1, w)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'Len': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(2.5)', 'R': 'IFCREAL(2.5)'})


def h(f):  # pset on the type
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    t = f.add('IFCWALLTYPE', gid(), None, 'WT', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.rel_type(t, [w])
    f.pset([t], 'MyType_Data', {'TypeCode': "IFCLABEL('T1')"})


def i(f):  # nominal value $ / empty string
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'Empty': "IFCLABEL('')", 'Null': '$'})


mk('a_pp', a)
mk('b_other', b)
mk('c_eberick', c)
mk('d_names', d)
mk('e_mixed', e)
mk('g_metres', g, units='m')
mk('h_type', h)
mk('i_empty', i)
print(' '.join(out))

    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2

    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, y, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)]), 3000)])
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w


def beam(f, s, name='B1', ot='Beam 200 x 500'):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, 3000, 2750))
    pos = f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(200, 500), 5000, pos)])
    b = f.add('IFCBEAM', gid(), None, name, None, ot, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('BEAM'))
    f.contain(s, b)
    return b

    w = wall(f, s1)

    f.pset([w], 'Pset_WallCommon', {'IsExternal': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)', 'FireRating': "IFCLABEL('REI 60')", 'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.F.)'})


def c(f):  # eberick on a beam
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    bm = beam(f, s1)
    f.pset([bm], 'AltoQi_Eberick_Viga', {'Fck (MPa)': 'IFCREAL(25.)', 'Seção': "IFCLABEL('20x50')", 'Cobrimento': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(30.)'})
    f.pset([bm], 'Pset_BeamCommon', {'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)', 'Span': 'IFCPOSITIVELENGTHMEASURE(5000.)', 'Reference': "IFCIDENTIFIER('V1')"})
    f.pset([bm], 'Pset_ConcreteElementGeneral', {'ConcreteCover': 'IFCPOSITIVELENGTHMEASURE(25.)', 'StrengthClass': "IFCLABEL('C25')"})


def d(f):  # names with odd characters
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {
        'A/B': "IFCLABEL('x')",
        'c (d)': "IFCLABEL('y')",
        'e-f': "IFCLABEL('z')",
        'g.h': "IFCLABEL('w')",
        '2nd': "IFCLABEL('v')",
        'k_l m': "IFCLABEL('u')",
        'ção': "IFCLABEL('t')",
        '  pad  ': "IFCLABEL('s')",

    })


def e(f):  # same parameter on two kinds; different value kinds
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    w2 = wall(f, s1, 2000, 'W2')
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'P': "IFCLABEL('x')", 'Q': 'IFCREAL(1.5)'})
    f.pset([w2], 'Project Parameters', {'P': 'IFCREAL(2.)', 'Q': 'IFCREAL(2.5)'})
    bm = beam(f, s1)
    f.pset([bm], 'Project Parameters', {'P': "IFCLABEL('b')"})


def g(f):  # metres file
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, 'W', None, None, f.lp(s1.lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -0.1), (5, -0.1), (5, 0.1), (0, 0.1)]), 3)])), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s1, w)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'Len': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(2.5)', 'R': 'IFCREAL(2.5)'})


def h(f):  # pset on the type
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)

    f.rel_type(t, [w])
    f.pset([t], 'MyType_Data', {'TypeCode': "IFCLABEL('T1')"})

    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'Empty': "IFCLABEL('')", 'Null': '$'})

mk('b_other', b)

mk('d_names', d)

mk('h_type', h)
mk('i_empty', i)

import math
def geo(a, b, deg):
    t = math.radians(deg)
    c = math.hypot(b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1])
    r = c/(2*abs(math.sin(t/2)))
    m = ((a[0]+b[0])/2, (a[1]+b[1])/2)
    h = r*math.cos(t/2)
    dx, dy = b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]; l = math.hypot(dx, dy); n = (-dy/l, dx/l)
    s = 1.0 if t > 0 else -1.0
    cen = (m[0]+n[0]*h*s, m[1]+n[1]*h*s)
    a0 = math.atan2(a[1]-cen[1], a[0]-cen[0])
    return cen, r, a0, t
def line_circle(a, b, c, r):
    d = (b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]); l = math.hypot(*d); d = (d[0]/l, d[1]/l)
    f = (a[0]-c[0], a[1]-c[1])
    along = -(f[0]*d[0] + f[1]*d[1])
    foot = (a[0]+d[0]*along, a[1]+d[1]*along)
    h2 = r*r - ((foot[0]-c[0])**2 + (foot[1]-c[1])**2)
    h = math.sqrt(h2)
    return [(foot[0]-d[0]*h, foot[1]-d[1]*h), (foot[0]+d[0]*h, foot[1]+d[1]*h)]

import sys, json
from fractions import Fraction as F
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-ops')
from exp import build, run

A = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[1].split(',')]
B = [float(x) for x in sys.argv[2].split(',')]
dl = float(sys.argv[3])
N = int(sys.argv[4])
text = build(['detail_line {"start": [%r, %r], "end": [%r, %r]}' % (A[0], A[1], B[0], B[1])])
cmds = []
pts = []
d = (B[0] - A[0], B[1] - A[1])
L = (d[0] ** 2 + d[1] ** 2) ** 0.5
n = (-d[1] / L, d[0] / L)
for k in range(1, N):
    u = k / N
    p = (round(A[0] + d[0] * u + n[0] * dl, 6), round(A[1] + d[1] * u + n[1] * dl, 6))
    pts.append((u, p))
    cmds.append('split {"id": 100002, "at": [%r, %r]}' % p)
    cmds.append('elements {"category": "line"}')
    cmds.append('undo {}')
ok, rep, proj = run(text, cmds)
FA = (F(A[0]), F(A[1])); dd = (F(B[0]) - FA[0], F(B[1]) - FA[1])
for i, (u, p) in enumerate(pts):
    els = json.loads(rep[3 * i + 1])['elements']
    e = [x for x in els if x['id'] == 100002][0]['end']
    t = ((F(p[0]) - FA[0]) * dd[0] + (F(p[1]) - FA[1]) * dd[1]) / (dd[0] ** 2 + dd[1] ** 2)
    tr = ((F(e[0]) - FA[0]) * dd[0] + (F(e[1]) - FA[1]) * dd[1]) / (dd[0] ** 2 + dd[1] ** 2)
    print('%.4f  dt=%+.3e  pos err=%+.3e mm' % (u, float(tr - t), float(tr - t) * L))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/params/p2'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, y=0.0, name='W'):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, y, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)]), 3000)])
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w


def a(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Other', {
        'A/B': "IFCLABEL('x')",
        'c (d)': "IFCLABEL('y')",
        'e-f': "IFCLABEL('z')",
        'g.h': "IFCLABEL('w')",
        '2nd': "IFCLABEL('v')",
        'x*y+z': "IFCLABEL('r')",
        'a  b': "IFCLABEL('q')",
        '(only)': "IFCLABEL('p')",
        'Ünï Cödé': "IFCLABEL('o')",
        'tab\tname': "IFCLABEL('n')",
        'x_1': "IFCLABEL('m')",
    })


def b(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Other', {
        'Int': 'IFCINTEGER(3)',
        'Area': 'IFCAREAMEASURE(2.5)',
        'Ident': "IFCIDENTIFIER('X')",
        'Logic': 'IFCLOGICAL(.T.)',
        'Logic2': 'IFCLOGICAL(.U.)',
        'Angle': 'IFCPLANEANGLEMEASURE(0.5)',
        'CountM': 'IFCCOUNTMEASURE(4.)',
        'Ratio': 'IFCPOSITIVERATIOMEASURE(0.5)',
        'Vol': 'IFCVOLUMEMEASURE(2.)',
        'Text': "IFCTEXT('t')",
        'Num': 'IFCNUMERICMEASURE(7.)',
        'Thermal': 'IFCTHERMALTRANSMITTANCEMEASURE(0.3)',
        'Bare': '1.5',
        'BareStr': "'s'",
    })


def c(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Pset_WallCommon', {'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)', 'Status': "IFCLABEL('NEW')", 'Reference': "IFCIDENTIFIER('R')", 'IsExternal': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.F.)'})
    f.pset([w], 'Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {'Length': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(5000.)'})
    f.pset([w], 'BIMCraft_Whatever', {'Thing': "IFCLABEL('x')"})
    f.pset([w], 'BIMCraft_Phasing', {'Phase Created': "IFCLABEL('New Construction')"})


def d(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'Int': 'IFCINTEGER(3)', 'Ident': "IFCIDENTIFIER('X')", 'Area': 'IFCAREAMEASURE(2.5)', 'Text': "IFCTEXT('t')"})


def e(f):  # same property in two psets of one element
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'SetA', {'Same': "IFCLABEL('first')"})
    f.pset([w], 'SetB', {'Same': "IFCLABEL('second')"})


def g(f):  # property name clash with project parameters
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Other', {'Fire Rating': "IFCLABEL('o')"})
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {'Fire Rating': "IFCLABEL('pp')"})


mk('a_names', a)
mk('b_kinds', b)
mk('c_skip', c)
mk('d_pp_kinds', d)
mk('e_twice', e)
mk('g_clash', g)
print(' '.join(out))

def variants(P, Q, cen, deg, t):
    ap = math.atan2(P[1]-cen[1], P[0]-cen[0]); aq = math.atan2(Q[1]-cen[1], Q[0]-cen[0])
    out = {}
    d = aq - ap
    dn = d % (2*math.pi) if t > 0 else -((-d) % (2*math.pi))
    out['deg(dn)'] = math.degrees(dn)
    out['deg(aq)-deg(ap)'] = math.degrees(aq) - math.degrees(ap)
    dd = math.degrees(aq) - math.degrees(ap)
    out['(deg)mod'] = dd % 360.0 if t > 0 else -((-dd) % 360.0)
    # via chord: arc from P to Q on circle radius r: 2*asin(chord/2r)
    r = math.hypot(P[0]-cen[0], P[1]-cen[1])

    x = math.degrees(2*math.asin(min(1, ch/(2*r))))
    out['asin'] = x if t > 0 else -x

    u = (P[0]-cen[0], P[1]-cen[1]); v = (Q[0]-cen[0], Q[1]-cen[1])
    ang = math.atan2(u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0], u[0]*v[0]+u[1]*v[1])

import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/params/p3'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, y=0.0, name='W'):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (0, y, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)]), 3000)])
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w

def a(f):
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Other', {n: "IFCLABEL('v-%s')" % n for n in NAMES})

    s1, s2 = base(f)
    w = wall(f, s1)
    f.pset([w], 'Project Parameters', {n: "IFCLABEL('v-%s')" % n for n in NAMES})

mk('b_reserved_pp', b)

import math
cases = [
    # (T, slope, o, target_geometry_top) base 3000 th 300
    (2550, 30, 0, 5118.653347947322 - 300),
    (3975, 35, 200, 6309.515833370093 - 300),
    (4050, 25, 200, 5426.297859585493 - 300),
    (3350, 25, 200, 5099.882498876994 - 300),
    (3100, 15, 200, 4387.635512173281 - 300),
    (2925, 35, 200, 5574.297918249897 - 300),
    (1850, 35, 200, 4821.574814674458 - 300),
    (3650, 25, 500, 5099.882498876994 - 300),
    # matched before
    (4150, 30, 500, 5453.738644055909),
    (2000, 30, 0, 4501.110699893027),
    (2000, 30, 500, 4212.435565298214),
]
base = 3000.0; th = 300.0
def forms(T, s, o):
    r = math.radians(s)
    r2 = s * math.pi / 180.0
    out = {}
    for rn, rr in (('rad', r), ('pi', r2)):
        t = math.tan(rr); c = math.cos(rr); sn = math.sin(rr)
        for hn, h in (('cos', th / c), ('sqrt', th * math.sqrt(1 + t * t)), ('hyp', th * math.hypot(1.0, t))):
            for tn, tt in (('tan', t), ('sc', sn / c)):
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'E')] = (base + h) + (T - o) * tt
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'F')] = (base + (T - o) * tt) + h
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'G')] = base + ((T - o) * tt + h)
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'H')] = (base - o * tt + h) + T * tt
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'I')] = ((base - o * tt) + T * tt) + h
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'J')] = (base + T * tt - o * tt) + h
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'K')] = (base + h) + T * tt - o * tt
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'L')] = base + (T * tt - o * tt + h)
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'M')] = (base + h - o * tt) + T * tt
                # plane through the eave with normal: z = (c0 - n.p)/nz
                nz = c; ny = -sn
                ze = base - o * tt
                c0 = nz * ze  # eave at y=0
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'P')] = (c0 - ny * T) / nz + h
                out[(rn, hn, tn, 'Q')] = (c0 + nz * h - ny * T) / nz
    return out
res = {}
for (T, s, o, tg) in cases:
    for k, v in forms(T, s, o).items():
        res.setdefault(k, []).append(v == tg)
best = sorted(res.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(kv[1]))[:12]
for k, v in best:
    print(k, sum(v), v)

import sys, json, random
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/loader-agent')
from lib import *
from cmpf import both, compare
from multiprocessing import Pool

src = open(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '/tmp/loader-agent/corpus/house.bimcraft', 'rb').read()
rng = random.Random(7)
cases = []
for i in range(60):
    n = rng.randrange(len(src))
    cases.append(('cut %d' % n, src[:n]))
for i in range(60):
    n = rng.randrange(len(src))
    b = bytearray(src)
    b[n] = rng.choice(b'{}[]:,"x0 -.eE\\\n\t')
    cases.append(('flip %d %r' % (n, chr(b[n])), bytes(b)))
for i in range(20):
    n = rng.randrange(len(src))
    b = bytearray(src)
    b[n:n] = rng.choice([b'\xff', b'\xc3', b'\xe2\x82', b'\x00', b'\xed\xa0\x80'])
    cases.append(('bytes %d' % n, bytes(b)))
cases.append(('bom', b'\xef\xbb\xbf' + src))
cases.append(('crlf', src.replace(b'\n', b'\r\n')))
cases.append(('trailing', src + b' x'))
cases.append(('trailing ws', src + b' \n\t'))
cases.append(('two docs', src + src))


def one(c):
    label, text = c
    o, m = both(text)
    return label, compare(o, m)


with Pool(8) as p:
    res = p.map(one, cases)
bad = 0
for label, d in res:
    if d:
        bad += 1
        print('DIFF', label)
        for l in d[:6]:
            print('    ', l[:250])
print(bad, 'of', len(cases), 'differ')
