Modify Sub Elements picks folding lines too, Revit's name for the creases no split line makes (`Model::shape_folds`,
  `view3d::shape_pick_plan`, `shape_pick_3d`), and Convert Lines makes the selected ones split lines, one way, as Revit's
  does (`SlabShapeEditor.CreateCreasesFromFoldingLines` in its API); tests `a_shapes_folding_lines_*`,
  `convert_lines_makes_a_selected_folding_line_a_split_line`.
- **Phase 4**, flat roofs, is built: a flat roof by footprint takes a shape through the same commands and tools
  (`Model::shapeable` sees its top as a floor's, `Model::roof_as_floor`), its underside following its top plumb
  (`roof_faces`, `roof_rise`), walls attached under it following its falls, its plan creases thin, its points snapped,
  kept by `edit_boundary` and carried by moves and mirrors; a pitched, extruded or joining roof refuses one, saying why
  (`Roof::unshapeable`). `ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has one for IfcOpenShell. Tests: the three `*roof*` tests in
  `shape_tests.rs`, and `a_flat_roof_by_footprint_is_shaped_as_a_floor_is_and_a_pitched_one_isnt` in the desktop's
  `tests/shape3d.rs`. A roof type's variable layer keeps a shaped roof's underside level at its base, as a floor's does
  (`Model::roof_under`, `roof_prisms`, `roof_solid`, `variable_under`): 3D layers, sections, attached walls, IFC (one
  closed Brep; `ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has both kinds) and the check (tests `a_roofs_variable_layer_*`,
  `a_section_shows_a_roofs_insulation_*`, `a_roof_point_that_would_leave_its_insulation_*`).
- **Phase 5**, the extras, is built:
  - **`falls`** (`crates/core/src/falls.rs`): a floor's or flat roof's shape from its drains and the least fall. Each
    drain takes the part of the outline nearer it than any other; where two parts meet a ridge runs at the top's height;
    from each drain a valley runs to each corner of its part; each drain goes down as far as the fall takes its farthest
    corner, to the tenth of a millimetre down. Every plane then falls at least as asked toward a drain, its lowest corner,
    and so does every valley. Round an opening, a valley runs from the drain round the opening's corners by the shortest
    way, each corner on the cone falling from the drain at the fall, so water reaching it runs on down. `ridges` drawn
    (each from the outline, an opening or another ridge to another) split the top into parts first, each needing a drain.
    The command checks every plane falls as asked to a drain or an opening's corner, and refuses, saying where, what
    doesn't. Refused too: a drain outside or in an opening, two within a millimetre, a corner a drain can reach only over
    the outline or a ridge (an L with one drain: add one on the other wing). Tests `falls_to_two_drains_*`,
    `falls_refuse_*`, `falls_run_round_an_opening_*`, `ridges_drawn_split_the_top_*`.
  - **IFC import of a slab whose top isn't one plane** (`import::shaped_top`): a level floor at its highest point, its
    upward faces' outline, each of their corners under that height (or inside) a point, and each edge two of them share at
    an angle a split line; as thick as it is under its highest corner. What doesn't fold into planes, or folds into others
    than its faces (a step), comes in as before. A roof's body read the same way comes in as a shaped flat roof, unless its
    footprint and pitch already make every corner of its top (a pitched roof stays pitched; an extruded one is read by its
    profile). A variable layer goes out with `Description` `'Variable'` and comes back marked; from a file that says
    nothing, a shaped slab whose underside is level gets its insulation nearest the top, else its substrate, marked
    variable. Tests `a_shaped_slab_exported_and_imported_*`, `a_shaped_floor_over_a_variable_layer_comes_back_*`,
    `a_shaped_flat_roof_comes_back_from_ifc_*`.
  - **Spot Slope** (`spot_slope`, `Spot::slope`, `Model::spot_slope`, `top_plane_at`): in a plan, an arrow downhill from
    the point clicked on a floor or a roof, with how steeply its top falls there, following it; Annotate > Dimension's
    Spot Slope places one. Tests `a_spot_slope_reads_*` and the desktop's
    `spot_slope_reads_the_fall_of_a_shaped_floor_where_its_clicked`.

Line numbers are as of `0733fd4`.

## What users expect

The workflow architects know from the established tools, in our own words:

- A floor (or a roof with no sloped edges) gets **points** on its top. Each point has a height relative to the top the
  element would have without them. The corners of the outline are points too, at 0 until raised or lowered.
- **Split lines** cross the top between two points. They are creases the surface must fold along, so the user decides
  where a ridge or a valley runs instead of leaving it to the triangulation.
- The surface between the points and lines is **flat triangles**. The tool picks the creases it needs and draws them
| `type` (floor, roof) | layers take `variable: true` | At most one per type; not on walls or ceilings. |
| `modify` (floor) | unchanged | Rejects `slope` or `arrow` on a shaped floor, with the reason (see Validation). |
| `falls` (phase 5) | `{id, drains: [[x, y], …], fall: 1.5, ridges?: [[[x, y], [x, y]], …]}` | Better than the established tools: sets point heights so water runs to the drains at no less than `fall` %, adding split lines along the valleys. Agents and architects describe a terrace this way, not point by point. |

Every reply lists the pieces' count and the lowest and highest point of the top. `inspect` on a floor already reports
`top: [lo, hi]` (`commands.rs:2122`); it must take the shape's points into account, not only the outline's.

## Validation (`Model::check`)

New rules, each with an error that says what to fix:

- A point outside the outline, or inside an opening: "point 100231 at (12500, 3400) is outside floor 100190: move it inside, or delete it".
- A split line that crosses another, crosses an opening, or leaves the outline (reuse `sketch::solve`'s problem kinds and wording).
- A split line end that is neither a point nor an outline corner.
- Two points within 1 mm of each other.
- A shape on a sloped floor (with `arrow`), or on a roof that isn't by footprint with `slope` 0. In version 1 the two are
  exclusive: shape a level element, and give its slope through the points.
- More than one variable layer in a type.
- **A variable layer thinner than nothing** anywhere: "at point 100231 the screed would be −12 mm: raise the point by 12
  mm or thicken the variable layer".
- With no variable layer, nothing bounds the depth: the slab just follows the top.

## What changes, consumer by consumer

| Consumer | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `Model::floor_slabs` (`model.rs:3755`) | one plane over the outline less openings | built on `floor_faces`; each piece less the openings |
| `Model::roof_faces` (`model.rs:3575`) | a flat roof is one plane | a shaped flat roof returns its pieces; `roof_rise` is plumb for them |
| 3D solids (`view3d.rs:511`, `612`) | `Solid::Slab` per piece | the same for constant thickness; `Solid::Prism` (top facet, flat bottom) with a variable layer |
| 3D layers (`view3d::layered`, `view3d.rs:741`) | a slab's layers in proportion; the `Prism` branch is walls only | a slab `Prism` branch: layers above the variable one from the top, below it from the bottom |
| Section layers (`render.rs:1230`) | each cut quad split in proportion to the layers' thicknesses | the same rule as 3D: fixed layers measured from the top or the bottom edge, the variable one between |
| Plan (`render.rs:1585`) | outline, openings, surface pattern, slope arrow | the pattern over each piece; split lines solid and generated creases dashed, thin, when the element is selected or being edited; each point's height as a label while editing (built as the desktop's overlay, not in `render.rs`, so it never prints) |
| Attached walls (`walls.rs:454`) | one plane over the floor's convex pieces | each piece with its own plane, as the roof branch above it does |
| Shafts (`Model::less_shafts`, `model.rs:3773`) | per slab face | already per face: no change, but a test |
| Move, copy, rotate, mirror (`commands.rs:8236`) | outline, openings, arrow, pattern | the points' `at` and the lines' ends too; a mirror keeps the heights |

import math, sys, json, pickle
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import nextf, ulpdiff
from polarc import geo
rows = pickle.load(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol83.pkl', 'rb'))
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter()
for dl, at, e1, e2 in rows:
    d = json.loads(dl)
    T = d['arc']; a1 = e1['arc']; a2 = e2['arc']; q = tuple(e1['end'])
    L = d['end'][0]
    cen, r, st, t = geo((0.0, 0.0), (L, 0.0), T)
    f0 = a1/T
    fs = [nextf(f0, j) for j in range(-4, 5) if T*nextf(f0, j) == a1 and T*(1 - nextf(f0, j)) == a2]
    ok = any((cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + t*f), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + t*f)) == q for f in fs)
    # ulp offsets of q's coordinates vs ours
    if not ok and fs:
        f = fs[0]
        qq = (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + t*f), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + t*f))
        print('T', T, 'f %.6f' % f, 'dx ulps', ulpdiff(q[0], qq[0]), 'dy ulps', ulpdiff(q[1], qq[1]), 'nfs', len(fs))
    cnt[(T, ok)] += 1
print(sorted(cnt.items()))

import json, math, pickle, sys, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
results = pickle.load(open('/tmp/rebar-agent/cols_rand.pkl', 'rb'))
score = {}
for f, line, res in results:
    if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
    p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1])
    bp = p.get('bars')
    if not bp or not bp.get('hook') or bp.get('jog'): continue
    j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
    elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
    if not t['round']: continue
    cv = p['cover']; ct, cb, cs = (cv['top'], cv['bottom'], cv['sides']) if isinstance(cv, dict) else (cv, cv, cv)
    ds = p['stirrup']['diameter'] if p.get('stirrup') else 0.0
    w = t['width']; hw = w / 2
    d = bp['diameter']
    ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
    hs, he = C.legs(bp['hook'])
    bars = [b['path'] for b in res['bars'] if b['layer'] == 'bars']
    n = bp['count']; r = hw - cs - ds - d / 2
    for thn, th in (('rust', ang * (math.pi / 180.0)),):
        s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
        o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]; ac = [c, s, 0.0]; up = [-s, c, 0.0]
        F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=ac, up=up)
        for i, path in enumerate(bars):
            for phn in ('a',):
                if phn == 'a': phi = 2 * math.pi * i / n
                elif phn == 'b': phi = i * (2 * math.pi / n)
                else: phi = (2 * math.pi / n) * i
                ps, pc = math.sin(phi), math.cos(phi)
                if hs > 0:
                    want = path[0]; tt = path[1][2] - o[2]; hk = hs; foot = path[1]
                else:
                    want = path[-1]; tt = path[-2][2] - o[2]; hk = he; foot = path[-2]
                myfoot = B.at(F, tt, r * pc, r * ps)
                cands = {'frame': B.at(F, tt, r * pc - pc * hk, r * ps - ps * hk), 'radial': B.at(F, tt, (r - hk) * pc, (r - hk) * ps)}
                cands['w1'] = [foot[ii] + ac[ii] * (-pc * hk) + up[ii] * (-ps * hk) for ii in range(3)]
                cands['w2'] = [foot[ii] + (ac[ii] * (-pc * hk) + up[ii] * (-ps * hk)) for ii in range(3)]
                cands['w3'] = [foot[ii] + (ac[ii] * (-pc) + up[ii] * (-ps)) * hk for ii in range(3)]
                cands['w4'] = [foot[ii] - (ac[ii] * pc + up[ii] * ps) * hk for ii in range(3)]
                cands['w5'] = [foot[ii] - ac[ii] * (pc * hk) - up[ii] * (ps * hk) for ii in range(3)]
                cc = [foot[0] - o[0], foot[1] - o[1], 0.0]
                cn = B.normalize(cc)
                cands['w6'] = [foot[ii] - cn[ii] * hk for ii in range(3)]
                cands['radial_world'] = [o[ii] + cn[ii] * (r - hk) + [0, 0, tt][ii] for ii in range(3)]
                cands['radial2'] = B.at(F, tt, pc * (r - hk), ps * (r - hk))
                for k, q in cands.items():
                    key = (thn, phn, k)
                    sc = score.setdefault(key, [0, 0, 0]); sc[1] += 1; sc[0] += (q == want); sc[2] += (myfoot == foot)
for k, v in sorted(score.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]): print(k, v)

import json, math, pickle, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
results = pickle.load(open('/tmp/rebar-agent/cols_rand.pkl', 'rb'))
score = {}
fails = {}
for f, line, res in results:
    if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
    p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1])
    bp = p.get('bars')
    if not bp or not bp.get('hook') or bp.get('jog'): continue
    j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
    elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
    if not t['round']: continue
    cv = p['cover']; ct, cb, cs = (cv['top'], cv['bottom'], cv['sides']) if isinstance(cv, dict) else (cv, cv, cv)
    ds = p['stirrup']['diameter'] if p.get('stirrup') else 0.0
    w = t['width']; hw = w / 2
    d = bp['diameter']
    ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
    hs, he = C.legs(bp['hook'])
    bars = [b['path'] for b in res['bars'] if b['layer'] == 'bars']
    n = bp['count']; r = hw - cs - ds - d / 2
    th = math.radians(ang) if False else ang * (math.pi / 180.0)
    s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
    o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]; ac = [c, s, 0.0]; up = [-s, c, 0.0]
    F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=ac, up=up)
    for i, path in enumerate(bars):
        phi = 2 * math.pi * i / n
        ps, pc = math.sin(phi), math.cos(phi)
        a, b = r * pc, r * ps
        ends = []
        if hs > 1.0: ends.append((path[0], path[1], hs))
        if he > 1.0: ends.append((path[-1], path[-2], he))
        for want, foot, hk in ends:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Round columns at random places and angles, and hook cases for them (rc_SEED.bimcraft / rc_SEED.txt)."""
import sys, random, subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil
seed = int(sys.argv[1]); n = int(sys.argv[2])
rng = random.Random(seed)
cmds = []
sizes = [round(rng.uniform(250, 900), rng.choice([0, 1, 2])) for _ in range(5)]
for k, w in enumerate(sizes):
    cmds.append('type {"category":"structuralcolumn","name":"RC %d","width":%s,"round":true}' % (k, w))
hosts = []
for i in range(10):
    k = rng.randrange(5)
    x = round(rng.uniform(-5000, 5000), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    y = round(rng.uniform(-5000, 5000), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    a = round(rng.uniform(-180, 180), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    cmds.append('structural_column {"at":[%s,%s],"type":"RC %d","angle":%s}' % (x, y, k, a))
    hosts.append((100002 + i, sizes[k]))
out = '/tmp/rebar-agent/rc_%d.bimcraft' % seed
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cl = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
for c in cmds: cl += ['--cmd', c]
cl += ['--save', 'o.bimcraft']
p = subprocess.run(cl, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.stderr: print(p.stderr)
shutil.copy(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft'), out)
shutil.rmtree(d)
cases = []
for _ in range(n):
    h, w = rng.choice(hosts)
    cover = rng.choice([20, 25, 30, 22.5, 37.3])
    dd = rng.choice([10, 12.5, 16, 20, 8.3])
    cnt = rng.randint(3, 12)
    r = w / 2 - cover - dd / 2
    hk = round(rng.uniform(2, 2 * r), rng.choice([0, 1, 3]))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        hook = '%s' % hk
    else:
        hook = '{"below":%s,"above":%s}' % (hk, round(rng.uniform(2, 2 * r), rng.choice([0, 1, 3])))
    cases.append('reinforce {"host":%d,"cover":%s,"bars":{"diameter":%s,"count":%d,"hook":%s},"clearance":1}' % (h, cover, dd, cnt, hook))
open('/tmp/rebar-agent/rc_%d.txt' % seed, 'w').write('@file %s\n' % out + '\n'.join(cases) + '\n')

import json, math, pickle, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
pk = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '/tmp/rebar-agent/rc1.pkl'
results = pickle.load(open(pk, 'rb'))
shown = 0
stats = {}
def ulps(x, y):
    if x == y: return 0
    return round((y - x) / math.ulp(x)) if x != 0 else 99
for f, line, res in results:
    if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
    p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1]); bp = p['bars']
    j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
    elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
    cs = p['cover']; d = bp['diameter']; r = t['width'] / 2 - cs - d / 2; n = bp['count']
    ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
    th = ang * (math.pi / 180.0); s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
    o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]
    F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=[c, s, 0.0], up=[-s, c, 0.0])
    hs, he = C.legs(bp['hook'])
    for i, path in enumerate([b['path'] for b in res['bars'] if b['layer'] == 'bars']):
        phi = 2 * math.pi * i / n
        pc, ps = math.cos(phi), math.sin(phi)
        ends = []
        if hs > 1.0: ends.append((path[0], path[1], hs))
        if he > 1.0: ends.append((path[-1], path[-2], he))
        for want, foot, hk in ends:
            tt = foot[2] - o[2]
            q = B.at(F, tt, (r - hk) * pc, (r - hk) * ps)
            if q != want:
                key = (ulps(q[0], want[0]), ulps(q[1], want[1]))
                stats[key] = stats.get(key, 0) + 1
                if shown < 12:
                    shown += 1
                    la, lb = (r - hk) * pc, (r - hk) * ps
                    print(line[:110], 'i', i, 'ang', ang, 'r', r, 'h', hk)
                    print('    local', la, lb, ' o', o[:2], ' got', q[:2], ' want', want[:2])
print(stats)

import math, sys, json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, os, pickle, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import chypot, ulpdiff, nextf
from polpl import Poly
def orig(cmds):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='a', dir='/tmp/views-lines/scratch')
    args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
    for c in cmds: args += ['--cmd', c]
    args += ['--save', 'o.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    e = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft')))['elements'] if p.returncode == 0 else None
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return e
CACHE = '/tmp/views-lines/pol88.pkl'
if os.path.exists(CACHE):
    rows = pickle.load(open(CACHE, 'rb'))
else:
    rows = []
    for l in open('/tmp/views-lines/t/sc_small.txt'):
        l = l.strip()
        if not l: continue
        dl, at = [x.strip() for x in l.split('|')]
        e = orig(['detail_line ' + dl, 'split {"id":100002,"at":%s}' % at])
        if not e: continue
        rows.append((json.loads(dl), json.loads(at), e['100002'], e.get('100003')))
    pickle.dump(rows, open(CACHE, 'wb'))
SQ5 = math.sqrt(5.0)
def search(P, p, form, Gv):
    D = P.drawn('a')
    best = None
    for k in range(len(D) - 1):
        (ia, fa, ua, A), (ib, fb, ub, B) = D[k], D[k+1]
        dx, dy = B[0]-A[0], B[1]-A[1]
        l2 = dx*dx + dy*dy
        s = ((p[0]-A[0])*dx + (p[1]-A[1])*dy)/l2 if l2 > 0 else 0.0
        s = max(0.0, min(1.0, s))
        Q = (A[0] + s*dx, A[1] + s*dy)
        dd = chypot(p[0]-Q[0], p[1]-Q[1])
        if best is None or dd < best[0]: best = (dd, ua + s*(ub - ua))
    dch, uc = best
    rng = float(len(P.segs))
    h = rng/len(D)
    a, b = max(uc - h, 0.0), min(uc + h, rng)
    Df = lambda u: (lambda c: chypot(c[0]-p[0], c[1]-p[1]))(P.at_u(u, 'a'))
    for _ in range(40):
        w = b - a
        if form == 0: c = b - Gv*w; d = a + Gv*w
        elif form == 1: c = a + (1 - Gv)*w; d = a + Gv*w
        elif form == 2: c = b - Gv*w; d = b - (1 - Gv)*w
        elif form == 3: c = a + (1 - Gv)*w; d = b - (1 - Gv)*w
        elif form == 4: c = b - w*Gv; d = a + w*Gv
        if Df(c) < Df(d): b = d
        else: a = c
    u = (a + b)/2
    q = P.at_u(u, 'a')
    if chypot(q[0]-p[0], q[1]-p[1]) < dch: return u, q
    return uc, P.at_u(uc, 'a')
for form in range(5):
    for gn, Gv in [('lit', 0.618033988749895), ('g1', (SQ5 - 1)/2)]:
        ok = 0; okq = 0
        for dl, p, e1, e2 in rows:
            if 'points' in dl: P = Poly(dl['points'], dl['arcs'])
            else: P = Poly([dl['start'], dl['end']], [dl['arc']])
            u, q = search(P, tuple(p), form, Gv)
            T = P.segs[0][2]
            a1 = e1['arc'] if 'arc' in e1 else e1['arcs'][-1]
            qo = tuple(e1['end']) if 'end' in e1 else tuple(e1['points'][-1])
            if T*u == a1: ok += 1
            if q == qo: okq += 1
        print(form, gn, 'arc', ok, 'pt', okq, len(rows))

import json, math, pickle, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
pks = sys.argv[1:] or ['/tmp/rebar-agent/rc1.pkl']
score = {}
def nrm(v):
    L = math.sqrt(v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1] + v[2] * v[2]); k = 1.0 / L
    return [v[0] * k, v[1] * k, v[2] * k]
def nrm2(v):
    L = math.sqrt(v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1])
    return [v[0] / L, v[1] / L, 0.0]
for pk in pks:
    results = pickle.load(open(pk, 'rb'))
    for f, line, res in results:
        if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
        p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1]); bp = p.get('bars')
        if not bp or not bp.get('hook') or bp.get('jog'): continue
        j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
        elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
        if not t['round']: continue
        cv = p['cover']; cs = cv if not isinstance(cv, dict) else cv['sides']
        ds = p['stirrup']['diameter'] if p.get('stirrup') else 0.0
        d = bp['diameter']; r = t['width'] / 2 - cs - ds - d / 2; n = bp['count']
        ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
        th = ang * (math.pi / 180.0); s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
        o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]
        ac = [c, s, 0.0]; up = [-s, c, 0.0]
        F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=ac, up=up)
        hs, he = C.legs(bp['hook'])
        for i, path in enumerate([b['path'] for b in res['bars'] if b['layer'] == 'bars']):
            phi = 2 * math.pi * i / n
            pc, ps = math.cos(phi), math.sin(phi)
            ends = []
            if hs > 1.0: ends.append((path[0], path[1], hs))
            if he > 1.0: ends.append((path[-1], path[-2], he))
            for want, fw, h in ends:
                tt = fw[2] - o[2]
                cw = B.at(F, tt, 0.0, 0.0)
                cands = {}
                cands['radial'] = B.at(F, tt, (r - h) * pc, (r - h) * ps)
                cands['W1'] = [cw[q] + (fw[q] - cw[q]) * ((r - h) / r) for q in range(3)]
                cands['W2'] = [fw[q] + (cw[q] - fw[q]) * (h / r) for q in range(3)]
                u = nrm([cw[q] - fw[q] for q in range(3)])
                cands['W3'] = [fw[q] + u[q] * h for q in range(3)]
                u2 = nrm([fw[q] - cw[q] for q in range(3)])
                cands['W4'] = [fw[q] - u2[q] * h for q in range(3)]
                cands['W5'] = [cw[q] + u2[q] * (r - h) for q in range(3)]
                u3 = nrm2([cw[q] - fw[q] for q in range(3)])
                cands['W6'] = [fw[q] + u3[q] * h for q in range(3)]
                rd = [ac[q] * pc + up[q] * ps for q in range(3)]
                cands['W7'] = [fw[q] - rd[q] * h for q in range(3)]
                cands['W8'] = [cw[q] + rd[q] * (r - h) for q in range(3)]
                cands['W9'] = [o[q] + rd[q] * (r - h) + [0, 0, tt][q] for q in range(3)]
                rdn = nrm(rd)
                cands['W10'] = [fw[q] - rdn[q] * h for q in range(3)]
                for kk, qv in cands.items():
                    key = kk
                    sc = score.setdefault(key, [0, 0]); sc[1] += 1; sc[0] += (qv == want)
for k, v in sorted(score.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]): print(k, v)

import math, sys, json, pickle, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import chypot, ulpdiff, nextf
from polpl import Poly
exec(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol88.py').read().split('for form in range(5):')[0].split("CACHE = ")[0])
rows = pickle.load(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol88.pkl', 'rb'))
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('p88', '/tmp/views-lines/pol88.py')
src = open('/tmp/views-lines/pol88.py').read().split('for form in range(5):')[0]
ns = {}
exec(src, ns)
search = ns['search']
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter()
for dl, p, e1, e2 in rows:
    if 'points' in dl: P = Poly(dl['points'], dl['arcs'])
    else: P = Poly([dl['start'], dl['end']], [dl['arc']])
    u, q = search(P, tuple(p), 0, 0.618033988749895)
    T = P.segs[0][2]
    a1 = e1['arc'] if 'arc' in e1 else e1['arcs'][-1]
    a2 = None
    if e2 is not None:
        a2 = e2['arc'] if 'arc' in e2 else e2['arcs'][0]
    g = 1.0 - u
    C = {
      'T*u': T*u,
      'T*(1-(1-u))': T*(1.0 - g),
      'T-T*(1-u)': T - T*g,
    }
    for k, v in C.items():
        cnt[(k, v == a1)] += 1
    if a2 is not None:
        cnt[('a2=T*(1-u)', T*g == a2)] += 1
print(sorted(cnt.items()))

from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c69'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn):
    f = F('IFC4', 'mm')
    f.header()
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    fn(f, s2)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


A = math.radians(30)


def roof(f, s, parts):
    rf = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, 'Roof', None, None, f.lp(s.lp), None, None, E('GABLE_ROOF'))
    f.contain(s, rf)
    f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, rf, tuple(parts))


def slab(f, s, items):
    return f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Roof slope', None, None, f.lp(s.lp), f.pds(f.shape(items)), None, E('ROOF'))



def swept(f, s, prof):
    rf = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, 'Roof', None, None, f.lp(s.lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb(prof), 12000, pos=f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0)))])), None, E('GABLE_ROOF'))
    f.contain(s, rf)


T30 = math.tan(math.radians(30))



def under(deg):
    def fn(f, s):
        swept(f, s, [(0, 0), (5000, 5000 * math.tan(math.radians(deg))), (10000, 0), (10000, 300), (5000, 300 + 5000 * T30), (0, 300)])
    return fn


for deg in (29.9, 29.5, 29, 28, 27, 25, 31, 32, 34):
    mk('u%s' % str(deg).replace('.', 'p'), under(deg))
print(' '.join(out))

import json, math, pickle, sys, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
pks = sys.argv[1:] or ['/tmp/rebar-agent/rc1.pkl']
score = {}
allm = 0; tot = 0
none = []
for pk in pks:
    results = pickle.load(open(pk, 'rb'))
    for f, line, res in results:
        if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
        p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1]); bp = p.get('bars')
        if not bp or not bp.get('hook') or bp.get('jog'): continue
        j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
        elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
        if not t['round']: continue
        cv = p['cover']; cs = cv if not isinstance(cv, dict) else cv['sides']
        ds = p['stirrup']['diameter'] if p.get('stirrup') else 0.0
        d = bp['diameter']; r = t['width'] / 2 - cs - ds - d / 2; n = bp['count']
        ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
        th = ang * (math.pi / 180.0); s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
        o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]
        F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=[c, s, 0.0], up=[-s, c, 0.0])
        hs, he = C.legs(bp['hook'])
        for i, path in enumerate([b['path'] for b in res['bars'] if b['layer'] == 'bars']):
            phi = 2 * math.pi * i / n
            pc, ps = math.cos(phi), math.sin(phi)
            a, b = r * pc, r * ps
            ends = []
            if hs > 1.0: ends.append((path[0], path[1], hs))
            if he > 1.0: ends.append((path[-1], path[-2], he))
            for want, fw, h in ends:
                tt = fw[2] - o[2]
                L = math.sqrt(a * a + b * b)
                cands = {
                    'radial': ((r - h) * pc, (r - h) * ps),
                    'frame': (a - pc * h, b - ps * h),
                    'scale': (a * ((r - h) / r), b * ((r - h) / r)),
                    'scale5': (a * (r - h) / r, b * (r - h) / r),
                    'scale6': ((a / r) * (r - h), (b / r) * (r - h)),
                    'scale7': ((r - h) / r * a, (r - h) / r * b),
                    'unitL': ((a / L) * (r - h), (b / L) * (r - h)),
                    'unitLk': ((a * (1 / L)) * (r - h), (b * (1 / L)) * (r - h)),
                    'unitL2': (a - (a / L) * h, b - (b / L) * h),
                    'unitL2k': (a - (a * (1 / L)) * h, b - (b * (1 / L)) * h),
                    'unitR': (a - (a / r) * h, b - (b / r) * h),
                    'unitRk': (a + (-a * (1 / r)) * h, b + (-b * (1 / r)) * h),
                }
                tot += 1
                ok = []
                for kk, (aa, uu) in cands.items():
                    qv = B.at(F, tt, aa, uu)
                    m = qv == want
                    sc = score.setdefault(kk, [0, 0]); sc[1] += 1; sc[0] += m
                    if m: ok.append(kk)
                if not ok: none.append((line[:100], i, n, r, h))
for k, v in sorted(score.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]): print(k, v)
print('none match', len(none), 'of', tot)
for x in none[:10]: print(x)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Columns (rectangular and round) at random places and angles, and jog cases (jg_SEED.bimcraft / .txt)."""
import sys, random, subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil
seed = int(sys.argv[1]); n = int(sys.argv[2])
rng = random.Random(seed)
cmds = []
types = []
for k in range(4):
    w = round(rng.uniform(250, 900), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    dp = round(rng.uniform(250, 900), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    cmds.append('type {"category":"structuralcolumn","name":"Q %d","width":%s,"depth":%s}' % (k, w, dp))
    types.append(('Q %d' % k, w, dp, False))
for k in range(3):
    w = round(rng.uniform(300, 900), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    cmds.append('type {"category":"structuralcolumn","name":"R %d","width":%s,"round":true}' % (k, w))
    types.append(('R %d' % k, w, w, True))
hosts = []
for i in range(14):
    ty = rng.choice(types)
    x = round(rng.uniform(-5000, 5000), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    y = round(rng.uniform(-5000, 5000), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))
    a = round(rng.uniform(-180, 180), rng.choice([0, 1, 2])) if rng.random() < 0.8 else 0
    hgt = round(rng.uniform(2500, 4000), rng.choice([0, 1]))
    cmds.append('structural_column {"at":[%s,%s],"type":"%s","angle":%s,"height":%s}' % (x, y, ty[0], a, hgt))
    hosts.append((100002 + i, ty, hgt))
out = '/tmp/rebar-agent/jg_%d.bimcraft' % seed
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cl = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
for c in cmds: cl += ['--cmd', c]
cl += ['--save', 'o.bimcraft']
p = subprocess.run(cl, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.stderr: print(p.stderr)
shutil.copy(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft'), out)
shutil.rmtree(d)
cases = []
for _ in range(n):
    h, ty, hgt = rng.choice(hosts)
    cover = rng.choice([20, 25, 30, 22.5, 37.3])
    dd = rng.choice([10, 12.5, 16, 20, 8.3])
    by = round(rng.uniform(5, 60), rng.choice([0, 1, 3]))
    ft = round(rng.uniform(300, hgt / 2), rng.choice([0, 1, 3]))
    jog = '{"by":%s,"from_top":%s%s}' % (by, ft, (',"slope":%s' % round(rng.uniform(1, 12), rng.choice([0, 1, 2]))) if rng.random() < 0.5 else '')
    if ty[3]:
        bars = '"diameter":%s,"count":%d' % (dd, rng.randint(6, 12))
    else:
        bars = '"diameter":%s,"x":%d,"y":%d' % (dd, rng.randint(2, 4), rng.randint(2, 4))
    hook = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        hook = ',"hook":%s' % round(rng.uniform(5, 150), rng.choice([0, 1]))
    anchor = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        anchor = ',"anchor":{"below":%s,"above":%s}' % (round(rng.uniform(0, 600), 1), round(rng.uniform(0, 600), 1))
    cases.append('reinforce {"host":%d,"cover":%s,"bars":{%s,"jog":%s%s}%s,"clearance":1}' % (h, cover, bars, jog, hook, anchor))
open('/tmp/rebar-agent/jg_%d.txt' % seed, 'w').write('@file %s\n' % out + '\n'.join(cases) + '\n')

import json, math, pickle, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
pks = sys.argv[1:] or ['/tmp/rebar-agent/jg1.pkl']
score = {}
ex = {}
def spread(a, b, n):
    if n == 1: return [(a + b) / 2]
    return [a + (b - a) * i / (n - 1) for i in range(n)]
for pk in pks:
    results = pickle.load(open(pk, 'rb'))
    for f, line, res in results:
        if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
        p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1]); bp = p.get('bars')
        if not bp or not bp.get('jog'): continue
        j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
        elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
        cv = p['cover']; cs = cv if not isinstance(cv, dict) else cv['sides']
        ds = p['stirrup']['diameter'] if p.get('stirrup') else 0.0
        d = bp['diameter']
        ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
        th = ang * (math.pi / 180.0); s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
        o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]
        ac = [c, s, 0.0]; up = [-s, c, 0.0]
        F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=ac, up=up)
        hs, he = C.legs(bp.get('hook'))
        by = bp['jog']['by']
        places = []
        if t['round']:
            n = bp['count']; r = t['width'] / 2 - cs - ds - d / 2
            for i in range(n):

from fractions import Fraction as Fr
# exact natural cubic interpolation through (0,0),(1000,500),(2000,0) at params s; returns control points
def solve_exact(s, pts):
    # unknowns: 5 control points; equations: interpolation at s0,s1,s2 + second derivative 0 at both ends
    import itertools
    kn = [s[0]]*4 + [s[1]] + [s[2]]*4
    def basis(u, i, p, k):
        # Cox-de Boor exact
        if p == 0:
            if kn[i] <= u < kn[i+1] or (u == kn[-1] and kn[i] < u <= kn[i+1]): return Fr(1)
            return Fr(0)
        a = Fr(0)
        if kn[i+p] != kn[i]: a += (u - kn[i])/(kn[i+p] - kn[i])*basis(u, i, p-1, k)
        if kn[i+p+1] != kn[i+1]: a += (kn[i+p+1] - u)/(kn[i+p+1] - kn[i+1])*basis(u, i+1, p-1, k)
        return a
    n = 5
    rows = []
    for j in range(3):
        rows.append([basis(Fr(s[j]), i, 3, 0) for i in range(n)])
    # second derivative at ends for clamped cubic: P0..P2 at start: 6/(d1 d2) etc; use finite formula
    d = s[1] - s[0]
    # for knots [0,0,0,0,a,b,b,b,b]: C''(0) = 6/(a*a)... derive numerically via exact second difference of basis? simpler: use known formula
    # C''(0) = 6/(t4-t1) * [ (P2-P1)/(t5-t2) - (P1-P0)/(t4-t1) ] for p=3 with t1=t2=t3=0
    t = kn
    r0 = [Fr(0)]*n
    A = Fr(6)/(t[4]-t[1]); B1 = Fr(1)/(t[5]-t[2]); B0 = Fr(1)/(t[4]-t[1])
    r0[0] = A*B0; r0[1] = -A*(B0 + B1); r0[2] = A*B1
    rn = [Fr(0)]*n
    # end: symmetric
    A = Fr(6)/(t[7]-t[4]); C1 = Fr(1)/(t[7]-t[4]); C0 = Fr(1)/(t[6]-t[3])
    rn[4] = A*C1; rn[3] = -A*(C1 + C0); rn[2] = A*C0
    M = rows + [r0, rn]
    rhs = [Fr(p) for p in pts] + [Fr(0), Fr(0)]
    # gaussian exact
    m = len(M)
    Aug = [M[i] + [rhs[i]] for i in range(m)]
    for c in range(m):
        piv = next(r for r in range(c, m) if Aug[r][c] != 0)
        Aug[c], Aug[piv] = Aug[piv], Aug[c]
        for r in range(m):
            if r != c and Aug[r][c] != 0:
                f = Aug[r][c]/Aug[c][c]
                Aug[r] = [Aug[r][k] - f*Aug[c][k] for k in range(m+1)]
    return [Aug[i][m]/Aug[i][i] for i in range(m)]
for s in [[0, 0.5, 1], [0, 1118.033988749895, 2236.06797749979]]:
    sx = solve_exact([Fr(v) for v in s], [0, 1000, 2000])
    sy = solve_exact([Fr(v) for v in s], [0, 500, 0])
    ctrl = [[float(a), float(b)] for a, b in zip(sx, sy)]
    kn = [float(s[0])]*4 + [float(s[1])] + [float(s[2])]*4
    print('s', s, 'ctrl', ctrl)
    for k in [16, 28, 36, 47]:
        u = s[0] + (s[1] - s[0])*k/256
        print('   k', k, deboor_v(ctrl, kn, 3, u, 'mix'))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c66'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn):
    f = F('IFC4', 'mm')
    f.header()
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    fn(f, s2)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


A = math.radians(30)


def roof(f, s, parts):
    rf = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, 'Roof', None, None, f.lp(s.lp), None, None, E('GABLE_ROOF'))
    f.contain(s, rf)
    f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, rf, tuple(parts))


def slab(f, s, items):
    return f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Roof slope', None, None, f.lp(s.lp), f.pds(f.shape(items)), None, E('ROOF'))


def a(f, s):  # each slope extruded square to it (as IfcOpenShell does)
    parts = []
    L = 5000 / math.cos(A)
    for sgn in (1, -1):
        prof = f.arb([(0, 0), (12000, 0), (12000, L), (0, L)])
        if sgn == 1:
            pos = f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (0, -math.sin(A), math.cos(A)), (1, 0, 0))
        else:
            pos = f.ax3((12000, 10000, 0), (0, math.sin(A), math.cos(A)), (-1, 0, 0))
        parts.append(slab(f, s, [f.extrude(prof, 250, pos=pos)]))
    roof(f, s, parts)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rotated hip roofs: the original's eave-corner heights (signs) per face, saved for formula search.
usage: roofprobe.py SEED N OUT.json"""
import json, math, random, re, subprocess, sys
seed, N, out = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
random.seed(seed)
D = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/probe'
roofs = []
for k in range(N):
    cx, cy = 30000.0 * (k % 10) + random.uniform(-500, 500), 30000.0 * (k // 10) + random.uniform(-500, 500)
    w, h = random.uniform(4000, 12000), random.uniform(3000, 8000)
    ang = random.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
    c, s = math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)
    pts = []
    for (u, v) in [(-w / 2, -h / 2), (w / 2, -h / 2), (w / 2, h / 2), (-w / 2, h / 2)]:
        pts.append([round(cx + u * c - v * s, 6), round(cy + u * s + v * c, 6)])
    lev = random.choice(['Level 1', 'Level 2'])
    slope = random.choice([20, 30, 35, 45])
    r = {"boundary": pts, "slope": slope, "level": lev}
    if random.random() < 0.3:
        r["offset"] = random.choice([100, 250, -300])
    roofs.append(r)
cmds = ['roof ' + json.dumps(r) for r in roofs]
open(D + '/roofprobe.txt', 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', D + '/roofprobe.txt', '--save', D + '/roofprobe.ifc'], capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.returncode:
    print(p.stderr[:2000]); sys.exit(1)
s = open(D + '/roofprobe.ifc').read()
ents = {int(m.group(1)): (m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in re.finditer(r'^#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', s, re.M)}
def refs(t): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', t)]
rf = [e for e in sorted(ents) if ents[e][0] == 'IFCROOF']
res = []
for r, e in zip(roofs, rf):
    shape = refs(ents[e][1])[1]
    pieces = []
    for rep in refs(ents[shape][1]):
        for item in refs(ents[rep][1])[1:]:
            if ents[item][0] != 'IFCFACETEDBREP':
                continue
            shell = refs(ents[item][1])[0]
            faces = refs(ents[shell][1])
            bound = refs(ents[faces[0]][1])[0]
            loop = refs(ents[bound][1])[0]
            pts = [ents[x][1].strip('()') for x in refs(ents[loop][1])][::-1]
            pieces.append(pts)
    res.append({'roof': r, 'pieces': pieces})
json.dump(res, open(out, 'w'))
print('roofs', len(res))

import math, sys, io, contextlib

        dx, dy = b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]
        s.append(s[-1] + math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy))
    return s
def span(knots, n, p, u):
    if u >= knots[n]:
        k = n - 1
        while k > p and knots[k] == knots[k+1]: k -= 1
        return k
    if u <= knots[p]:
        k = p
        while k < n - 1 and knots[k] == knots[k+1]: k += 1
        return k
    lo, hi = p, n
    mid = (lo + hi)//2
    while u < knots[mid] or u >= knots[mid+1]:
        if u < knots[mid]: hi = mid
        else: lo = mid
        mid = (lo + hi)//2
    return mid
def basis_ders(knots, p, k, u, nd):
    ndu = [[0.0]*(p+1) for _ in range(p+1)]
    left = [0.0]*(p+1); right = [0.0]*(p+1)

    for j in range(1, p+1):
        left[j] = u - knots[k+1-j]
        right[j] = knots[k+j] - u
        saved = 0.0
        for r in range(j):
            ndu[j][r] = right[r+1] + left[j-r]
            temp = 0.0 if ndu[j][r] == 0.0 else ndu[r][j-1]/ndu[j][r]
            ndu[r][j] = saved + right[r+1]*temp
            saved = left[j-r]*temp
        ndu[j][j] = saved
    ders = [[0.0]*(p+1) for _ in range(nd+1)]
    for j in range(p+1): ders[0][j] = ndu[j][p]
    a = [[0.0]*(p+1) for _ in range(2)]
    for r in range(p+1):
        s1, s2 = 0, 1
        a[0][0] = 1.0
        for kk in range(1, min(nd, p)+1):
            d = 0.0
            rk = r - kk; pk = p - kk
            if r >= kk:

                a[s2][0] = 0.0 if den == 0.0 else a[s1][0]/den
                d = a[s2][0]*ndu[rk][pk]

                d += a[s2][kk]*ndu[r][pk]

    if order == 'interp-first':

                b[r] = [b[r][0] - f*b[c][0], b[r][1] - f*b[c][1]]
    x = [[0.0, 0.0] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n-1, -1, -1):
        sx, sy = b[i]
        for k in range(i+1, n):
            sx -= a[i][k]*x[k][0]; sy -= a[i][k]*x[k][1]
        x[i] = [sx/a[i][i], sy/a[i][i]]
    return x
def solve_lu(a, b):
    # Doolittle LU with partial pivoting, then forward/back substitution
    import copy
    n = len(a); A = [r[:] for r in a]; P = list(range(n))
    for c in range(n):
        piv = max(range(c, n), key=lambda r: abs(A[r][c]))
        A[c], A[piv] = A[piv], A[c]; P[c], P[piv] = P[piv], P[c]
        for r in range(c+1, n):
            A[r][c] /= A[c][c]
            for k in range(c+1, n): A[r][k] -= A[r][c]*A[c][k]
    bb = [b[P[i]][:] for i in range(n)]
    y = [[0.0, 0.0] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        sx, sy = bb[i]
        for k in range(i): sx -= A[i][k]*y[k][0]; sy -= A[i][k]*y[k][1]
        y[i] = [sx, sy]
    x = [[0.0, 0.0] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n-1, -1, -1):
        sx, sy = y[i]
        for k in range(i+1, n): sx -= A[i][k]*x[k][0]; sy -= A[i][k]*x[k][1]
        x[i] = [sx/A[i][i], sy/A[i][i]]
    return x
SOLVERS = {'gj': solve_gj, 'ge': solve_ge, 'ge-nopiv': lambda a, b: solve_ge(a, b, False), 'lu': solve_lu}

            for k in range(c+1, n): A[r][k] -= A[r][c]*A[c][k]
    bb = [b[P[i]][:] for i in range(n)]
    y = [[0.0, 0.0] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):

        for k in range(i): sx -= A[i][k]*y[k][0]; sy -= A[i][k]*y[k][1]

        for k in range(i+1, n): sx -= A[i][k]*x[k][0]; sy -= A[i][k]*x[k][1]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The first edge event of a quad's straight skeleton, in high precision and in several float
ways, to compare with the original's written ridge points."""
import json, sys, math
from decimal import Decimal as D, getcontext
getcontext().prec = 60
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
idx = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0
b = [tuple(map(float, p)) for p in d[idx]['roof']['boundary']]
print('pieces', d[idx]['pieces'])
n = len(b)
def hp():
    P = [(D(x), D(y)) for x, y in b]
    E = []
    for i in range(n):
        a, c = P[i], P[(i + 1) % n]
        ex, ey = c[0] - a[0], c[1] - a[1]
        l = (ex * ex + ey * ey).sqrt()
        dx, dy = ex / l, ey / l
        E.append((a, (dx, dy), (-dy, dx)))
    V = []
    for i in range(n):
        e1, e2 = E[(i - 1) % n], E[i]
        n1, n2 = e1[2], e2[2]
        det = n1[0] * n2[1] - n1[1] * n2[0]
        vx = (1 * n2[1] - 1 * n1[1]) / det
        vy = (n1[0] * 1 - n2[0] * 1) / det
        V.append((vx, vy))
    res = []
    for i in range(n):
        j = (i + 1) % n
        dd = E[i][1]
        rate = (V[j][0] - V[i][0]) * dd[0] + (V[j][1] - V[i][1]) * dd[1]
        if rate < 0:
            ln = (P[j][0] - P[i][0]) * dd[0] + (P[j][1] - P[i][1]) * dd[1]
            t = ln / (-rate)
            res.append((t, i, (P[i][0] + V[i][0] * t, P[i][1] + V[i][1] * t), (P[j][0] + V[j][0] * t, P[j][1] + V[j][1] * t)))
    res.sort()
    return res
for t, i, x, y in hp()[:2]:
    print('hp edge', i, 't', t, 'pt from i', [str(round(v, 9)) for v in x], 'from j', [str(round(v, 9)) for v in y])

    if mode == 'div': s = [x/Lt for x in s]
    elif mode == 'mul': s = [x*(1.0/Lt) for x in s]
    knots = [s[0]]*4 + s[1:m] + [s[m]]*4
    n = m + 3
    def row(u, d):
        k = span(knots, n, 3, u)
        ders = basis_ders(knots, 3, k, u, d)

        for j in range(4): r[k-3+j] = ders[d][j]

import sys, json, subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil, pickle, concurrent.futures
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-add01394c801ae7f2/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
results = pickle.load(open(sys.argv[1], 'rb'))
flt = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 and not sys.argv[2].startswith('-') else None
verbose = '-v' in sys.argv
def run(item):
    f, line, res = item
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); shutil.copy(f, d)
    cl = [MINE, 'run', os.path.basename(f)]
    for x in line.split(' ;; '): cl += ['--cmd', x]
    cl += ['--save', 'o.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(cl, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    mine = {'stderr': p.stderr.strip(), 'stdout': p.stdout}
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft')):
        j = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft')))
        mine['bars'] = [v for k, v in j['elements'].items() if v['category'] == 'rebar']
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return f, line, res, mine
items = [r for r in results if not flt or flt in r[1]]
stats = {}; nok = 0; firsts = {}
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    for f, line, o, m in ex.map(run, items):
        if o['stderr'] or m['stderr']:
            if o['stderr'] == m['stderr'] and o['stdout'] == m['stdout']: nok += 1; continue
            key = ('error', o['stderr'][:70] if o['stderr'] else 'orig ok', m['stderr'][:70] if m['stderr'] else 'mine ok')
            stats[key] = stats.get(key, 0) + 1
            firsts.setdefault(key, line)
            continue

from fitsolve import *
exec(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol93.py').read().split('for mode, order')[0].split("data = pickle")[0])
src = open('/tmp/views-lines/pol93.py').read()
ns = {}
exec(src.split('for mode, order')[0], ns)
system_norm = ns['system_norm']; data = ns['data']
for dl, i, e1, e2 in data:
    fit = [list(map(float, p)) for p in dl['fit']]
    st = dl.get('start_tangent'); et = dl.get('end_tangent')
    A, B, kn, s = system_norm(fit, st, et, 'interp-first', 'div')
    ctrl = solve_ge(A, B)
    u0, uc, u1 = s[0], s[i], s[-1]
    L1 = [tuple(deboor_v(ctrl, kn, 3, u0 + (uc - u0)*k/256, 'mix')) for k in range(257)]
    L2 = [tuple(deboor_v(ctrl, kn, 3, uc + (u1 - uc)*k/256, 'mix')) for k in range(257)]
    h1 = sum(1 for p in e1['fit'] if tuple(p) in set(L1)); h2 = sum(1 for p in e2['fit'] if tuple(p) in set(L2))
    print(dl, i, 'piece1 %d/%d piece2 %d/%d' % (h1, len(e1['fit']), h2, len(e2['fit'])), 'ctrl', ctrl[:3])
    # nearest sample to the first few original points
    for p in e1['fit'][1:4]:
        best = min(L1, key=lambda q: (q[0]-p[0])**2 + (q[1]-p[1])**2)
        print('    orig', p, 'ours', best)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""batch.py cases.txt [-v]: each line 'fixture|cmd ;; cmd ...' (fixture a path; '-' for none);
runs cmp.py on `run in.bimcraft --cmd ... --save out.bimcraft` and prints SAME/DIFF per line."""
import os, subprocess, sys
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a408f9f6869b9e8e8/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
verbose = '-v' in sys.argv
args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != '-v']
lines = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(args[0]) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
env = dict(os.environ, MINE=MINE)
nd = 0
for l in lines:
    fx, cmds = l.split('|', 1)
    fx = fx.strip()
    cl = []
    files = []
    for f in ('red.png', 'green.png', 'blue.png'):
        files += ['-f', '/tmp/edit-library/' + f]
    run = ['run']
    if fx != '-':
        files += ['-f', fx]
        run.append(os.path.basename(fx))
    for c in cmds.split(' ;; '):
        run += ['--cmd', c.strip()]
    run += ['--save', 'out.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/tools/cmp.py'] + files + ['--'] + run, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    res = p.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    ok = res and res[-1] == 'SAME'
    if not ok:
        nd += 1
    print(('SAME ' if ok else 'DIFF ') + l[:250])

"""Run a batch of comparisons: batch.py name  (reads /tmp/edit-files/batches/<name>.py, which defines S
as a list of (files, args) or (files, args, cwd_sub))."""
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/edit-files')
from cmp2 import compare

name = sys.argv[1]
only = [int(x) for x in sys.argv[2:]]
ns = {}
exec(open('/tmp/edit-files/batches/%s.py' % name).read(), ns)
S = ns['S']
n_ok = 0
for i, sc in enumerate(S):
    if only and i not in only:
        continue
    files, args = sc[0], sc[1]
    cwd = sc[2] if len(sc) > 2 else None
    ok, rep = compare(files, args, cwd)
    n_ok += ok
    print('#%d %s %s' % (i, 'SAME' if ok else 'DIFF', ' '.join(a for a in args if a != '--cmd')[:230]))
    if not ok:
        for l in rep[:int(os.environ.get('N', '20'))]:
            print('    ' + l[:300])
print('%d/%d same' % (n_ok, len(only) if only else len(S)))

import json, math, pickle, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import pycol as C, beam_lib as B
pks = sys.argv[1:] or ['/tmp/rebar-agent/jg1.pkl']
score = {}
ex = {}
def spread(a, b, n):
    if n == 1: return [(a + b) / 2]
    return [a + (b - a) * i / (n - 1) for i in range(n)]
def add(p, q): return [p[0] + q[0], p[1] + q[1], p[2] + q[2]]
def sub(p, q): return [p[0] - q[0], p[1] - q[1], p[2] - q[2]]
def mul(p, k): return [p[0] * k, p[1] * k, p[2] * k]
for pk in pks:
    results = pickle.load(open(pk, 'rb'))
    for f, line, res in results:
        if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
        p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1]); bp = p.get('bars')
        if not bp or not bp.get('jog'): continue
        j0 = C.load(f); e = j0['elements'][str(p['host'])]
        elev, t, base, top = C.col_geom(j0, e)
        cv = p['cover']; cs = cv if not isinstance(cv, dict) else cv['sides']
        ct = cv if not isinstance(cv, dict) else cv['top']; cb = cv if not isinstance(cv, dict) else cv['bottom']
        ds = p['stirrup']['diameter'] if p.get('stirrup') else 0.0
        d = bp['diameter']
        ang = e.get('angle', 0.0)
        th = ang * (math.pi / 180.0); s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
        o = [e['at'][0], e['at'][1], base - elev]
        ac = [c, s, 0.0]; up = [-s, c, 0.0]
        F = dict(o=o, al=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ac=ac, up=up)
        hs, he = C.legs(bp.get('hook'))
        jg = bp['jog']; by = jg['by']; ft = jg['from_top']; slope = jg.get('slope', 6.0)
        H = top - base
        anc = p.get('anchor') or {}
        T0 = -anc['below'] if anc.get('below') is not None else cb
        T1 = H + anc['above'] if anc.get('above') is not None else H - ct
        J0 = H - ft; J1 = J0 + by * slope
        places = []
        if t['round']:
            n = bp['count']; r = t['width'] / 2 - cs - ds - d / 2
            for i in range(n):
                phi = 2 * math.pi * i / n
                pc, ps = math.cos(phi), math.sin(phi)
                a, b = r * pc, r * ps
                places.append((a, b, (-a / r, -b / r)))

# exact natural cubic spline (chord-length params) -> evaluate exactly, then round, compare with original samples
def nat_spline_exact(ts, ys):
    n = len(ts) - 1
    h = [ts[i+1] - ts[i] for i in range(n)]
    # second derivatives M: M0 = Mn = 0
    A = [[Fr(0)]*(n+1) for _ in range(n+1)]; r = [Fr(0)]*(n+1)
    A[0][0] = Fr(1); A[n][n] = Fr(1)
    for i in range(1, n):
        A[i][i-1] = h[i-1]; A[i][i] = 2*(h[i-1] + h[i]); A[i][i+1] = h[i]
        r[i] = 6*((ys[i+1] - ys[i])/h[i] - (ys[i] - ys[i-1])/h[i-1])
    # solve
    m = n + 1
    Aug = [A[i] + [r[i]] for i in range(m)]
    for c in range(m):
        for rr in range(m):
            if rr != c and Aug[rr][c] != 0:
                f = Aug[rr][c]/Aug[c][c]
                Aug[rr] = [Aug[rr][k] - f*Aug[c][k] for k in range(m+1)]
    M = [Aug[i][m]/Aug[i][i] for i in range(m)]
    def ev(i, tau):
        hh = h[i]; Aa = 1 - tau; B = tau
        return Aa*ys[i] + B*ys[i+1] + ((Aa**3 - Aa)*M[i] + (B**3 - B)*M[i+1])*hh*hh/6
    return ev
for dl, i, e1, e2 in data:
    if 'start_tangent' in dl or 'end_tangent' in dl: continue
    fit = [[Fr(p[0]), Fr(p[1])] for p in dl['fit']]
    # chord lengths as floats (sqrt) then exact
    ts = [Fr(0)]
    for a, b in zip(dl['fit'], dl['fit'][1:]):
        ts.append(ts[-1] + Fr(math.sqrt((b[0]-a[0])**2 + (b[1]-a[1])**2)))
    evx = nat_spline_exact(ts, [p[0] for p in fit]); evy = nat_spline_exact(ts, [p[1] for p in fit])
    # piece 1 covers segments 0..i-1; samples at global index-param u = k/256 * i
    S1 = []
    for k in range(257):
        u = Fr(i*k, 256)
        seg = min(int(u), len(fit) - 2); tau = u - seg
        S1.append((float(evx(seg, tau)), float(evy(seg, tau))))
    hits = sum(1 for p in e1['fit'] if tuple(p) in set(S1))
    # also t-param sampling (raw chord length)
    S2 = []
    for k in range(257):
        t = ts[0] + (ts[i] - ts[0])*Fr(k, 256)
        seg = 0
        while seg < len(ts) - 2 and t > ts[seg+1]: seg += 1
        tau = (t - ts[seg])/(ts[seg+1] - ts[seg])
        S2.append((float(evx(seg, tau)), float(evy(seg, tau))))
    hits2 = sum(1 for p in e1['fit'] if tuple(p) in set(S2))

underneath.
- **A real building model.** Doors and windows live in their walls, rooms find their boundaries from the walls around
  them, walls joined at a corner stay joined when one moves, dimensions and tags follow what they measure and name, and
  every change is checked against the model's rules and can be undone.
- **Open files.** IFC2x3 and IFC4 come in from Revit and other BIM tools, and IFC4 goes back out, checked with
  IfcOpenShell. Sheets print to PDF; any view saves as PNG, plans as SVG. Revit's own `.rvt` format has no public
  specification; `bimcraft-cli` reads a `.rvt` file with a reader fenced in [docs/rvt-provenance.md](docs/rvt-provenance.md):
  `info` shows its release, levels and element counts by category, and `run` and `convert` (and the MCP server's `open`) import
  its levels, walls, floors and ceilings, doors and windows, columns, rooms and roofs (flat ones by footprint, and gables and sheds
  by extrusion) into a project, listing what was left out and why. The desktop app's File > Open takes a `.rvt` too: it is read
  while the window says so, comes in as a new unsaved project, and a "Revit import report" lists what came in and what was left out.
- **Built for agents.** Every tool, button and field is a command. Agents call any of them with JSON, inspect the model to
  check their work, and render any view to look at it, over MCP or the CLI.
- **Fast and native.** Pure Rust and egui: no Electron, no web view. Packaged for Windows, Linux and macOS; developed on
  Linux, and the macOS app isn't tried by hand yet.
- **Free.** MIT OR Apache-2.0, with no account and no subscription.

## What works today

BIMCraft is in early, fast development. Honest status:

| Area | Works today |
|---|---|
| Datums | Levels with elevations, each a plane over its extent (a rectangle in plan; by default the model's, a metre past it): sections and elevations draw a level where they see its extent, and the 3D view outlines its plane (its far two edges, all four when selected), hidden behind what's in front, its name lettered on a head past the far edges' right end, a click on either picking it; selected, its ends in a section or an elevation and the middles of its plane's edges in 3D are grips that drag its extent; grids that name themselves 1, 2, 3… or A, B, C… |
| Walls | Chains of walls, straight or curved (each turning `arc` degrees), on any of Revit's six location lines (the wall's or its core's centre line, a finish or a core face, exterior or interior); compound types with layers (structure, substrate, thermal, membrane, finish) from the exterior in, the exterior being to the left of start to end, so walls drawn clockwise face out; joins at any angle, mitred, three or more walls sharing a node, a wall ending on another stopped at its face, and sharp corners squared off; base level and offset; the top at a level or an unconnected height (by default, up to the next level), or attached to the underside of a roof or a floor (a base, onto one), following it where it's over the wall; flip, as Revit's arrows do |
| Doors, windows | Hosted in walls: place one at a point on the wall (`at`), or by wall and offset; marks number themselves, on in the series they are in (`P1`, `P2` → `P3`; `J-09` → `J-10`) and kept through IFC as the doors' and windows' tags; flip facing and hand; refused when they don't fit their wall or overlap. Of one of the project's own types (a width, a height, a sill), or of a family of their own: a new project comes with a single door, a double door, a sliding door, a fixed window, a casement window and a sliding window, each saying how it opens (swing, double swing, sliding, double sliding, folding or fixed, which IFC's operation types and the schedules carry), and more load from `.json` files. A family's forms (frame, leaf, handle, sashes, panes) are drawn in the opening, its `Width` and `Height` size the hole in the wall, its `Sill Height` is a window's sill, its formulas read `Wall Thickness`, and its plan symbols (a door's swing) go with it as it flips; sections show them beyond their line, never cut |
233:| Massing | A mass is an outline extruded from a level (and an offset) up to the next level, a level or a height, as Revit's conceptual mass is, in its own category (`mass`) that Visibility/Graphics hides (Show Mass, MH, does it for a view in one step): dashed in plan where the cut plane passes through it and in a section where the line cuts it (outlined, not filled), a see-through solid in 3D. Give it a `top` outline with as many points as its footprint (twin for twin, the same way round) and it is lofted straight between the two, or a `lean` (the footprint moved sideways for its top: a sloped mass); the plan then draws the outline at the height it cuts, the section the line where it cuts the skin, 3D a closed skin of triangles, and area, perimeter and volume, per level too, come from the cross sections between the outlines, exactly. `mass_floors` makes a floor at each level it crosses, outlined as the mass is there; the floors hold their mass and level, so running it again updates them instead of doubling them (`prune` deletes the ones on levels the mass no longer crosses; without it they are listed as `stale`). `wall_by_face` (on faces that stand plumb), `floor_by_face` and `roof_by_face` (on the top outline) make a wall on each edge, and a floor and a roof on its top face, and remember their mass and face: `update_by_face` (UF) rebuilds them from the mass as it is now, as Revit's Update to Face does, and refuses the lot, naming each, when a face is gone. The `massfloor` schedule has a row for each level each mass crosses (floor area, perimeter, and the volume up to the next level or the mass's top, to sum into gross floor area and volume); the `mass` schedule one row for each mass. IFC writes a mass as a building element proxy of object type `Mass` (a lofted one as a closed face set, with a `BIMCraft_Mass` property set that says how its corners pair up), and reads one back; a mass with a courtyard in it, or whose outline changes from base to top with no such set, is left out and listed. Masses take the project parameters, phases and design options as other elements do, and move, copy, mirror and rotate with them. What a mass made is ordinary in a copy, after a split, in IFC and once its mass is deleted |
238:| Structure | Beams, structural columns, isolated footings, wall (strip) footings and structural floors, Revit's Structure tab on the design in [docs/disciplines.md](docs/disciplines.md). A beam, or a wall footing, is a **run**: a straight element from one point to another, of a type with a section (`width` across by `depth` deep, or round) made of a material of the library, at a height over its level (the height of its top, middle or bottom line at each end, so it can slope up to 75°), in a named `system`; a chain of points makes one for each step. A structural column is a column of its own category and types; an isolated footing is a column laid down, its top at the level by default and as thick as `thickness`. A floor says it is `structural`. In plan a run hangs under its level (seen from it, with its centre line dashed to pick it by), crosses the cut plane (in poché) or lies overhead (dashed); a section cuts a rectangular run across its section, and the 3D view draws a sloped prism or, round, a tube; snaps find their ends and middles. Each has a schedule (Id, Type, Level, Length, Width, Depth, with System to group a schedule by), a place in Visibility/Graphics, project parameters and phases, and its IFC class: IfcBeam, IfcColumn, IfcFooting (`PAD_FOOTING`, `STRIP_FOOTING`) and IfcSlab, each with `LoadBearing` in its `Pset_*Common`, swept along its own axis; IFC import reads them back, taking a column or slab whose `Pset_*Common` says it carries load as structural |
243:| Reinforcement | `rebar` makes reinforcing bars: a round bar of a diameter (3 to 100 mm) and a steel grade (CA-50 unless told) bent along points in mm, in the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces, which it goes with; `closed` makes a hoop, and `count` with `step` a layer of bars or hoops along a beam. A schedule of rebar lists grade, diameter, length, count and weight (steel at 7850 kg/m³) and, grouped, is a bar schedule. IFC writes and reads each as an `IfcReinforcingBar`, aggregated to its host. The 3D view draws them as tubes (inside their host, so hide it to see them), a section draws the bars it cuts as dots over the poché, and a plan draws each bar of its level as a thin line (solid under the cut plane, dashed over it and under the view range's top, a bar that stands as a dot, bars lying on one another drawn once), hidden with the category. `reinforce` arms a beam, a column, a footing or a floor (round columns and footings, and sloped floors, too) by rules: the engineer gives the cover (or the host's `Cobrimento` parameter) and how many bars, how thick and how far apart (a beam's bars below and above, stirrups with closer ends and hooks, skin bars and anchors; a column's bars on each face, stirrups and ties; a footing's two layers of mesh with their ends turned up; a floor's meshes below and above, stopping short of its outline and openings), and it lays them out inside the cover, checks they fit with room between them and says what to change; a beam's bars and a column's end in hooks if told, some of a beam's bottom bars bend up at each end to the top at an angle (`bent`) and a column's bars step in toward its axis near the top (`jog`); each bar is on a layer, and reinforcing again replaces what it made and leaves bars drawn by hand. `hosts` arms a list alike, all or none (up to 1000 hosts and 20000 bars), and `reinforcement_preset` keeps a named set of the parameters for a kind of host in the project, which `reinforce` takes with `preset` and lets what is given replace. The numbers are the engineer's; `check` "NBR 6118" (with the aggressiveness class and `fck`) adds notes, never a refusal, where the bars made fall short of its usual limits (cover, bar sizes and spacings, stirrups, least and most steel, skin bars), typed from public handbooks and not from the standard's text, so check one against a copy before relying on it. On the desktop, the Structure tab's Reinforce (RF) opens a dialog for the elements selected (any number, of one kind), with the fields of their kind, saying a refusal inside itself, keeping what was typed for the next of its kind, saving the fields as a preset to choose for another and deleting one, and with Remove Bars for the bars it made. Not yet: bends other than a hook, a bent-up bar and a column's jog, round beams, bars beyond a section's cut seen through the concrete. |
246:| Editing | Modify any field, of one element or many in one step (a wall put on another location line stays where it is); move, copy, rotate and mirror, with the walls joined to them stretching to stay joined and doors and windows going with their walls (a mirrored wall runs back the other way, its exterior mirrored); trim or extend two walls to a corner; split a wall, an arc into two arcs; flip walls; delete (a wall takes its doors and windows with it, and they their tags; a roof or floor walls are attached to lets them go); undo and redo |
247:| Snaps and the ruler | Points picked while drawing stick to what the plan has there, as Revit's snaps do: the ends, middles and centres of walls (an arc's too), grids and components, the centres of columns, structural columns and footings with the corners and edge middles of their outlines (a round one's four quadrants), so a wall can start flush with a column's edge, and the corners of floors, ceilings, roofs and shafts; where two straight walls or grids cross; the foot of the perpendicular from the last point to a straight wall or grid; and a wall's centre line, so a wall drawn onto it meets it. It also sticks to the anchors of notes, dimensions, tags, spot elevations, section and elevation marks, detail groups and repeating details; a camera's mark gives its eye and target, never the body, lens or name it is drawn with. Each shows its own marker and its name. A direction from the last point sticks to multiples of an angle (5°, 15°, 30°, 45° or 90°; 15° by default), from east and from the line before it, so corners come out exact, sharp ones too: a dashed guide shows it, and where it crosses a wall or grid the point lands there. The line being drawn carries a ruler: graduations at round lengths, its length and its angle (at the corner it turns once there's a line before it, drawn as an arc). Manage > Snaps switches each snap and sets the angle steps, and Revit's SE, SM, SI, SC, SP and SN take one snap alone for the next point (SO none, SS back); Measure (ME) lays a ruler between two snapped points and reads its length, parts and angle; the `measure` command does the same. Each plan, section and elevation has a background grid, a main grid and a subgrid with their own spacing, divisions, colours and pens, turned by an angle, kept in the view's graphics and controlled by its template; Grid snapping (Manage > Snaps, or the grid menu in the view control bar) lands a free point on its crossings |
248:| Annotation | Aligned dimensions between parallel references, one segment or a chain: wall faces, centre lines and ends, door and window centres and jambs, grids; and between endpoints (a wall's ends and its faces' corners, a line's or a grid's ends, a jamb's), aligned along them or linear, horizontal or vertical, as the cursor lies or the Options Bar says (Auto, Aligned, Horizontal, Vertical; Space steps them); angular dimensions between two lines that meet, radial and diameter ones on round columns, curved walls, circles and arcs, and arc length ones along a curved wall or an arc; all measuring the model as it is, so they follow what they measure (a change that would turn a reference out of parallel with the others is refused). In a 3D view, aligned dimensions between two points or edges of the model (square to an edge), kept by the view and drawn over it, on either painter and on the sheets that hold it. A dimension's number takes a typed length and moves what it measures; locked segments show their padlocks always; Align leaves a padlock that keeps the two lines aligned after every change, refusing one the other locks can't hold with. Dimension types, as Revit's type parameters: continuous, baseline or ordinate strings, diagonal, arrow, open arrow or dot ticks, pens, colour, the dimension and witness lines' extensions, gaps and control, and the numbers' font, size, lettering, offset, background, read convention, units and rounding; a dimension's own prefix, suffix, text above and below, Replace With Text and Equality Display (EQ). Tags on any element showing its type, a door's or window's mark, a room's name or any field of its schedule, going where their doors and windows go, with or without a leader; tag everything not tagged yet in one go. Text notes in plans, sections, elevations and on sheets, at any angle, over several lines, with a leader, of a text type (font, size, bold, italic, underline, width factor, colour and a border: any font the system has, Arial by default, which a look-alike such as Liberation Sans stands in for where it isn't installed, or IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono or our single-stroke lettering; any script a font on the system has, CJK included), written and rewritten on the canvas (Shift+Enter breaks a line), and with Override Formatting, parts of them bold, italic or underlined whatever their type; spot elevations reading the top of what they stand on in plan (a floor, a roof's slope, a stair's tread), or the height of a point in a section |
249:| Views | A floor plan per level with Revit's view range: cut at its cut plane (1200 mm up by default), what lies below seen from it down to the bottom, faint beyond it down to the view depth, and roofs overhead up to the top: wall poché with clean joins at any angle, compound walls' layers, hatched with their materials' cut patterns where they're wide enough (else lighter where they aren't structure), door swings, window glass, room tags, grid bubbles, dimensions, door and window tags; PNG and SVG, which letter the view's name at the plan's bottom left (the window letters it too, over the canvas and on the screen only, which File > Settings can hide; a viewport on a sheet has its own title). Sections and elevations along any line: the cut in poché (a roof's along its slope, a compound wall's, floor's, roof's or ceiling's with its layers), what lies beyond in hidden line, levels named with their heights, grids; the four building elevations in one go; their marks on every plan; PNG. Crop regions on plans and sections: the view shows only what's inside, grids stopping at its edge with their bubbles. A reflected ceiling plan per level: its walls cut at 2300 mm (over the doors, through the windows), looking up at the ceilings, their tiles and the shafts through them, and at the beams and columns over the cut up to the ceilings, in projection (one over a ceiling is hidden by it). A 3D view, from any angle: walls with their doors and windows cut out, slabs and ceilings with their shafts cut out, columns, stairs and roofs, door leaves and glass, shaded (each layer in its material's colour), with an edge wherever faces meet, but none between the facets of a curve (a curved wall's, a round form's, an imported mesh's where its triangles turn less than 20°), which shades smoothly across them; PNG. A plan or a section always has a scale, 1 : n (1 : 100, or 1/8" = 1'-0" in feet and inches, until set): it stands for paper at that scale, and its annotation (lettering, grid bubbles, marks, dimension ticks) and its line weights are that paper's, so on screen a line is as thick as it would print at the zoom (at least a pixel; Thin Lines draws all of them one). A line weight is a pen, 1 to 16, or 0, a hairline, the thinnest line the screen, a PNG or a printer draws, at any scale and zoom; what pens 1 to 16 draw is the project's Line Weights (Manage > Line Weights, as Revit's): the model's pens at each of a list of scales, a view taking the nearest scale's, and the annotation's (dimensions, tags, text, grids, levels, marks) at any scale, edited by scale, added and deleted, applied as one undo step and saved with the project. Which pen each model category draws its own lines in, cut and seen, is the project's Object Styles (Manage > Object Styles, as Revit's), in every plan and section, a view's Visibility/Graphics over them. Detail lines draw in one view (a plan, a section, an elevation or a sheet) in a line style: a pen, a colour and a line pattern, its freely ordered gaps, straight strokes, dots, centered parallel offsets, waves, zigzags and text in mm on paper so it reads the same at any scale; the Line Pattern Creator previews straight or curved paths and letters text with bundled IBM Plex Sans, while geometry and dimensions keep the centerline (Manage > Line Styles, styles and patterns made, changed, renamed and deleted as one undo step; a project starts with Thin, Medium and Wide Lines, a Hairline, Hidden, Centre and Overhead Lines). A cut wall's outline is inked over its poché, and not across where walls join. A plan or a section has a detail level too: coarse (what it cuts in one poché, an opening as its gap and jambs), medium (a compound element's layers and an opening's leaf, swing and glass) or fine, as it has always drawn (the layers' patterns too); the 3D view has a visual style: shaded, hidden line (paper-white faces with their edges, what a face hides staying hidden) or wireframe (every edge, seen through the faces). A viewport takes its view's scale; a sheet keeps annotation at paper size. A view fitted into an image (a PNG, Zoom to Fit) leaves as much room round it as its annotation takes at its scale, which grows with the scale, so 1 : 500 doesn't cut its grid bubbles or level names off. A level can have more plans than its own, as Revit's Duplicate View makes them (`duplicate_view`, DP): each a plan view with its own view range, crop and graphics and its own dimensions, tags, notes and spot elevations over the same model; with detailing it starts with its source's annotation; a dependent view follows its parent's view range and graphics (scale and detail too), has a crop of its own, and shows its parent's annotation as well as its own. They go on sheets, take view templates and have ceiling plans as levels do. Sections, elevations, schedules, sheets and the 3D view aren't duplicated yet. The 3D view is parallel (axonometric) or in perspective, as through a camera: picked from Projection in its Properties (or `perspective`), seen through a lens of a focal length typed there, from an eye raised or lowered to a height typed there, and orbited, panned, zoomed, picked and edited as ever, on the processor or the graphics card. The Camera tool (`camera`) makes a view of its own, as Revit's does: an eye and a target are clicked in a plan (each at a height over it, typed in the Options Bar), and a named 3D view in perspective opens looking from the eye at the target; it is listed under 3D Views in the Project Browser, opens from its own camera, and its name, eye, target and lens are read and changed in Properties, whether it is open or its mark on the plan is picked (`camera` reads or changes one too, by name or id; a view with no camera shows the azimuth and elevation it is framed by on a sheet instead). The camera shows on its level's plan as a mark at its eye with a line to what it looks at: it is picked there and opened by its right-click menu (or a double click), and its eye and target follow the mouse as the view is orbited, panned or zoomed, so leaving the view and coming back stands it where it was left. The 3D view has a section box, as Revit's: six planes square to the axes that keep what lies between them, the model's surfaces and its point clouds alike, turned on and off with BX or its Properties, each face dragged by its grip in the view or typed in Properties, its extents kept while it's off; the levels it doesn't reach are left out. A plan can follow it (Section Box in the plan's Properties): it then shows what the box keeps, cut at the box's top, seen down to its bottom and cropped to its sides, and snaps to a scan where the box's top cuts it |
261:| Revit files (read only; the command line and the desktop) | A Revit `.rvt` or `.rfa` file of release 2015 to 2027 (checked on Autodesk's sample projects of 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026, and the Snowdon Towers files) is read by a reader of its own, `crates/rvt`, ported in part from [rvt-rs](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs) and fenced by [docs/rvt-provenance.md](docs/rvt-provenance.md). `info` shows its release, build and document GUID, the last save (the saver's name when worksharing records it, and the path it was saved to; shown by `info`, never written into a project or an IFC file), the title, the levels with their names and elevations, and the number of elements in each `BuiltInCategory`, how many of them are placed instances. `run x.rvt`, `convert x.rvt out.ifc` and the MCP server's `open` import the file as a new project: its levels, straight and curved walls with their compound layers and materials (the exterior on the side the file's flip says), floors and ceilings from their sketches (holes and separate loops included), doors and windows in the walls that hold them, columns, rooms with their numbers and names, and roofs (by footprint, those that rise coming in level, and ones by extrusion whose profile is straight lines in a plane square to an axis and whose box the profile and the type's thickness reproduce to a millimetre), converted from feet to millimetres and checked by `Model::check`. Only what a record says is read, and the reply says what is not. Where the record's own box gives a stand-in (a curtain wall as the plane of its box, a sloped or stepped floor, ceiling or roof level at the bottom of its box, a sketch that closes nothing as the footprint of its box, a column as the rectangle of its box) the element comes in as that stand-in and a note in `skipped` says what was not read of it; that is an approximation, and it is not counted as read whole. Anything else the reader cannot decode (a roof by extrusion that is not a straight-line profile, a skylight, a room no walls enclose, stairs, groups, families) is left out and listed in the reply's `skipped` as `N kinds left out, why`. In the desktop, File > Open, the system's open event (Finder, Open With) and a file named on the command line take a `.rvt`: the window stays alive while a box says "Opening a Revit file", asks about unsaved changes first as for any file, and the project that comes in is new and unsaved (Save asks for a `.bimcraft` name; nothing is written back to the `.rvt`, and it is not in File > Open Recent). The status box says how many elements came in and how many were left out, and File > Revit import report lists what came in by category and the notes of what was left out, grouped by cause with their ids. A build without the reader has no `.rvt` option and says why. Joins are BIMCraft's own, and a door's swing is not read. Checked against rvt-rs's own IFC export of the same files, the imported walls, floors, ceilings, openings, columns and roofs agree to a fraction of a millimetre (walls differ where a join is a butt there and a mitre here). A file is read under limits (its size, its streams, what each inflates to) and a damaged or hostile one is an error that says what is wrong. Nothing is taken from inside the file (families, templates, icons) for BIMCraft's own content. Builds that include the reader are Apache-2.0 (see License); `--no-default-features` leaves it out |
