You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler written in Rust; README at /workspace/README.md, design notes in /workspace/docs/, especially docs/areas/levels-walls-roofs.md, docs/areas/massing.md, docs/shape-editing.md), as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Many agents work in parallel; you are a sub-agent of the ARCH agent (architecture: walls, floors, roofs, rooms, stairs, masses, sketches, shapes). You work in your own git worktree.

## Hard rules (violating any fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it ONLY by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`.
- No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only (no crates).
- Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, under /tmp/<your-name>/. Commit only Rust.
- Only edit the files you are told you own; the only other edits allowed are registering your module/commands in `src/arch/mod.rs` (a `pub mod` line, entries in `COMMANDS`, a dispatch arm, a check arm) or `src/geom/mod.rs` (a `pub mod` line). List any such edit in your final report.

## Getting started
1. Your worktree must start from the ARCH agent's commit 6a1b9e5 (branch `worktree-agent-aa380c34464cd9919`). Run `git log --oneline -1`; if HEAD isn't 6a1b9e5 (or a descendant of it), run `git reset --hard 6a1b9e5`.
2. Build with `cargo build --release` (about 15 s); the binary is `<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli`.
3. Probe tools are in /tmp/arch-agent/tools (copy them to your own /tmp dir; each takes the env var `MINE=<your binary>`):
   - `o.py [-m] [-c cats] [-n] cmd1 cmd2 ...` runs commands as a script on a fresh project with the original (or yours with -m), prints replies and the saved elements.
   - `each.py [-b] [-P prefixcmd]... [-i file] lines...` runs each line as its own script (after the prefix commands) and prints the result of the last; `-b` runs both programs and marks SAME/DIFF.
   - `order.py [-p prefixcmd] cmd '{bad params}' '{good params}'` finds the order in which a command validates its parameters.
   - `craft.py [-b] base.bimcraft 'python on d / E' [cmd]` writes a modified copy of a project file, opens it and runs a command (the original checks the model when opening, so this shows the model's rule messages and their order).
   - `fl.py [-b] groups.txt` (env CATS, KEYS) runs groups of commands (blank-line separated) and prints chosen fields of chosen categories.
   - `MINE=<your binary> python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py -- run --cmd '...' --cmd '...' --save x.bimcraft` runs both programs in fresh dirs and diffs exit code, stdout, stderr and every file written, after normalising GUIDs. Prints SAME or the diff. The hidden tests do this kind of comparison on many inputs, so match replies, error texts, saved files and undo labels exactly.
   - Useful: `/workspace/executable commands` prints the catalog with each command's `params` text.

## The codebase (read what you need; you are in a git worktree)
- `src/json.rs`: `Value` (insertion-ordered `Map`), `jobj!{}`, `to_compact`, `kind_name()` (serde's "invalid type" wording), float formatting identical to serde_json.
- `src/project.rs`: `Project` = `doc` + `elements: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (each element a JSON object in the original's field order: `guid`, `category`, then its struct's fields) + `library` (`{kind, name, guid}`: types are kind `type:wall` etc., families `family`, family types `family-type` named "Family: Type"); `alloc_id()`, `find_guid`, `guid_of`, `lib_guid(kind, name)`, `lib_name(guid)`. Elements reference levels, hosts, types… by GUID in the file.
- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute` runs a command, then `crate::arch::check_edits(before, after, cid)` (outline simplicity of what changed) and `crate::check::check` (every module's `check(pr)`; ARCH's is `crate::arch::check`, which runs each element's rules in id order, then cross-element rules), rolls back on any error, and records an undo step labelled by the catalog label.
- `src/commands/params.rs`: parameter readers with the original's texts (`req_num`, `opt_num` "must be a number in mm", `opt_text`, `opt_bool`, `req_point`, `opt_point`, `point_of`, `id_of`; |mm| <= 1e9). `src/model.rs`: `levels`, `elev`, `level_param`/`resolve_level` (with the original's errors), `level_above`, `find`, `normalize_guid`.
- ARCH so far (`src/arch/`): `util.rs` (helpers: `d(x)` = Rust Display of f64 as the messages print numbers, `dp(p)`, `num/numd/text/flag/pt/pts/rings` accessors, `pv/ring_v/rings_v`, `cat`, `by_ref`/`ref_word`/`ref_value`, `level_of`, `elev`, `level_guid`, `level_name`, `computation_height`, `type_names`, `type_def`, `type_guid`, `type_name`, `default_type`, `type_ref`, `check_type`, `thickness`, `layers`, `opt_ref`, `m2` (area mm² → m² 2 decimals), `put`), `walls.rs` (`Wall` struct: location line, centre line, `arc()`, `length()`, `base()`, `top()`, `spans(z)`; `cmd_wall`, `make_wall`, `cmd_flip`, `check_wall`, `joined_centres`), `openings.rs` (doors/windows, marks `next_series`), `slabs.rs` (floor/ceiling/shaft commands and checks, `clean`, `de_rings`/`de_points` serde-like readers, `opt_boundary`, `check_rings`), `roofs.rs` (roof command and checks, `wall_footprint`, `round3`), `rooms.rs` (room, room_separator, `space_at` room regions at centre lines and faces), `outline.rs` (`level_outline`: a level's wall outline and courtyards), `edits.rs` (`check_edits`), `mod.rs` (dispatch + `check`).
- `src/geom/`: `mod.rs` (P2 = [f64; 2] and vector ops, `area`, `inside`, `seg_dist`, `Arc` (centre, radius, a0, sweep) and `straight`), `graph.rs` (planar graph of segments: `Graph::build`, `faces()` traced as the original does; `arc_points`), `offset.rs` (`offset_ring` per-edge offsets), `sketch.rs` (a first sketch problem engine: `Problem`, `describe`, `ring_problems`, `parse`, `solve_one`, `to_value`), `tri.rs` (empty).
- Other areas are done by other agents (don't implement them): `modify`, `move`, `copy`, `delete` etc. (EDIT), `inspect`, `elements`, `schedule` (READERS), views/graphics (VIEWS), types/families/structure (STRUCTURE), IFC. Our build does not have them yet, so test your commands through scripts that use only ARCH commands plus `level`, `grid`, `undo`, `redo`, `save`, `open`.
- New elements get their phase/option with `crate::styles::phasing::stamp_new(&s.project, s.now_phase.as_deref(), s.now_option.as_deref(), &mut e)` before insertion (see `walls::make_wall`).

## How to work
Probe the original widely: normal cases, every optional parameter, edge cases, every error and the order of checks (`order.py`), and what the saved file holds (field order, defaults omitted or written, number formatting). Write the code, then compare with `each.py -b` / `fl.py -b` / `cmp.py` until SAME. Error texts must match character for character (numbers in messages are usually Rust's `{}` Display of f64; points `[x, y]`). Keep a list of what still differs.

## Finish
Commit your work on your worktree branch (`git add -A && git commit -m "..."`), and make your final message a concise report: the branch name and commit, per command what matches and what doesn't, any edits outside your files, and any function other code must call (or that you need from others).

steps.message:
Both commands are done and committed on branch `worktree-agent-add01394c801ae7f2` (latest commit `0d77366`). The full regression (2391 cases) passes 2384. Of the 7 failures, 3 wait on other parts (EDIT's `delete`, READERS' `inspect`) and 4 are an unsolved last-digit difference in column jogs. The commits touch only `src/structure/rebar.rs` and `src/structure/reinforce/*`.

**`rebar`**
- 169 of 169 probes match: replies, saved JSON, every refusal text and the order of checks, `rebar::check` (including hand-edited files) and the elements view. The undo label ("Rebar") matches.
- 21 of 24 host cases match. The other 3 are `rebar` followed by `delete` or `inspect`, which belong to EDIT and READERS.
- Deleting a host also deletes its bars; the original replies `{"deleted":[host, bars…]}`. EDIT has to do this through `delete_bars_of`.
- The IFC asset scenario saves an identical .bimcraft (cmp.py SAME). The .ifc itself is written by the export agent.

**`reinforce`**
- **Beams:** 383 of 383 probes and 690 of 690 random cases, sloped and justified beams included. The original measures a beam's lengths with `hypot`. On a sloped beam the half-depth used is depth/2 × length along the slope ÷ plan length; on a flat beam it is exactly depth/2.
- **Columns:** round-column hooks 300 of 300, older random set 237 of 240.
- **Column jogs:** 237 of 300 random cases. Where the column is turned to an angle, the original's step points sit 1–10 last-digit units off the straight bar, and I found no formula that reproduces this. Jogged bars' heads, legs, ties and stirrups all match.
- **Footings:** 44 of 44 probes and 180 of 180 random cases.
- **Floors:** 560 of 560, including a new set of 300 sloped-floor cases. The original measures the slope arrow with `hypot`. A layer sits off × √(1+tan²) below the top, and the hooks follow (−a, −b, 1) divided by its length.
- **`check` "NBR 6118":** 120 probe cases and about 3,000 random cases match exactly, including:
  - every note's text and their order;
  - the one in 20000-bar refusal: "…arm fewer elements at once, or widen a spacing";
  - with several hosts, each note and each refusal ends with "(for the {category} {id})". This also covers the `grade`, `clearance` and `check` refusals, which the original reads host by host.
- The 1000-bars-per-host limit for floors (openings included) and footings matches. The undo label is "Reinforce".

**Stand-ins in my own files**
- `floor.rs` has a private reader for ARCH's floor JSON.
- `beam.rs` computes its own beam centre line, because MEMBERS' `run_geom` axis is off in the last digits on sloped beams. MEMBERS may want the same formula (lengths by `hypot`, half-depth as above).

**What other areas must call or can use** (all in `crate::structure::rebar`)
- `length(&[[f64;3]]) -> f64`, `area(f64) -> f64`, `weight_kg(diameter: f64, length: f64) -> f64` (steel at 7850 kg/m³).
- `path_of(&Value) -> Option<Vec<[f64;3]>>`, `bar_length(&Value) -> f64`, `bar_weight_kg(&Value) -> f64`, `bar_grade(&Value) -> String`.
- `bar_json(level_guid: &str, host_guid: Option<&str>, path: &[[f64;3]], diameter: f64, grade: &str, layer: Option<&str>) -> Value`.
- `bars_of_host(&Project, host_guid: &str) -> Vec<u64>`.
- `delete_bars_of(&mut Project, host_guid: &str) -> Vec<u64>`: EDIT's `delete` must call this and list the bars after the host.
- Also public: `HOST_CATS`, `read_ref`, `resolve_ref`, `level_of`, `round2`, `round3`, `check`, `element_view`.
- For IFC export: bar length is `length`, area is `area`; the original prints 6 decimals.

The regression scripts and caches are in `/tmp/rebar-agent/`. The main ones:
- `reg.py all_reg.txt` (built by `mkall.py`) runs everything against the original.
- `notes_cmp.py -a` compares the check's notes.
- `cmpbars.py *.pkl` compares bars point by point.
- `gen_*.py` make the random projects.

import json, math
vals = {int(k): (tuple(v[0]), tuple(v[1])) for k, v in json.load(open('/tmp/views-notes/arcvals.json')).items()}
a_ = (1000.0, 5000.0); b_ = (3000.0, 5000.0)
n = 42
deg = 90.0
t = math.radians(deg)
ch = math.hypot(b_[0]-a_[0], b_[1]-a_[1])
R = ch / (2 * abs(math.sin(t / 2)))
m = ((a_[0]+b_[0])/2, (a_[1]+b_[1])/2)
C = (m[0], m[1] + R*math.cos(t/2))
a0 = math.atan2(a_[1]-C[1], a_[0]-C[0])
forms = {
 'rad step': lambda k: a0 + (t / n) * k,
 'deg step': lambda k: math.radians(math.degrees(a0) + (deg / n) * k),
 'deg k/n': lambda k: math.radians(math.degrees(a0) + deg * k / n),
 'a0+t*(k/n)': lambda k: a0 + t * (k / n),
 'lerp': lambda k: a0 * (1 - k / n) + (a0 + t) * (k / n),
 'a0 + k*t/n': lambda k: a0 + k * t / n,
 'mul_add': lambda k: math.fsum([a0, (t / n) * k]),
}
for name, f in forms.items():
    pts = [(C[0] + R*math.cos(f(k)), C[1] + R*math.sin(f(k))) for k in range(n+1)]
    ok = sum(1 for k, (fr, to) in vals.items() if fr in (a_, b_) or fr in pts)
    ok2 = sum(1 for k, (fr, to) in vals.items() if to in (a_, b_) or to in pts)
    print(name, ok + ok2)
# also: points as centre + (cos, sin) * R vs R*cos
for name, f in forms.items():
    pts = [(C[0] + math.cos(f(k)) * R, C[1] + math.sin(f(k)) * R) for k in range(n+1)]
    pts2 = [(R * math.cos(f(k)) + C[0], R * math.sin(f(k)) + C[1]) for k in range(n+1)]
    for nm, ps in (('cos*R', pts), ('R*cos+C', pts2)):
        ok = sum(1 for k, (fr, to) in vals.items() if fr in (a_, b_) or fr in ps)
        ok2 = sum(1 for k, (fr, to) in vals.items() if to in (a_, b_) or to in ps)
        print(name, nm, ok + ok2)

        continue

    which = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else len(cuts) - 1
    print(len(cuts), 'cuts; showing', which)
    polys = []
    for line in cuts[which].strip().split('\n'):
        tag, path, n, pts = line.split(' ', 3)
        if n == '0':
            continue
        pts = [tuple(round(c, 3) for c in p) for p in json.loads(pts)]
        polys.append((tag + ':' + path, int(n), pts))
    mir = comps[0].get("mirrored", False)
    seq = []
    for t in orig[int(os.environ.get('PIECE', '0'))]:
        tv = [tuple(round(c * (-1 if (mir and j == 1) else 1), 3) for j, c in enumerate(v)) for v in t]
        cands = [i for i, (path, n, pts) in enumerate(polys) if all(any(max(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(v, q)) < 2e-3 for q in pts) for v in tv)]
        seq.append(cands)
    out = []
    for c in seq:
        s = '/'.join('%d:%s' % (i, polys[i][0]) for i in c) if c else '?'
        if not out or out[-1][0] != s:
            out.append([s, 1])
        else:
            out[-1][1] += 1
    print(' '.join('%s x%d' % (s, k) for s, k in out))
    if os.environ.get('TREE'):
        for i, (path, n, pts) in enumerate(polys):
            print(i, path, n, pts[:4])

"""Work planes through three points: the triangle's least height, about 1 mm?"""
import sys, json, copy, math
from multiprocessing import Pool
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/loader-agent')
from lib import *
d = load('/tmp/loader-agent/corpus/c8.bimcraft')
cases = json.load(open('/tmp/loader-agent/t104_cases.json'))


def least_height(p):
    u = [p[1][i] - p[0][i] for i in range(3)]
    v = [p[2][i] - p[0][i] for i in range(3)]
    n = [u[1] * v[2] - u[2] * v[1], u[2] * v[0] - u[0] * v[2], u[0] * v[1] - u[1] * v[0]]
    nn = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in n))
    sides = [math.dist(p[0], p[1]), math.dist(p[1], p[2]), math.dist(p[0], p[2])]
    return nn / max(sides)


def one(c):
    label, pts = c
    res = []
    for exe in (ORIG, MINE):
        e = copy.deepcopy(d)
        e['elements']['100113']['work_plane'] = {'points': pts}
        code, msg, _ = open_file(e, exe=exe, save=False)
        res.append('collinear' if code and 'along a line' in msg else ('OK' if not code else msg[:100]))
    return label, pts, res


with Pool(8) as pool:
    for label, pts, (o, m) in pool.map(one, cases):
        print('%s %-22s h=%.6f O: %s' % ('same' if o == m else 'DIFF', label, least_height(pts), o))

"""Unified diff of the original's and my normalised export of a case.
usage: fulldiff.py CASE [MAXLINES] [CONTEXT]"""
import os, sys, difflib
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools')

bim = os.path.join(case.D, name + '.bimcraft')
if not os.path.exists(bim):
    case.build(name)
a = case.norm(case.export(case.ORIG, bim)[3]).splitlines()
b = case.norm(case.export(case.MINE, bim)[3]).splitlines()
for i, l in enumerate(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=ctx)):
    if i >= mx:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Two walls at a node, with location lines and types varied: for the first wall's end, which of
its faces the original mitres to the other's and which it squares off, with the crossing's
distance along the face, to find the limit."""
import json, math, re, subprocess, sys, random
D = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/probe'
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1)
TYPES = {"Generic - 200mm": 200.0, "Exterior - 300mm": 300.0, "Interior - 100mm": 100.0}
LOCS = ["centre", "exterior-finish", "interior-finish", "core-centre", "exterior-core", "interior-core"]
def fmt(x):
    s = '%.6f' % (x + 0.0)
    return s.rstrip('0')
def norm(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0] ** 2 + v[1] ** 2); r = 1.0 / l
    return (v[0] * r, v[1] * r)
def perp(v): return (-v[1], v[0])
def add(a, b): return (a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1])
def sub(a, b): return (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])
def mul(a, k): return (a[0] * k, a[1] * k)
def cross(a, b): return a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0]
def dot(a, b): return a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1]
cases = []
cmds = []
for k in range(80):
    ox, oy = 15000.0 * (k % 10), 15000.0 * (k // 10)
    ta, tb = random.choice(list(TYPES)), random.choice(list(TYPES))
    la, lb = random.choice(LOCS), random.choice(LOCS)
    ang = random.choice([25, 40, 60, 75, 90, 110, 130, 150, 165]) * random.choice([1, -1])
    N = (ox + 5000.0, oy)
    S = (ox, oy)
    r = math.radians(180 - ang)
    E = (round(N[0] + 4000 * math.cos(r), 3), round(N[1] + 4000 * math.sin(r), 3))
    cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [list(S), list(N)], "type": ta, "location": la}))
    cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [list(N), list(E)], "type": tb, "location": lb}))
    cases.append((S, N, E, ta, tb, la, lb, ang))
open(D + '/mitre2.txt', 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', D + '/mitre2.txt', '--save', D + '/mitre2.ifc', '--save', D + '/mitre2.bimcraft'], capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.returncode:
    print(p.stderr[:2000]); sys.exit(1)
s = open(D + '/mitre2.ifc').read()
ents = {int(m.group(1)): (m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in re.finditer(r'^#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', s, re.M)}
def refs(t): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', t)]
proj = json.load(open(D + '/mitre2.bimcraft'))
types = proj['types']['wall']
def offsets(tname, loc):
    td = types[tname]
    t = td['thickness']
    ext, core = 0.0, t
    ls = td.get('layers') or []
    th = [l.get('thickness', 0.0) for l in ls]
    stt = [l.get('function') == 'structure' for l in ls]
    if any(stt):
        a = stt.index(True); b = len(stt) - 1 - stt[::-1].index(True)
        ext = sum(th[:a]); core = sum(th[a:b + 1])
    d = {"exterior-finish": 0.0, "interior-finish": t, "exterior-core": ext, "interior-core": ext + core, "core-centre": ext + core / 2.0}.get(loc, t / 2.0)
    return t, d, t - d
walls = [e for e in sorted(ents) if ents[e][0] == 'IFCWALL']
out = []
for ci, (S, N, E, ta, tb, la, lb, ang) in enumerate(cases):
    wa = walls[2 * ci]
    shape = refs(ents[wa][1])[1]
    prof_pts = None
    for rp in refs(ents[shape][1]):
        if "'Body'" in ents[rp][1]:
            solid = refs(ents[rp][1])[-1]
            prof = refs(ents[solid][1])[0]
            poly = refs(ents[prof][1])[-1]
            prof_pts = set(ents[x][1] for x in refs(ents[poly][1]))
    tA, leftA, rightA = offsets(ta, la)
    tB, leftB, rightB = offsets(tb, lb)
    dA = norm(sub(N, S)); nA = perp(dA)
    dB = norm(sub(E, N)); nB = perp(dB)
    loc = lambda q: '(%s,%s)' % (fmt(dot(sub(q, S), dA)), fmt(dot(sub(q, S), nA)))
    # me = A's end: u = -dA, lp = A's right face end, rp = A's left face end
    u = mul(dA, -1.0)
    me_lp = add(N, mul(perp(u), rightA))
    me_rp = sub(N, mul(perp(u), leftA))
    b_lp = add(N, mul(nB, leftB))
    b_rp = sub(N, mul(nB, rightB))
    def xt(a, d, b, e):
        den = cross(d, e)
        return cross(sub(b, a), e) / den if abs(den) > 1e-12 else None
    lt = xt(me_lp, u, b_rp, dB)
    rt = xt(me_rp, u, b_lp, dB)
    res = {}
    for nm, a_, t_ in [('l', me_lp, lt), ('r', me_rp, rt)]:
        if t_ is None:
            continue
        mit = loc(add(a_, mul(u, t_)))
        sq = loc(a_)
        res[nm] = ('M' if mit in prof_pts else '') + ('S' if sq in prof_pts else '')
        out.append({'face': nm, 't': t_, 'tA': tA, 'tB': tB, 'la': la, 'lb': lb, 'ang': ang, 'res': res[nm],
                    'offA': rightA if nm == 'l' else leftA, 'offB': rightB if nm == 'l' else leftB})
json.dump(out, open(D + '/mitre2_%s.json' % (sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '1'), 'w'))
for o in out:
    print('%s t=%9.2f tA=%3d tB=%3d offA=%6.1f offB=%6.1f ang=%4d %-16s %-16s -> %s' % (o['face'], o['t'], o['tA'], o['tB'], o['offA'], o['offB'], o['ang'], o['la'], o['lb'], o['res']))

import sys, json, copy
from multiprocessing import Pool
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/loader-agent')
from lib import *
d = load('/tmp/loader-agent/corpus/c8.bimcraft')
T = '100106'
print(json.dumps(d['elements'][T]))
R = lambda f, t, **kw: dict({'from': f, 'to': t}, **kw)
cases = [
    ('runs ok', T, {'runs': [R(0, 2, bold=True), R(2, 4, italic=True)]}),
    ('runs overlap', T, {'runs': [R(0, 3, bold=True), R(2, 4, italic=True)]}),
    ('runs out of order', T, {'runs': [R(2, 4, bold=True), R(0, 2, italic=True)]}),
    ('run empty', T, {'runs': [R(2, 2, bold=True)]}),
    ('run backwards', T, {'runs': [R(3, 1, bold=True)]}),
    ('run past text', T, {'runs': [R(0, 999, bold=True)]}),
    ('run nothing set', T, {'runs': [R(0, 2)]}),
    ('runs without override', T, {'override_format': False, 'runs': [R(0, 2, bold=True)]}),
    ('override without runs', T, {'override_format': True, 'runs': []}),
    ('run at text end', T, {'runs': [R(0, len(d['elements'][T]['text']), bold=True)]}),
    ('run past by one', T, {'runs': [R(0, len(d['elements'][T]['text']) + 1, bold=True)]}),
    ('text empty', T, {'text': ''}),
    ('text spaces', T, {'text': '   ', 'runs': []}),
    ('text long', T, {'text': 'x' * 10001, 'runs': []}),
    ('text 10000', T, {'text': 'x' * 10000, 'runs': []}),
    ('shaped floor slope', '100080', {'slope': 10}),
    ('shaped floor slope no arrow', '100080', {'slope': 10, 'arrow': None}),
    ('shaped floor slope 80', '100080', {'slope': 80}),
]


def one(c):
    label, eid, upd = c
    res = []
    for exe in (ORIG, MINE):
        e = copy.deepcopy(d)
        x = e['elements'][eid]
        for k, v in upd.items():
            if v is None:
                x.pop(k, None)
            else:
                x[k] = v
        code, msg, _ = open_file(e, exe=exe, save=False)
        res.append(msg.replace('open: x.bimcraft: ', '')[:200] if code else 'OK')
    return label, res


with Pool(8) as pool:
    for label, (o, m) in pool.map(one, cases):
        print('%s %-26s O: %s' % ('same' if o == m else 'DIFF', label, o))

the first difference on.  python3 ifcpaths2.py CASESFILE TITLE"""
import sys, os, json, importlib.util
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/family-agent')
from ifccmp import run_case, rnd

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('c', sys.argv[1])
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)
dbg = '/tmp/family-agent/dbg.txt'
if os.path.exists(dbg):
    os.remove(dbg)
os.environ['CSGDBG'] = dbg
PIECE = int(os.environ.get('PIECE', '0'))
for title, fam, comps in m.CASES:
    if title != sys.argv[2]:
        continue
    orig, mine, err = run_case(fam, comps[:1])
    cuts = open(dbg).read().split('== cut\n')[1:]
    which = int(os.environ.get('CUT', len(cuts) - 1))
    polys = []
    for line in cuts[which].strip().split('\n'):
        tag, path, n, pts = line.split(' ', 3)
        if n == '0':
            continue
        pts = [tuple(round(c, 3) for c in p) for p in json.loads(pts)]
        polys.append((tag + ':' + path, int(n), pts))
    mir = comps[0].get("mirrored", False)

    def seq_of(tris):
        out = []
        for t in tris:
            tv = [tuple(round(c * (-1 if (mir and j == 1) else 1), 3) for j, c in enumerate(v)) for v in t]

            s = '/'.join('%d:%s' % (i, polys[i][0]) for i in cands) if cands else '?'
            if not out or out[-1][0] != s:
                out.append([s, 1])
            else:
                out[-1][1] += 1
        return out

    so, sm = seq_of(orig[PIECE]), seq_of(mine[PIECE])

    if os.environ.get('TREE'):
        for i, (path, n, pts) in enumerate(polys):
            if path.startswith(os.environ['TREE']):
                print(i, path, n, pts)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Free straight walls on a face location line: the sign of their profile's corners on the
location line (y 0 in the wall's axes), against hypotheses. Writes and builds x_face_fuzz."""
import json, math, random, re, subprocess, sys
random.seed(5)
D = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/cases/'
cmds = []
walls = []
for k in range(80):
    x0 = 12000.0 * (k % 10) + round(random.uniform(-3000, 3000), 2)
    y0 = 12000.0 * (k // 10) + round(random.uniform(-3000, 3000), 2)
    a = random.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
    L = random.uniform(3000, 7000)
    x1, y1 = round(x0 + L * math.cos(a), 2), round(y0 + L * math.sin(a), 2)
    loc = random.choice(['exterior-finish', 'interior-finish'])
    cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]], "location": loc}))
    walls.append(((x0, y0), (x1, y1), loc))
open(D + 'x_face_fuzz.txt', 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', D + 'x_face_fuzz.txt', '--save', D + 'x_face_fuzz.bimcraft', '--save', D + 'x_face_fuzz.ifc'], capture_output=True, text=True)
s = open(D + 'x_face_fuzz.ifc').read()
ents = {int(m.group(1)): (m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in re.finditer(r'^#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', s, re.M)}
def refs(t): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', t)]
def fmt(x):
    s = '%.6f' % (x + 0.0)
    return s.rstrip('0')
def norm(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0] ** 2 + v[1] ** 2); r = 1.0 / l
    return (v[0] * r, v[1] * r)
stats = {}
wl = [e for e in sorted(ents) if ents[e][0] == 'IFCWALL']
for (st, en, loc), w in zip(walls, wl):
    shape = refs(ents[w][1])[1]
    prof = None
    for r in refs(ents[shape][1]):
        if "'Body'" in ents[r][1]:
            solid = refs(ents[r][1])[-1]
            pr = refs(ents[solid][1])[0]
            poly = refs(ents[pr][1])[-1]
            prof = [ents[x][1].strip('()').split(',') for x in refs(ents[poly][1])][:-1]
    # the corners on y 0: start and end
    zs = [q for q in prof if q[1] in ('0.', '-0.')]
    ex, ey = en[0] - st[0], en[1] - st[1]
    L = math.sqrt(ex * ex + ey * ey)
    d = norm((ex, ey)); n = (-d[1], d[0])
    off = 0.0
    cands = {
        'start': (st[0] + n[0] * off, st[1] + n[1] * off),
        'endA': (st[0] + d[0] * L + n[0] * off, st[1] + d[1] * L + n[1] * off),
        'endB': (en[0] + n[0] * off, en[1] + n[1] * off),
        'endC': (st[0] + n[0] * off + d[0] * L, st[1] + n[1] * off + d[1] * L),
    }
    loc_y = lambda p: (p[0] - st[0]) * n[0] + (p[1] - st[1]) * n[1]
    for q in zs:
        is_end = float(q[0]) > 1.0
        for cn, P in cands.items():
            if (cn == 'start') == is_end:
                continue
            ok = fmt(loc_y(P)) == q[1]
            stt = stats.setdefault(cn, [0, 0])
            stt[0 if ok else 1] += 1
print(stats)

import math, sys, json, pickle
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import chypot, ulpdiff, nextf
rows = pickle.load(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol88.pkl', 'rb'))
G = 0.618033988749895
def geo_cot(a, b, deg):
    t = math.radians(deg)
    dx, dy = b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]
    c = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
    s = 1.0 if t > 0 else -1.0
    h = (c/2.0)/math.tan(abs(t)/2.0)*s
    r = c/(2.0*abs(math.sin(t/2.0)))
    m = ((a[0]+b[0])/2, (a[1]+b[1])/2)
    l = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy); k = 1.0/l
    nrm = (-dy*k, dx*k); cen = (m[0] + nrm[0]*h, m[1] + nrm[1]*h)
    st = math.atan2(a[1]-cen[1], a[0]-cen[0])
    return cen, r, st, t
def chords(r, t):
    step = 2.0*math.acos(1.0 - 0.25/r)
    return max(math.ceil(abs(t)/step), math.ceil(abs(math.degrees(t))/5.0), 1)
for dl, p, e1, e2 in rows:
    if 'points' in dl: continue
    T = dl['arc']
    cen, r, st, t = geo_cot(tuple(map(float, dl['start'])), tuple(map(float, dl['end'])), T)
    n = chords(r, t)
    a1o = e1['arc']
    out = []
    for dom, scale in [('f', 1.0), ('deg', T), ('rad', t)]:
        E = lambda u: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + t*(u/scale) if dom != 'f' else st + t*u), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + t*(u/scale) if dom != 'f' else st + t*u))
        if dom == 'deg': E = lambda u: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + math.radians(u)), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + math.radians(u)))
        if dom == 'rad': E = lambda u: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + u), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + u))
        pts = [(k*scale/n if dom != 'f' else k/n, E(k*scale/n if dom != 'f' else k/n)) for k in range(n + 1)]
        best = None
        for i in range(n):
            (ua, A), (ub, B) = pts[i], pts[i+1]
            dx, dy = B[0]-A[0], B[1]-A[1]
            s_ = ((p[0]-A[0])*dx + (p[1]-A[1])*dy)/(dx*dx + dy*dy)
            s_ = max(0.0, min(1.0, s_))
            Q = (A[0] + s_*dx, A[1] + s_*dy)
            dd = chypot(p[0]-Q[0], p[1]-Q[1])
            if best is None or dd < best[0]: best = (dd, ua + s_*(ub - ua))
        dch, uc = best
        hh = scale/(n + 1)
        lo, hi = max(uc - hh, 0.0) if scale > 0 else min(uc - hh, 0.0), min(uc + hh, scale) if scale > 0 else max(uc + hh, scale)
        a, b = (lo, hi) if lo < hi else (hi, lo)
        Df = lambda u: (lambda c: chypot(c[0]-p[0], c[1]-p[1]))(E(u))
        for _ in range(40):
            w = b - a
            c = b - G*w; d = a + G*w
            if Df(c) < Df(d): b = d
            else: a = c
        u = (a + b)/2
        q = E(u)
        if chypot(q[0]-p[0], q[1]-p[1]) >= dch: u = uc
        if dom == 'f': a1 = T*u

import math, sys, json, pickle
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import chypot, ulpdiff, nextf
rows = pickle.load(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol88.pkl', 'rb'))
G = 0.618033988749895
def geo_cot(a, b, deg):
    t = math.radians(deg)
    dx, dy = b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]
    c = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
    s = 1.0 if t > 0 else -1.0
    h = (c/2.0)/math.tan(abs(t)/2.0)*s
    r = c/(2.0*abs(math.sin(t/2.0)))
    m = ((a[0]+b[0])/2, (a[1]+b[1])/2)
    l = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy); k = 1.0/l
    nrm = (-dy*k, dx*k); cen = (m[0] + nrm[0]*h, m[1] + nrm[1]*h)
    st = math.atan2(a[1]-cen[1], a[0]-cen[0])
    return cen, r, st, t
def chords(r, t):
    step = 2.0*math.acos(1.0 - 0.25/r)
    return max(math.ceil(abs(t)/step), math.ceil(abs(math.degrees(t))/5.0), 1)
for dl, p, e1, e2 in rows:
    if 'points' in dl: continue
    T = dl['arc']
    cen, r, st, t = geo_cot(tuple(map(float, dl['start'])), tuple(map(float, dl['end'])), T)
    n = chords(r, t)
    a1o = e1['arc']
    out = []
    for dom, scale in [('f', 1.0), ('deg', T), ('rad', t)]:
        E = lambda u: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + t*(u/scale) if dom != 'f' else st + t*u), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + t*(u/scale) if dom != 'f' else st + t*u))
        if dom == 'deg': E = lambda u: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + math.radians(u)), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + math.radians(u)))
        if dom == 'rad': E = lambda u: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + u), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + u))
        pts = [(k*scale/n if dom != 'f' else k/n, E(k*scale/n if dom != 'f' else k/n)) for k in range(n + 1)]
        best = None
        for i in range(n):

            s_ = max(0.0, min(1.0, s_))

            dd = chypot(p[0]-Q[0], p[1]-Q[1])
            if best is None or dd < best[0]: best = (dd, ua + s_*(ub - ua))

            c = b - G*w; d = a + G*w

            else: a = c

        if dom == 'f': a1 = T*u
        elif dom == 'deg': a1 = u
        else: a1 = math.degrees(u)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Two walls at a node, the first on a face location line: the sign of y (in its axes) of its
mitred corner on that line, against ways of crossing the two faces' lines."""
import json, math, re, subprocess, sys, random
D = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/probe'
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3)
TYPES = {"Generic - 200mm": 200.0, "Exterior - 300mm": 300.0, "Interior - 100mm": 100.0}
def fmt(x):
    s = '%.6f' % (x + 0.0)
    return s.rstrip('0')
def norm(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0] ** 2 + v[1] ** 2); r = 1.0 / l
    return (v[0] * r, v[1] * r)
def perp(v): return (-v[1], v[0])
def add(a, b): return (a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1])
def sub(a, b): return (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])
def mul(a, k): return (a[0] * k, a[1] * k)
def cross(a, b): return a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0]
def dot(a, b): return a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1]
cases = []
cmds = []
for k in range(100):
    ox, oy = 15000.0 * (k % 10) + round(random.uniform(-2000, 2000), 2), 15000.0 * (k // 10) + round(random.uniform(-2000, 2000), 2)
    a0 = random.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
    L = random.uniform(3000, 6000)
    S = (ox, oy)
    N = (round(ox + L * math.cos(a0), 2), round(oy + L * math.sin(a0), 2))
    ang = random.choice([40, 60, 75, 90, 110, 130, 150]) * random.choice([1, -1])
    a1 = a0 + math.radians(180 - ang)
    E = (round(N[0] + 4000 * math.cos(a1), 2), round(N[1] + 4000 * math.sin(a1), 2))
    la = random.choice(['exterior-finish', 'interior-finish'])
    tb = random.choice(list(TYPES))
    lb = random.choice(['centre', 'exterior-finish', 'interior-finish'])
    cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [list(S), list(N)], "location": la}))
    cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [list(N), list(E)], "type": tb, "location": lb}))
    cases.append((S, N, E, la, tb, lb))
open(D + '/mitre3.txt', 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', D + '/mitre3.txt', '--save', D + '/mitre3.ifc'], capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.returncode:
    print(p.stderr[:2000]); sys.exit(1)
s = open(D + '/mitre3.ifc').read()
ents = {int(m.group(1)): (m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in re.finditer(r'^#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', s, re.M)}
def refs(t): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', t)]
walls = [e for e in sorted(ents) if ents[e][0] == 'IFCWALL']
stats = {}
for ci, (S, N, E, la, tb, lb) in enumerate(cases):
    wa = walls[2 * ci]
    shape = refs(ents[wa][1])[1]
    prof = None
    for rp in refs(ents[shape][1]):
        if "'Body'" in ents[rp][1]:
            solid = refs(ents[rp][1])[-1]
            pr = refs(ents[solid][1])[0]
            poly = refs(ents[pr][1])[-1]
            prof = [ents[x][1].strip('()').split(',') for x in refs(ents[poly][1])][:-1]
    tA = 200.0
    leftA, rightA = (0.0, 200.0) if la == 'exterior-finish' else (200.0, 0.0)
    t_b = TYPES[tb]
    leftB, rightB = {'centre': (t_b / 2, t_b / 2), 'exterior-finish': (0.0, t_b), 'interior-finish': (t_b, 0.0)}[lb]
    dA = norm(sub(N, S)); nA = perp(dA)
    dB = norm(sub(E, N)); nB = perp(dB)
    u = mul(dA, -1.0)
    # the face of A on its location line: A's left face if exterior-finish (offset 0), else right
    if la == 'exterior-finish':
        # A's left face is me.rp side (from the end, A's left is to the right of u)
        a_pt = sub(N, mul(perp(u), leftA))   # me.rp
        b_pt = add(N, mul(nB, leftB))        # B's left face (cw neighbour's left line)
        b_off_n, b_c = nB, leftB
        a_n, a_c = nA, leftA
    else:
        a_pt = add(N, mul(perp(u), rightA))  # me.lp (A's right face)
        b_pt = sub(N, mul(nB, rightB))       # B's right face
        b_off_n, b_c = nB, -rightB
        a_n, a_c = nA, -rightA
    den = cross(u, dB)
    if abs(den) < 1e-9:
        continue
    t = cross(sub(b_pt, a_pt), dB) / den
    if abs(t) > max(tA, t_b):
        continue
    P1 = add(a_pt, mul(u, t))
    s_ = cross(sub(a_pt, b_pt), u) / cross(dB, u)
    P2 = add(b_pt, mul(dB, s_))
    # Cramer on (normal, offset) lines: nA.p = nA.S + a_c (A's face), nB.p = nB.N + b_c
    cA = dot(nA, S) + a_c
    cB = dot(nB, N) + b_c
    det = nA[0] * nB[1] - nA[1] * nB[0]
    P3 = ((cA * nB[1] - cB * nA[1]) / det, (nA[0] * cB - nB[0] * cA) / det)
    locy = lambda P: dot(sub(P, S), nA)
    locx = lambda P: dot(sub(P, S), dA)
    zs = [q for q in prof if q[1] in ('0.', '-0.') and float(q[0]) > 1.0]
    want = None
    for q in zs:
        if q[0] == fmt(locx(P1)):
            want = q[1]
    if want is None:
        continue
    for cn, P in [('own', P1), ('other', P2), ('cramer', P3)]:
        ok = fmt(locy(P)) == want
        stt = stats.setdefault(cn, [0, 0])
        stt[0 if ok else 1] += 1
print(stats)

"""paramguids.py [exe] FILE...: the parameter (and other library) entries' guids a program gives each file."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

args = sys.argv[1:]
exe = '/workspace/executable'
if args and not args[0].endswith('.ifc'):
    exe = args.pop(0)
for f in args:
    out = tempfile.mktemp(suffix='.bimcraft')
    subprocess.run([exe, 'convert', os.path.basename(f), out], cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)), capture_output=True)
    if not os.path.exists(out):
        print(f, 'no output')
        continue
    d = json.load(open(out))
    os.unlink(out)
    print('==', f)
    for k, x in d['library'].items():
        if x.get('kind') in ('parameter',):
            print('  ', k, x.get('kind'), x.get('name'), x.get('guid'))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert Revit files to IFC with both programs; compare (normalised).
usage: rvtcmp.py FILE..."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, difflib
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools')
import case
def conv(exe, src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rvtx')
    out = os.path.join(d, 'out.ifc')
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([exe, 'convert', src, out], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        return -9, '', 'timeout', ''
    s = open(out, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read() if os.path.exists(out) else ''
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr, s
tot = same = 0
for src in sys.argv[1:]:
    a = conv(case.ORIG, src)
    b = conv(case.MINE, src)
    x = case.norm(a[3]).splitlines()
    y = case.norm(b[3]).splitlines()
    ok = x == y and a[0] == b[0]
    tot += 1
    same += ok

    d = json.load(open(out))
    os.unlink(out)
    lib = sorted(d['library'].items())
    return [x.get('guid') for k, x in lib][:5], d


base = open(os.path.join(D, 'a.ifc')).read()

    'sip13len': sip(struct.pack('<Q', len(data)) + data),
    'sip13ff': sip(data + b'\xff'),
    'sip24': sip(data, c_rounds=2, d_rounds=4),
    'len': len(data),
}
gens = {'splitmix': splitmix, 'xoshiro**': xoshiro_ss, 'xoshiro++': xoshiro_pp, 'xorshift64*': xorshift64s, 'wyrand': wyrand, 'lcg': lcg, 'pcg32': pcg32_pair}
for hn, hv in hashes.items():
    for gn, gf in gens.items():
        g = gf(hv)
        outs = [next(g) for _ in range(4000)]
        hits = 0
        where = []
        for i, x in enumerate(outs):
            for v in (x, int.from_bytes(x.to_bytes(8, 'little'), 'big')):
                if (v & ~(0xf << 12) & M64) in known_hi:
                    hits += 1
                    where.append(('hi', i))
                if (v & ~(0x3 << 62) & M64) in known_lo:
                    hits += 1
                    where.append(('lo', i))
        if hits:
            print('HIT', hn, gn, hits, where[:10])
print('done')

import re
import struct
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/seed')
M64 = (1 << 64) - 1
M32 = (1 << 32) - 1
exec(open('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/seed/hyp.py').read().split('hashes = {')[0].split("print(len(known), 'guids known')")[1].replace('\nM64', '\n#'), globals())

path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/seed/a.ifc'
outp = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/seed/a.bimcraft'
data = open(path, 'rb').read()
G = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
known = set(G.findall(open(outp).read()))
masked = set()
for g in known:
    b = bytes.fromhex(g.replace('-', ''))
    b = bytearray(b)
    b[6] &= 0x0f
    b[8] &= 0x3f
    masked.add(bytes(b))


def mask(b):
    b = bytearray(b)
    b[6] &= 0x0f
    b[8] &= 0x3f
    return bytes(b)


def fx(b):
    h = 0
    K = 0x517cc1b727220a95
    i = 0
    while i + 8 <= len(b):
        w = struct.unpack('<Q', b[i:i + 8])[0]
        h = ((rotl(h, 5) ^ w) * K) & M64
        i += 8
    if i + 4 <= len(b):
        w = struct.unpack('<I', b[i:i + 4])[0]
        h = ((rotl(h, 5) ^ w) * K) & M64
        i += 4
    while i < len(b):
        h = ((rotl(h, 5) ^ b[i]) * K) & M64
        i += 1
    return h


def rotl32(x, k):
    return ((x << k) | (x >> (32 - k))) & M32


def chacha_block(key_words, counter, nonce_words, rounds):
    c = [0x61707865, 0x3320646e, 0x79622d32, 0x6b206574]
    st = c + key_words + [counter & M32, (counter >> 32) & M32] + nonce_words
    x = st[:]

    def qr(a, b, c_, d):
        x[a] = (x[a] + x[b]) & M32
        x[d] = rotl32(x[d] ^ x[a], 16)
        x[c_] = (x[c_] + x[d]) & M32
        x[b] = rotl32(x[b] ^ x[c_], 12)
        x[a] = (x[a] + x[b]) & M32
        x[d] = rotl32(x[d] ^ x[a], 8)
        x[c_] = (x[c_] + x[d]) & M32
        x[b] = rotl32(x[b] ^ x[c_], 7)
    for _ in range(rounds // 2):
        qr(0, 4, 8, 12)
        qr(1, 5, 9, 13)
        qr(2, 6, 10, 14)
        qr(3, 7, 11, 15)
        qr(0, 5, 10, 15)
        qr(1, 6, 11, 12)
        qr(2, 7, 8, 13)
        qr(3, 4, 9, 14)
    out = [(x[i] + st[i]) & M32 for i in range(16)]
    return b''.join(struct.pack('<I', w) for w in out)


def pcg32_seed(state, n=32):
    MUL = 6364136223846793005
    INC = 11634580027462260723
    out = b''
    while len(out) < n:
        state = (state * MUL + INC) & M64
        xs = (((state >> 18) ^ state) >> 27) & M32
        rot = state >> 59
        x = ((xs >> rot) | (xs << ((-rot) & 31))) & M32
        out += struct.pack('<I', x)
    return out


def chacha_stream(seed32, rounds, nbytes):
    kw = list(struct.unpack('<8I', seed32))
    out = b''
    ctr = 0
    while len(out) < nbytes:
        out += chacha_block(kw, ctr, [0, 0], rounds)
        ctr += 1
    return out


def check_stream(name, s):
    hits = []
    for off in range(0, len(s) - 16, 4):
        if mask(s[off:off + 16]) in masked:
            hits.append(off)
    if hits:
        print('HIT', name, hits[:10])


variants = {
    'raw': data,
    'ff': data + b'\xff',
    'len': struct.pack('<Q', len(data)) + data,
}
seeds = {}
for vn, v in variants.items():
    seeds['fnv1a/' + vn] = fnv1a64(v)
    seeds['sip13/' + vn] = sip(v)
    seeds['sip24/' + vn] = sip(v, c_rounds=2, d_rounds=4)
    seeds['fx/' + vn] = fx(v)
for sn, sv in seeds.items():
    seed32 = pcg32_seed(sv)
    for rounds in (8, 12, 20):
        check_stream('%s chacha%d' % (sn, rounds), chacha_stream(seed32, rounds, 64 * 160))
    # the u64 generators again with fx
    for gn, gf in {'splitmix': splitmix, 'xoshiro**': xoshiro_ss, 'xoshiro++': xoshiro_pp, 'wyrand': wyrand}.items():
        g = gf(sv)
        outs = [next(g) for _ in range(3000)]
        for order in ('be', 'le'):
            s = b''.join(x.to_bytes(8, 'big' if order == 'be' else 'little') for x in outs)
            check_stream('%s %s %s' % (sn, gn, order), s)
print('done')

"""hyp3.py: guesses with cryptographic digests of the file as the generator's seed."""
import hashlib
import re
import struct
import sys

exec(open('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/seed/hyp2.py').read().split("variants = {")[0], globals())


def xoshiro_state(s, plus=False):
    s = list(s)
    while True:
        if plus:
            r = (rotl((s[0] + s[3]) & M64, 23) + s[0]) & M64
        else:
            r = (rotl((s[1] * 5) & M64, 7) * 9) & M64
        t = (s[1] << 17) & M64
        s[2] ^= s[0]
        s[3] ^= s[1]
        s[1] ^= s[2]
        s[0] ^= s[3]
        s[2] ^= t
        s[3] = rotl(s[3], 45)
        yield r


variants = {'raw': data, 'ff': data + b'\xff', 'len': struct.pack('<Q', len(data)) + data}
for vn, v in variants.items():
    digs = {
        'sha256': hashlib.sha256(v).digest(),
        'sha1': hashlib.sha1(v).digest() + b'\0' * 12,
        'md5x2': hashlib.md5(v).digest() * 2,
        'blake2b': hashlib.blake2b(v, digest_size=32).digest(),
        'blake2s': hashlib.blake2s(v).digest(),
        'sha512': hashlib.sha512(v).digest()[:32],
    }
    for dn, d in digs.items():
        name = '%s/%s' % (dn, vn)
        # the digest itself as guids
        check_stream(name + ' digest', hashlib.sha256(v).digest() + hashlib.md5(v).digest() + hashlib.sha1(v).digest())
        for rounds in (8, 12, 20):
            check_stream('%s chacha%d' % (name, rounds), chacha_stream(d, rounds, 64 * 160))
        st = list(struct.unpack('<4Q', d))
        for plus in (False, True):
            g = xoshiro_state(st, plus)
            outs = [next(g) for _ in range(3000)]
            for order in ('big', 'little'):
                check_stream('%s xoshiro%s %s' % (name, '++' if plus else '**', order), b''.join(x.to_bytes(8, order) for x in outs))
        # a u64 of the digest as seed for the u64 generators
        for k in (struct.unpack('<Q', d[:8])[0], struct.unpack('>Q', d[:8])[0]):
            for gn, gf in {'splitmix': splitmix, 'xoshiro**': xoshiro_ss, 'xoshiro++': xoshiro_pp, 'wyrand': wyrand}.items():
                g = gf(k)
                outs = [next(g) for _ in range(3000)]
                for order in ('big', 'little'):
                    check_stream('%s u64 %s %s' % (name, gn, order), b''.join(x.to_bytes(8, order) for x in outs))
            for rounds in (8, 12, 20):
                check_stream('%s pcg->chacha%d' % (name, rounds), chacha_stream(pcg32_seed(k), rounds, 64 * 160))
        # md5/sha of (digest, counter)
        s = b''
        for i in range(600):
            s += hashlib.md5(d[:16] + struct.pack('<Q', i)).digest()
        check_stream(name + ' md5ctr', s)
print('done')

steps.message:
I've committed everything on branch `worktree-agent-a3aa4b1d689cb6d8a`; the last commit is `f08c785` and the working tree is clean. The local suite now gives 1114/1173 identical to the original. The remaining differences are about two-thirds other agents' commands (split, duplicate_view, sheet, elevation, inspect, the dimension check). The rest are last-digit differences in my offset, trim and refit output, listed below.

**What changed since the last report**
- **Nearest point on a curve.** I found the original's method and reimplemented it. It finds the nearest chord, then runs 40 golden-section steps in the curve's own parameter. The search bracket is the parameter range divided by the number of drawn points on each side, clipped to the range. The refined point is used only if it is nearer than the chord. A polyline's parameter is segment index plus fraction (this is why the original splits [1000,300] to `300.00000000000006`). Circles and ellipses run in degrees, splines on their knots.
  - Against the original's full-precision split output: circles 65/65, ellipses 18/18, control splines 154/154. Polyline arcs are 124/192 for single arcs and 49/72 for polylines; the rest differ in the last few bits of a point or turn.
- **Splitting.** Arc halves now turn `arc·f` and `arc·(1−f)`, which matched 192/192. A spline through points is split by refitting each half (256 samples, unrounded points, the tangent kept where it is cut).
- **Arc centre.** It is now computed as half the chord over tan(half the turn). That raised exact matches on inside points from 75 to 95 of 128.
- **Ellipses** are drawn and evaluated by their parameter in degrees, as their span is stored.
- **trim_extend.** The end-moved arc turn is now the crossing's angle in degrees.
- **trim_extend undo.** It now records its own undo step even when no line changes, as the original does.

**Per command**
- **`detail_line`, `join_polyline`, `explode`:** match in every test of mine. The only differences are cases that use another agent's command (`inspect`, `duplicate_view`, or the dimension check).
- **`vertex`:** every test matches, including points off the convex side of arcs (e.g. `15.000000027`), spline knots at full precision, fitted splines and closed polylines. On new cases it went from 12/15 to 15/15.
- **`convert_spline`:** spline-through-points → control points matches. Control points → spline through points matches when the refit is short. Long refits drift apart (cs2 2/9, cs3 5/7, cs4 4/10, cs1 28/29) because the selection of new points cascades from tiny differences.
  - The cause is that the original evaluates splines through points differently from my B-spline, in the last bits. I couldn't pin down its formula; it is not exact rational evaluation, Hermite, Bernstein or de Boor with several solver variants.
- **`offset`:** lines and arcs match except a 1–2 ulp difference in a trimmed offset arc's turn (4 cases). Offsets of ellipses and splines pick different points for the same reason as above (4 cases).
- **`trim_extend`:** lines match. For arcs, the start-moved turn and some crossings differ by a few ulps. When both ends are exactly equally near the keep point, the original sometimes extends the other end (2 cases). te5 is 20/26 and te2 is 42/44.
  - The new end-moved formula traded two te2 extension cases for two te5 trim cases. A 26-case survey slightly favoured it, but neither formula matches most cases, because the crossing point itself differs in the last bits.

**API changes others will see (in `src/views/curves.rs`)**
- `Near` has a new field `param`: the curve's own parameter (polyline segment index plus fraction, degrees for circles and ellipses, knots for splines).
- New: `Curve::cut_near(&Near)` (used by `split_at`), `refit_with(.., round)`, and the constants `GOLDEN` and `NARROWINGS`.
- `refine_through` and `Bspline::polish` were removed.
- EDIT's `split` for detail lines should call `lineedit::split_line`, which is now much closer to the original.

**Still needed outside my files (unchanged from my last report)**
- **Core:** substitute library GUIDs with names in all parameters.
- **Loader:** call `lines::normalize` when a file is opened, and check the model on open.
- **Shared helpers:** `model::resolve_level` and `common::find_view` differ from the original (a GUID that isn't found should give the name error; a numeric string that isn't an element should say "is not a view").
- **DIMS:** its check should refuse dimensions on joined polylines.
- **EDIT:** move, rotate and mirror should use `Curve::map`/`moved`/`turned`/`mirrored`.
- **Views:** deleting a view should delete its lines.

Scratch scripts and probes are in `/tmp/views-lines/` (outside the repo).

"""infos2.py: compare `info x.ifc` between the original and mine, leaving out keys mine lacks
(the inspect reader's, not the import's)."""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess

MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a269fc74daf28a975/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
GUID = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
files = sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/assets/**/*.ifc', recursive=True))
same = 0
for f in files:
    outs = []
    for exe in ('/workspace/executable', MINE):
        p = subprocess.run([exe, 'info', os.path.basename(f)], cwd=os.path.dirname(f), capture_output=True, text=True)
        try:
            outs.append(json.loads(p.stdout))
        except Exception:
            outs.append({'error': p.stdout + p.stderr})
    o, m = outs
    missing = sorted(set(o) - set(m))
    extra = sorted(set(m) - set(o))
    for k in missing:
        o.pop(k)
    a = GUID.sub('G', json.dumps(o, sort_keys=True))
    b = GUID.sub('G', json.dumps(m, sort_keys=True))
    ok = a == b
    same += ok
    print('SAME' if ok else 'DIFF', f.replace('/workspace/assets/', ''), 'mine lacks', missing, 'extra', extra)
    if not ok:
        for k in sorted(set(o) | set(m)):
            if json.dumps(o.get(k), sort_keys=True) != json.dumps(m.get(k), sort_keys=True):
                print('    key', k, json.dumps(o.get(k), sort_keys=True)[:300], '|', json.dumps(m.get(k), sort_keys=True)[:300])
print(same, 'of', len(files))

steps.message:
The loader now behaves like the original on every file I could produce, and the work is committed on `worktree-agent-a67e925de02b79509` (latest commit `a55e539`, 20 commits on top of `main`). Files saved after opening are byte-identical modulo GUIDs and uids, error and open-reply messages match, and opening the 3.7 MB highrise takes 0.8 s against the original's 0.6 s.

**Checked against the original (GUIDs normalised):**
- **Round trips:** every corpus file (house, c1–c3, c8, highrise, all 9 languages) saves identically through `run --save`, `convert` and the `open`/`save` commands. So do files the original saved after `symbol_set`, `falls`, `convert_spline`, `explode`, `make_fill_pattern`, `reset_shape`, `add_point`, `purge` and `detail_line`/`text` variants.
- **Damaged files:** in my small-file and byte-damage suites (103 + 52 hand-written files, 145 cuts and flips, 8000 random mutations), every reader error matches. The few remaining differences are other modules' model checks.
- **No false refusals:** scaling every number of every element 4,364 ways, mine never refused a file the original opened, and saved files matched whenever both opened them. 1,500 random detail lines matched exactly.
- **Schema:** 10,294 type probes covering every field of every struct gave no reader differences.
- **Fixed this session:**
  - **Sets:** three fields are sorted, de-duplicated sets: graphics `layers`, CAD import `hidden`, template `controls`.
  - **Part GUIDs:** a part (layer, form, symbol, sketch line…) whose GUID is already taken by an element, a library entry or an earlier part gets a fresh one.
  - **Small fixes:** family `mesh` is a list of triangles; a file with no `format` reads as the oldest format; a 2-point polyline whose turns are all zero is a line; a `through` point within 1 mm of the chord means a straight line.
- **Linked CAD drawings** are re-read before the model check: the extension rule ("a .pdf file isn't a CAD drawing…"), the DXF reader's own messages, and the file's content replacing the stored drawing.
- **Open-time check order:** sections first, then every element in id order following its category's own order, then library ids (including "has the GUID of element N"), then references by id. A pairwise fault probe over every category matched 770 of 772 combinations.

**Still different:**
- **Frozen rooms:** a frozen room with no `kept` boundary gets one computed from the walls by the original; mine keeps none.
- **Cross-module order:** with several faults, the first error reported can differ.
  - The point-cloud check (cloud module) runs before my element pass. A deleted level gives the original "wall 100007: level … doesn't exist" but mine "pointcloud 100164: …".
  - Family, view-filter and type checks belong between my section checks.
  - A preset error is outranked by a dimension-type error in mine, because the styles text check does both.
- **Other modules' rules I don't implement**, for example:
  - families ("family `Box`: parameter `Width` holds a number, not "zz"")
  - view filter categories, wall-type layer sums
  - geometry: doors fitting walls, openings inside outlines, sketch loops, wall and room tops
  - size rules such as "riser must be above zero" and "a boundary needs 3 to 10000 points"
  - view names and view-range order, sheet sizes, schedule fields and filters
  - the CAD placement check, and the 8192-points arc rule
- **Corpus files c4–c7 fail to open in mine** with "wall 100168: `Mass Face` isn't a parameter of walls" (walls made by `wall_by_face`). That comes from the styles module's parameter check.
- **DWG files:** a linked DWG with a valid version header counts as reloaded but keeps its stored content; the original's DWG reader isn't replicated.

**Public API added or changed:**
- `crate::load::load` (kept) and `crate::load::load_report` → `(Project, left_out)`.
- `crate::readers::file`: `read`, `Read`, `check_opened`, `read_element`, `read_member_element`, `FORMAT`, `LIB_KINDS`, `MODEL_FIELDS`.
- `refcheck`: `check`, `elements`, `styles`, `materials`, `detail_groups`, `templates`, `runs`, `library_ids`, `kind_name`.
- `notes`: `reload_cads(path, &mut Project)` and `reload_links` replace `reload`; `link_error` stays.
- New `dxf::check`, and a `Set<T>` type in the schema language.
- `de`, `ids::Alloc`, `sync`, `refs`, `builtin::section` and `hooks::take_sizes` are unchanged from before.
- Other modules' functions I call: `crate::styles::text::check`, `presets::check`, `electrical::check`, `parameters::check_project`, then `crate::check::check`.

**Edits outside `src/load.rs` and `src/readers/file/`:**
- `src/readers/mod.rs`: `pub mod file;` only.
- `src/commands/basic.rs`, `open_project_file`: re-read CAD drawings, check the model, read links, and build the reply with `left_out`, `left_out_count`, `links_not_loaded` and `cads_not_reloaded`.
- `src/json.rs`: "EOF while parsing a list" when a file ends right after `[`.

**For you and the module owners:**
- **Styles bug:** walls made by face carry a `Mass Face` param that the styles parameter check rejects; that blocks c4–c7 from opening.
- **Cloud bug:** its check shows the raw GUID for a level of the wrong category ("level 93090f3c-…"), where the original shows "level 100007".
- **Check order:** to match the original exactly, each module needs a per-element check the open pass can call in id order.
- **Duplicated rules:** my refcheck carries some rules other agents may also write (detail lines, text runs, 3D-view ranges, roof slopes). Duplicates are harmless if the wording stays identical.
- **Decision for you:** whether `crate::check::check` should also call refcheck after every command; it currently runs only on open.

"""areaforms.py: which triangle-area formula, with 'last of the biggest', picks the original's
triangle in every room case."""
import itertools
import math
import os
import sys

sys.argv = ['x']
exec(open('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/rooms_tie.py').read().split("for f in os.sys.argv[1:]:")[0])

cases = {
    'r_rot30': (1065.384, 2154.701), 'r_rot60': (-154.701, 2398.717), 'r_rot120': (-3154.701, 2797.435),
    'r_rot200': (-1423.358, -1936.964), 'r_rot300': (3309.401, -398.717), 'sq': (2666.667, 2666.667),
    'r_off': (3000.0, 2333.333), 'r_wide': (5333.333, 1333.333), 'r_tall': (1333.333, 5333.333), 'r5': (4000.0, 2666.667),
}
for extra in ('hexa', 'kite', 'trap', 'trap2', 'tri2'):
    pass


def cr(o, a, b):
    return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])


forms = {}
for k in range(3):
    forms['cross@%d' % k] = (lambda k: lambda t: abs(cr(t[k], t[(k + 1) % 3], t[(k + 2) % 3])) / 2)(k)
    forms['crossrev@%d' % k] = (lambda k: lambda t: abs(cr(t[k], t[(k + 2) % 3], t[(k + 1) % 3])) / 2)(k)
forms['shoelace'] = lambda t: abs(sum(t[i][0] * t[(i + 1) % 3][1] - t[(i + 1) % 3][0] * t[i][1] for i in range(3))) / 2
forms['shoelace2'] = lambda t: abs(sum((t[(i + 1) % 3][0] - t[i][0]) * (t[(i + 1) % 3][1] + t[i][1]) for i in range(3))) / 2
forms['shoelace3'] = lambda t: abs(sum(t[i][0] * (t[(i + 1) % 3][1] - t[(i + 2) % 3][1]) for i in range(3))) / 2


def heron(t):
    a = math.dist(t[0], t[1])
    b = math.dist(t[1], t[2])
    c = math.dist(t[2], t[0])
    s = (a + b + c) / 2
    return math.sqrt(max(s * (s - a) * (s - b) * (s - c), 0))


forms['heron'] = heron
forms['cross_noabs'] = lambda t: cr(t[0], t[1], t[2]) / 2
forms['cross_nohalf'] = lambda t: abs(cr(t[0], t[1], t[2]))
# relative to the polygon's first point
results = {}
for name, f in forms.items():
    ok_all = True
    for cn, want in cases.items():
        path = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/rm2/%s.ifc' % cn
        tris = ears(poly_of(path))
        best = None
        for t in tris:
            a = f(t)
            if best is None or a >= best[1]:
                best = (t, a)
        t = best[0]
        c = ((t[0][0] + t[1][0] + t[2][0]) / 3, (t[0][1] + t[1][1] + t[2][1]) / 3)
        ok = abs(round(c[0], 3) - want[0]) < 0.002 and abs(round(c[1], 3) - want[1]) < 0.002
        if not ok:
            ok_all = False
    results[name] = ok_all
    print(name, 'ALL OK' if ok_all else '-')

"""earvariants.py: which ear-clipping start and pick rule gives the original's room point in every case."""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import tempfile

exec(open('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/rooms_tie.py').read().split("def ears(poly):")[0])


def orig_point(f, cache={}):
    if f in cache:
        return cache[f]
    out = tempfile.mktemp(suffix='.bimcraft')
    subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'convert', os.path.basename(f), out], cwd=os.path.dirname(f), capture_output=True)
    d = json.load(open(out))
    os.unlink(out)
    pts = [v['point'] for v in d['elements'].values() if v.get('category') == 'room']
    cache[f] = pts[0] if pts else None
    return cache[f]


def clip(v, scan):
    v = list(v)
    tris = []
    while len(v) > 3:
        n = len(v)
        done = False
        order = range(n) if scan == 'fwd' else range(n - 1, -1, -1)
        for j in order:
            a, b, c = v[(j + n - 1) % n], v[j], v[(j + 1) % n]
            if cross(a, b, c) <= 0:
                continue
            ok = True
            for q in v:
                if q in (a, b, c):
                    continue
                if cross(a, b, q) >= 0 and cross(b, c, q) >= 0 and cross(c, a, q) >= 0:
                    ok = False
                    break
            if ok:
                tris.append((a, b, c))
                v.pop(j)
                done = True
                break
        if not done:
            break
    if len(v) == 3:
        tris.append(tuple(v))
    return tris


def starts(v):
    out = {}
    n = len(v)
    out['file'] = 0
    out['lowy'] = min(range(n), key=lambda i: (v[i][1], v[i][0]))
    out['lowx'] = min(range(n), key=lambda i: (v[i][0], v[i][1]))
    out['lowy_hix'] = min(range(n), key=lambda i: (v[i][1], -v[i][0]))
    out['hiy'] = max(range(n), key=lambda i: (v[i][1], v[i][0]))
    out['hix'] = max(range(n), key=lambda i: (v[i][0], v[i][1]))
    return out


files = sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/rm2/*.ifc')) + sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/rm/**/*.ifc', recursive=True))
data = []
for f in files:
    try:
        p = poly_of(f)
    except Exception:
        continue
    want = orig_point(f)
    if want is None:
        continue
    data.append((f, p, want))
print(len(data), 'rooms')
for orient in ('ccw', 'cw'):
    for sname in ('file', 'lowy', 'lowx', 'lowy_hix', 'hiy', 'hix'):
        for scan in ('fwd', 'bwd'):
            for pick in ('last', 'first'):
                ok_all = 0
                bad = []
                for f, p, want in data:
                    v = list(p)
                    area = sum(v[i][0] * v[(i + 1) % len(v)][1] - v[(i + 1) % len(v)][0] * v[i][1] for i in range(len(v)))
                    if (area < 0) != (orient == 'cw'):
                        v.reverse()
                    k = starts(v)[sname]
                    v = v[k:] + v[:k]
                    tris = clip(v, scan)
                    best = None
                    for t in tris:
                        a = abs((t[1][0] - t[0][0]) * (t[2][1] - t[0][1]) - (t[1][1] - t[0][1]) * (t[2][0] - t[0][0])) / 2
                        if best is None or (a >= best[1] if pick == 'last' else a > best[1]):
                            best = (t, a)
                    t = best[0]
                    c = ((t[0][0] + t[1][0] + t[2][0]) / 3, (t[0][1] + t[1][1] + t[2][1]) / 3)
                    if abs(round(c[0], 3) - want[0]) < 0.002 and abs(round(c[1], 3) - want[1]) < 0.002:
                        ok_all += 1
                    else:
                        bad.append(os.path.basename(f))
                print(orient, sname, scan, pick, ok_all, 'of', len(data), bad[:6])

                ok += 1
            else:
                bad.append(os.path.basename(f))

"""smtest.py OUT.bimcraft: are the guids' 64-bit halves SplitMix64 outputs of states k*gamma apart?"""
import re
import sys

M64 = (1 << 64) - 1
GAMMA = 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
G = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
guids = []
for g in G.findall(open(sys.argv[1]).read()):
    if g not in guids:
        guids.append(g)
print(len(guids), 'guids')


def inv_xorshift(z, k):
    # invert z ^= z >> k
    x = z
    s = k
    while s < 64:
        x = z ^ (x >> k)
        s += k
    return x & M64


def unmix(z):
    # splitmix64 finaliser: z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * C1; z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * C2; z ^ (z >> 31)
    C1 = 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    C2 = 0x94d049bb133111eb
    i1 = pow(C1, -1, 1 << 64)
    i2 = pow(C2, -1, 1 << 64)
    z = inv_xorshift(z, 31)
    z = (z * i2) & M64
    z = inv_xorshift(z, 27)
    z = (z * i1) & M64
    z = inv_xorshift(z, 30)
    return z


def unmix_murmur(z):
    # murmur3 fmix64: z ^= z >> 33; z *= C1; z ^= z >> 33; z *= C2; z ^= z >> 33
    C1 = 0xff51afd7ed558ccd
    C2 = 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53
    z = inv_xorshift(z, 33)
    z = (z * pow(C2, -1, 1 << 64)) & M64
    z = inv_xorshift(z, 33)
    z = (z * pow(C1, -1, 1 << 64)) & M64
    z = inv_xorshift(z, 33)
    return z


# candidate 64-bit values for each half, with the masked bits free
cands = {}
for gi, g in enumerate(guids):
    b = bytes.fromhex(g.replace('-', ''))
    for order in ('big', 'little'):
        hi = int.from_bytes(b[:8], order)
        lo = int.from_bytes(b[8:], order)
        # where the version nibble and the variant bits sit for this byte order
        if order == 'big':
            hv = [(hi & ~(0xf << 12)) | (k << 12) for k in range(16)]
            lv = [(lo & ~(0x3 << 62)) | (k << 62) for k in range(4)]
        else:
            hv = [(hi & ~(0xf << 52)) | (k << 52) for k in range(16)]
            lv = [(lo & ~(0x3 << 6)) | (k << 6) for k in range(4)]
        for v in hv:
            cands.setdefault(order, []).append((v, gi, 'hi'))
        for v in lv:
            cands.setdefault(order, []).append((v, gi, 'lo'))
for name, inv in (('splitmix', unmix), ('murmur', unmix_murmur)):
    for order, lst in cands.items():
        states = {}
        for v, gi, part in lst:
            states.setdefault(inv(v), []).append((gi, part))
        hits = 0
        for s, who in states.items():
            for k in range(1, 9):
                t = (s + k * GAMMA) & M64
                if t in states:
                    hits += 1
                    if hits <= 5:
                        print('HIT', name, order, k, who, states[t])
        print(name, order, 'hits', hits)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The original imports each IFC (or Revit) file into a project; both programs then export that
project; compare (order of storey-sorted lists ignored).
usage: impcmp.py FILE..."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools')
import case
src = open('/tmp/ifc-export-agent/tools/rvtcmp3.py').read()
fix_src = src[src.index('    import re as _re'):src.index('    x = fix(case.norm(a[3]))')]
ns = {}
exec('import re as _re\ndef make():\n' + fix_src + '    return fix\n', ns)
fix = ns['make']()
D = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/impproj'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
tot = same = 0
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    base = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0]
    bim = os.path.join(D, base + '_' + str(abs(hash(f)) % 10000) + '.bimcraft')
    p = subprocess.run([case.ORIG, 'convert', f, bim], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode:
        print(base, 'import failed', p.stderr[:100]); continue
    a = case.export(case.ORIG, bim)
    b = case.export(case.MINE, bim)
    x = fix(case.norm(a[3]))
    y = fix(case.norm(b[3]))
    ok = x == y and a[0] == b[0]
    tot += 1; same += ok
    first = ''
    if not ok:
        import difflib
        for l in difflib.unified_diff(x, y, lineterm='', n=0):
            if l.startswith(('-#', '+#', '-I', '+I')):
                first = l[:150]
                break
    print('%-30s %s %d/%d lines %s' % (base, 'SAME' if ok else 'DIFF', len(x), len(y), first))
print(same, '/', tot)

Other sub-agents do views/sheets/crops; 3D views, dimension_3d, spots; graphics/filters/templates; text/tag/linework; detail lines; regions/groups — "Don't do theirs." Match the original exactly (replies, error texts and their order, saved file field order and number formatting, undo labels, model check messages). You may add child modules of your own files… Do NOT edit `src/views/mod.rs`, `src/views/common.rs`, `src/views/model.rs` or anything outside `src/views/`; if you need a change there, copy what you need into your own files and say so in your final report."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Project model: elements as JSON (insertion-ordered Map), GUID references, library entries (kind "dimension-type"), `dimension_types` section keyed by name.
   - Dimension saved field order: guid, category, level, view, kind, orient, refs, at, type, prefix, suffix, above, below, replace, equality, texts, equal, locked, alignment. refs `{id: guid, face, point?}`; texts `[{segment, prefix, suffix, above, below, replace}]` sorted by segment; locked `[{segment, length}]` (length unrounded current value).
   - Command param check order for `dimension`: level → at → kind → orient → refs (array; each parsed+resolved in order) → type → prefix,suffix,above,below,replace → equality; then check-time: type exists → count by kind → orient only for linear → per ref (exists, category, face, shape) → "twice" → parallel/square; "points all in one place".
   - Point picks within 100 mm (inclusive), candidates in element-id order (first wins ties): walls cut by plan (base ≤ cut < top; cut = level elevation + view_range.cut), each wall: centre/left/right as full-span lines (s0..s1), start face, end face; doors/windows in cut walls; grids. Picks after the first ref filtered: aligned → parallel to first ref's line; linear/angular → non-parallel. Endpoint picks (unfiltered): wall centre/left/right ends, door/window line ends, grid ends, plan's detail line ends. Radial/diameter picks: round columns (cut), curved wall arcs, detail circles/arcs; arc_length: curved walls/arcs only.
   - Stations = crossing of dimension line through `at` along measure dir (lines) / projection (points); dir = linear orient axis, else perpendicular to first line, else first point→next distinct point; made eastward (x>1e-9, else north).
   - Parallel tolerance |cross| ≤ 1e-3; values rounded r2 (hundredths); labels: mm 0 dec round-half-away, cm 1 dec trimmed (mm*0.1), m 2 dec (mm*0.001), ft 2 dec, in/ft-in sixteenths; type `decimals`/`units` override; baseline/ordinate; equality text for aligned/linear only; segment texts override field by field; replace replaces whole label; radial "{sym} {len}" (no space if sym empty); angular "{r2}°".
   - Wall joins (geom.rs): L-joint ends within 1 mm & heights overlap; nodes sorted by angle of outward directions; face meets CCW/CW neighbour's face; sharp limit |along| ≤ thickest at node + 1e-9 else squared; location-line faces keep P when the mitre point is forward (real partners only); curved walls' own corners radial/free; straight walls meet curved neighbours' tangent lines; walls a node lies within (|off| ≤ t/2+1e-9, along margin > 1 mm from ends) join the node as two virtual rays (curved: tangent face lines at P); pure T stage (only when no L partners): P band [-t/2, t/2+1], per-face caps with reach max(tW,tO); face beyond near face failing reach invalidates T; end faces at farthest projections s0/s1 from right→left.
   - Moves (as `move`): wall line translated; joined neighbours' shared ends at intersection rounded r3p; T ends slide; free ends unrounded; doors keep absolute position (moved with host by v), offset recomputed via reciprocal-normalized dir (noise matches original e.g. 2999.9999999999995); grids unrounded; detail lines rounded r3p.
   - keep: runs of locked segments rigid, equal ties all (locked length if any; locked lengths must agree within TOL else "its locked segments differ in length, so they can't be equal"; without locks ends stay); runs placed by moved stations (must agree else "what the command moved pulls its locked segments apart"), else by first station; moved = element JSON differs from before OR moved by keep earlier in this call; TOL 0.01; PASSES 16; before from snapshot ring when not given.

   - src/views/dims/refs.rs (~336 lines): Face/End/Target/Ref/RefIn/IdIn, serde-like parsing with exact messages (e.g. "{json} is not a reference {id, face?} or a point [x, y]: unknown field `x`, expected one of `id`, `face`, `point`", "`endpoint` is a point [x, y], not …", "`abc` is not a GUID (xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx) or an id", "invalid length 0, expected struct Reference with 3 elements"), named/named_guid/category_words/what.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""randjoin.py seed n: builds a random wall layout with the original and compares every wall's
face and end points between the two programs."""
import subprocess, json, os, sys, random, tempfile, shutil
seed = int(sys.argv[1]); n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 4
random.seed(seed)
types = ['Generic - 200mm', 'Exterior - 300mm', 'Interior - 100mm']
locs = ['centre', 'exterior-finish', 'interior-finish', 'core-centre', 'exterior-core', 'interior-core']
cmds = []
def pt():
    return [random.randint(-8, 8) * 500, random.randint(-8, 8) * 500]
for k in range(n):
    kind = random.random()
    t = random.choice(types)
    extra = ''
    if random.random() < 0.3:
        extra += ',"location":"%s"' % random.choice(locs)
    if kind < 0.5:
        # a polyline, closed or not
        m = random.randint(2, 4)
        pts = [pt() for _ in range(m)]
        closed = 'true' if (m >= 3 and random.random() < 0.5) else 'false'
        cmds.append('wall {"points":%s,"closed":%s,"type":"%s"%s}' % (json.dumps(pts), closed, t, extra))
    else:
        arc = (",\"arc\":%d" % random.choice([-120,-60,-30,30,60,90,150])) if random.random() < 0.5 else ""
        cmds.append("wall {\"points\":%s,\"type\":\"%s\"%s%s}" % (json.dumps([pt(), pt()]), t, extra, arc))
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/views-dims')
args = ['/workspace/executable', 'run']
for c in cmds:
    args += ['--cmd', c]
args += ['--cmd', 'grid {"start":[-100000,-50000],"end":[100000,-50000]}', '--cmd', 'grid {"start":[-50000,-100000],"end":[-50000,100000]}', '--save', 'r.bimcraft']
p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'r.bimcraft')):
    print('build failed', p.stderr.strip()[:200]); sys.exit(0)
pr = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'r.bimcraft')))
proj = '/tmp/views-dims/rand%d.bimcraft' % seed
shutil.copy(os.path.join(d, 'r.bimcraft'), proj)
shutil.rmtree(d)
walls = [k for k, e in pr['elements'].items() if e['category'] == 'wall']
grids = [k for k, e in pr['elements'].items() if e['category'] == 'grid']
refs = []
for w in walls:
    for face in ['centre', 'left', 'right', 'start', 'end']:
        for point in ['start', 'end']:
            refs.append('{"id":%s,"face":"%s","point":"%s"}' % (w, face, point))
out = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/views-dims/ptcmp.py', proj, grids[0], grids[1]] + refs, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
print('seed', seed, out.strip().split('\n')[-1])
if 'same' in out and out.strip().split('\n')[-1].split('/')[0] != out.strip().split('\n')[-1].split('/')[1].split(' ')[0]:
    print('\n'.join(cmds))
    print(out)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Wall 100003 (y = 5850, x 150 -> 7850, 300 thick) ending on the arc wall (8000,0)->(8000,6000),
arc -90, 200 thick: where its faces meet the arc wall's faces (chords or circle)."""
import math
def norm(v):
    l = math.hypot(*v); r = 1.0 / l
    return (v[0] * r, v[1] * r)
S, E, arc = (8000.0, 0.0), (8000.0, 6000.0), -90.0
sweep = math.radians(arc)
c = math.hypot(E[0] - S[0], E[1] - S[1])
d = norm((E[0] - S[0], E[1] - S[1]))
R = c / (2 * math.sin(abs(sweep) / 2))
h = (c / 2) / math.tan(sweep / 2)
cen = ((S[0] + E[0]) * 0.5 - d[1] * h, (S[1] + E[1]) * 0.5 + d[0] * h)
print('R', R, 'centre', cen)
a0 = math.atan2(S[1] - cen[1], S[0] - cen[0])
# segments
r_ = abs(R)
turn = (r_ * abs(sweep)) / r_
k = max(math.ceil(turn / math.radians(5)), math.ceil(abs(sweep) / (2 * math.acos(1 - 1 / r_))))
print('segs', k)
for off in [100.0, -100.0]:
    rr = R - off if sweep > 0 else R + off
    pts = [(cen[0] + math.cos(a0 + sweep * i / k) * rr, cen[1] + math.sin(a0 + sweep * i / k) * rr) for i in range(k + 1)]
    for fy in [5700.0, 6000.0]:
        # crossing of the line y = fy with the chords
        for i in range(k):
            p, q = pts[i], pts[i + 1]
            if (p[1] - fy) * (q[1] - fy) <= 0 and p[1] != q[1]:
                t = (fy - p[1]) / (q[1] - p[1])
                x = p[0] + (q[0] - p[0]) * t
                print('off', off, 'face y', fy, 'chord', i, 'x', x, 'local x', x - 150.0)
        # with the circle
        dy = fy - cen[1]
        if abs(dy) <= rr:
            dx = math.sqrt(rr * rr - dy * dy)
            print('off', off, 'face y', fy, 'circle x', cen[0] - dx, cen[0] + dx, 'local', cen[0] - dx - 150.0, cen[0] + dx - 150.0)

"""xopairs.py OUT.bimcraft: for pairs of guids likely made one after the other, solve a xoshiro256**
state from their four halves and look for the guid it would make next anywhere in the file."""
import json
import re
import sys

sys.argv = sys.argv[:2]
out = sys.argv[1]
exec(open('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/seed/xotest.py').read().split("if __name__ == '__main__':")[0])
txt = open(out).read()
G = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
allg = set(G.findall(txt))
d = json.loads(txt)
lib = d['library']
pairs = []
els = d['elements']
ks = sorted(els.keys(), key=int)
for a, b in zip(ks, ks[1:]):
    pairs.append(('el %s,%s' % (a, b), els[a].get('guid'), els[b].get('guid')))
lk = sorted(lib.keys(), key=lambda k: -int(k))
for a, b in list(zip(lk, lk[1:]))[:6]:
    pairs.append(('lib %s,%s' % (a, b), lib[a].get('guid'), lib[b].get('guid')))


def guid_of(a, b, order):
    by = bytearray(a.to_bytes(8, order) + b.to_bytes(8, order))
    by[6] = (by[6] & 0x0f) | 0x40
    by[8] = (by[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80
    h = by.hex()
    return '%s-%s-%s-%s-%s' % (h[:8], h[8:12], h[12:16], h[16:20], h[20:])


for name, g1, g2 in pairs:
    if not g1 or not g2:
        continue
    for order in ('big', 'little'):
        for swap in (False, True):
            outs = []
            for g in (g1, g2):
                hi, lo = halves(g, order)
                pr = [(hi, 'hi'), (lo, 'lo')]
                if swap:
                    pr.reverse()
                outs.extend(pr)
            frees = [free_bits(order, w) for _, w in outs]
            nfree = sum(len(f) for f in frees)
            found = False
            for combo in range(1 << nfree):
                vals = []
                c = combo
                for (v, w), fb in zip(outs, frees):
                    for bit in fb:
                        v = (v & ~(1 << bit)) | ((c & 1) << bit)
                        c >>= 1
                    vals.append(v)
                eqs = []
                for n, v in enumerate(vals):
                    s1 = out_to_s1(v)
                    for i in range(64):
                        eqs.append((S1[n][i], (s1 >> i) & 1))
                x = solve(eqs)
                if x is None:
                    continue
                pred = run(state_words(x), 12)
                for k in range(4, 12, 2):
                    a, b = pred[k], pred[k + 1]
                    if swap:
                        a, b = b, a
                    if guid_of(a, b, order) in allg:
                        print('FOUND', name, order, swap, k)
                        found = True
                if found:
                    break
            print(name, order, 'swap' if swap else '', 'found' if found else '-')
            sys.stdout.flush()
