1	# Levels, walls, roofs, floors, ceilings, shafts, stairs
2	
3	Moved from the root `CLAUDE.md`, word for word: the root keeps the rules and the map, and this file is read when the area is touched.
4	
5	Levels have elevations, and each is a plane over its `extent` (`Model::level_extent`; without one, `Model::model_extent`):
6	sections and elevations draw a level over as much of its extent as they see, and the 3D view outlines it, depth-tested and
7	picked as the level; unselected, its two edges nearer the camera are left out. Its name goes on a `view3d::LevelHead`, an
8	unseen vertical plane past the right end of its far edges, where an elevation marker family will stand. Selected alone, a
9	level's ends in a section are grips (`Model::level_extent_along`) and so are its plane's edge middles in 3D
10	(`geom::edge_grips`, `Camera::on_plane`); both run `modify {extent}`.
11	A section or an elevation cropped shows its line's length and its crop's heights; uncropped, everything along its line
12	(`render::crop_region` is none, and there are no grips).
13	A level is also its plan: its view range (`Model::plan_range`)
14	cuts 1200 mm above it unless set, and its crop region bounds what the plan shows. Rooms find their walls at 1200 mm whatever
15	a plan cuts (`Model::bounding`). In a section or an elevation, points run along its line from its start, and up; on a sheet,
16	they're paper mm from its bottom left corner; notes and spot elevations live in those terms in their view.
17	A wall's `start` and `end` are on its location line: its centre line unless `location` says otherwise (`walls::faces`).
18	Its exterior is to the left of start to end, as in Revit, so walls drawn clockwise face out; a compound type lists its
19	layers from the exterior in, and a floor, roof or ceiling type from the top down (IFC import turns a wall round, or a slab's
20	layers over, by the way its layer set's usage stacks them). A layer's material is a name in the project's library
21	(`Model::materials`): its colour shades the layer in 3D, its cut pattern is a drafting pattern (`GAP` px apart on screen and
22	paper, where the layer is `PATTERN_ROOM` px wide), its surface pattern a model pattern (`MODULE` mm, its real size). A curved wall turns `arc` degrees, counter-clockwise positive (`walls::Axis`). Where walls meet,
23	their faces meet in mitred caps at any angle, and a wall ending on another stops at its face (`walls::cap`); plans, 3D,
24	sections and IFC all draw that outline (`walls::outline`, `walls::prisms`). Room areas are measured at the walls' centre
25	lines, run on or back to meet at joins (`walls::centre_line`). A room separator (`roomseparator`, made by `room_separator` a line per segment) bounds rooms as a wall's centre line
26	would and nothing else: it is no edge of a floor, a ceiling or a roof (`Model::bounding_lines` takes it, `wall_lines` and
27	`face_lines` don't; an end drawn to a wall's face runs on to its centre line there, so the line splits rooms measured at
28	the centre lines too), it is drawn in plan only, and it goes to IFC as an `IfcVirtualElement` of `ObjectType` `RoomSeparation`
29	with an `Axis` polyline on its storey, which the import reads back. The desktop's Room Separator, beside Room, lays one a
30	click from the point before until Esc. A room's height is Revit's: from `base_offset` over its level up to `limit_offset` over
31	its Upper Limit, `top_level` (none: Not Bounded, the offset then over its own level). A new room reaches 300 mm under the
32	level above (`ROOM_BELOW_ABOVE`), or with none above is Not Bounded and 2500 mm tall; a room read from a file without them is
33	Not Bounded, 2500 mm. `Model::room_span` and `room_height` give it, `elements` its `unbounded_height` and `volume_m3` (the area times that height, not cut by floors or roofs), and the IFC
34	space is swept that tall. A room's colour on plans (`Room::colour`) styles that solid in IFC as other elements' colours do: an
35	`IfcStyledItem` on the swept solid, its unnamed `IfcSurfaceStyle` shading in the colour (`IfcSurfaceStyleShading`, which IFC4's
36	rendering style extends; `Step::surface_style`, which a material's style shares), so a viewer shades the space in it. The import
37	reads it back from the colour the space's body is styled in (`import::item_colours`), so a round trip keeps it and a space
38	another program styled comes in filled in its colour; a room that isn't enclosed has no body, so no colour, in IFC. A frozen room (`frozen`, an instance parameter: `room {frozen}` or `modify {id, frozen}`) keeps the
39	boundary it has when frozen, both ways it can be measured (`Room::kept`, given after the command that froze it by
40	`Model::keep_rooms`, which the engine calls after every command, and let go when it is thawed): `room_region_at` returns it
41	and the plan draws it without finding the level's lines, so the walls are never searched for it again, which saves the time
42	of many rooms; moved, rotated or mirrored, its boundary goes with it, and only a bounded room can be frozen. Walls and columns (and structural columns) bound
43	rooms while their Room Bounding is on (`Wall::room_bounding`, `Column::room_bounding`, on unless set; `Model::room_bounding`,
44	`bounding_columns`, `room_lines`): a column's outline either way rooms are measured, a free one an island. A wall with it off
45	still bounds floors and roofs picked by their walls. Walls and columns bound a level's rooms where its
46	Computation Height (`Level::computation_height`, 1200 mm unless set) cuts them; room separation lines bound them whatever
47	it is. Two rooms can't share a space (`Model::room_bound`, `Unbound`): the one placed first (the lower id) keeps it, the
48	other is unbounded, and `room` and `inspect` warn. A room can be placed where nothing encloses it: unbounded, it covers a
49	`UNBOUNDED_ROOM` square round its point (`Model::room_outline`), as Revit's. A plan labels it NOT ENCLOSED, or REDUNDANT where another
50	room has its space. Its reference, a cross from the point it was placed at out along the diagonals to its boundary
51	(`geom::ray_hit`), drawn as the room's own lines (a click on it picks the room), is the subcategory `roomreference` under
52	Rooms, off unless shown (`graphics {show: ["roomreference"]}`), beside `roomseparator`, the separation lines.
53	Subcategories are general (`graphics::SUBCATEGORIES`: a key, its category, a name, whether it is off unless shown):
54	a view holds them as categories, with `Override::shown` for the ones off unless shown, `Graphics::hides` answers for
55	them (a category hidden hides its subcategories), and Visibility/Graphics folds them under their category. In a 3D
56	view rooms are off until shown (`graphics::OFF_IN_3D`, `Graphics::shows_in_3d`; `graphics {view: "{3D}", show: [rooms]}`,
57	or ticked in its Visibility/Graphics), every new 3D view so; shown, each is drawn as below, fainter than a selected one,
58	and a selected room is seen whatever the view says: a see-through solid in the selection's colour from its bottom to its top
59	(`orbit::room_solid`, drawn over the picture, so it shows through walls). With `room_area {at: "finish"}` (`Model::room_area`, Revit's Area and
60	Volume Computations) room areas are measured at the walls' faces instead (`face_lines` and the separators), the floor inside them; the IFC space
61	takes that outline, and its `Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities` give both whichever is set: `GrossFloorArea` and `GrossPerimeter` at
62	the centre lines, `NetFloorArea` and `NetPerimeter` at the faces, `Height` (the room's Unbounded Height) and `GrossVolume` and `NetVolume`. Walls, slabs, doors and windows
63	carry theirs too (`ifc::wall_quantities`): a wall its `Length` on its axis, `Width`, `Height` and side and volume, gross and less the
64	doors and windows in it (each cut to its height; joins aside), or only `Length` and `Width` when attached, as its height then varies;
65	a level slab its `Width` (depth), `Perimeter` and area and volume less its openings, a sloped one only its `Width`; a door or window
66	its `Width`, `Height`, `Perimeter` and `Area`. An attached top or base follows the roof's or floor's plane
67	over each part of the wall (a roof's slopes each over its own part of the plan); a mirrored wall runs back the other way.
68	A wall's top is `Model::own_top`, and 3D, sections, plans, IFC and what a wall is attached to all read it there (`walls::heights`
69	takes it, or what the wall is attached to): its `top_level`'s elevation plus its `top_offset` (file format 15, Revit's Top Offset,
70	mm, negative below the level), or its base plus its `height` when it has no top level, which an offset does not touch.
71	`Model::check` refuses a wall whose top does not come out above its base, saying how tall it comes out and by how much to raise it.
72	The Properties palette shows Top Offset under Top Constraint for a wall that has one.
73	A roof by footprint is the straight skeleton of its outline and its `courtyards` (`skeleton::faces`: the outline
74	counter-clockwise, the courtyards clockwise, the roof to the left of every edge): each edge moves in at speed 1, a gable's at
75	0, and its slope rises from it, reaching the roof's base `overhang` in from its eaves; a courtyard's edges number on after
76	the outline's, and every ring keeps its numbers whichever way round it runs, so `gables` stay put through a mirror.
77	`Roof::slopes` (file format 15) gives each edge a slope of its own, in degrees, numbered as `gables` are: 0 is the roof's `slope`,
78	and an empty list, every edge. `Model::roof_faces` then moves an edge in at the run over the rise of its slope, scaled so the
79	shallowest moves at 1 (every edge at one slope still moves at exactly 1), so edges of different slopes reach the same height
80	together and the slopes meet along their hips; the eaves stay level, the roof's base `overhang` in from them lowered by the roof's
81	`slope`, whatever the edges' own. A gable stays upright whatever its slope, and a flat roof (`slope` 0) keeps its `slopes` as it keeps
82	its `gables`, unused. `Model::check` refuses a list of the wrong length, saying how many edges there are, and a slope outside 0
83	to 75°, saying which edge. A sketch line may carry a `slope` (`SketchLine::slope`; the Slope row of Properties, with one line of a
84	roof's sketch picked, sets it): the roof keeps it as the `slopes` of the edges along that line (`sketch::along`), never in its
85	`sketch`, which `sketch::check` refuses to hold one. `edit_boundary` keeps the slope of an edge that stays or that a new
86	line cuts in two (an edge lying along an old one), the lines' own `slope` (0 sets the roof's) winning over it, and without
87	`slope` on the lines it keeps what the edges had; `edit_boundary` without a sketch gives the lines with the slope their edges share.
88	Over the walls (`floor_outline`, which `roof_footprint` grows by the overhang), a loop of them standing free inside the outer
89	ones, joined to none of them and with no room in it, is a courtyard, open through the floor and the roof; one joined to them,
90	or with a room in it, is rooms, and both run over it.
91	`Model::roof_faces` are its slopes, each the loops round it in plan (a slope can close round a courtyard whose far side is a
92	gable) with the plane of its underside, trimmed where it `join`s another; `Model::roof_pieces` are those less their holes
93	and its `openings`, convex where cut. A floor's top is at its level plus `offset`,
94	or with a slope arrow, there at the arrow's tail and rising `slope` degrees toward its head (`Model::floor_top`); it's its
95	type's thickness across the slope, so plumb it's thicker. Its `openings` are holes inside it, apart, and `Model::floor_slabs`
96	what's left, convex where cut. A floor's `shape` (IDEAS MOD-16, [design](../shape-editing.md)) folds its top into planes:
97	points `z` mm above (negative, below) where the top would be without them, and split lines it folds along, each a part
98	with an id and a GUID (`ShapePoint`, `SplitLine`). `Model::shape_planes` triangulates its outline, openings, points and
99	lines (`triangulation::constrained`), lifts each corner by the point there (a corner with none stays at 0) and merges
100	neighbours in one plane; `Model::floor_faces` are those planes in convex pieces, or the unshaped top, and `floor_slabs`,
101	the 3D view, sections and the element's details take them. In IFC a shaped slab is one closed `IfcFacetedBrep`
102	(`Model::shape_solid`: its top's planes, the same planes under them, plumb sides round its outline and openings, each
103	corner written once), and a sloped or shaped slab gives `GrossVolume` and `NetVolume`, its plan through its depth plumb;
104	every floor's details give `volume_m3`, what's left of it in plan (shafts too) through that depth. A shaped floor is its type's thickness plumb, so its planes meet
105	underneath too, and has no slope arrow (`Model::check`, `shape_ok`, refuses one, and points outside the outline or in an
106	opening, points within a millimetre of each other, a split line's end that is no point and no corner, and lines that
107	cross). A wall attached to one follows `Model::shape_triangles`, its top over the whole outline as if its openings were
108	closed, as a slope arrow's plane runs on over them. Plans draw each plane's edges as thin as the outline. `edit_shape`
109	gives the shape anew or says what it is, `add_point`, `add_split_line` and `reset_shape` change it a piece at a time (an
110	end of a line that is no point becomes one, at the height the top has there), `edit_boundary` keeps what stays inside the
111	new outline and its openings, cuts a split line where it leaves them, and gives each new end and each new corner a point at
112	the height the top had there, so a hole cut through a shaped top leaves it as it was round the hole; it names what it
113	`dropped`, `cut` and `added`. Moves and mirrors take the shape along, and snaps find its points. A flat roof by
114	footprint (`slope` 0, no extrusion, joining none) takes a shape too (`Roof::shape`, `Roof::unshapeable` says why another
115	can't): the commands, checks and both views' tools see its top as a floor's (`Model::shapeable`, `Model::roof_as_floor`:
116	its footprint, its courtyards and openings as openings, at its top), and `roof_faces` lays each plane's underside its
117	thickness below, plumb (`roof_rise`), so its slabs, IFC, sections and the walls attached under it follow its falls; plans
118	draw its creases thin. Under its type's variable layer a shaped roof's underside stays level at its base
119	(`Model::roof_under`, `roof_prisms`), as a floor's does: its layers in 3D and sections share `Variable::bounds` through
120	`Model::variable_under`, walls attached under it stop at that underside, IFC writes it as one closed faceted Brep
121	(`Model::roof_solid`), and `Model::check` refuses a point that leaves the layer thinner than nothing. `falls` (`falls.rs`) gives a floor or a flat roof its shape from its drains and the least fall:
122	catchments nearest each drain, ridges between them at the top's height, valleys from each drain to its catchment's corners,
123	each drain as deep as the fall takes its farthest corner; round an opening the valleys turn at its corners, which lie on
124	the drain's cone, and ridges drawn part the top first. A slab or flat roof whose top isn't one plane comes in from IFC
125	shaped (`import::shaped_top`), its variable layer marked by its `Description` or, under a level underside, guessed
126	(`import::guess_variable`); and a spot slope (`Spot::slope`) reads a floor's or roof's fall in a plan. A layer of a floor or roof type may be `variable` (one a type at most; never a wall's or a ceiling's): under a
127	shaped floor of that type, the underside stays level where the unshaped floor's was (`Model::floor_under`), the layers
128	above the variable one follow the top, those below it stay level, and the variable one takes up the difference
129	(`Variable::bounds`, which the 3D view's layers and sections share). Its pieces are then prisms from that level underside
130	(`Model::floor_prisms`), its volume is less where its top falls (`Model::floor_volume`, `model::volume` for IFC), a wall
131	attached under it stops at the level underside, and `Model::check` refuses a point that would leave the variable layer
132	thinner than nothing, saying by how much to raise it. Reinforcement arms a shaped floor only when a variable layer lies
133	over all its structure: the bars keep to the layers under it, as on a level floor that thick. Without one it refuses,
134	saying why. In the desktop, a floor selected shows Shape Editing in its contextual tab: Slope Arrow, Modify Sub Elements (a point, a corner or an edge's two ends,
135	`Floor::shape_pick`, to the Options Bar's Elevation), Add Point (a
136	click on the top, at the Options Bar's Elevation, above the unshaped top or, with Absolute, above the level; empty, the
137	top's height there), Add Split Line (two clicks, snapping to points, corners and edges) and Reset Shape, each a command.
138	While one is on, each point's height is labelled beside it (`Model::shape_labels`); under Modify Sub Elements a point's
139	grip drags it in plan at its height, its split lines with it (`Shape::moved`), in one `edit_shape`. In the 3D view the
140	same tools work on the floor's top: each point's and corner's grip drags its height up or down, and clicks land on the top
141	(`view3d::shape_handles`, `on_floor_top`, `shape_pick_3d`); both views run `shape.rs`. While a grip is held, either
142	view draws the creases its release will leave (`Model::shape_creases` of the floor with the shape it would have). Type Properties ticks a floor's or a roof's variable layer. A ceiling's `offset` is its underside; its `openings` are holes as a floor's
143	are, and `Model::ceiling_slabs` what's left. A shaft cuts each floor,
144	ceiling and roof its span reaches into over its outline, all the way through (`Model::less_shafts`). A stair or a ramp
145	is runs and landings laid out from its start (`stairs::stair`, `stairs::ramp`): a landing after `at` risers (a ramp's, `at`
146	mm up), as deep as the runs are wide, the next run turning by its `turn`; a railing on one follows its walk line moved out to
147	its side (`stairs::railing`), so it goes wherever its host goes. `modify` merges into fields that are objects (JSON Merge Patch), so `{"view_range": {"cut": 1500}}` keeps the rest; an element's own field can't be
148	called `category`, the tag every element carries.
149	
150	Sketches (`sketch.rs`) are how an outline is drawn, the one solver everything with an outline and holes uses: floors,
151	ceilings, roofs by footprint, shafts and filled regions now, topography next. A sketch is `SketchLine`s, straight or
152	arcs (a point `through`), in any order, either way round; `sketch::solve` cuts arcs into chords no more than 5° round,
153	welds ends within `TOL`, then names every problem at once with the lines it's about, what to fix first first
154	(`Problem::rank`: a line too short or out of range; two lines crossing, or one ending part way along another; two along
155	each other; three or more at a point; an end no other meets; a loop with no area), and otherwise walks the loops and nests
156	them by how many others each is inside: even, an outline (counter-clockwise), odd, a hole (clockwise) of the innermost loop
157	round it, so an island in a hole is an outline again. `solve_one` wants one outline (a floor's, a roof's). The element
158	keeps the sketch it was drawn or last edited by (`sketch` on floors, ceilings, roofs and shafts; empty when it was made
159	over the walls or read from a file): each line is a part with an id and a GUID of its own (`HasPart`, listed in
160	`parts_now` by the element's GUID), going with the element when it moves and new on a copy; part ids are not given
161	again once a line is gone, for as long as the project is open (the library remembers the lowest it has held; a file holds the
162	ids in use, so one a line had before it was deleted and the file saved may be given again after the file is reopened). Commands take `sketch` (lines `[[x,y],[x,y]]`, arcs `[[x,y],[x,y],[x,y]]`, or
163	`{start, end, through?, id?}`) in place of `boundary` and its holes; `edit_boundary` without one gives the lines to edit
164	(the kept sketch while it still draws the outline, `sketch::draws`, else the outline's edges as new lines) and with one
165	redraws it, a line sent back with its `id` keeping it (keeping a roof's gables on edges that stay); the `sketch` command
166	solves without making anything. Messages name a line by its id, or its place in the list while it has none. A boundary
167	given as points is cleaned (a repeated point dropped, and one within a millimetre of the last), and every outline a command
168	makes or changes, whichever command (`floor`, `modify`, `edit_boundary`, `move`…), is judged as the sketch of its edges
169	(`Model::check_edits`, asked by the engine after each command but Insert from File): a floor's, ceiling's or roof's boundary,
170	an opening or a courtyard, a shaft's boundary, that crosses itself or lies along itself, has an edge ending part way along
171	another, or a spike or keyhole slit, is refused, saying which edges and where, and what to do: redraw it with `edit_boundary`; give
172	`boundary` or `sketch` (with the walls that touch at a corner named only when it was taken from walls), or simple `openings` or
173	`courtyards` for one of those rings, for one a command was making;
174	redraw the mass whose outline it is, for one made by face or by `mass_floors` (a mass itself may still have a bow tie outline,
175	a spike or a corner touching an edge, so the message says the outline isn't simple, not that it crosses itself);
176	and, for a roof's opening, which `edit_boundary` does not edit, give `modify` a simple `openings`, and from `dormer` change the
177	dormer's width, height or position. That is a change from the base, which let
178	`modify` and the commands that weren't given points set such an outline. `Model::check` doesn't judge the whole project by
179	it: a file, an IFC import or a Revit import with a keyhole outline still opens, and what leaves its outline alone (`modify`
180	of its offset, `delete`, `edit_boundary` with a sketch that is simple) still works, and so does what moves, copies, turns or mirrors
181	it, which makes it no worse (a copy is judged against the elements the command was given, so a new floor drawn with a bow tie
182	the file also holds is refused); what changes its shape is asked to redraw it first. One line that crosses itself (a closed polyline round a bow tie, a spline with a loop) is found as two lines
183	crossing are, and a sketch is refused at once past 200,000 straight pieces (a circle is up to 8,193 of them), or when its
184	pieces lie so close together that telling which cross would take six million steps.
185	
186	The desktop's sketch mode (`crates/ui-egui/src/sketch.rs`) holds the lines until Finish Edit Mode, which solves them
187	first and says what's wrong for whoever drew it (`sketch::friendly`: what to fix, kind by kind, where, in the project's
188	units, and the lines by id) with those lines in the error colour; solved, it runs the command. Draw has every shape of
189	the Draw panel (`draw.rs`; lines, rectangles, polygons, circles, the arcs, Fillet Arc on two sketch lines, splines, ellipses,
190	polylines, Pick Lines: see [views and graphics](views-and-graphics.md)) and Pick Walls (a line along each wall's location
191	line, an arc along an arc wall); a sketch line is any curve, so a circle or an ellipse is a loop of its own. Modify picks
192	sketch lines (a click, a window box from the left, a crossing box from the right), a picked line's handles (its corners, a
193	spline's points, a circle's centre) are grips that take every one joined there with them, and Delete removes them; Ctrl+Z takes back a line; the plan's snaps take the
194	sketch's own ends, middles, crossings and curves as well as visible view-specific detail (`snap::in_sketch`). Floor, Ceiling, Roof and Shaft each start a new one (Boundary
195	Line, Sketch Ceiling); Edit Boundary redraws one selected. The Mode panel (Finish, Cancel; Edit Boundary) stands at the
196	ribbon's right end.
197	
198	What the line tools hold to, and don't (`curves.rs`, `draw.rs`, `sketch.rs`). A curve is drawn as chords none further than `FLAT`
199	(0.25 mm) from it: a polyline's arcs, a circle, a spline and a fitted spline (a span of a spline is cut by the greatest
200	second derivative on it, so a ten metre arch is hundreds of chords), up to `MAX_DRAWN` extra points in all; a polyline whose
201	arcs would take more is refused, and a circle past about 3.4 km of radius (`MAX_DRAWN` chords stray `FLAT` from it there) is drawn coarser than `FLAT` rather than in more, 0.37 mm off at 5 km and 2 mm off at 27 km.
202	An arc, a circle or an ellipse reaches no further than `MAX_COORD` from the origin, as a wall's arc must; a spline lies inside
203	its control points, and a fitted spline is held to its points only, a cubic through them straying a little past. A curve's
204	start and end are the points it was given. Offset moves a polyline's lines along themselves and its arcs about their own
205	centres and makes each corner where the moved sides cross; it gives nothing where a side would vanish or turn round, or a
206	corner is so sharp its mitre would be 50 offsets long, and it does not trim a fold it makes in a concave shape (Revit's
207	does); an ellipse or a spline offsets to a fitted spline within 0.05 mm. Fillet on walls keeps their doors and windows
208	where they stand and refuses to cut one off, but does not stretch a third wall that ended on the corner. A detail line with
209	no style gets Thin Lines by the project's name, else the English one, else the thin black solid style. Of the line tools,
210	Revit has default shortcuts for Trim/Extend to Corner (TR), Offset (OF), Fillet (FL), Split (SL) and Detail Line (DL), which
211	`corner`, `offset`, `fillet`, `split` and `detail_line` have; it has none for Trim/Extend to a boundary, vertices, Convert
212	Spline, Edit Boundary, line patterns and styles or fill patterns, which have none here. Explode Polyline is EX, ours (PX is
213	the desktop's Plumbing Fixture).

import json, sys, subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil
# usage: gen_fx.py out.json expr1 expr2 ...  -> runs `family` with number params each a formula, prints values
exprs = sys.argv[1:]
params = [
    {"name": "A", "kind": "length", "value": 1200},
    {"name": "B", "kind": "length", "value": 500},
    {"name": "C", "kind": "number", "value": 3},
    {"name": "D", "kind": "number", "value": -2.5},
    {"name": "Z", "kind": "number", "value": 0},
    {"name": "Yes", "kind": "yesno", "value": True},
    {"name": "No", "kind": "yesno", "value": False},
    {"name": "Ang", "kind": "angle", "value": 45},
    {"name": "Long Name X", "kind": "length", "value": 10},
]
for i, e in enumerate(exprs):
    params.append({"name": "F%d" % i, "kind": "number", "formula": e})
fam = {"name": "FX", "category": "generic", "parameters": params, "types": {"T": {}}}
cmd = 'family ' + json.dumps(fam)
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--cmd', cmd, '--cmd', 'family {"name":"FX"}'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
shutil.rmtree(d)
out = p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')
err = p.stderr.decode().strip()
if err:
    print('ERR', err)
for line in out:
    try:
        v = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        print(line); continue
    if 'values' in v:
        vals = v['values']['T']
        for i, e in enumerate(exprs):
            print('%-40s -> %r' % (e, vals.get('F%d' % i, '<missing>')))
        print('warnings', v.get('warnings'))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""sharp3.py loc_a loc_b ta tb ang...: wall A from (5000,0) to the joint (0,0) and B from the joint
at ang degrees, with locations; prints both programs' corners at the joint."""
import subprocess, json, os, tempfile, shutil, sys, math
orig = '/workspace/executable'
mine = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa68fa9ebdf329369/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
la, lb, ta, tb = sys.argv[1:5]
def corners(ang):
    a = math.radians(ang)
    bx, by = 5000 * math.cos(a), 5000 * math.sin(a)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/views-dims')
    cmds = ['wall {"points":[[5000,0],[0,0]],"type":"%s","location":"%s"}' % (ta, la), 'wall {"points":[[0,0],[%r,%r]],"type":"%s","location":"%s"}' % (bx, by, tb, lb),
            'grid {"start":[-100000,-50000],"end":[100000,-50000]}', 'grid {"start":[-50000,-100000],"end":[-50000,100000]}']
    args = [orig, 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        args += ['--cmd', c]
    subprocess.run(args + ['--save', 'p.bimcraft'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    res = []
    for exe in (orig, mine):
        out = []
        for r in ['{"id":100002,"face":"left","point":"end"}', '{"id":100002,"face":"right","point":"end"}', '{"id":100003,"face":"left","point":"start"}', '{"id":100003,"face":"right","point":"start"}']:
            xy = []
            for g, at in (('100005', '[-60000,0]'), ('100004', '[0,-60000]')):
                p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', 'p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'dimension {"refs":[{"id":%s},%s],"at":%s}' % (g, r, at)], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
                xy.append(round(json.loads(p.stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1])['values'][0] - 50000, 2))
            out.append(xy)
        res.append(out)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return res
for s in sys.argv[5:]:
    o, m = corners(float(s))
    print(s, 'SAME' if o == m else 'DIFF', o, '' if o == m else m)

== wall Wall ['WA']
{points: [[x,y],…], closed?, type?, level?, top_level?, top_offset?, height?, base_offset?, arc?, location?, attach_top?, attach_base?, room_bounding?} one wall per segment of its location line; up to the next level, or `height` mm tall (unconnected), or up to `top_level`, `top_offset` mm above it (0; negative, below it; the top must stay above the base). `arc`: degrees each turns from its start to its end, counter-clockwise (180, a half circle bulging to its right). `location`: the line of it the points are on: centre (the default), core-centre, exterior-finish, interior-finish, exterior-core or interior-core; its exterior side is to the left of its start to its end, so walls drawn clockwise face out. `attach_top`, `attach_base`: a roof or floor its top follows from below, or its base stands on. `room_bounding`: false for a wall rooms run past (a low wall, a balustrade); true, the default, bounds them
== door Door ['DR']
{at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?, flip_hand?} in the wall under `at`, or in `wall` centred `offset` mm from its start; with `family`, a door family's `type` (its first by default), which sizes the opening and draws the door
== window Window ['WN']
{at: [x,y] | wall: id, offset?, sill?, type?, family?, level?, mark?, flip_facing?} like door; `sill` defaults to the type's (a family's `Sill Height`)
== room Room ['RM']
{point: [x,y], level?, name?, number?, top_level?, limit_offset?, base_offset?, frozen?} bounded by the walls and the room separation lines around the point (walls the level's `computation_height` cuts; separation lines whatever their height). Placed where nothing encloses it, or in a space another room has (two rooms can't share one; the first keeps it), it is placed unbounded, a 1000 mm square, and the reply has a `warning`. Its height is Revit's: from `base_offset` mm over its level (0) up to `limit_offset` mm over its upper limit `top_level` (null: Not Bounded, over its own level). Unless given, 300 mm under the level above (`top_level` that level, `limit_offset` -300), or with none above, not bounded and 2500 mm tall. `elements` gives its `unbounded_height` and `volume_m3`, its area times that height. `frozen` (a yes or no; also `modify {id, frozen}`) keeps the boundary the room has now: it keeps its size whatever the walls do, and the walls are never searched for it again, which saves time in a project of many rooms. Unfrozen, it follows the walls again. Only an enclosed room can be frozen
== room_separator Room Separator []
{points: [[x,y],…], level?, closed?} room separation lines along `points`, one per segment (`closed` joins the last to the first): they bound rooms as walls do, to split an open space (a living room and its corridor) into rooms, and are nothing else, with no solid, no cut and no area. Returns their ids
== move Move ['MV']
{ids: [id,…], by: [dx, dy], end?: start|end} moves elements in plan; walls joined to a moved wall stretch to stay joined, and doors and windows slide along their walls. With `end`, only that end of one wall moves
== delete Delete ['DE']
{ids: [id,…]} deleting a wall deletes its doors and windows, deleting those their tags; a view takes its notes and spot elevations, and what a spot elevation reads takes it; dimensions lose what's deleted

You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler
written in Rust; README at /workspace/README.md), as a new Rust program built only from observed
behaviour. Many agents work in parallel, each owning one area. The VIEWS area (views and annotation,
`src/views/`) is owned by the agent that launched you; it split the area between several sub-agents.
Your part is given in your prompt. Do it fully and exactly; don't do the other parts.

- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it ONLY by running it (args, stdin,
  files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete
  it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`.

- Edit only the files your prompt gives you. You may add child modules of your own files

  `src/views/mod.rs`, `src/views/common.rs`, `src/views/model.rs` or anything outside `src/views/`; if you
  need a change there, copy what you need into your own files and say so in your final report.
- Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, in your own `/tmp/views-<yourpart>/`.
  Commit only Rust (your files). Don't write report/summary .md files into the repo.
- Never use bare `git stash`. Don't push. Don't touch other worktrees or branches but your own.

## Your worktree and base
You run in your own git worktree. FIRST run `git log --oneline -3`: your branch must contain commit
`9de3863` ("Views: the constraints hook…", after "Views: the module's skeleton…"). If it doesn't, run `git merge 9de3863` (or, in a fresh
clean worktree, `git reset --hard 9de3863`). Build with `cargo build --release --offline`
(about 15 s); the binary is `<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli`.

## The codebase (read the parts you need)
- `src/json.rs`: `Value` (insertion-ordered `Map`; `insert_sorted` for BTreeMap-like maps; `Value::f`,
  `Value::u`, `Value::s`; `jobj!{"k" => v, …}`), serde_json-identical parse errors and float
  formatting (`1000.0`, `1e+16`), `to_compact`/`to_pretty`, `.sorted()`. Command replies are printed
  with keys sorted (as serde_json::Value), so a reply's key order doesn't matter; a saved element's
  field order DOES (match the original's saved files exactly).
- `src/project.rs`: `Project` = `doc` (top-level sections in file order; `insert_top`, `section_mut`,
  `TOP_ORDER`) + `elements: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (each element a JSON object in the original's field
  order) + `library: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (`{kind, name, guid}` entries; ids count down from 999999 via
  `alloc_lib_id`, shared with the "parts" elements and types hold, e.g. a region's sketch lines
  `{id, guid, start, end}`, never reused in a session). `alloc_id()` for element ids; `find_guid`,
  `ids_of(cat)`, `lib_find(kind,name)`, `lib_guid`, `lib_name(guid)`, `lib_add`. Elements reference each
  other and library entries by GUID (`crate::rand::guid()` makes one).
- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute(cmd, params)`: resolves the command, snapshots the project, runs
  it, then runs `crate::check::check` (which calls every module's `check(pr)`, ours via
  `src/views/mod.rs::check`, which calls your file's `check`), rolls back on any error, and records an
  undo step labelled by the command's catalog label when the project changed (call
  `crate::views::mark_step()` in a command that must make a step even unchanged).
- `src/commands/params.rs`: param readers with the original's texts (`` `x` in mm is required``,
  `` `x` must be a number in mm, got … ``, points, text ≤ 256 chars; |mm| ≤ 1e9). Many commands have
  texts of their own: always probe.
- `src/model.rs`: levels by elevation, `resolve_level`/`level_param` with the original's errors (`tag`
  and `dimension` take `level`), `find` by id/GUID, `normalize_guid`, `level_of_view`.
- `src/styles/` (done by another agent): line patterns/styles, fill patterns, filled region types,
  text types, dimension types, line weights, object styles, units, phases, phase filters, design

`MINE=<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py [-f file_to_copy_into_cwd]

git add src/structure/family/geom.rs src/structure/family/check.rs src/structure/family/mod.rs src/structure/component.rs && git commit -q -m "Structure families: forms as the original's triangles, in its order, for IFC

Extrusions and revolves are built as the original's triangle lists (caps
per profile ear at the end and the start, then the sides edge by edge),
turned out as it turns them; a profile is reversed as given when it runs
clockwise. A mirrored component swaps each triangle's last two corners.
Voids cut each solid before them whose box (what is left of it) meets

"""A heavy cut: a revolved 60-corner profile cut by another; times both programs and compares
what `elements` says of the component."""
import sys, json, math, time, subprocess
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/family-agent')
from lib import ORIG, MINE

n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 60
prof = [[round(150 + 40 * math.cos(2 * math.pi * k / n) * (1 + 0.3 * (k % 2)), 3), round(100 + 40 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * k / n) * (1 + 0.3 * (k % 2)), 3)] for k in range(n)]
prof2 = [[round(150 + 30 * math.cos(2 * math.pi * k / n), 3), round(130 + 30 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * k / n), 3)] for k in range(n)]
fam = {"name": "H", "types": {"T": {}}, "forms": [
    {"plane": "xz", "profile": prof, "axis": [[0, 0], [0, 10]], "from": 0, "to": 360},
    {"plane": "xz", "profile": prof2, "axis": [[0, 0], [0, 10]], "from": 0, "to": 360, "void": True}]}
args = ['run', '--cmd', 'family ' + json.dumps(fam), '--cmd', 'component {"family":"H","at":[0,0]}', '--cmd', 'elements {"category":"component"}']
outs = []
for exe in (ORIG, MINE):
    t = time.time()
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd='/tmp/family-agent')
    outs.append(p.stdout.splitlines()[-1] if p.stdout else p.stderr[:300])
    print(exe.split('/')[-1], '%.2f s' % (time.time() - t))
print('same' if outs[0] == outs[1] else 'DIFF\n' + outs[0][:600] + '\n' + outs[1][:600])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""T-junctions: a wall ending inside another at a depth and an angle; which of its faces the
original cuts at the other's face on its side, and which it squares, with the cut's distance
along the face and where the face's end stands across the other wall."""
import json, math, re, subprocess, sys
D = '/tmp/ifc-export-agent/probe'
def fmt(x):
    s = '%.6f' % (x + 0.0)
    return s.rstrip('0')
cases = []
cmds = []
k = 0
for tA, tname in [(100.0, "Interior - 100mm"), (300.0, "Exterior - 300mm")]:
    for th in [30, 50, 70, 90, 110, 130, 150]:
        for e in [-100.0, -70.0, -40.0, 0.0, 40.0, 70.0, 99.0]:
            ox, oy = 20000.0 * (k % 10), 20000.0 * (k // 10)
            k += 1
            cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [[ox, oy], [ox + 10000, oy]]}))
            r = math.radians(th)
            endp = (ox + 5000.0, oy + e)
            startp = (round(endp[0] + 4000 * math.cos(r), 3), round(endp[1] + 4000 * math.sin(r), 3))
            cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [list(startp), list(endp)], "type": tname}))
            cases.append((tA, th, e, startp, endp, ox, oy))
open(D + '/teeprobe.txt', 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', D + '/teeprobe.txt', '--save', D + '/teeprobe.ifc'], capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.returncode:
    print(p.stderr[:2000]); sys.exit(1)
s = open(D + '/teeprobe.ifc').read()
ents = {int(m.group(1)): (m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in re.finditer(r'^#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', s, re.M)}
def refs(t): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', t)]
walls = [x for x in sorted(ents) if ents[x][0] == 'IFCWALL']
out = []
for ci, (tA, th, e, S, N, ox, oy) in enumerate(cases):
    wa = walls[2 * ci + 1]
    shape = refs(ents[wa][1])[1]
    prof = None
    for rp in refs(ents[shape][1]):
        if "'Body'" in ents[rp][1]:
            solid = refs(ents[rp][1])[-1]
            pr = refs(ents[solid][1])[0]
            poly = refs(ents[pr][1])[-1]
            prof = [tuple(float(v) for v in ents[x][1].strip('()').split(',')) for x in refs(ents[poly][1])][:-1]
    dx, dy = N[0] - S[0], N[1] - S[1]
    L = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    d = (dx / L, dy / L)
    n = (-d[1], d[0])
    # the end cap: profile points with x beyond L - 1000
    capx = [q for q in prof if q[0] > L - 1500]
    res = {}
    for face, yy in [('left', tA / 2), ('right', -tA / 2)]:
        pts = [q for q in capx if abs(q[1] - yy) < 1e-6]
        if not pts:
            res[face] = None
            continue
        x = max(q[0] for q in pts) if len(pts) == 1 else pts[0][0]
        # where would it be cut: the face line meets y = oy + 100 (the other's top face)
        P0 = (S[0] + n[0] * yy, S[1] + n[1] * yy)
        # P0 + d * s, y = oy + 100
        s_cut = (oy + 100.0 - P0[1]) / d[1] if abs(d[1]) > 1e-12 else None
        face_end_y = P0[1] + d[1] * L - oy
        res[face] = ('CUT' if s_cut is not None and abs(x - s_cut) < 1e-3 else ('SQ' if abs(x - L) < 1e-3 else 'x=%.3f' % x),
                     'cutdist=%.1f' % (L - s_cut) if s_cut is not None else '', 'faceend_y=%.1f' % face_end_y)
    out.append((tA, th, e, res))
    print('tA=%3d th=%3d e=%6.1f  left %s  right %s' % (tA, th, e, res['left'], res['right']))

p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', D + '/teeprobe.txt', '--save', D + '/teeprobe.ifc'], capture_output=True, text=True)
if p.returncode:
    print(p.stderr[:2000]); sys.exit(1)
s = open(D + '/teeprobe.ifc').read()
ents = {int(m.group(1)): (m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in re.finditer(r'^#(\d+)=(\w+)\((.*)\);$', s, re.M)}
def refs(t): return [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'#(\d+)', t)]
walls = [x for x in sorted(ents) if ents[x][0] == 'IFCWALL']
out = []
for ci, (tA, th, e, S, N, ox, oy) in enumerate(cases):
    wa = walls[2 * ci + 1]
    shape = refs(ents[wa][1])[1]
    prof = None
    for rp in refs(ents[shape][1]):
        if "'Body'" in ents[rp][1]:
            solid = refs(ents[rp][1])[-1]
            pr = refs(ents[solid][1])[0]
            poly = refs(ents[pr][1])[-1]
            prof = [tuple(float(v) for v in ents[x][1].strip('()').split(',')) for x in refs(ents[poly][1])][:-1]
    dx, dy = N[0] - S[0], N[1] - S[1]
    L = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    d = (dx / L, dy / L)
    n = (-d[1], d[0])
    # the end cap: profile points with x beyond L - 1000
    capx = [q for q in prof if q[0] > L - 1500]
    res = {}
    for face, yy in [('left', tA / 2), ('right', -tA / 2)]:
        pts = [q for q in capx if abs(q[1] - yy) < 1e-6]
        if not pts:
            res[face] = None
            continue
        x = max(q[0] for q in pts) if len(pts) == 1 else pts[0][0]
        # where would it be cut: the face line meets y = oy + 100 (the other's top face)
        P0 = (S[0] + n[0] * yy, S[1] + n[1] * yy)
        # P0 + d * s, y = oy + 100
        s_cut = (oy + 100.0 - P0[1]) / d[1] if abs(d[1]) > 1e-12 else None
        face_end_y = P0[1] + d[1] * L - oy
        res[face] = ('CUT' if s_cut is not None and abs(x - s_cut) < 1e-3 else ('SQ' if abs(x - L) < 1e-3 else 'x=%.3f' % x),
                     'cutdist=%.1f' % (L - s_cut) if s_cut is not None else '', 'faceend_y=%.1f' % face_end_y)
    out.append((tA, th, e, res))
    print('tA=%3d th=%3d e=%6.1f  left %s  right %s' % (tA, th, e, res['left'], res['right']))

import math, itertools
def unit_r(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+v[1]*v[1]); k = 1.0/l
    return (v[0]*k, v[1]*k)
def unit_d(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+v[1]*v[1])
    return (v[0]/l, v[1]/l)
def sub(a,b): return (a[0]-b[0], a[1]-b[1])
def add(a,b): return (a[0]+b[0], a[1]+b[1])
def mul(a,k): return (a[0]*k, a[1]*k)
def dot(a,b): return a[0]*b[0]+a[1]*b[1]
def cross(a,b): return a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0]
def left(d): return (-d[1], d[0])

CASES = {
    # name: (A start, A end (node), B start (node), B end, tA, tB, expected: True = mitre kept)
    '109': ((3000.0,-2000.0),(2500.0,1500.0),(2500.0,1500.0),(-1000.0,-2000.0),200.0,200.0, True),
    '127': ((-500.0,-500.0),(3000.0,-1000.0),(3000.0,-1000.0),(2000.0,-2000.0),100.0,100.0, False),
}

def variants(a0, a1, b0, b1, ta, tb, unit):
    p = a1
    dA = unit(sub(a1, a0)); dB = unit(sub(b1, b0))
    uA = mul(dA, -1.0); uB = dB
    th = max(ta, tb)
    res = {}
    # cos/sin based
    c = dot(uA, uB); s = abs(cross(uA, uB))
    res['c'] = c; res['s'] = s
    # along = (t/2) * (1 + c) / s  (equal thickness)
    res['along_cs'] = (ta / 2) * (1 + c) / s
    # half angle via atan2
    ang = math.atan2(cross(uA, uB), dot(uA, uB))
    res['ang'] = abs(ang)
    res['along_tan'] = (ta / 2) / math.tan(abs(ang) / 2)
    # bisector
    bis = unit(add(uA, uB))
    sh = abs(cross(bis, uA))  # sin(half)
    res['along_bis'] = (ta / 2) * dot(bis, uA) / sh
    # line meets through the node: A's face at offA through p + nA*offA, B's face p + nB*offB
    for offA, offB in [(ta/2, tb/2), (-ta/2, -tb/2), (ta/2, -tb/2), (-ta/2, tb/2)]:
        pA = add(p, mul(left(dA), offA)); pB = add(p, mul(left(dB), offB))
        den = cross(dA, dB)
        t = cross(sub(pB, pA), dB) / den
        x = add(pA, mul(dA, t))
        res['node_t%+d%+d' % (offA, offB)] = t
        res['node_al%+d%+d' % (offA, offB)] = dot(sub(x, p), uA)
        res['node_dist%+d%+d' % (offA, offB)] = math.sqrt(dot(sub(x, p), sub(x, p)))
        # start-based lines
        pA2 = add(a0, mul(left(dA), offA)); pB2 = add(b0, mul(left(dB), offB))
        t2 = cross(sub(pB2, pA2), dB) / den
        x2 = add(pA2, mul(dA, t2))
        res['st_al%+d%+d' % (offA, offB)] = dot(sub(x2, p), uA)
        res['st_dist%+d%+d' % (offA, offB)] = math.sqrt(dot(sub(x2, p), sub(x2, p)))
    return res

for unit in (unit_r, unit_d):
    for name, (a0, a1, b0, b1, ta, tb, exp) in CASES.items():
        r = variants(a0, a1, b0, b1, ta, tb, unit)
        print(name, unit.__name__, 'expect', 'kept' if exp else 'squared')
        for k, v in r.items():
            print('   ', k, repr(v))

== mass_floors Mass Floors ['MF']
{mass?, type?, prune?} a floor of the footprint at each level the mass crosses, from the one at its base up to, not including, the one at its top; every mass when no `mass`. The floors it makes hold their mass and level (`Mass Floor`), so a second run makes no second floor: it gives the ones there the mass's footprint now (and the `type` if given), and lists in `stale` those on a level the mass no longer crosses, which `prune` deletes. The reply has `ids` (every floor of the mass), `made`, `updated`, `stale` and `removed`. `schedule {category: massfloors}` lists each mass's floor area and volume on each level
== rebar Rebar []
{points: [[x,y,z],…], diameter, host?, grade?, layer?, closed?, count?, step?, level?} a reinforcing bar bent along `points` (mm; z over the level), `diameter` mm thick (3 to 100), of steel `grade` (CA-50 unless told). `host` is the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces (the level is then its level) and it goes with; `closed` joins the last point to the first, a hoop. With `count` bars (up to 1000), each is `step` [dx,dy,dz] from the last: a layer of bars, or hoops along a beam. Returns their ids. Its schedule lists Grade, Diameter, Length and Weight (kg, of steel at 7850 kg/m³), and a grouped one is a bar schedule
== reinforce Reinforce []
{host | hosts: [id, …], preset?, cover?, grade?, grade_stirrup?, clearance?, …} bars by rules for a beam, a column, a footing or a floor: the engineer says how many, how thick and how far apart (no standard's number sets them) and it lays them inside the cover and checks that they fit, saying what to change. All: `cover` (mm: one number, or {top, bottom, sides}, top and bottom the faces of a beam, a footing or a floor and the ends of a column; else the host's Cobrimento or ConcreteCover parameter), `grade` (CA-50), `grade_stirrup` (the stirrups' and ties'), `clearance` (least mm between bars; their thickness, at least 20, unless told). A spacing is the most between bars: they are spread evenly, so the last is where the first is from the other end. Beam: `bottom` and `top` {count, diameter, hook?} (`hook`, the straight leg in mm turned up from the bottom bars and down from the top ones at both ends, or {start, end}); `bottom.bent` {count, angle?, top?} bends `count` of the inner bottom bars up at each end (layer `bent`): they run `top` mm along the top face from each end (a fifth of the length unless told), slope down `angle` degrees (15 to 75, 45 unless told) and run along the bottom, and have no hook; `stirrup` {diameter, spacing, ends?: {length, spacing}, hook?} (`ends` closer in the first and last `length` mm; `hook` a tail in mm at the ends); `skin` {diameter, spacing} up each side between the rows; `anchor` {start?, end?} mm the bars run past the ends (0 flush, none a cover short). Column: `bars` {diameter, x?, y?, hook?, jog?} (`hook`, a leg turned into the section at the foot and the top, or {below, above}; `jog` {by, from_top, slope?} steps the bars in `by` mm toward the axis, starting `from_top` mm below the top and running `slope` mm up for each mm across (6 unless told), to leave room for the column above; bars along each face across its width and across its depth, corners counted, 2 each; a round column takes `count` instead of x and y, evenly round its circle, with hoops of 24 sides), `stirrup`, `ties` {diameter, hook?} across a rectangular section between bars that are not at a corner (`hook`, a tail in mm at each end), `anchor` {below?, above?}. Footing: `mesh` {x?, y?: {diameter, spacing}, hook?} (hook turns the ends up; a round footing's bars stop at its circle). Floor: `bottom` and `top` {x?, y?: {diameter, spacing}, hook?} (bars along east and north; `hook`, a leg turned up from a bottom mesh and down from a top one), stopping a cover sh
== detail Detail Level []
{view, detail?: coarse | medium | fine} how much a plan, a section or an elevation draws of what it cuts: coarse, one poché and openings as their gaps; medium, compound layers with the lines between them and an opening's leaf, swing and glass; fine (the default), the layers' patterns and a floor's surface pattern too. Without `detail` it only says what the view has
== favorite Favorites []
{action?: list|save|load|delete, kind?: material|family, name?, as?, replace?, path?} the user's favorites, kept in a file of their own (`path`; by default in their configuration folder) for every project to use: `save` the project's material or family `name` (a material with the picture its texture is made of, a family with the materials it is made of), under another name with `as`; `load` a favorite into the project, under another name with `as`, or over one it has already with `replace`; `delete` one from the favorites; `list` them (the default)
== paint Paint ['PT']
{id | ids, face?, material} paints a face of the elements with a material of the library, as Revit's Paint does: its colour and texture show in the 3D view over what their types are made of. `face`: a wall's `exterior` or `interior`, a floor's, roof's or ceiling's `top` or `bottom`, and `all` for a column, a component, a door, a window, a stair, a ramp or a railing; without it, every face the elements have. `material` null takes the paint off
== symbol_set Load Symbol Set []
{set: arei, names?: en|nl|fr} loads a set of families that are plan symbols and nothing else, each of one type `Standard` with no forms: `arei` is the Belgian AREI/RGIE's graphical symbols (Table 2.23: switches, sockets, light points, appliances, sources, domotics, protection), 76 families, switches in the switch category, sockets in outlet, luminaires in lighting and the rest generic. `names` is the language of their names, English, Dutch or French as the source prints them; as given none, French in a French project and English otherwise. A family the project has by that name stays as it is, so loading twice changes nothing; the reply lists `loaded` and `kept`. Place them as components
== create_group Create Group ['GP']
{ids, name?} a detail group made of detail lines, filled regions and text notes of one view, as Revit's Create Group: they become type `name`'s members (Group 1, 2… unless told), and one group of it takes their place, its origin the middle of them. Place it again with detail_group; ungroup gives its members back. Returns {id, name}
== repeating_detail Repeating Detail []
{type, start: [x,y], end: [x,y], spacing, mirrored?, view?} detail group `type` repeated along the line from `start` to `end`, every `spacing` mm from `start` (at most 2000 of them), each turned along the line, as Revit's Repeating Detail Component: brick coursing, blocking, batt ties. A view draws up to 10000 group members in all (a repeat places each member of the type again), so a type of 100 members repeats up to 100 times. Returns {id, count}
== group_type Detail Groups []
{name?, rename?, delete?: true} a detail group type: `rename` renames it, its groups following; `delete` takes it away while none of it is placed. Without `name`, it lists each with its members and how many are placed
== work_plane Work Plane []
{view?: a 3D view's name or id ({3D} unless given), level?: a level's name or id, points?: [[x, y, z], [x, y, z], [x, y, z]], surface?: {point: [x, y, z], normal: [x, y, z]}, offset?: mm} what a 3D view sketches on, as Revit's Work Plane > Set: a level; the plane through three `points` (not along a line), facing up unless upright; or a surface of the model, a point of it and the way it faces (a wall's face, picked). Any of them may be moved `offset` mm along its normal (up, for a level; 0 unless given), and may lie at any angle, upright too: what a tool may sketch on it is up to the tool (a floor, a ceiling, a roof and a shaft need a level plane, and stand on the highest level at or below it). Given only `offset`, the plane as it is is moved by that instead. Given nothing, it's the lowest level again, as it is until set. A level deleted takes its work plane with it. Says the plane: a point of it (`origin`), its `normal`, its height at the origin where it isn't upright (`z`) and its `slope` in degrees from level

import json, subprocess, tempfile, shutil
Ms = ['0', '0.001', '1', '1000', '1000000', '1000000000', '123.456']
ds = []
for e in range(-16, 0):
    for k in (1, 2, 3, 5, 7):
        ds.append('%de%d' % (k, e))
exprs = []
for M in Ms:
    for d in ds:
        exprs.append((M, d, '%s = %s + %s' % (M, M, d)))
params = []
for i, (M, d, e) in enumerate(exprs):
    params.append({"name": "F%d" % i, "kind": "number", "formula": e})
fam = {"name": "FX", "category": "generic", "parameters": params, "types": {"T": {}}}
dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--cmd', 'family ' + json.dumps(fam), '--cmd', 'family {"name":"FX"}'], cwd=dd, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
shutil.rmtree(dd)
lines = p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')
print(p.stderr.decode()[:500])
v = json.loads(lines[-1])['values']['T']
for M in Ms:
    row = []
    last_true = None; first_false = None
    for i, (MM, d, e) in enumerate(exprs):
        if MM != M: continue
        val = v['F%d' % i]
        row.append((float(d), val))
    row.sort()
    s = ' '.join('%s:%d' % (d, int(val)) for d, val in [(dd_, vv) for dd_, vv in row])
    # threshold: largest d true
    trues = [d for d, val in row if val == 1.0]
    falses = [d for d, val in row if val == 0.0]
    print(M, 'max true', max(trues) if trues else None, 'min false', min(falses) if falses else None)

import math, itertools
# walls: 1 (0,0)->(4000,1000); 4 (-1000,4000)->(0,0); thickness 200 -> h=100 (left face = interior since drawn CCW)
want = (72.76068751089917, 121.26781251816692)
A0=(0.0,0.0); A1=(4000.0,1000.0); B0=(-1000.0,4000.0); B1=(0.0,0.0)
h=100.0
def normals(a0,a1,h):
    dx=a1[0]-a0[0]; dy=a1[1]-a0[1]; L=math.hypot(dx,dy); L2=math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)
    out={}
    out['n=(-dy/L,dx/L)*h'] = ((-dy/L)*h, (dx/L)*h)
    out['n=(-dy*h/L,dx*h/L)'] = (-dy*h/L, dx*h/L)
    out['n=(-dy,dx)*(h/L)'] = (-dy*(h/L), dx*(h/L))
    out['n=(-dy/L2,dx/L2)*h'] = ((-dy/L2)*h, (dx/L2)*h)
    out['n=(-dy,dx)/L*h'] = (-dy/L*h, dx/L*h)
    out['n=-(dy/L)*h'] = (-(dy/L*h), dx/L*h)
    u=(dx/L,dy/L)
    out['u then n'] = (-u[1]*h, u[0]*h)
    out['u2 then n'] = (-(dy/L2)*h, (dx/L2)*h)
    inv=1.0/L
    out['inv'] = (-dy*inv*h, dx*inv*h)
    out['inv2'] = ((-dy*inv)*h, (dx*inv)*h)
    return out
def lines(a0,a1,n):
    p=(a0[0]+n[0],a0[1]+n[1]); q=(a1[0]+n[0],a1[1]+n[1])
    return p,q
def inters(p1,p2,q1,q2):
    out={}
    d=(p2[0]-p1[0],p2[1]-p1[1]); e=(q2[0]-q1[0],q2[1]-q1[1])
    den=d[0]*e[1]-d[1]*e[0]
    t=((q1[0]-p1[0])*e[1]-(q1[1]-p1[1])*e[0])/den
    out['p+t d']=(p1[0]+t*d[0],p1[1]+t*d[1])
    s=((q1[0]-p1[0])*d[1]-(q1[1]-p1[1])*d[0])/den
    out['q+s e']=(q1[0]+s*e[0],q1[1]+s*e[1])
    # cramer line eq
    a1_=p2[1]-p1[1]; b1_=p1[0]-p2[0]; c1=a1_*p1[0]+b1_*p1[1]
    a2_=q2[1]-q1[1]; b2_=q1[0]-q2[0]; c2=a2_*q1[0]+b2_*q1[1]
    det=a1_*b2_-a2_*b1_
    out['cramer']=((b2_*c1-b1_*c2)/det,(a1_*c2-a2_*c1)/det)
    # p + d * t with t computed via cross(q1 - p1, e) / cross(d, e) with other order
    t2=((q1[0]-p1[0])*e[1]-(q1[1]-p1[1])*e[0])/(d[0]*e[1]-d[1]*e[0])
    out['p+d*t2']=(p1[0]+d[0]*t2,p1[1]+d[1]*t2)
    # lerp form
    out['lerp']=(p1[0]*(1-t)+p2[0]*t, p1[1]*(1-t)+p2[1]*t)
    out['lerp2']=(p1[0]+(p2[0]-p1[0])*t, p1[1]+(p2[1]-p1[1])*t)
    out['lerp_s']=(q1[0]*(1-s)+q2[0]*s, q1[1]*(1-s)+q2[1]*s)
    # determinant form (wikipedia)
    x1,y1=p1;x2,y2=p2;x3,y3=q1;x4,y4=q2
    D=(x1-x2)*(y3-y4)-(y1-y2)*(x3-x4)
    out['wiki']=(((x1*y2-y1*x2)*(x3-x4)-(x1-x2)*(x3*y4-y3*x4))/D, ((x1*y2-y1*x2)*(y3-y4)-(y1-y2)*(x3*y4-y3*x4))/D)
    return out
NA=normals(A0,A1,h); NB=normals(B0,B1,h)
for (kn,na) in NA.items():
    nb=NB[kn]
    pa=lines(A0,A1,na); pb=lines(B0,B1,nb)
    for order in [0,1]:
        if order==0: r=inters(pa[0],pa[1],pb[0],pb[1])
        else: r=inters(pb[0],pb[1],pa[0],pa[1])
        for k,v in r.items():
            mark = '<<<<' if v==want else ('x' if v[0]==want[0] else ('y' if v[1]==want[1] else ''))
            if mark: print(kn, order, k, v, mark)
# unit direction based lines
print('done')

c=(0.0,0.0)
def unit(a,b):
    dx=b[0]-a[0]; dy=b[1]-a[1]; L=math.hypot(dx,dy); return (dx/L, dy/L)
u1=unit((0.0,0.0),(4000.0,1000.0))   # wall 1 out of c
u4=unit((-1000.0,4000.0),(0.0,0.0))  # wall 4 into c
n1=(-u1[1],u1[0]); n4=(-u4[1],u4[0])
h=100.0
cands={}
s=(n1[0]+n4[0], n1[1]+n4[1])
dot=n1[0]*n4[0]+n1[1]*n4[1]
cands['h*(n1+n4)/(1+dot)'] = (c[0]+h*s[0]/(1+dot), c[1]+h*s[1]/(1+dot))
cands['(n1+n4)*(h/(1+dot))'] = (c[0]+s[0]*(h/(1+dot)), c[1]+s[1]*(h/(1+dot)))
# bisector unit * h / cos(half)
sl=math.hypot(*s); b=(s[0]/sl, s[1]/sl)
cosh=b[0]*n1[0]+b[1]*n1[1]
cands['b*h/cos'] = (c[0]+b[0]*h/cosh, c[1]+b[1]*h/cosh)
cands['b*(h/cos)'] = (c[0]+b[0]*(h/cosh), c[1]+b[1]*(h/cosh))
# half angle from directions
# tangent form: offset point = c + n1*h + u1 * (h * tan(theta/2)) etc
cr = u4[0]*u1[1]-u4[1]*u1[0]
dt = u4[0]*u1[0]+u4[1]*u1[1]
# intersection of line c+n1 h + t u1 with c + n4 h + s u4: t = h*(n4-n1)·?
# Solve: n1 h + t u1 = n4 h + s u4
den = u1[0]*u4[1]-u1[1]*u4[0]
w=( (n4[0]-n1[0])*h, (n4[1]-n1[1])*h )
t = (w[0]*u4[1]-w[1]*u4[0])/den
cands['n1h + t u1'] = (c[0]+n1[0]*h+t*u1[0], c[1]+n1[1]*h+t*u1[1])
cands['n1h + t u1 b'] = (n1[0]*h+u1[0]*t, n1[1]*h+u1[1]*t)
ss = (w[0]*u1[1]-w[1]*u1[0])/den
cands['n4h + s u4'] = (c[0]+n4[0]*h+ss*u4[0], c[1]+n4[1]*h+ss*u4[1])
# tan half
th = (1-dt)/cr if cr!=0 else 0
for k,v in cands.items():
    print(k, v, '<<<' if v==want else '')
print('want', want)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""bound.py n seed: builds two walls meeting exactly at the sharpness limit (equal thickness),
asks the original whether each corner of A's end is mitred, and prints the candidate formulas."""
import subprocess, json, os, sys, tempfile, shutil, math, random
orig = '/workspace/executable'
n = int(sys.argv[1]); random.seed(int(sys.argv[2]))
TY = {100.0: 'Interior - 100mm', 200.0: 'Generic - 200mm', 300.0: 'Generic - 300mm'}

def unit(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+v[1]*v[1]); k = 1.0/l
    return (v[0]*k, v[1]*k)
def sub(a,b): return (a[0]-b[0], a[1]-b[1])
def add(a,b): return (a[0]+b[0], a[1]+b[1])
def mul(a,k): return (a[0]*k, a[1]*k)
def dot(a,b): return a[0]*b[0]+a[1]*b[1]
def cross(a,b): return a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0]
def left(d): return (-d[1], d[0])

def query(d, refs):
    out = []
    for r in refs:
        xy = []
        for g in ('100005', '100004'):
            p = subprocess.run([orig, 'run', 'p.bimcraft', '--cmd', 'dimension {"refs":[{"id":%s},%s],"at":[-60000,-60000]}' % (g, r)], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
            xy.append(json.loads(p.stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1])['values'][0] - 50000)
        out.append(xy)
    return out

def one():
    while True:
        v = (random.randint(-9, 9), random.randint(-9, 9))
        if v != (0, 0):
            break
    sgn = random.choice([1, -1])
    w = (3*v[0] - 4*sgn*v[1], 4*sgn*v[0] + 3*v[1])

steps.message:
I've finished the ARCH area. It's committed on branch `worktree-agent-aa380c34464cd9919`, latest commit `208af63`, with a clean tree. Almost everything matches the original exactly; the differences left are mostly last-digit rounding (about 1e-13) on diagonal walls and arcs.

**Checks run:** a regression suite of 110 script files run on both programs, comparing replies, errors and saved files with GUIDs normalised: 1210 groups the same, 87 different. Of the 87, 27 are `modify` lines (an edit command my build doesn't have), 3 use `column`, which my build lacks, and the rest are the rounding cases listed below. The fuzzers on new seeds had no differences (3 × 80 parameter runs, 3 × 40 random command sequences). The unit tests pass.

**Fixed this session:**
- **Floors from walls:** the outline now starts at the same corner as the original's, including when a dangling wall is drawn before the loop. This also fixed some overlapping-loop and diagonal cases.
- **T-junctions:** a later wall's or separator's end on an earlier line now lands where the original puts it, including the case within 1 mm of a corner, where the original treats a line's start and end differently.
- **Rooms:**
  - Rooms now read walls first, then room separators, then columns; this decides where frozen rooms' saved outlines start.
  - Adding a room no longer recomputes every earlier room; 30 rooms over 122 walls went from 10.3 s to 1.1 s of CPU (the original takes 5.8 s).
- **Inputs given as arrays:** `roof extrusion`, stair/ramp `landings` and `edit_shape` points and lines now accept the field-list form, with the original's error texts. Shape points and lines also validate `id`/`guid` as the original does.
- **Shape point ids after `open`:** new point and line ids now go below the ones already in the file, as the original's do.

**Per command:**
- **Same in every test:** `door`, `window`, `shaft`, `dormer`, `room_separator`, `stair`, `ramp`, `railing`, `mass`, `mass_floors`, `wall_by_face`, `floor_by_face`, `roof_by_face`, `update_by_face`, `show_mass`, `add_point`, `add_split_line`, `reset_shape`, `flip`, and `roof` (all forms).
- **`wall`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `room`, `sketch`, `edit_boundary`, `edit_shape`:** match, except where diagonal walls join or arcs are traced. There my wall-join arithmetic differs from the original's; for example, a closed triangle's corner comes out as exactly 0 in mine and 6.5e-14 in the original. Arc points differ in the last digits. Also:
  - Frozen rooms' saved outline at the wall faces differs in the last digits on diagonals.
  - A room separator ending inside a wall near a corner gives a different face outline.
  - With an "exterior-finish" loop plus an overlapping interior wall, one corner is off in the last digit.
  - I spent a long time trying to reproduce the original's join arithmetic and couldn't find the exact formula.
- **`falls`:** fo1 20/20, fr2 12/14. Still different: a drain exactly on a diagonal ridge, and a single ridge from the outline to an opening where the original says the top "can't fall".

**Edits outside `src/arch` and `src/geom` (6 lines, unchanged since before):**
- `src/main.rs`: `pub mod geom;`
- `src/session.rs`: calls `crate::arch::check_edits(before, after, cid)` before `crate::check::check`.
- `src/styles/parameters.rs`: adds `"Mass Face"` to `RESERVED`.

**What other areas must provide or call:**
- **Readers:** the loader should run `crate::check::check` on open, with errors as `open: {path}: {msg}`. They can use:
  - `rooms::room_area`, `room_space`, `space_at`, `region_at_faces`, `column_outline`
  - `slabs::net_area`, `openings::opening_size`, `stairs::layout`, `railing_path`, `risers`, `stair_length`, `ramp_length`
  - `roofs::roof_faces`, `ridge`, `outline`, `plan_area`, `eave_height`, `mass::Mass`, `slices`
- **Edit:** `move`, `rotate` and `mirror` must also transform frozen rooms' saved outlines and shape points. My outline check lets these commands through unchecked.
- **IFC and views:**
  - `walls::footprint`, `walls::joined_centres`, `walls::Wall`
  - `hosts::pieces`, `z_at`, `wall_heights`, `height_along`
  - `shape::lift` with the new `geom::tri::plane_groups` (which triangles merge into each face of a shaped top), plus `geom::skeleton`, `geom::tri` and `geom::graph`. The shaped-floor asset's top face count (6) matches what `edit_shape` reports.
  - One difference: the IFC wall profile includes the centre-line corner points, but `walls::footprint` gives a plain 4-corner ring.
- **Shared code:**
  - `project.rs` `lowest_lib_id` doesn't look at ids stored inside elements. I work around it for shape ids, but other areas allocating ids after `open` could collide.
  - `cloud::file::ref_of` accepts `"+5"` as an id; the original rejects it.
- **Structure:** rooms read `column` and `structuralcolumn` elements; my build has no `column` command.

Scratch scripts and test inputs are in `/tmp/arch-agent/` (`reg2.py` runs the regression).

import math, itertools
want = (72.76068751089917, 121.26781251816692)
A0=(0.0,0.0); A1=(4000.0,1000.0); B0=(-1000.0,4000.0); B1=(0.0,0.0)
h=100.0
def frame(a0,a1):
    dx=a1[0]-a0[0]; dy=a1[1]-a0[1]; L=math.hypot(dx,dy)
    u=(dx/L,dy/L); n=(-u[1],u[0]); return u,n,L
uA,nA,LA=frame(A0,A1); uB,nB,LB=frame(B0,B1)
def cross(a,b): return a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0]
res=[]
# P = base + u*t + n*h  for base in {A0, A1, B0, B1}
for (base, u, n, L, name) in [(A0,uA,nA,LA,'A0'),(A1,uA,nA,LA,'A1'),(B0,uB,nB,LB,'B0'),(B1,uB,nB,LB,'B1')]:
    # the other line
    if name.startswith('A'): ob, ou, on = B0, uB, nB
    else: ob, ou, on = A0, uA, nA
    # line1: base + n h + t u ; line2: ob + on h + s ou
    p=(base[0]+n[0]*h, base[1]+n[1]*h); q=(ob[0]+on[0]*h, ob[1]+on[1]*h)
    w=(q[0]-p[0], q[1]-p[1])
    t=cross(w,ou)/cross(u,ou)
    cands={
      'base+u*t+n*h': (base[0]+u[0]*t+n[0]*h, base[1]+u[1]*t+n[1]*h),
      'base+(u*t+n*h)': (base[0]+(u[0]*t+n[0]*h), base[1]+(u[1]*t+n[1]*h)),
      'base+n*h+u*t': (base[0]+n[0]*h+u[0]*t, base[1]+n[1]*h+u[1]*t),
      'p+u*t': (p[0]+u[0]*t, p[1]+u[1]*t),
    }
    # t computed relative to base without offset then offset
    w0=(ob[0]-base[0], ob[1]-base[1])
    t0=(cross(w0,ou) + h*(cross(on,ou)-cross(n,ou)))/cross(u,ou)
    cands['t0 base+u*t0+n*h']=(base[0]+u[0]*t0+n[0]*h, base[1]+u[1]*t0+n[1]*h)
    for k,v in cands.items():
        res.append((v==want, v[0]==want[0], v[1]==want[1], name, k, v))
res.sort(key=lambda x:(not x[0], not x[1], not x[2]))
for r in res[:10]: print(r)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For several turn angles, is an L of two 300 walls joined (left face end of wall 1 != its endpoint)?"""
import sys, subprocess, json, math
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
angs = [float(a) for a in sys.argv[1:]]
for turn in angs:
    t = math.radians(180 - turn)  # direction of second wall: turn measured as interior angle
    # wall1 east from (0,0) to (10000,0); wall2 from (10000,0) at interior angle `turn` (between the walls)
    # interior angle a: second wall direction = (cos(180-a), sin(180-a))
    d = (math.cos(t), math.sin(t))

want = (72.76068751089917, 121.26781251816692)
A0=(0.0,0.0); A1=(4000.0,1000.0); B0=(-1000.0,4000.0); B1=(0.0,0.0)
h=100.0
def frame(a0,a1):
    dx=a1[0]-a0[0]; dy=a1[1]-a0[1]; L=math.hypot(dx,dy)
    u=(dx/L,dy/L); n=(-u[1],u[0]); return u,n,L,dx,dy
uB,nB,LB,dx,dy=frame(B0,B1)
res={}
for along_name, along in [('L-100', LB-100), ('L-100 sqrt', math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)-100)]:
    x,y = along, h
    res[along_name+' a']=(B0[0]+uB[0]*x+nB[0]*y, B0[1]+uB[1]*x+nB[1]*y)
    res[along_name+' b']=(B0[0]+(uB[0]*x+nB[0]*y), B0[1]+(uB[1]*x+nB[1]*y))
    res[along_name+' c']=(B0[0]+(uB[0]*x-uB[1]*y), B0[1]+(uB[1]*x+uB[0]*y))
    res[along_name+' d']=(uB[0]*x+nB[0]*y+B0[0], uB[1]*x+nB[1]*y+B0[1])
    # rotation matrix with cos/sin from atan2
    ang=math.atan2(dy,dx); c=math.cos(ang); s=math.sin(ang)
    res[along_name+' rot']=(B0[0]+c*x-s*y, B0[1]+s*x+c*y)
    res[along_name+' rot2']=(c*x-s*y+B0[0], s*x+c*y+B0[1])
    res[along_name+' rot3']=(B0[0]+(c*x-s*y), B0[1]+(s*x+c*y))
for k,v in res.items():
    print(k, v, v==want, v[0]==want[0], v[1]==want[1])
print(want)

    dx=a1[0]-a0[0]; dy=a1[1]-a0[1]; L=math.hypot(dx,dy)
    u=(dx/L,dy/L); n=(-u[1],u[0]); return u,n,L,dx,dy
uB,nB,LB,dx,dy=frame(B0,B1)
res={}
for along_name, along in [('L-100', LB-100), ('L-100 sqrt', math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)-100)]:
    x,y = along, h
    res[along_name+' a']=(B0[0]+uB[0]*x+nB[0]*y, B0[1]+uB[1]*x+nB[1]*y)
    res[along_name+' b']=(B0[0]+(uB[0]*x+nB[0]*y), B0[1]+(uB[1]*x+nB[1]*y))
    res[along_name+' c']=(B0[0]+(uB[0]*x-uB[1]*y), B0[1]+(uB[1]*x+uB[0]*y))
    res[along_name+' d']=(uB[0]*x+nB[0]*y+B0[0], uB[1]*x+nB[1]*y+B0[1])
    # rotation matrix with cos/sin from atan2
    ang=math.atan2(dy,dx); c=math.cos(ang); s=math.sin(ang)
    res[along_name+' rot']=(B0[0]+c*x-s*y, B0[1]+s*x+c*y)
    res[along_name+' rot2']=(c*x-s*y+B0[0], s*x+c*y+B0[1])
    res[along_name+' rot3']=(B0[0]+(c*x-s*y), B0[1]+(s*x+c*y))
for k,v in res.items():
    print(k, v, v==want, v[0]==want[0], v[1]==want[1])
print(want)

== cad_layers CAD Layers []
{id, hide?: [layer, …], show?: [layer, …], view?} a CAD import's layers, each with its colour and linetype and whether it's shown; `hide` and `show` change which it shows in every view, or with `view` in that view only (its Visibility/Graphics, by the drawing's name)
== reload_cad Reload CAD []
{cad} reads a linked CAD drawing's file again, so every import of it shows what the file holds now (opening the project does too). Returns whether it changed
== reinforcement_preset Reinforcement Presets []
{name?, kind?: beam|column|footing|floor, params?, rename?, delete?: true} a named set of the parameters `reinforce` takes for one kind of host (`params`: its `cover`, `grade`, `grade_stirrup`, `clearance` and what its kind takes, and not `host`), kept in the project; `reinforce` with `preset` takes it and lets what is given with it replace its own. Without `name`, lists them. It is not checked against any host until it arms one
== text_type Text Types []
{name?, font?, size?, bold?, italic?, underline?, width_factor?, color?, border?, border_offset?, border_pen?, like?, rename?, delete?: true} a text type of the project's: its `font`, any the system has, or one BIMCraft carries (IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono, BIMCraft Lettering: single-stroke capitals); Arial, the default, letters on any system (where it isn't installed, Liberation Sans, Arimo, Helvetica or the like stands in, else IBM Plex Sans), and a font a file names that this system hasn't is stood in for likewise. Its capitals' height on paper (`size`, mm, 2.5 for a new one), bold, italic and underlined or not (a family's own bold and italic faces where it has them), `width_factor` (1: as the font draws it), its colour ("#rrggbb" or [r, g, b], black unless told), and whether a border is drawn round its notes, `border_offset` mm on paper out from their text (where a leader starts too; 1), in pen `border_pen` (0 to 16; 1). A new one starts as `like` says, or as 2.5mm Arial. A project starts with 2.5mm, 3.5mm and 5mm. `rename` renames it, its notes following; `delete` takes it away while no note is of it. Without `name`, it lists every type, the fonts this system has, and the font that letters each type here (`drawn_with`)
== dimension_type Dimension Types []
{name?, like?, rename?, delete?: true, …values} a dimension type of the project's, as Revit's type parameters, lengths mm on paper. Graphics: `string` continuous|baseline|ordinate (Dimension String Type; baseline lines `baseline_spacing` apart, 7), `tick` diagonal|arrow|open_arrow|dot|none, `tick_size` (2), `line_pen` and `tick_pen` (0 to 16; 4 and 7), `color` ("#rrggbb" or [r, g, b]), `line_extension` past the outer witness lines (0.8), `witness` gap_to_element|fixed (Witness Line Control), `witness_length` when fixed (5), `witness_gap` off what it measures (0.6), `witness_extension` past the dimension line (0.8), `centre_mark` on radial and diameter ones. Text: `font` (as text types take; Arial), `text_size` (2.5), `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `width_factor` (1), `text_offset` off the line (1), `background` opaque|transparent, `read` up_then_left|up_then_right (Read Convention), `units` (mm, cm, m, in, ft, ft-in; null for the project's) and `decimals` (0 to 6; null as the units show), `radius_symbol` (R), `diameter_symbol` (Ø), `equality_text` (EQ). A new one starts as `like` says, else as the default. A project starts with `Diagonal - 2.5mm Arial` (aligned, linear, angular and arc length dimensions start in it) and `Arrow - 2.5mm Arial` (radial and diameter ones). `rename` renames it, its dimensions following; `delete` takes it away while no dimension is of it. Without `name`, it lists every type
== line_pattern Line Patterns []
{name?, segments?: [{dash: mm} | {space: mm} | "dot" | {dot_length: mm} | {offset: {length, count, distance}} | {wave: {length, frequency, amplitude}} | {zigzag: {length, frequency, amplitude}} | {text: {length, size, text}}, …], rename?, delete?: true} a line pattern of the project's: 1–32 freely ordered graphic segments, each 0.05–100 mm long on paper, so it reads the same at any scale. Offsets have 2–9 lines spaced symmetrically; frequency is cycles per segment, 0.1–100; amplitude and spacing are mm. Text uses bundled IBM Plex Sans, size is maximum capital height (shrinks to fit length), 1–256 single-line characters, following the curve. All graphics preserve the centerline. A project starts with Dash, Long Dash, Dot, Dash Dot, Hidden and Centre; Solid is a line with none. `rename` renames it, the line styles using it following; `delete` takes it away, while no style uses it. Without `name`, it lists every pattern
== line_style Line Styles []
{name?, pen?, color?: "#rrggbb" | [r, g, b], pattern?: name | "Solid", rename?, delete?: true} a line style of the project's, as Revit's: the pen (0, a hairline, to 16) its lines draw in, their colour (black unless told) and their line pattern. A new one needs `pen`; one changed keeps what it isn't given. A project starts with Hairline, Thin Lines, Medium Lines, Wide Lines, Hidden Lines, Centre Lines and Overhead Lines. `rename` renames it, the lines drawn in it following; `delete` takes it away, while no line is drawn in it. Without `name`, it lists every style
== fill_pattern Fill Patterns []
{name?, target?: drafting|model, lines?: [{angle, spacing, origin?: [x, y], shift?, dashes?: [mm, -mm, …]}, …], drawn?: scale | null, rename?, delete?: true} a fill pattern of the project's, as Revit's (and a PAT file's): families of parallel lines, each at `angle` degrees through `origin`, its lines `spacing` apart and each `shift` along from the last, whole or dashed (`dashes`: a dash's length, a space's as a negative one, 0 a dot); no lines, it fills solid. A drafting pattern's lengths are mm on paper, the same at any scale; a model pattern's mm in the building. A project starts with Solid fill, Diagonal Up and Down, Crosshatch, Diagonal Crosshatch, Horizontal, Vertical, Sand, Brick 225 x 75 and Tile 300. `rename` renames it, the region types filling with it following; `delete` takes it away while no type uses it. `drawn` is the scale (1 : n, its n) of the view one made of lines (`make_fill_pattern`) was drawn in: such a one given a new `target` and no `lines` is rescaled, a drafting one being the drawing on paper at that scale; null forgets it. Without `name`, it lists every pattern
== filled_region_type Filled Region Types []
{name?, foreground?: pattern | null, foreground_color?, background?: pattern | null, background_color?, masking?, rename?, delete?: true} a filled region type of the project's: its foreground pattern over its background one, each in its colour ("#rrggbb" or [r, g, b], black unless told), over the paper when `masking` (it hides what's under it). A new one starts with none. A project starts with Solid Black, Diagonal Up, Crosshatch, Sand, Brick and Masking. `rename` renames it, its regions following; `delete` takes it away while no region is of it. Without `name`, it lists every type
== line_weights Line Weights []
{model?: [{scale, widths}, …], annotation?: [16 widths], reset?: true} the project's line weights, as Revit's Manage > Line Weights: what each pen draws on paper, mm. `model` gives, whole, the model's pens 1 to 16 at each of its scales (1 to 32 of them, 1 : `scale`): a view draws its walls, doors, patterns and the rest of the model in the column of the scale nearest its own (by how many times finer or coarser; the finer of two as near). `annotation` gives the 16 pens that dimensions, tags, text, grids, levels and marks draw in, at any scale. Each width is 0.01 to 20 mm; pen 0 is always a hairline. `reset` goes back to what a project in its units starts with (the model's pens wider at finer scales; at 1 : 100, pen 4 is 0.18 mm and pen 10 0.35 mm). Without any, it says what they are, each scale named as the project's units name it, and `own` whether the project has set them
== object_styles Object Styles []
{categories?: {category: {projection?: pen, cut?: pen}, …}, reset?: true} the project's object styles, as Revit's Manage > Object Styles: the pen (0, a hairline, to 16) each model category draws its lines in where it is seen (`projection`) and where a view cuts it (`cut`), in every plan and section; a view's Visibility/Graphics overrides them. A category given keeps the pen it isn't given. The rest of an element's lines keep their own: a compound wall's layers, a door's jambs, a stair's walk line. `reset` goes back to what a project starts with (cut pen 10 and seen pen 4; a door's and a window's cut 6, a railing seen 6, a mass 4 both). Without either, it says each model category's, `own` whether the project has set it apart
